<meta>This is the title page of the work "Pa’amon ve-Rimmon." It serves as a combined edition of two earlier summaries of Rabbi Moses Cordovero’s seminal Kabbalistic text, "Pardes Rimmonim" (The Orchard of Pomegranates). The imagery of bells and pomegranates is a biblical reference to the hem of the High Priest's robe.</meta>

# The Book
## Bell and Pomegranate
->Upon the edges of the Holy Orchard: full and overflowing: Old and New, this is the book<- <note>The "Holy Orchard" refers to the *Pardes Rimmonim* by Moses Cordovero. The title "Bell and Pomegranate" refers to Exodus 28:34, describing the High Priest's vestments.</note>
# Pomegranate Nectar and the Book of the Pomegranate Sliver

How good and how pleasant it is to dwell together—both of them intended one thing: a summary that is good, sweet, and useful. Both of them teach for our benefit: whether to begin in the <term>Wisdom of Kabbalah|Jewish mysticism</term> to enter the "Gate of the King," or to understand the <term>Work of Creation|The mysteries of the physical universe</term> and the <term>Work of the Chariot|The mysteries of the Divine realm</term>, and to descend into the depths of the <term>Halakha|Jewish law</term>. Happy is the people for whom it is thus! These works existed long ago, each one on its own from days of old; but now they shall be joined as one, prepared with additional explanations on the book *Pomegranate Nectar* from the mouth of the Elder, the universal sage, distinguished in Torah and piety, the great Kabbalist, our teacher and rabbi, Mordechai, son of the pious one, our teacher and rabbi, Jacob (of blessed memory), from Prague, of the Przybram family. These are clear matters, as all eyes shall see in their uprightness. This was brought to the printing house by his son, the pious and humble Torah scholar, our teacher and rabbi, Jacob. And a blessing upon the head of the providers: the Torah scholars, the first being our teacher and rabbi, Moshe Dias the Sephardi <note>Refers to Jews of Spanish or Portuguese descent, common in Amsterdam at this time.</note>, and the second being our teacher and rabbi, Shimon, son of our teacher and rabbi, Naftali Katz from Schoerzin <note>Likely referring to a town near Frankfurt</note>, the beadle and faithful servant of the holy community of Amsterdam. They supported him, one on this side and one on that side, to bring merit to the public. May it be the Divine will that the Divine Presence rests upon the work of our hands. May the Holy Temple be rebuilt in our days and may the Torah increase within our borders. And may God show us wonders from His Torah "as the sun rises in its strength." <note>A quote from Judges 5:31.</note>
Amen.

<meta>This page serves as the author's formal introduction to his work, *Sefer Petahiah*. It connects the text to the previous page's catchword "Knorr" (referring to Christian Knorr von Rosenroth, the famous Christian Hebraist, or perhaps a printing reference) and establishes the author's relationship with his patrons and his intellectual lineage, specifically his debt to the teachings of Moshe Cordovero.</meta>

# Author’s Introduction
## Opening

**The Author says:** I have written this book, *Petahiah*, in my own language <note>The author likely refers to a more accessible style of Hebrew or a translation of concepts into a more modern idiom for his time.</note> to make known the one who awakens with awe. It is a work of majesty and merit, for it was my lot to have grace bestowed upon my heart. Who am I, and what is my strength, that I should be counted among those who have a portion in this? I have not lived in vain, and certainly have not caused harm, for here is this agreement <note>Referring to a formal rabbinic approval or *haskamah*</note> that my dear friend, the distinguished leader Rabbi Yohanan, son of Mordechai Hayyat of Poland, urged upon me. He is a diligent student who seeks the good of his people, a hero in the study of Torah and in the words of the *Tosafot* <note>Medieval commentaries on the Talmud</note> beyond all his peers. Now he has taken it upon himself to bring this composition to light, because of his love for this wisdom. He did not come from the ends of the earth or the farthest reaches of the north just to hear a word, but rather the word of the Lord and the depths of my inquiries. At the opening of his desire, it was a simple matter—he felt something was missing, and so he urged me to return to this work and fashion a crown for the sages of the Germanic lands <note>original: "Ashkenaz"</note>. May the Lord strengthen them in their days; may peace be abundant for them. For according to the depth of their wisdom in the Mishna, the Gemara <note>The two main components of the Talmud</note>, and the intricacies of their sharp pilpul <note>A method of talmudic study involving intense logical analysis</note> and their sharpness in holy knowledge and reasoning, so too do their doubts and riddles increase. Thus they shall bear fruit and see their small efforts grow into branches, building this heavenly work with all their heart and soul.

**Furthermore,** it is better for me to address those who preceded me, who printed matters by permission of what I have written. They produced the finest flour <note>A metaphor for refined scholarship</note> and transformed it, even if they followed a system where they brought in students who listened to my voice in learning. Indeed, many in the days of my youth cried out for it—a great group of wonder-workers and scribes who are the recorders. In the place of their greatness, they marveled at his grasp of the traditions. Therefore, all the leaders and elders humbled themselves to hear these lovely lessons. They turned their faces to read the Five Books of Moses <note>The Torah</note> for one hour every day, and the book *Pardes Rimmonim* <note>The "Pomegranate Orchard," the foundational work of the Kabbalist Moshe Cordovero</note> in a holy way and with clear language, as if it were flowing freely for them. This was done so that the law would not be without a reason. It was a common saying in their mouths that the elder rabbis would not allow the elders or our brothers to neglect the ethics of the Prophet. It was not clear to my palate or to others, including all the heads of these provinces among the sages and masters of charms. At that time, they all learned, and every man opened himself up like a flock to the praise of the Lord; otherwise, the earth would be filled with the knowledge of God.

**I,** the lowliest of those appointed, set my heart to sit and expound upon the Torah of Moses. The voice of the author of the book—he is the well-known sage of the book *Kadmoni* <note>Perhaps referring to a "primordial" or ancient source</note>—who bequeathed the Torah and performed wonders of wisdom in his commentary on the *Zohar* and the *Tikkunim* <note>Foundational texts of Jewish mysticism</note>. His friends established themselves through him, and those who peered into his book of understanding gained wisdom. There are many pamphlets from what was not printed of the *Zohar*, including the Song of Songs, Lamentations, and a commentary on *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an early mystical text</note>, and a commentary on the prayers according to the tradition of every man. His soul is met by the book *Ohr Yakar* <note>"Precious Light," Moshe Cordovero's massive commentary on the Zohar</note>, which is mentioned many times in *Pardes Rimmonim* and in many other places. This is in addition to a great and glorious oxen <note>metaphor for a heavy/substantial work</note> of sermons following the literal meaning <note>term: Peshat (the plain or literal sense of scripture)</note>, the very flow of the life of the Torah. Now, see for the children of Israel, who produce arrangements to strengthen the small ones, to be given to children as sweet and soft snacks; one simply receives from them great voices like the voice of pure gold. His voice is that of the honored teacher and Rabbi, Moses <note>Referring to Moshe Cordovero, known as the Ramak</note>, the holy one, chosen to exalt and magnify his glory, like a commentary of holy blackness and depth. His hand was steady in the way of the "levies" and the "principle." It is written: *This is the book of Elijah*, and in it are twelve springs of water and tribes like mountains, according to the judgment of God, according to the traditions. I have already been observing: the *Pardes* is nothing less than a ruler over these times. To all these things are added and beautified pamphlets and books, large and small, books like a vision of perfume.

**Moreover,** he was a great sage in <term>Gematria</term> <note>The mystical practice of calculating the numerical value of Hebrew words to find deeper meanings</note>, a glory who spent all his days teaching students the living Torah. He was also a gatherer for the way, judging righteously between a man and his brother, between a stranger and his fellow. He was a distinguished authority, our teacher and Rabbi, Moses Cordovero, of blessed memory, the teacher of all the children of the exile, a pious man in his literal interpretations. Upon his grave, it is said that the Torah was given to him. Come and see what a great man has preceded us! After him, he sent a burden of glory, and they accompanied him before the bier, an intermediate man who could be included, whom man is commanded to follow, and from whom man draws understanding.

<margin>Merit</margin>
**My teacher,** Rabbi Azriel, of blessed memory, was a man of understanding whose old age was always dedicated to study. He brought me in, and for his sake, I was bound to this house of radiant wisdom. Through his blessing, I heard, and the soul of the mentioned sage shall rejoice here. The "orchard" <note>Referring again to the *Pardes*</note> is like a fool's rest, lying in peace. When I reached my portion, I stood to gaze with my soul, so that the book of the *Pardes* would not be hidden from me. Through the kindness of the supporters, I was fattened and I heard; and like Moses, my eyes were opened. I found rest in arranging my compositions—blessed is the one whose writing they have recorded in the Heavenly Academy. See, my work is the work of Heaven. Was it not a book? It was a scroll, and I have given it. I marvel at the mentioned bodies who support the elders and the youths alike. They became perfect through my words, and there is a day for this. Therefore, with these words, the Merciful One has not allowed me to forget all that is involved. And even so, by the name of God, I have again put my hand and doubled the wisdom and the taste of the core of the book and all these latter calls.

**At that time,** the sages desired to arrange the work in this manner. I saw the book *Pardes*—that in the first twenty-two "Gates," the matters of the World of Emanation <note>term: Atzilut (the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah)</note> were not fully explained. I made it into a section of its own, for my voice—and afterwards my heart's reason—knew it well. I wrote in it that he had done the same in his precious introductions, which were already printed by his son, a young but wise man. Many things that were not explained there in detail come out perfectly in this book. In the fourth book, the flow of the *Pardes* is according to the values of the "Knorr" <note>Probably referring to the *Kabbala Denudata* by Knorr von Rosenroth, or a specific arrangement of the text</note>. The work is vast and deep in that part—a great sea, undoubtedly. I too, in my poverty, have approached it with inquiries and conclusions of the discourse, as the good hand of the Lord was upon me, with many explanations of verses from the Torah, Prophets, and Writings, and the *Zohar* of our Sages of blessed memory. It sits and is clarified and exact, containing a "taste for praise" in this perfect understanding. The second part I have called *One Language*. It was spoken on the day I stood; perhaps the Lord will be gracious and I will merit to do great things with it. For my heart has sought the depths of what I have brought near according to the deep logic in it, which is also mentioned in the book of *Elijah*. I turned and looked, and in the end, everything related to this work is gathered together—limitless waters with the appropriate family, several steps for the Babylonians in the sources of the Gemara. This book shall be for a remembrance, and they shall continue to add to it. This aforementioned book, at the end of the book of separate inquiries, has not yet been refined by my judgment from potential to actual. I am at the Gate of Wisdom, weighing the deeds of the *Pardes*. May the Blessed One, in His mercy and abundant kindness, grant me the merit to magnify the Torah of truth and to glorify the Holy One, according to what flows from the hand of the Lord, the Opener. For the companion is great and mighty, and the Torah is like a circle upon the soul of the pure one. When she approaches, her brother-in-law will understand us for days, and there shall be rest.

**However,** this is the day I hoped for, to prove to a lowly generation that one should distance himself from this illness. The merit of this book is great, for it has been hidden under my hand for more than thirteen years, as is fitting for it to be complete.

<summary>In this introduction, the author outlines his motivation for adapting Rabbi Moshe Cordovero’s *Pardes Rimmonim* for a Germanic Jewish audience, emphasizing the need to make complex Kabbalistic concepts accessible to those trained in traditional Talmudic study. He cites the encouragement of Rabbi Yohanan of Poland and his own teacher, Rabbi Azriel, as the catalysts for completing this work after thirteen years of preparation.</summary>

<meta>The previous page established the author's intent to make the deep wisdom of Moses Cordovero accessible to the Ashkenazic communities. This page continues that mission by providing formal Rabbinic Approbations (*Haskamot*), which served both as religious endorsements and as a form of copyright protection for the publishers in 18th-century Amsterdam.</meta>

# Approbations of the Two Great Luminaries, the Famous Geniuses, "Sinai" and the "Uprooters of Mountains" <note>Traditional titles for scholars: "Sinai" refers to one with vast, structured knowledge, while "Uprooter of Mountains" refers to one with sharp, analytical brilliance.</note>
## Builders of Fences: The Sages and Rabbis of the Holy Sephardic Community of Amsterdam:

This was the practice in Israel in former times, to print two precious volumes as one: the book *Asis Rimmonim* <note>original: "Essence of Pomegranates"</note> and its companion, the holy and wondrous work of Kabbalah <term>Kabbalah: Jewish mystical tradition</term> known as *Pelach HaRimmon* <note>original: "Slice of the Pomegranate"</note>. These are the works of the holy master, Moses Cordovero <note>A 16th-century master of Kabbalah in Safed, whose systematic approach defined the field before the Lurianic period.</note>, may his memory be a blessing.

Now, the wise Rabbi Mordechai, son of the pious Jacob of blessed memory—a judge from the holy community of Prague—has arisen to bring these works together for a sacred purpose. He has added his own insights to open the gates of Torah for those wishing to enter the wisdom of Kabbalah, providing "fine pearls" of commentary. He has greatly expanded upon the book *Asis Rimmonim*.

At this time, the Lord has stirred the spirit of the distinguished Rabbi Jacob, son of the pious Rabbi Jacob the Judge, along with the learned Shimon, son of Naphtali Katz, and the nobleman Moses Diaz and his partners, including Joseph Diaz the Spaniard. They have joined hands to bring this work to the printing press with great beauty. These two books are now joined together, along with the extensive additions contributed by the pious Rabbi Mordechai of Prague. 

To ensure their success and protect their investment, it is forbidden for any other person to print these works or cause them harm by infringing on their rights. Therefore, I have issued this decree: no person in Israel shall print this book, in its current form or individually, for a period of **ten consecutive years** without the permission of the aforementioned partners. May the blessing of the Lord rest upon those who listen.

Written here in the holy community of the *Talmud Torah* <note>The name of the unified Sephardic community in Amsterdam.</note> of Amsterdam, on the 18th day of the month of Tammuz.

->May a good blessing come upon those who support this beauty and glory.<-
->The year 5466 [1706] according to the minor count.<-
->**Solomon de Oliveira**<- <note>A famous Sephardic scholar, poet, and grammarian in Amsterdam.</note>
->I am occupied with the study of Torah and the Divine service among the chosen people of the Sephardic community in this mother city in Israel, Amsterdam.<-
->The humble **Solomon, son of Jacob Ayllon**, of blessed memory.<- <note>The Chief Rabbi of the Sephardic community of Amsterdam at the time.</note>

## Approbations of the Exalted Rabbis, Wearers of the "Crown of a Good Name," the Judges of the Holy Ashkenazic Community of Amsterdam:

"Happy is he who comes here with his learning in hand." What his heart has learned and received through true Kabbalah is presented by the Rabbi, our teacher Jacob, son of the distinguished judge, Rabbi Mordechai, of blessed memory. How pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity to engrave with an iron pen the books *Asis Rimmonim* and *Pelach HaRimmon*, including the additions of his father. Joining him in this pure work is the learned Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Naphtali Katz. Both have intended to benefit the public and those who perform commandments. It is only right that they should not suffer financial loss. 

Therefore, the perfect sages of the Sephardic community have already issued bans and excommunications <term>Herem: A rabbinic decree of excommunication used here to enforce copyright.</term> against any person in Israel, whether themselves or through an agent, who might print this book without permission for ten years from this day. I, too, agree to cast these high bans upon anyone who violates these recorded agreements.

->Spoken by the humble one, Judah Leib<-
->son of Asher Anshel of Hamburg<-
->Serving the holy work of the Ashkenazic community<-
->in Amsterdam, currently serving during the interval<-
->between rabbis <note>original: "between king and king," meaning he was serving as the interim Chief Rabbi.</note> (formerly head of the court in Rotterdam).<-

We have heard the voice of the "waves of the sea"—the geniuses and leaders of the community. This garden is locked for ten years. "Do not eat from it, do not touch it" <note>A playful reference to the Garden of Eden, warning others not to "touch" the printing rights.</note> to print it elsewhere, lest you face the consequences. 

->Spoken by the small Pinchas Zelig, son of Moses, of blessed memory<-
->of Poznań, now a judge and scribe of this holy community.<-

<column-break/>

Behold their wondrous work! The great Kabbalist and judge of Prague, the pious Rabbi Mordechai son of Jacob, has drawn up water from the depths. He has strolled through the "Great Orchard" <note>A reference to *Pardes Rimmonim*, Cordovero's magnum opus; *Pardes* means orchard.</note> to gather lilies. He has added to the *Asis Rimmonim* and clarified difficult passages. The law of truth was in his mouth. Now his son, the pious and humble Jacob, has arisen with his supporters—Moses Diaz and the faithful communal servant Shimon Katz—to bring this to the press along with the holy book *Pelach HaRimmon* by our great master, Moses Cordovero. 

It is proper to protect them from boundary-jumping <term>Hasagat Gevul: The Torah prohibition against encroaching on another's livelihood.</term>. Therefore, I agree with the Sephardic geniuses in their decree of excommunication against any who infringe on their rights for ten years. May the one who listens be treated pleasantly and receive a good blessing.

->Spoken by **Joseph, son of Reuben Judah Katz**, of blessed memory<-
->(Great Judge of the community of Amsterdam)<-
->The 11th of the month of Tammuz, 5466 [1706].<-

These too have longed to bring to life the books *Asis Rimmonim* and *Pelach HaRimmon*. The Sephardic sages have issued their decree, and we join them. This delightful book shall not be coveted by others for ten years.

->The youngest of the fellowship of the Rabbis of the Academy of the glorious community of Amsterdam (formerly head of the court in Grewin).<-

<column-break/>

> I shall sing to my beloved a song of friendship regarding his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fruitful hill. It is a garden and an orchard of olives and pomegranates, a tree planted by streams of water which yields its fruit in its season. These are *Asis Rimmonim* and *Pelach HaRimmon*, which were once a "locked garden," their treasures hidden and concealed. No man knew their place until the pious Rabbi Mordechai, son of Jacob, judge of Prague, planted a tamarisk tree. He dug and found the wells which the "servants of the King" <note>Meaning previous scholars.</note> had stopped up. A river now flows from it to water the flocks. Previously, these teachings were scattered, one here and one there, but now they are unified. His son, the learned Rabbi Jacob, has joined with him, as have the noble Moses Diaz and the faithful Shimon Katz. These three are joined as one.

The rabbis grant a ten-year copyright protection to the publishers and editor, Mordechai of Prague, praising the work's spiritual and educational value.</summary>

# Author’s Preface
## Opening

<margin>The Editor says</margin> I, the transcriber of the book *The Engravings of the Seal* <note>original: Pituchei Chotam</note>, have come forth to publish this magnificent pamphlet and to grant the public merit through it. For this was my intention: "If I am not for myself, who will be for me? And if not now, when?" <note>A famous quote from Ethics of the Fathers 1:14</note>. Especially since I have added love and affection for it, following the agreement of the leader who encouraged me, my dear friend, the leader Rabbi Isaac, son of Mordecai Chait <note>Chait literally means "tailor" in Hebrew/Yiddish</note> of Poland. He is a veteran student who seeks the good of his people and stands as a fence within the kingdom of the Torah. Like the words of the *Tosefot* <note>A group of medieval commentators on the Talmud</note> regarding all those of his age, he has now taken upon himself a complete "exile" <note>A practice of wandering or traveling for spiritual penance or study</note> to merit his wife and children through the comforts of salvation. He shall acquire the land to the far north to hear the word of God. After he showed compassion and did His will, there was nothing hidden that I did not read, for his power of study is recognized. He chose to do this to bring satisfaction to the holy sages and the rabbis of our neighborhood. May God strengthen them as their fortress and grant them peace. According to the depth of their wisdom in the **Mishna** and the **Gemara** <note>The two primary components of the Talmud</note> and their sharp analytical debates <term>Pilpul: a method of Talmudic study involving intense logical analysis</term>, they increase their labor and actions. Thus, their piety shall spread to perform their work for the sake of Heaven with all your heart and soul.

**Furthermore**, it occurred to me that no one preceded me in printing this with the permission of what you wrote and added from the first edition. It is equal in taste, for they used to include important matters and various collections. Many among them were built upon a great foundation of sages and scribes of the first generations <note>original: Rishonim</note>. In the place of their greatness, we find their humility before the eyes of all who see them. They merited to hear words of study and returned them to their mouths to read into the ears of others—one report every day from the book *The Orchard of Pomegranates* <note>original: Pardes Rimonim, the seminal work of Rabbi Moses Cordovero</note> in a short path and clear language. They are like food seasoned with salt and spices, so that the law does not remain without "taste." This is a common saying among our rabbis: "Wheat in small bundles" <note>An idiom meaning complex ideas condensed into small, manageable portions</note>. I did not turn back or turn away from our peace or the peace of others. All the leaders of these provinces in matters of law and practice, according to our knowledge, let no one be missing. Praise be to God, "the earth is full of the knowledge of the Lord."

**I**, a dweller of these surroundings, took it to heart. I sat and expounded upon the Torah of Moses—referring to the author of this book, the famous sage, the master of the "Vineyard" and the "Straightening" <note>Refers to Cordovero's works *Elim* and *Tomar Devorah*</note> who magnified the Torah. He performed wonders in his commentary on the *Zohar* <note>The primary text of Jewish mysticism</note>, the *Precious Light* <note>original: Or Yakar</note>. His companions, his strength, and the praises of Spain—our rabbis there were nurtured by him. Many of his pamphlets were printed with warning and brilliance, such as the *Song of Songs* and *Lamentations*, as well as his commentary on the *Book of Formation* <note>original: Sefer Yetzirah</note> and the commentary on the prayers of the entire year. All these were composed by the holy investigator at the time he wrote the precious book *Or Yakar*, which the mouth of the master will take many times into the *Orchard of Pomegranates* <note>Pardes Rimonim</note> and many corrections. This alone is a great and scattered treasure of sermons according to the literal meaning <term>Pshat: the plain or literal meaning of scripture</term>. The words of the Torah are the very life of the Children of Israel—sweet like honey, small droplets for infants and nurslings to suckle. It was received according to great voices, the voice of the mighty Lord. His glory grew in the holy commentary of the Torah, with depth and wide reach in the path of brevity. It is written: "This is the book of the generations of Israel," twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees in peace. I realized that the *Pardes* is nothing less than a sharp tool for those who study these compositions. Above all these are additions and sanctifications in many books, large and small, books without end.

**Moreover**, he was a great power in the **Gemara**, the master Yom Tov <note>Possibly referring to Yom Tov Lipmann Heller or a similar contemporary scholar</note>. All his days he arranged the students, and he was also fixed in the Torah to judge righteousness between a man and his brother. He was a distinct teacher of the Levites, a holy and pious man. In the eulogies at his grave, what did they say of our wisdom? "The end of the Torah." Come and see what a great man he was, upon whom the pillars of the world trembled. He found wisdom and brought forth understanding.

**The merit** of my teacher, Rabbi Ovadia <note>possibly 'Orel'</note> son of Isaac Chait of Mantua, and his righteousness shall stand forever. He brought me in and helped me. This sealed work was given in his "pomegranate" <note>A metaphor for the Pardes Rimonim</note>, and I acted. May the soul of the wise author rejoice with the pious in glory and rest on its bed in peace. For when I reached the age of wisdom, I was sent the book *The Pardes* by one of his students. I rejoiced and delved into it, and from there my eyes were opened. I found rest in the order of the compositions after I was in the Yeshiva <note>Academy for Torah study</note> of Velu. This is my work—heavenly work, not of the flesh. I revealed its hidden parts and gave it immediately to the designated friends to spread before them. Daily I spoke of it. Therefore, these things were first gathered without being broken or shattered. I added my hand a second time and doubled it into ten sections, and these are the words.

**At the time** the agreement was made to arrange the work in this manner, I saw the book *The Pardes*. In its first twenty-two branches, the words were famous throughout the world of thinkers. It was easy for the eyes to see on its own. My heart was amazed because I aimed for the knowledge of the elder author as well. Afterward, he made his introductions, which I had already printed. This is a precious part for the young and the old. Many of his words in his commentary there are sufficient. This book comes to be established in the order of the *Kavvanot* <term>Kavvanot: mystical intentions or meditations during prayer</term>, which is a great and wide sea without doubt. I too, among the first, joined in the inquiries with the author's difficulties, by the good hand of God upon me. There are also many fruits—verses from the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings, and the teachings of our Sages from the Mishna, Gemara, and Midrash, which have a "taste of praise" <note>original: Ta'am l'shvach - a legal term for a significant improvement or addition</note> in this perfect wisdom. I called this section *The Language of the Living*. I hope to merit making a wise edition as is in my heart. The author was deep in his roots in the book *Ghalika* in two tracts. In my standing, all the merits of this work shall complete my composition. At the end, I added appropriate additions. My heart rejoices in the labor of this book. Its light shall be seen, and they will add to the splendor of the gate. At the end of the book are the "Burning Sermons" which I have not yet brought from potential to reality. This is in the *Gate of the Script*, which is one of the gates of the *Pardes*. May the Blessed One, in His mercy and great kindness, choose me to magnify the true Torah and glorify His holy name through me.

**However**, this is the day I have hoped for, to bring it to the light of the world. The account is sent, and in the book *Shelach HaRimon* <note>The Branch of the Pomegranate</note>, happy is he who has it now under my hand, covered in blessing more than them all, the crown of the soul, as is fitting to be.

# Approvals of the two great and famous lights, "Sinai" and "uprooters of mountains"
<note>These are traditional titles for great scholars: "Sinai" refers to one with vast, encyclopedic knowledge of tradition, while "uprooter of mountains" refers to one with sharp, analytical brilliance.</note>
## Builders of the fence: The sages and rabbis of the Holy Spanish Community in Amsterdam:

<columns>2</columns>

This was the custom of old in Israel, and even before then, many precious books were carved like sapphires, as written in the book *The Assembly* <note>original: Kohelet / Ecclesiastes</note>. Specifically, the book *The Slice of the Pomegranate* <note>original: Pelach ha-Rimmon</note> and the book *The Juice of Pomegranates* <note>original: Asis Rimmonim</note>. Now, Rabbi Mordecai, son of the pious Rabbi Jacob (of blessed memory), judge and teacher of the Holy Community of Prague, and his associates, have sought to gather together many words with great strength regarding the book *Juice of Pomegranates*, so that all may labor and join in this most wonderful work. And so, at this time, God has stirred the spirit of the worthy Rabbi Jacob, son of the pious Rabbi Wolcher, judge and teacher of the Holy Community of Prague, along with his partners, the honored Joseph Diaz and the good and learned Rabbi Simon, son of Rabbi Naphtali Katz, to receive together the two aforementioned books. This is to be done with the addition of the book *The Slice of the Pomegranate*, to place them upon the printing presses and to give them a resting place. They have been granted permission to print a new edition and to hold the exclusive rights that belong to all who print. It is forbidden for anyone else to interfere for a period of ten years. He who "breaks the fence" <note>An idiom for violating a rabbinic decree</note> shall be bitten by a snake <note>A traditional warning of spiritual punishment</note>, and he who obeys shall be blessed. Written in the Holy Community of the "Study of the Torah" <note>The name of the Sephardic congregation in Amsterdam is Talmud Torah</note> in Amsterdam, on the 11th day of the month of Tammuz, in the year 5466 <note>July 1706</note>.
**Solomon de Oliveira** <note>A famous rabbi, grammarian, and poet in Amsterdam</note>.
Signed by the one standing over the Torah and the service among the faithful of the people, the humble Solomon, son of Jacob de Oliveira, of blessed memory.

<column-break/>

Two are bound together as one: the book *Juice of Pomegranates* and the holy book of the source, which is *The Slice of the Pomegranate* by the holy Rabbi Mordecai, of blessed memory. They lack nothing for a person to find rest, to open the gates of enlightenment, and to enter the wisdom of the **Kabbalah** <note>Jewish mysticism</note>. Originally, these were printed separately, but now God has stirred the spirit of the learned Rabbi Jacob, son of the pious Rabbi Wolcher, with his group, the learned Rabbi Simon son of Naphtali Katz and the honored Joseph Diaz, to join these works together so they may be one in their possession. They shall be available to all, and everyone's hand shall be equal in them, with the great addition added to the book *Juice of Pomegranates* by Rabbi Mordecai, son of the pious Rabbi Jacob, judge of Prague. They have brought this to the printing house to merit the public, a fitting and exalted task. No man shall enter their boundary to print these books again, neither together nor separately, for a period of ten years without permission from the aforementioned partners. He who listens shall dwell in safety, and blessings shall come upon them. Written here in the Holy Community of the Spanish, may God preserve them, in this city of Amsterdam.

<columns>1</columns>

# Approvals of the distinguished Rabbis who use the "Crown of a Good Name," the judges of the city of the Holy Ashkenazi Community in Amsterdam:

<columns>3</columns>

Happy is he who comes here with his learning in his hand! What his heart has learned and received through true tradition is brought by the Rabbi, Jacob, son of the distinguished judge, Rabbi Mordecai, of blessed memory. He has joined a good union—how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together!—to engrave with an iron pen the book *Juice of Pomegranates* and the book *The Slice of the Pomegranate* with the addition added by his father. Joined with him is the pure-hearted and learned Rabbi Simon, son of Rabbi Naphtali Katz. Both of them intended this for one purpose: to merit the public. As messengers of a **Mitzvah** <note>A religious commandment or good deed</note>, they deserve not to be harmed. Therefore, the perfect sages of the Holy Spanish Community have decreed bans and excommunications <note>original: cherem</note> so that no person in Israel, neither he nor his messenger, shall print the aforementioned book without the permission of those named above, from today for ten consecutive years. Who has seen these decrees and would not agree with them? Therefore, I also agree to cast heavy bans upon anyone who violates these recorded approvals.
**The words of Judah Leib, son of Abraham Asher Anshel of Hamburg**, serving the Holy Ashkenazi Community in Amsterdam at this time, "between kings" <note>original: bein malka l'malka—likely meaning he is serving during a transitional period between chief rabbis</note>. (Formerly Chief Justice of the Holy Community of Radoshkovichy).

<column-break/>

Behold the awesome deeds of the One who reveals wonders! This was brought forth by the great Kabbalist and Judge of Prague, the pious Rabbi Mordecai, son of the pious Rabbi Jacob. He strolled in the "Great Orchard" <term>Pardes: A term for the four levels of Torah interpretation, often specifically referring to Kabbalah</term> after filling his belly <note>An idiom meaning he first mastered the primary legal texts of the Talmud before studying mysticism</note> to gather roses. He added to the *Juice of Pomegranates* and through his wisdom, light filled the world. His mouth spoke the Torah of truth, and no injustice was found on his lips. Now his son, the pious and humble Rabbi Mordecai, has risen with those who assist in this good deed: Moses Diaz and the learned Rabbi Simon, son of Rabbi Naphtali Katz (of blessed memory), the faithful beadle of our community. They have brought it to print along with the work *The Slice of the Pomegranate*. We agree with the Sephardic geniuses in their decree; a ban of "death" <note>Metaphorical for spiritual excommunication</note> is placed on anyone who encroaches on their boundary and prints these within ten years.
**Joseph, son of Reuben Judah Katz** (Great Judge of the Holy Community of Amsterdam).
11th of Tammuz, 5466.

<column-break/>

I shall sing for my beloved a song of friendship! My friend had a vineyard on a fruitful hill. His mouth tasted this orchard and garden, a "pomegranate fountain" planted by streams of water which gives its fruit in its season. *Juice of Pomegranates* and *The Slice of the Pomegranate* were once a locked garden, sealed and hidden treasures. No man knew their place or their entry. But then a "Plant of Delight" was planted: Rabbi Mordecai, son of the pious Rabbi Jacob, judge of Prague. He dug and found the wells that the "servants of the King" <note>Earlier scholars</note> had stopped up, and from them the flocks are watered. Previously, they were separate flocks, scattered in the corners of the vineyard, not approaching one another. Now his son, the learned Rabbi Jacob, has risen to join them, together with the wealthy Rabbi Moses Diaz and the learned Rabbi Simon, son of Rabbi Naphtali the Priest, the faithful beadle of Amsterdam. They have joined the vineyard, "grapes with grapes," a good thing. They have made the Tabernacle one, with three books opened for life. They teach the people knowledge. Hearing the voice of the Sephardic sages and their decrees, we also declare: this gate is closed! No other person in the world shall print this lovely book for ten years. Of this well in the garden, it is said: "You shall not eat of it nor touch it" <note>A play on the prohibition in Eden</note> to print it, lest you die.
**The words of Pinchas Selig, son of Moses** (formerly of the Holy Community of Poznan, and now Judge and Scribe of Amsterdam).

### Preface and Apology of the Proofreader, R.S.K.

Let the "pious" ascend and let the "teachers" rejoice—the "guide" <note>original: *moreh*—a likely reference to Maimonides' *Guide for the Perplexed* or teachers of wisdom in general</note> for all who long for their goodness. Those who make mention of an ancient righteous one in his inheritance and nourishment shall be understood, and "intercessors" <note>original: *melitzim*—referring to those who interpret or speak on behalf of others</note> through the words of the wise and their riddles shall speak of righteousness. For though the "dreams of Ludia" <note>original: *halomot Ludia*—a Talmudic idiom for seeing things that are impossible or nonsensical</note> are lofty, and there are many laws, they only speak of foolish gold. Their entire purpose is to increase the wealth of the "cluster" <note>original: *eshkol*—a reference to a scholar of vast knowledge</note>, yet even at night, they diminish. It is better for everyone not to taste of it, for no one knows what a day may bring. I shall set aside the source entirely; we were then content, so what should bring you to a sign? Who can prevail over his sins? For the "Silent One" <note>original: *ALM*—a mystical name/concept</note> is hidden, and the highest level is beyond every name of man; the Scripture wonders at him. How beautiful is the "Silent One," which is numerical value 110 <note>original: *ALM* (Aleph-Lamed-Mem) equals 111, but the text notes a specific calculation of 110</note>, and he has nothing to hold them with, for by his gift he lives. The righteous are great even in their death; these are the members of the world, but they have this "cleansing son" <note>original: *ben menaki*</note>. Only a man can hold them at his doorways, but he has no power for merits except to fill his void. The Torah is "lying in a corner" <note>A reference to the Talmudic saying that the Torah is neglected and lacks seekers</note>; there is none to search for it or seek it out to bring it to life. The children of the Most High are few who take it upon themselves to be "associates" <note>original: *chaverim*—members of a holy brotherhood of study</note> and listeners. "And the Lord hearkened and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him for those who fear the Lord and think upon His name." We rely on numerical values <note>original: *gematria*</note> and occupy ourselves with the lower aspects of the world, while that which ascends to the light is not seen by anyone behind them. They do not belong to the day in the holy arrangement, and their entire aim is to "join the tent" <note>A Tabernacle metaphor</note> with those initials... they are few...

And there is also a group that loves the laws, the words of the living God, their truth, their permanence, and their height; the outer shell <note>original: *kelipah*—a Kabbalistic term for the "husk" or external layer that conceals the holy spark</note> departed from within. Because of what is decreed upon these, he spoke willfully against my "membranes" <note>original: *kerumotai*</note>... regarding wisdom in the heart, its life is beautiful in the sun, for its princes are looted in the city that was broken for her. And regarding the students, they "opened their mouths wide" and leaned upon glass... Woe to the children who have been exiled from their father’s table <note>A common metaphor for Israel in exile</note>, the table of the holy Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>original: *Ha-Rashbi*—the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, whose books have become withered. These people spend their days until their souls are exhausted, and different printed versions have been published that violate the simple meaning in confusion. We have gathered life; the glass is not like a mouse, and the waves of life... I shall finally enter his street... and he shall cast us into the furnace. My words were appointed, which were not read or bought correctly from all the words of my books. Whoever tastes of cheapness, let his eyes be upon me, and let the black letter... on the beauty of the entrances. You simple ones shall become wise, for the smooth heart does not understand the taste of the warm ones, the wise ones—masters of the Scripture, masters of the Talmud, and masters of the Kabbalah. Now they shall slip away, rest, and be fruitful; they shall become strong and clothe themselves in shame. For the stammering tongue is the correct one to surround it with the closed understanding of iniquities, gatherings, and vengeances. And he whose honor is diminished among my people, let him clear the paths and crooked ways, and their darkness is a path... the highway has worn away.

My response is a joyous and complete rebuke, pure and without "peel." There are no disputes, no breach, and no cry in the streets. And let all that is written be far away, and let it live and turn the straying hearts that wander on the path of all the earth. The Lord counts the hearts of the thousands of Israel who tremble over the business of Your house. "And every man shall come to his place in peace," until he directs and straightens the speech of stumbling. And you, open the eyes of your intellect, etc. And this is what is written in the holy Book of Zohar, in the portion of *Beha'alotkha*, of blessed memory:

"Come and see how precious are the words of Torah! For in every single word there are upper levels, and the Torah is called a 'supernal whole.' We have learned: everything that was included in the general rule and then singled out... these are the people of Israel. The Torah is the 'Supernal Torah,' the 'Torah of Truth.' And sometimes it is said that the truth is the covering of the Torah. One who looks only at the light's covering is like that fool who says that the story is the main thing... but the Torah is holy and supernal. Would a king of flesh and blood not have better things to do than to write down the mundane words of Esau and Hagar, or Laban and Jacob, or the words of the donkey, or Balaam? If it were just stories, we could write better stories today! Rather, all the words of the Torah are its 'body.' Come and see: the upper world and the lower world are weighed in the same balance. Israel below corresponds to the angels above. As it is written: 'He makes His angels spirits.' When they descend below, they must clothe themselves in the garments of this world, or else the world could not endure them. So too with the Torah: it created the worlds and sustains them. When it descended to this world, if it had not clothed itself in these garments—which are the stories of the world—the world could not have endured it. Therefore, the story of the Torah is only its garment. One who thinks that the garment is the Torah itself and nothing more, his spirit shall perish; he has no portion in the World to Come. For this reason, King David said: 'Open my eyes, that I may behold wonders out of Your Torah'—meaning, what is *under* the garment of the Torah. There is a garment that everyone sees, and those fools, when they see a person in a beautiful garment, they look no further. But the importance of the body is the soul. The Torah has a body, and these are the 'Bodies of the Torah' <note>original: *Gufey Torah*—referring to the essential laws</note>. This body is clothed in garments, which are the stories of this world. The fools of the world look only at the garment, which is the story of the Torah; they know nothing more and do not look at what is beneath the garment. Those who know more do not look at the garment, but at the body beneath it. But the wise, the servants of the Supernal King—those who stood at Mount Sinai—look only at the Soul, which is the root of everything, the actual Torah. And in the time to come, they are destined to look at the 'Soul of the Soul' of the Torah. Come and see: so it is above; there is a garment, a body, a soul, and a soul of the soul..."

# Preface

Review every word of the Torah—their details and their nuances—with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, and above all, with the fear of Heaven, before they are printed. Let them be sent to the press <note>original: *la’amod*—literally "to stand," referring to setting the type for the printing press</note> to endure through every investigation. For I know that the people of Israel are holy, and they all desire and yearn for this hidden "child" <note>referring to the revealed wisdom of the book</note> to be born. By transcribing these matters as they truly are, the light goes forth and spreads throughout the world.

Let them read of the "Will of the Lord," for the name of the book I have cherished is *The Desire of the Lord's Will*. It shall be sent as a *Kindness to Abraham* <note>original: *Hesed le-Avraham*—this is the title of the primary work by Rabbi Abraham Azulai (c. 1570–1643) being discussed or edited here</note>. Regarding the contradictions within these works, they are now handed over to the public. It has become clear to me that the time has come to establish this in "distant life" <note>likely referring to the enduring life of a printed book versus a manuscript</note>. Though the writer’s voice may falter and his heart be divided by distractions, and though the writer’s fatigue and errors of the pen <note>original: *ta'ut ha-kalmos*—a standard disclaimer for scribal errors</note> are inevitable, who will have pity? Except for the poor and the sick, let the printing press rest. I have come to make its contents known to the public; it is better to have a strong foundation in a place where nothing existed before, prepared in all things and guarded. For every error and every desire to understand is for the good—to benefit all who long for wisdom and to dedicate it to the entire congregation of Israel.

What is more, I have now added strength upon strength to its explanation and a great connection to its sanctity. It is not traded away like something lacking; rather, it is that which a blessing rests upon, rising to the "table of kings" <note>meaning it is fit for the highest scholars</note>. The Sages called it the "investigations of the Orchard" <term>Pardes: The 'Orchard' of mystical knowledge; also refers specifically to the system of Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</term>. This book follows the paths of all things without end. I have set my eyes upon it to search and correct it, so that its lack might become pleasant to the soul of every reader, and its "drink" might be sweet to him. Upon every single "daughter" <note>referring to branches of wisdom or groups of students</note> of the classes of the wise, it shall cast a protective shadow. I have not come to scatter or to remove, but like a person harvesting, to bring heart to the explanation. This search for life and the explanation of the corrections is all done for the sake of Heaven, and it is praiseworthy.

I call heaven and earth to witness for me that I also investigated my own goodness—to taste a little "honey from the tip of the staff" <note>A biblical reference to Jonathan in 1 Samuel 14, meaning to gain a small but vital bit of enlightenment</note>. God forbid that I should act out of arrogance. This explanation comes from the writings of the great scholars and the many noble speakers among the leaders and the prominent figures. Regarding the holy portion in the purification of *Kindness to Abraham*: my heart did not grow haughty, nor did my eyes raised too high to approach the holiness of the author (of blessed memory) and his words. 

This work did not come to be through the deeds of the land that are prideful. It was fulfilled because everything that is hidden and covered shall be revealed. Words were stirred within me that were not previously known to every "gate of the eyes of the intellect." Whoever delays these words in the great assembly, in the synagogues and study halls, in order to be a great and expert Rabbi—may they be pardoned. Through his books, I found praise to God. My heart gave him fear and honor in both worlds, like all the students who searched before me and were privileged to see and feel the holiness. He spent all his years in the Torah, and one year of favor to remember nights as days, always taking his portion. Through his wisdom, the "drink" shall be strengthened as a "staff of life," and his Torah shall live according to the simple meaning of the words of the *Zohar* <term>Zohar: The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</term> and those who accompany them.

His mouth called out toward the holy. Whoever is proficient in the words of the ancients in their simple sense but fails to see the depth is destined to give an account in judgment. For he has opened the gates of the Temple to the simple meaning, which should not be left to the dust. Let no one hide this matter, for he <note>the author</note> opened his holy heart to the gates and the insights of the Wisdom of Truth <note>original: *Hokhmat ha-Emet*—a common synonym for Kabbalah</note>. Within them, every person who fears the Lord can approach his words and enter the "inner palace" <term>Traklin: The inner hall or palace, representing the deeper mysteries of God</term> to hear the teachings face to face, and not merely as a shadow of words. 

Perhaps if my teacher, the Rabbi, **Rabbi Israel Ba'al Shem [Tov]** <note>original: *Ha-Besht*—the founder of the Hasidic movement</note> had not opened these hundred gates—he who has a portion in the distance and in the midrashic studies—we would not have merited the Torah. This is a beautiful sign in his learning. Those who recognize and shield his words have fulfilled the verse: "For the gain from it is better than gain from silver" [Proverbs 3:14]. My heart was awakened when I heard his words, which are like a tasty and honorable medicine, softened by his hands.

Indeed, just as the words of the *Pardes* were chosen from among the ancients, so too were the words of the **Ari** <term>Ari: Rabbi Isaac Luria (1534–1572), the most influential Kabbalist of the modern era</term> chosen. This speaker of truth—his words shall be established. In this book, which is beautiful to the holy author, as well as in the teachings of the Ari, each has profound "lips" and a wonderous radiance. All your values shall be weighed against the "Holy Sanctuary." This work is like a deep well, drawing grace in the chapters of the "Living Holy Creatures" <note>original: *Hayot ha-Kodesh*—an order of angels associated with Ezekiel's vision of the Chariot</note> within the Chariot of the intellect in prophecy. 

Just as it is common to bring together the simple meanings of the ancients with the *Pardes*, it is not good to turn back from this. Let the wise man give us his hand. It is fitting to bring together the wisdom of the Ari with this book. Upon these words, a covenant is made. Let the reader take this pamphlet and be mindful of the Holy One, blessed be He, who grants wisdom. I have sought this all my days. All the theoretical details that were destroyed so that one could contemplate His world shall now be examined. One may enter through the common paths of the *Pardes* and its surroundings. There is no doubt that this is a straight, perfect, and clear path. It shall include the "Wisdom of the Living." The spirit of the Kabbalists who were before us, whose words reached us through the **Ari**, was used to investigate the "Lower Worlds." He told of their arrival, that they are engaged in the "Balance" <note>original: *Matkla*—referring to the *Sifra Di-Tzeniuta* (Book of Concealment) in the Zohar, which uses the metaphor of a balance/scale</note> and the protections of the Upper Realm.

I have placed my covenant in this heavenly work to inform and to be known. I have set a boundary for every change of report. Even so, it is good for me to hesitate in certain places. This is only because a change is permitted, not to be overbearing over all reasoning, but to nurture my own mind and the mind of every pure-hearted person. May the Merciful One grant us merit. This work is prepared in all things and guarded for the order of study for this ancient book. 

Moreover, the "Gates" of the book shall now be twenty-two, corresponding to the number of the letters of the Hebrew alphabet from which the Torah is built. Its chapters shall begin according to the orders of the Tabernacle <note>original: *Mishkan*</note>. Correspondingly, every day the blessings of the "Tribe of Man" <note>likely referring to the general human condition or a specific liturgical grouping</note> shall be distributed to their Creator. Let the heart of the holy one know the matter of the work of the "Vision." Let there be no blemish. From all of creation, let praise and glory rise to the King, the Merciful God, the One and Only, the Dear, who is exalted above all blessing and praise.

<summary>This preface explains the editor's efforts to harmonize the Kabbalistic systems of Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (the Pardes) and the Ari, while emphasizing the revolutionary "opening of the gates" provided by the Ba'al Shem Tov. The book is structured into 22 gates to match the Hebrew alphabet and follows the symbolic layout of the biblical Tabernacle.</summary>

# Preface and Apology of the Editor

Regarding the secret mentioned by our Sages, of blessed memory, that "his lips move in the grave" <note>A Talmudic concept (Yebamot 97a) suggesting that when a scholar's teachings are repeated after their death, it is as if they are still speaking</note>, it is most precious that scholars are able to learn from him. As was written in the chapter of *Horkenos* <note>Likely referring to *Pirkei D’Rabbi Eliezer*</note>, therefore, heaven forbid that one should think this matter pertains only to the literal meaning. There is no doubt that the matter rises to the level of Kabbalah <term>the Jewish mystical tradition</term> in the mystery of the "levels of value." Furthermore, it possesses a third virtue:

For one who occupies themselves with this wisdom will know how to cherish their Creator and serve Him with a whole heart. As Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman, or Nachmanides (1194–1270), a foundational Spanish scholar and mystic</note>, of blessed memory, explained on the Torah portion of *Beshalach*: "The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth." This means knowing the preciousness of one's Creator and serving Him with a whole heart. As Ramban explained: "It is fitting for the Holy One to be at the King's table." From then on, Israel knew a supreme level... as it is written: "And it shall be right in your eyes" and "Before you, right and proper." He gave His statutes and laws to Israel. Similarly, in the future, one will know how to speak the holy secret... the building of the Chosen House <term>the Holy Temple</term> depends on it. It appears that the service of the Lord is upon us, to know how to articulate the essence of His service. From this, the disqualification of the prayers of those who do not know how to cherish their Master becomes clear. This matter cannot be achieved except through the study of the wisdom of Kabbalah.

Furthermore, there is a fourth virtue: for in every portion and part, each person according to their merit and soul... the inner part is clothed in the secret of a "garment," a body, a soul, and a spirit... like the secret of the intention of "the fat" <note>original: *nikkur*—the laws of removing forbidden fats and veins from meat</note> according to the literal meaning and the world of Creation. Above this, the power is not clothed except through the secret of Kabbalah and one's intention within it. Without a doubt, for one who occupies themselves with this wisdom, it is said that "all is for the Name" <note>done for the sake of God</note>...

The fifth revealed virtue: one who occupies themselves with this wisdom will know how to choose many holy matters of the Torah that are hidden from the masters of the literal meaning (*Peshat*), such as the matter of "added letters," words written but not read, and words read but not written <note>Scribal traditions known as *Keri* and *Ketiv*</note>. One might think these are <unclear>errors</unclear>, heaven forbid, but they are purposeful. As Ramban explained, and as stated in the *Zohar* <term>the primary work of Jewish mysticism</term> on the portion of *Beshalach*: "There is not a word in the Torah that does not contain supreme secrets and holy reasons... and how many <unclear>laws</unclear> there are for those who know them." However, it may happen that a small <unclear>flaw</unclear> appears to the grammarians <note>those who study the Hebrew language's literal structure</note>... and in our opinion, there is a "superfluous" thing in the Torah portion of *Yitro*... but through the virtue of the literal meaning, there are words in the Torah that are corrected and precise according to the way of the *Peshat*...

It appears that the scribe was writing the correct *Haftarah* <note>The selection from the Prophets read after the Torah portion</note>... for according to the literal meaning, "the Torah speaks in the language of man" <note>A famous principle meaning the Torah uses human metaphors to describe the Divine</note>. But for those who know the wisdom... I say that these are from the words of the Torah that are hidden and stored away...

The sixth revealed virtue: one who occupies themselves with this wisdom, and whose mouth reveals it, will undoubtedly experience a revelation of the "Fear of Heaven" and "Fear of Sin." It will increase their fervor in divine service. This is a proven fact: even just reciting the language of the *Zohar* brings its flavor into the soul and the heart with the fear of the Lord. It is as if one is dwelling with the righteous in the Garden of Eden.

The seventh revealed virtue: I have moved my feet and my tongue regarding the printing... we were explaining the literal meaning along with the <unclear>teachings</unclear> of our teacher, the Maharal of Prague, and the Levite... to occupy ourselves with the verses of the Torah without deep analysis. But these matters were <unclear>difficult</unclear>... and I copied them into a separate notebook...

The ninth virtue: that which I have also seen... for one who prepares himself in his prayer according to the truth of the literal meaning and seeks help... for the literal meaning (*Peshat*) is in the place where the "husks" <term>klipot; forces of impurity</term> can reach. Therefore, external forces try to prosecute. However, according to the way of Kabbalah, they have no dominion there at all.

The tenth virtue: what I have tested and covered... those who have not ascended to the heights of holiness will not be completed in the wisdom of the Torah. Even if they speak and discuss the *Sefirot* <term>the ten divine emanations</term>, they will not truly understand or resemble those who walk in wisdom... even in simple matters. This is the reason they were undoubtedly necessary... and more of these virtues will be called upon as the reader sees fit, with God's help.

Ramban wrote: Our Sages said that fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all were given to Moses except for one, as it says: "You have made him a little lower than the angels." This number is hinted at in the Torah in the Counting of the Omer and on the Day of Atonement. Everything that was given to Moses our Teacher regarding the gates of understanding was written in the Torah, either explicitly or by a hint in the words, or through *Gematria* <term>numerical value of letters</term>, or in the shape of the letters... in the breaks, the flourishes, and the crowns of the letters... just as a skilled physician uses medicines at a specific time for the body that needs them... so too the orders of the Torah are for the repair of the body and the soul. Happy is he who merits to enter those gates... for just as the philosophers seek the end of the wisdom of nature, so the end of the Torah is the wisdom of Kabbalah. It is the knowledge of the combining of letters... and this was the goal... and therefore it says: "And you shall guard and do them, for this is your wisdom." He also wrote before this: "And if so, all the sciences... were handed down from mouth to mouth and hinted at in the Torah." From this, the philosopher was forced to consult the Geonim <term>rabbinic leaders</term> of the holy community of Venice... and the wisdom of Kabbalah is true without doubt or hesitation, while the philosopher is confused.

<margin>Ramban also wrote: We have a tradition that the entire Torah consists of the Names of the Holy One, blessed be He, for the words can be divided into names... such as the first word *Bereshit* [In the beginning] being re-read as *Bara-shit* [He created six].</margin>

<summary>The editor outlines ten spiritual "virtues" of Kabbalah, arguing that mystical study protects the soul from impure forces, explains scribal anomalies, and represents the ultimate purpose of the Torah. He cites Ramban's view that the entire Torah is a sequence of Divine Names and that its letters contain medical and spiritual healing properties.</summary>

# Preface and Apology of the Editor

In the aspect of the "Glory of Israel" <note>Tiferet Yisrael; a common title for books and a reference to one of the Divine Emanations</note> for generation after generation, the upright shall dwell in their habitations. This is the Holy Ancient Power <note>original: "chaila atika kadisha," a Zoharic term for the highest level of divinity</note>, and all is one, and one is all. Woe to the lives of the fools who have no pity on the honor of their Master, whose radiance of their mouths is mere empty storytelling. They pray only in this state of exile and no more, ignoring the Rectification of the Beard <note>original: "Tikun de-Dikna," a complex Kabbalistic metaphor for the flow of divine mercy</note> while gazing at vanities. By taking up these precious teachings, one gains a greater portion in that Rectification, leading to spiritual freedom. This is why the distant children do not wish to look upon the portion that gladdens the soul. Consequently, all their sins and deeds and stories remain in a state of shameful repair. So it is written in the Midrash of our Sages, of blessed memory, and by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in the Holy Zohar: "Know the conclusion and bring joy to your heart through Him, for He is God." It is a strength for all of you who labor in the Torah to know the wisdom of the matter, for all who know and gaze upon the upper mysteries are rewarded.

For when a person leaves this world to be hidden away, all the judgments of the world pass away. Not only that, but twelve gates of the mysteries of wisdom are opened for him, and the secrets of the Higher Wisdom are revealed to him. Furthermore, the Holy One, blessed be He, designates for him that purple garment <note>original: "porpura," a royal robe</note> in which all the forms are engraved. The Holy One, blessed be He, joins with him in the Garden of Eden. The soul that remains for a person is meant to gaze upon the mystery of your Master—what is for the soul's benefit and what serves for its delight. These teachings will be built within you and given to you, and the rectifications of the body will be transformed and mended, readying the soul to enter into judgment before the King of All. To know and to gaze upon the mysteries and their meanings—these are what fill the soul with wisdom. 

The Sun of the Soul is the foundation of all existence, even in the grave, and even more so to gaze upon life and know the world in which one exists. For what purpose should one be mended? To delight in the later, higher days of the upper worlds. A person should look to these "Living Waters" in the Torah. Anyone who does not have a portion in laboring in that world without knowledge—that is, if he has no deeds of "restfulness"—is cast out from all the gates of that world. 

Thus wrote the Remaz <term>Rabbi Moshe Zacuto (1625–1697), a famous kabbalist</term>, of blessed memory, in his book *The Collection* (*Sefer HaLeket*): "Behold, the ultimate purpose of knowledge in this existence is to know the Cause and the Reason and the other matters mentioned in the essay." And the author <term>Rabbi Meir Poppers</term>, of blessed memory, wrote: "The reason for engaging in Torah day and night is to know its vitality—the existence of Being in spirituality and their secret through hints." Therefore, I intended to create this book to choose the paths that lead a man to wisdom. I have chosen a junction of paths, with the help of Heaven, titled **A Path for the Righteous** (*Orach L'Tzadik*). 

"The beginning of wisdom" <note>A reference to Psalm 111:10</note> is the entrance to the inner treasury. For the inner treasury is the one associated with vitality, as explained by the holy Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz, of blessed memory, in his essay: "All hope of thought precedes its antiquity," etc. He also wrote: "It is possible to specify that the mentioned treasury is the wisdom of performing the commandments according to the Secret of the Higher Wisdom, which is the Wisdom of Kabbalah... the knowledge of the reasons for the commandments." It is for this that we pray every day: "Enlighten our eyes in Your Torah." For what do we lack in our standing? "Give our hearts the ability to understand, to discern, to listen, to learn, and to teach." For His Torah includes "enlightening our eyes" in the portion of those hidden things designated for this Higher Wisdom. Regarding this, King David said: "Open my eyes, that I may behold wonders from Your Torah" <note>Psalm 119:18</note>. And so said David ben Isaac: "My heart is the secret of the festival," a connection and a saying that were like a general proficiency in the community. Without this wisdom, which has no end—for all the rectifications of the 'sustenance force' come from it—one cannot grasp the "Great Eye" <note>A metaphor for Divine Providence</note>, blessed be He. This wisdom is full of forty shades of the heavens, a light before me.

Furthermore, the author of the book, **Rabbi Meir Poppers**, of blessed memory, elaborated further. The wise reader who cares for his soul should pay attention to what the master Rabbi Moshe Cordovero <term>the Ramak (1522–1570), head of the Safed school of Kabbalah</term>, of blessed memory, wrote in the book **The Pleasant Light** (*Or Ne'erav*), in Part 2: "Since our occupation is with the hidden treasury in the study of Divine matters, there is no doubt that the things upon which this gift is built are for a person to recognize his Creator according to his perception." As it says, "Know the God of your father." He wrote in the explanation of this commandment: "The secret of foundations and the pillar of hidden things is to know that there is a First Existence, and He brings all existences into being." This is true knowledge, even if it is a small amount of perception of the Divine according to the power of human intellect. Thus the verse says: "Know the God of your father and serve Him." For to serve Him properly, one requires this knowledge—the knowledge of His inner nature and His conduct. This is represented by the name and the sign of "The Service," which is the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu u-Shechinteh," the male and female aspects of the Divine</note>. He was precise in saying "and serve Him," meaning the service of this union. 

Therefore, it is not fitting for any member of Israel to be exempt from perceiving this commandment according to his strength. One cannot fulfill it perfectly without the knowledge of this wondrous Kabbalah, which is the Wisdom of God. As it is written: "And you shall desire to know." For it is written: "You shall fear the Lord your God." If one does not know the greatness of His loftiness, His Divinity, and how He includes all existence, how can one truly fear Him? How can a person reach the levels written of if they stay at the level of a "small act"? Without this, fear will flee from him. 

For He is the "Ancient of Days" <note>A biblical term for God used in Daniel and Kabbalah to describe the most ancient aspect of the Divine</note> who sits, and "the hair of His head is like pure wool" <note>Daniel 7:9</note>, and He sits on a throne of sparks of fire. As it is written: "His throne was fiery flames" and "the Lord your God is a consuming fire." If a person does not have these descriptions in his mind, his faith will falter and his awe will not increase except according to his imagination. However, the one who begins to know His preciousness—that He is stripped of all physical boundaries—will not find it difficult to understand that even the smallest of His servants cannot be compared to these things. 

A person might fall into wonder and ask: "Who am I?" For a person is like a mustard seed <note>A classic metaphor for insignificance in the face of the cosmos</note> within the first celestial wheel, and that wheel is like a mustard seed within the second wheel, and so on through the third, each inside the other. All of them together are like a mustard seed within the expanse of the heavens described in the "Work of Creation" <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit</term>. And all those are like a mustard seed within the seal of the heavens described in the "Work of the Chariot" <term>Ma'aseh Merkavah</term>. When a person increases his knowledge through this study, he will be humbled and desire in his heart to stand before these servants. He will fear His loftiness with the ultimate fear. This wisdom will be included in his soul. 

Regarding these commandments, they explained in the Zohar, in the portion of *Bereshit* (Genesis), the "Virtues" which this wisdom holds over other parts of our holy Torah: 
First, when a person occupies himself with the Divine Attributes, they act above, and the Attributes are rectified according to the one who occupies himself with them. He attains supreme purity and correct knowledge. So we explained in the Zohar... 
And there is a second virtue: in this world, he will engage...

The editor cites prominent authorities like Moshe Cordovero and Meir Poppers to frame Kabbalah not as an optional mystery, but as the core requirement for fulfilling the commandment to "know" and "serve" God.</summary>

Pomegranate Segment &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gate 1: Ten and Not Nine &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Pomegranate Nectar
