### Chapter 1: An Explanation
<margin>
Counting the Sephirot: According to the custom of the Kabbalists, they agreed that they number twenty <note>original: "esrim"; this likely refers to a double counting of internal and external aspects</note>. However, in the *Book of Creation* <note>Sefer Yetzirah</note>, which is attributed to Abraham our Father, peace be upon him—though some attribute it to Rabbi Akiva—they are ten.
</margin>

<image-desc>A rectangular decorative woodcut border with elaborate floral and foliate scrollwork frames the title of the section.</image-desc>
->The First Gate<-

And they are Wisdom, Understanding, etc. This is to say that the Ten Sephirot <term>Sephirot: the ten divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe</term> are like a vessel for the body; the number ten corresponds to the soul... centered in the middle by the "word of the tongue" and the "word of the member" <note>original: "milat lashon u-milat ma'or"; a reference to the two 'covenants' of speech and circumcision</note> <gloss>and the fifth husk... because of common stumbling blocks regarding the boundary and the hidden, for that which is not grasped cannot be attained. It is not only with the enlightened of the Children of Israel that the path is as distant as the stars</gloss>. Therefore, the author of the *Book of Creation* called them "Sephirot of Nothingness" <term>Belimah: a term from Sefer Yetzirah meaning "restraint" or "nothingness"</term>, meaning vessels of power. The term "Sephirot" itself relates to the word for "number" <note>original: "mispar"</note>, meaning they are judged by the name of number, even though they are called "nothingness." The matter is based on the "name of number," for their count is ten <gloss>(five) is the number</gloss> of the foundations. For the Scripture says: "When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers" (Psalm 8:4). Learn from the verse that He carved and wrote when He cut the heavens and the earth <gloss>...to the foundations which are a nickname for the Sephirot... and to the submissions they are ten... because the creation of the world was subtle, they are ten. It says that this is not a distinction <gloss>(by reason)</gloss> that the number of foundations is five against ten (and likewise with the feet) and all of them reach the number twenty... what was said is five against them... and they are never more than the ten Sephirot of Purity... <gloss>as explained in the Gate of Wisdom</gloss>. And it is said that they are never more than five... and the beginners are toward the Lord, blessed be He... <gloss>(and as said)</gloss> that they are twenty, meaning that when one understands the unity... the five on the right and the five on the left are one thing, totaling ten Sephirot... so there is no difference between the ten Sephirot and the thirty-two paths <note>original: "l-v netivot"</note>... whether one wishes for twenty systems or ten, the factor that decides between the five and the five is the tongue, which decides between the reaches of the hands, and the covenant of the member between the five and five lower ones</gloss>. And perhaps this is what the author of the *Book of Creation* intended when he said "ten against ten" and "the unique covenant is aligned in the middle." Regarding the unity of "five against five" (of the Sephirot), the commentators offer two explanations: The first is that the Sephirot are arranged into two systems... and the second system is of research and investigation... and because the matter of tradition <note>Kabbalah</note> is not proven to everyone in a divided way, they intended it well. For such is the opinion of the author of the *Book of Creation*, especially regarding the Phylacteries <term>Tefillin</term>, where the scrolls of the head correspond to... and the scrolls of the hand to... and likewise in the matter of the blessings, each Sephirah in its proper repair for the unification of the Higher Chariot.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 1
<image-desc>A rectangular decorative woodcut border identical to the one in the left column frames the title of the section.</image-desc>
->The First Gate<-

->We have learned there in the Book of Creation:<-

Ten Sephirot of Nothingness <term>Belimah</term>: the number of ten fingers, five opposite five, and a single covenant aligned in the middle—in the word of the tongue and in the word of the member <note>the covenant of circumcision</note>. Thus taught Rabbi Akiva from the mouth of the tradition <note>Kabbalah</note>, stretching back to Abraham our Father, peace be upon him. And in the chapter "Ha-Titkabel" it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Shamua said to his students, "My children, repeat my traits, for they are the 'heave-offerings of heave-offerings' <note>the best of the best</note> from the traits of Rabbi Akiva." Here we have a verse and a teaching that the Sephirot are ten. The word itself is derived from "The heavens declare [mesaprim] the glory of God" (Psalm 19:2), as explained in the *Tikunim* and the *Book of Clarity* <note>Sefer HaBahir</note>. Rabbi Shem Tov explained it as the "revelation of thoughts," "the hidden things," and "the separate forms." He intended that they are a likeness to their source in the "Sparkling Radiance" <term>Tzachtzachot: the three hidden lights above the first Sephirah</term> that are unified in the essence of the Root in the world of Thought. Let people not think that the Sephirot themselves are "separate forms" <note>independent deities or forces</note>, for it is their nature to be counted as one, as will be explained. Others explain that "telling" <note>sippur</note> is permitted regarding them, but not regarding the Infinite <term>Ein Sof: God as He is in Himself, beyond all attributes</term>. Furthermore, the word implies "clarity," like the sapphire <note>original: "sapir"</note> which has no color of its own, but in it all colors are visible. It also implies "number" <note>mispar</note>, and it is also related to the word for a "border city" <note>sefar</note>, because the boundary of existence is drawn from them. The word *Belimah* is derived from the term "to muzzle" <note>balam</note>, for the Sephirot cover the Holy, and they themselves are covered and hidden; thus it is proper to "muzzle" our mouths from speaking of their essence. The explanation we need here is that the Sephirot are "without substance" <note>beli mah</note> that can be grasped, as it is written: "He hangs the earth on nothingness" <note>Job 26:7; "beli-mah"</note>. It is also written, "And the earth was chaos" <note>tohu</note>, which refers to something that is becoming but is not yet graspable. (The editor's note: It seems the explanation is that the Ten Sephirot are without the name "MAH" <note>the divine name of G-d associated with the world of Rectification</note>, which is the sustenance within the secret of "What [mah] is his name?"). Occupation with them is part of the "Secret of the Lord for those who fear Him" (Psalm 25:14)—the "sons of the prophets," the "enlightened of Israel," and the "remnant of His inheritance" who make themselves upright and whose hearts worry within them. These are the survivors worthy of having the "heads of chapters" <note>the outlines</note> of this wisdom transmitted to them. And it is found in *Genesis Rabbah*: Rav Huna in the name of Bar Kappara opened with the verse, "Let the lying lips be stilled" (Psalm 31:19)—let them be bound, let them be made mute, let them be silenced—those who speak of the Righteous One <note>the Life of the Worlds</note> with arrogance, who distances Himself from His creatures so that one might say, "I am expounding on the Work of Creation" <note>Ma'aseh Bereshit</note>, thereby despising the honor of the Place <note>HaMakom: a name for God</note>. Rabbi Yosi bar Hanina said: Anyone who honors himself through the shame of his fellow has no share in the World to Come; how much more so regarding the honor of the Place! He explained that "arrogance" <note>etek</note> refers to the titles that the Infinite One removed <note>he'etik</note> for Himself from the perspective of His actions alone <note>the Sephirot</note>, and this is the general principle of this wisdom. The "number of ten fingers" refers to the palaces <term>Heikhalot</term> of the craftsmanship of the Holy One, blessed be He. Our King David said of them, "When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers," and the Prophet said, "My hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spanned the heavens" (Isaiah 48:13), explaining that they are five opposite five.

It explores the etymology of "Sephirot" (number, clarity, or boundary) and "Belimah" (restraint or nothingness), emphasizing that while they are the tools of creation, their true essence remains beyond human comprehension.</summary>

<meta>The previous page introduced the "Pomegranate Nectar" (Asis Rimonim), a foundational Kabbalistic summary. This page continues the front matter, transitioning from the printer's or editor's technical notes on the manuscript's condition to a formal, poetic preface by the author's son. It establishes the spiritual requirements for studying these secrets.</meta>

It is said to the afflicted soul, and this was the end of the matter: he who wishes to learn the entirety of the Torah, thus it is established for the wise. He shall be like a brother <note>original: "ahi," likely a poetic play on "the letter Aleph"</note>, he shall cut and engrave, and it shall be his occupation. He shall receive kingship and his knowledge shall be broadened, for God is with him in his deeds, and the King shall increase in his ascents, and the "Nectar" <note>Asis</note> shall provide its taste and fragrance.

Furthermore, it was hidden from us what the **Maharamak** <term>Maharamak: Rabbi Moses Cordovero (1522–1570), one of the most influential figures in the history of Jewish mysticism</term> wrote in his book *Chesed L'Avraham* <note>Abraham's Kindness</note> in the first chapter. These are his words: "In the time of my youth, I saw this matter: first, one must prepare oneself with submissiveness to enter this Sanctuary <note>Heikhal</note> in order to strip away the 'Husks of Exile' <term>Kelipot: 'shells' or 'husks' that represent the forces of impurity or concealment in the world</term> that prevent us from attaining the path of truth. One should involve themselves deeply in it, and eventually, they will reach the goal of this wisdom. Second, one should cling to the 'filling of the belly' with the laws of the Gemara <note>Talmud</note> and the explanation of the commandments according to their plain meaning, following the explanations of **Maimonides** <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon, the great medieval legalist</term>. Third, let us also be guided by the Scriptures, even if only a little. May God assist our thoughts to refrain from physical vessels and pleasures as much as possible in this time of ours; then surely the gates of wisdom will be opened to him. Fourth, regarding the age: there is no doubt that it is not fitting for a person to enter this wisdom unless he has reached adulthood, is purified and settled, and not all temperaments are equal. Furthermore, one must wait at least until reaching twenty years, or until forty years <note>referring to the traditional age restrictions for studying Kabbalah</note>, etc." 

This aligns with our opinion, and we have completed it. Nevertheless, everything is according to the purity of the heart; such a person is worthy to learn. Surely every day is easy for a person to learn, but certain times are more prepared for deep understanding, such as the nights close to the Sabbath and New Moons. Then, in the days of favor, one will find revelations. So too on the eve of the Sabbath from the afternoon onwards, and especially on the Ten Days of Repentance. I have tested this many times and found it to be a straight path. 

The signs of merit are there, for there is a great light, and those mentioned are refined and move within this wisdom, which is the life of the world and its death, as **Rashbi** <term>Rashbi: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</term> said: "For the world shall be blessed through it." I knew the reader would wonder: "How can we in our generation reach such high levels?" But consider this: the merit of studying the Torah according to its plain meaning is like a shield for us and our wisdom. The words of the Zohar are like pearls for a person, according to their heart's capacity... in the "Measure of the Stature" <term>Shiur Komah: a Kabbalistic concept regarding the divine 'body' or dimensions of the emanations</term>. And in this, the praiseworthy shall praise himself! It is natural and known that I, the author, say: "The ways of the Lord are straight; the righteous walk in them and the rebellious stumble in them." This is what Rabbi Eleazar said in the Midrash... <note>original: "msd'd," likely an abbreviation for a Midrashic source</note>. 

And regarding the place of our beginning... and in the first chapter of Pesachim regarding the "poor of the flock"... therefore, one should intend... and regarding things that are harmful by nature... as recorded in Yoma... and things that are beneficial by nature, which is the refinement of the simple, the restoration of the soul, and the enlightening of the eyes. 

This work was brought to the printing press by the refined and prominent man, the son of the master and teacher **Rabbi Shimon**, son of the honorable teacher **Rabbi Naphtali Hertz Katz**, may his memory be for a blessing in the world to come. He was like a pillar for the masses in the House of Israel, standing in the breach of the Kabbalah. He brought it to the printer <note>ha-madpis</note>, and they labored and brought it to light, finding it sweet to the palate. He was a master of deeds and a master of will who approached the inner sanctum and ate from the Tree of Life. He brought it to the press to enlighten the eyes of all. They searched and found it, and I corrected it by the hand of the editor. 

The content of the "Pomegranate Nectar" by our teacher **Rabbi Jacob**, along with many new insights from his father, the Divine Kabbalist **Rabbi Isaac**, with many added glosses upon the foundations, found within the borders of the margins, and also from above and below. There was also a small manuscript by our teacher **Rabbi Solomon** found written on slips of paper placed between the pages. From this, we hoped to write, and we did all in our power to set it in its place. 

The original manuscript was blurred and written over erasures. Many times, it was inverted from top to bottom and bottom to top, and from many pages that were moved backward and forward. I have come to this place today to become accustomed to it; see the language and understand its reasons, which are clarified in my deeds. Our father, the Sage, stated that in every place where our teacher **Rabbi Moses** <note>Cordovero</note> is mentioned, it is from the original text, and afterwards, the additions are more numerous than the core. This is clarified in our place. We did not spare any effort and did all we could to correct all his words. If any error escaped us, may the reader judge us favorably, and may the merits of the authors, which are many, stand for us. 

I have counted "Bell and Pomegranate" <note>Pa'amon ve-Rimon, a reference to priestly garments</note> because the three letters are hints of the three authors who kept the watch of the Torah. I also acted according to the initials of "My son Jacob," and "Behold, Sinai is our King," etc. All of this is known in the secret of the "vessels." May my wisdom return to me... the protector of the Torah watch, standing and serving in the "Small Sanctuary" <note>Mikdash Me'at</note> of the Ashkenazi congregation in Glowitz.

-> Shimon, son of the master and teacher Rabbi Naphtali Hertz Katz, of blessed memory, from Schwerin. <-

### Slice of the Pomegranate: Gate of "Ten and Not Nine" — Pomegranate Nectar

...circumcision <note>Hebrew: *Milah*</note>, and between the ten fingers of his hands, which is the **Covenant of the Tongue**. The meaning of "cutting a covenant" refers to the binding of the crowns of the letters and the transmission of wisdom to know their combinations, through which the world was created. In the first *Mishnah* <note>The first teaching of *Sefer Yetzirah*, the Book of Formation</note>, a law was given regarding the **Emanation** <term>Atzilut: The highest of the four spiritual worlds, the realm of pure divinity</term> that it shall not deviate from ten levels. From the fact that it did not distinguish between the five fingers and the five toes, we learn to apply what is said of one to the other, for they are "Front and Back" and nothing else. Afterward, it says that **Abraham our father** (peace be upon him) merited to become a "Chariot" <note>A vehicle for Divine presence</note> for the Supernal ones. He was prepared first from below to above, and they assisted him afterward to "tell the end from the beginning."

### It Will Be Explained
In what follows, it will be clarified that the **Direct Light** <term>Or Yashar: Divine energy flowing downward from God into the world</term> is associated with **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note> and **Mercy**. Within it, there is a "saving congregation." Therefore, **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note> inclines toward Kindness; it is the decider for that side, for the "Voice" is comprised of water, fire, and wind. Its source is the "Tongue-Shofar" within **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, and it ascends through the three highest Sefirot, mediates between the "Arms" <note>Chesed and Gevurah</note>, and flows downward. It is also called the **Covenant of the Mouth**. It is possible to explain the "Covenant of the Tongue" as being on the side of its reception from Understanding, and the "Blessing of the Mouth" as being on the side of its influence upon **Kingship** <note>Malchut</note>. The **Returning Light** <term>Or Chozer: Divine energy reflecting back from the world to its Source</term> is associated with **Judgment** <note>Din</note>, and within it is a "judging congregation." Therefore, the **Righteous One** <note>Tzaddik, associated with the Sefirah of Yesod</note>, the "Foundation of the World," is its mediator. Just as the tongue only decides a matter <note>original: "milah," also meaning word</note> when it is upon it and its covenant is faithful to it, so too the "sign of the covenant" <note>the reproductive organ</note> only decides by means of the **Crown** <note>Atara</note> that is revealed at the head of the Righteous One by the removal of the foreskin. This is the secret of the Covenant: the revelation of the letter *Yod* within the letter *Heh*. This is the meaning of "And this..." within His host, and through this merit, they shall "see the face of the Master three

# Chapter 3: Thus we Have Learned
That the mediator is never an 
additional limb, nor is there

that decides independently. Rather, "the priest assists the priest." Therefore, the Teacher <note>the author of Sefer Yetzirah</note> did not mention the **Covenant of Unity** in the specific mediations, but only the **Covenant of the Tongue** separately and the **Covenant of Circumcision** separately. This is because in them, there is no perfect equalization—not "five against five"—nor did he intend for a middle point. However, in the comprehensive mediation of the whole "Tree," he taught the completion of the mediation and the equalization in all its parts until it becomes a Covenant of Unity. Its rectifications are the Tongue and the "Exposed Part" <note>the organ of circumcision</note> when they are fully matured. Here, he called it the "Word of the Tongue" in the secret of the mediation that requires Voice and Speech, which are **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note> and **Kingship** <note>Malchut</note>, for a "word" cannot be imagined without both. And for **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>, he called it the "Exposed Part," for it is exposed and clings in perfect unity. According to this, it seems reasonable to us that the Teacher meant: the first five of the "Direct Light" correspond to the last five of the "Returning Light"—meaning the "beginning of thought is the end of action." Automatically, this implies the rest: the [last five] of the Direct Light correspond to the first [five] of the Returning Light—the "end of thought and the beginning of action." This is the secret of "their end is wedged in their beginning and their beginning in their end." It is also possible to explain "five against five" as the five mediations that exist in one Tree: First, in the secret of **Knowledge** <note>Da'at</note> which mediates between the thirds of **Greatness** <note>Chesed</note> and **Strength** <note>Gevurah</note> that are hidden in **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> and **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>. For Knowledge is nothing but their collection and partnership to decide and mediate peace between them. We shall focus in the "World of Nothingness" <term>Beli-mah: A term from Sefer Yetzirah for the Sefirot</term> on the future benefits to be drawn from the secret of Knowledge in the ten-level structure. There is a second mediation for this, belonging to **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note> between Greatness and Strength; and a third for **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note> between **Victory** <note>Netzach</note> and **Splendor** <note>Hod</note>. the mediators, behold, there are ten against ten. Therefore, "one does not add to the number and one does not subtract from the number." <note>original: "Eser v'lo tesha, eser v'lo achat esreh" — Ten and not nine, ten and not eleven</note>. And in the explanation of these words, it is explained that the intention is that we should not think the **Crown** <note>Keter</note> is not part of the count of the Sefirot. Truly, they are "Knowledge" <note>original: "Da'ata"</note> as is known, but Kingship is essentially within the Emanation <note>Atzilut</note>, even if not all its qualities are [visible], because it was diminished as explained in the "Gate of the Diminution of the Moon." Similar to these words, it is said that there are ten "Measures" <note>Middot</note> of the Tongue, and they are six from the side of the **Holy Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, which is comprised of ten Sefirot... totaling thirty Sefirot without separation.

And the explanation of what they said, "And if you should say..." the intention is that we should not say they are the ten powers of Kingship and according to this it would be possible to say Kingship is separate from the ten... as mentioned, for He is the Decreer who unifies

# Pomegranate Nectar: Gate 1, "Ten and Not Nine" — Slice of the Pomegranate

Upon them are the faces of **Man, Eagle, Lion, and Ox**, which total 157 <note>Hebrew: *Kuf-Nun-Zayin*. This numerical value (Gematria) relates to specific angelic configurations in Cordovero's system</note>. And **Kingship** <note>Malchut</note>, which was sweetened, contains the faces of Man, Lion, Ox, and Eagle, totaling 180 <note>Hebrew: *Kuf-Nun-Kaf-Yod*</note>. The **Crown** <note>Keter</note> includes everything above, and Kingship includes everything below; thus, the **Ancient One** <term>Atik: An aspect of the Divine associated with the highest level of Keter, representing the "Ancient of Days"</term> encompasses three systems, as mentioned. 

In this same way, the **Standing Covenant** <note>The physical sign of the covenant</note> which encompasses between the eighty <note>Representing a numerical or structural category</note> and the three, like the Crown, is in the "thickness" of **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>, which is filled above and below and binds the upper beings to the lower ones. This applies to us regarding the count of the **Emanations** <term>Sefirot: The ten creative attributes or "numbers" through which God reveals Himself</term>, in their glory and light, which flow into the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> and Kingship <note>Malchut</note>.

The author of the *Book of Formation* <note>Sefer Yetzirah</note> intended to see with a gentle tongue... for the word **Tongue** hints at the attribute of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, just like the voice that emerges through the power of the tongue. This refers to Tiferet emerging from **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>. The power of the voice is famously comprised of water, fire, and air; these are the three quantities of Tiferet, for the voice travels between the water and the fire, which are **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note> and **Severity** <note>Gevurah</note>.

**Chapter 2 and the Second Explanation:** The second corresponds to **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>. The "Five" <note>referring to the five fingers</note> corresponds to the five [Sefirot], and the "Voice" teaches of five types, which are the 100 Sefirot... Kindness <note>Chesed</note> is the right hand. Tiferet's essence is the **Middle Pillar** <term>Middle Pillar: The central axis of the Sefirotic tree that balances the Right (Mercy) and Left (Judgment) sides</term>, though some say its essence is Kindness, as it is known to "incline toward Kindness." 

And the "Five" from the left side are the 100 Sefirot... all judgment and the voice of the Left, which is 180 <note>Kuf-Nun-Kaf-Yod</note>, and the left hand. Understanding <note>Binah</note> is also associated with Judgment in its aspect called the "Worker of Severities," for judgment is awakened from it. The **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note> is also primarily associated with all the Severities... Thus, the **Unique Covenant** <note>The organ of circumcision</note> at the center of the line is Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, which decides between Judgment and Kindness, as is known. 

**Chapter 3:** Furthermore, Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> decides between **Greatness** <note>Gedulah/Chesed</note> and **Splendor** <note>Hod</note>, and between **Severity** <note>Gevurah</note> and **Victory** <note>Netzach</note>. Proof for this is found in the words of Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai in the *Faithful Shepherd* <note>Ra’aya Meheimna, a section of the Zohar</note> on the verse "I was not..."

**Chapter 4:** From the logic of the 180 <note>Kuf-Nun-Kaf-Yod</note>, Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> receives from Greatness and flows into Victory and Splendor. And when the verse speaks of the one who bestows, it refers to the flow from Greatness (which Tiferet receives) and to Victory, which is the flow from Severity... this will be explained further in the "Gate of the Crowns."

**Also:** From the words of the earlier Kabbalists, it is explained that a specific color is added to the white, and a specific mystery is added to the white, as will be explained in the "Gate of Colors." The general point of these matters is to hint at the balancing: five against five. This includes Understanding against Wisdom, Greatness against Severity, and Greatness against Splendor while Severity is against Victory. The place that lacks balancing is between Victory, Splendor, and the Foundation; it is the **Covenant** <note>Yesod</note> that decides between them, as will be explained in the "Gate of Balances."

<column-break/>

...Five. The commentators said "Upper ones to lead the Upper ones," meaning the leadership of the higher realms is through the **Great Court** <term>Beit Din: A spiritual tribunal or court of judgment</term> that resides in Severity <note>Gevurah</note>, which judges the "Chariot-Throne" from the power of Understanding <note>Binah</note>. The leadership of the lower realms is through the **Lower Court** which resides in Kingship <note>Malchut</note>, to judge in the worlds of **Formation** <note>Yetzirah</note> and **Action** <note>Asiyah</note>.

Similarly, they divided the system into the 32 Paths <note>The 32 Paths of Wisdom mentioned in Sefer Yetzirah</note>. Even though the Work of Creation is explained entirely in the world of **Emanation** <note>Atzilut</note>, and also in **Creation** <note>Briyah</note>, **Formation** <note>Yetzirah</note>, and **Action** <note>Asiyah</note>, the division is nevertheless agreed upon. Whether from the "Paths," for 32 teeth are divided in man into two systems, or from the Ten Sefirot, as proven in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan), which explains the four sections of the **Head-Tefillin** <term>Tefillin: Ritual leather boxes containing Torah verses worn during prayer</term> as Wisdom, Understanding, Greatness, and Severity, while the **Hand-Tefillin** represents Beauty, Foundation, Victory, and Splendor. 

In this way, the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei HaZohar</note> explained two Chariots whose order is the faces of **Man, Eagle, Lion, and Ox**, which exist in the world of "Nothingness" <note>Beli-mah</note>. They exist in a hidden power, as recorded in the Zohar regarding the "Stature" <note>Shiur Komah</note> and the "Divine Image." These two Chariots are included in the **Crown** <note>Keter</note> and **Kingship** <note>Malchut</note>.

**Furthermore:** The commentators explained that the **Right Hand** includes Crown, Wisdom, Greatness, Beauty, and Victory. The **Left Hand** includes Understanding, Severity, Splendor, Foundation, and Kingship, according to their inclination. For Understanding is called "Worker of Severities," and the **Middle Pillar** <note>Tiferet</note> takes from the right, especially the Supernal Crown, while the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> binds to the left, especially Kingship <note>Malchut</note>. The parable of the fingers is the proof that there is no "knowledge" of a Sefirah in the world of Nothingness except as will be explained. Behold, Beauty and Foundation together shall be "twinned" to decide between them, as explained in the *Tikunim*.

## Chapter 2: Behold the Covenant of Unity mentioned in the Mishnah in the middle
->The Five against Five, for which there is a reason<-

One does not [distinguish] between the hands and the feet; if so, the "Image" <note>Tzelem</note> would depart from being joined with them to be counted as twenty. The Sage <note>The author of Sefer Yetzirah</note>, peace be upon him, wrote in the book that the **Feet** hint at the world of **Creation** <note>Briyah</note>, which is a "shadow" <note>Tzel</note> to the world of Emanation. Others said they are the Ten Sefirot within the attributes of Kingship. However, "both these and those are the words of the Living God," for the **Fingers of the Hands** hint at the collective "Crowns" of Emanation that appear in Kingship to reveal actions, while the **Toes of the Feet** are the sources of the world of Creation that sparkle within Kingship. From there, the "shadow" returns backward ten degrees.

This is the meaning in the *Monograph of Letters*, where it is written: the letter **Yod** <note>י</note> is Understanding, the head; the letter **Vav** <note>ו</note> is the body; the letter **Dalet** <note>ד</note> refers to the four: two hands and two feet. The head includes the "Upper Three" Sefirot, and the body includes the "Six Extremities" <note>the directions of the physical world</note>. Kingship <note>Malchut</note> includes within itself the branches that spread out to produce "the tool for its work." Thus, the hands and feet are the "rectifications" of the **One Adam** <term>Adam Kadmon: The primordial "Universal Man" or first blueprint of creation</term> pictured for us in the world of Nothingness with simple power.

Therefore, the Priests in the Temple walked **barefoot**, so that nothing would intervene between them and the floor... Similarly, regarding the **Basin** <note>Kiyor</note>, the Priest places his right hand upon his right foot and sanctifies, and likewise with the left, to purify Kingship in all its aspects from the impurity that seeps out and takes hold of the "surplus of the nails" which are burned. 

**We have also learned** there that the Holy One, Blessed be He, cut a covenant with Abraham between the ten toes of his feet, and that is the **Covenant of Circumcision** <note>Brit Milah</note>.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the precise number of the Sefirot, specifically addressing why traditional sources sometimes mention thirteen attributes or eighteen configurations while the Book of Formation insists on "Ten and not nine, ten and not eleven." # Pomegranate Nectar: Gate 1, "Ten and Not Nine" — Slice of the Pomegranate

->It is said: "Ten and not eleven," and one should be precise in this path...<-

We have learned that there are thirteen attributes <note>original: *middot*</note>, yet we also learned there are thirteen Sefirot; however, these thirteen attributes are the thirteen "branches" of the ten Sefirot. It is written in the writings of the sages of blessed memory that these thirteen attributes are branches and "offspring" that emerge from the ten levels called Sefirot. These correspond to one another, along with the two intentions of the "Head of Heads" <term>Resha de-Lo Etyada: The "Unknown Head," the highest, most hidden part of the Crown (Keter)</term>. 

Know that there are no "new" intentions to be found here regarding thirteen Sefirot; rather, the core of the law is as stated: "Ten and not eleven." These thirteen attributes are indeed the Sefirot themselves, but the Teacher <note>referring to Rabbi Moses Cordovero</note> certainly admits that they are not the hidden Sefirot. Rather, these thirteen are the "garments" of the hidden essence, manifesting from the subtle existence of the Sefirah as will be explained in the Gate of Locations. 

Just as we do not find it difficult to say that there are ten [Sefirot] of Emanation, ten of Creation, ten of Formation, and ten of Action <note>These are the Four Worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah</note>, so too it should not be difficult for us to understand the male and female aspects within the hidden realms. Because the Crown <note>Keter</note> is not counted as part of the "paired" attributes, it does not produce a separate hidden manifestation. These are unified in their honor. The revealed ones are for the lower worlds, and for the upper worlds, the count never exceeds ten. The "two" that the Teacher mentioned are the sources for the ten Sefirot, as will be clarified in this Gate.

Similarly, what was mentioned in the *Baraita* of Rabbi Eliezer the Great regarding the "eighteen curtains" <note>original: *pargod*</note> and the "thirteen places of the souls," these thirteen are the secret of the Upper System. The commentators have already explained that these are the "Three Eyes of God" which act as kings, and are not actual "Emanations" <note>Atzilut</note>, but rather two entities that are called "Kings." These are the "secret of the body" as explained by Ibn Ezra: they are "Kings of God" corresponding to the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note>, "Crowned by God" corresponding to the Crown <note>Keter</note>, and "Splendor of God" <note>referring to specific angelic or structural ranks below the Sefirot</note>.

Furthermore, concerning what the sages said regarding the "Curtain" <note>Pargod</note>: this is a partition and a veil <insert>between</insert> the World of Emanation and the other worlds beneath it. Likewise, the "Throne" refers to the Throne of Glory which is the "General Throne" including the three lower worlds. This is the meaning of "Throne" in the language of Creation <note>Beriah</term>. Similarly, regarding the "Thirteen Places of the Souls," these are the chambers [of the palace], and they are sealed within the Glory. This refers to the level of the "Living Souls" which is below the Throne of Glory, and they are called the Garden of Eden. 

It is possible that the "Upper System" refers to the World of Action <note>Asiyah</note>, which is the "Upper System" of the physical world, placed beneath the World of Formation <note>Yetzirah</note>. Ultimately, in every general count of the Sefirot, there are never more than ten. Anyone who adds or subtracts from ten is a sinner and causes harm to himself; this is the secret of "Ten and not nine," as refined by the Infinite <note>Ein Sof</note>.

**The Chapter on Reality.** The existence of these Ten is necessary according to the Written Mystery. First, because we are "Believers, the sons of Believers" in the Primal Cause. Even in the specific details mentioned, we say that He oversees every Sefirah. Since the simple Unity is the Cause of all causes and the Reason of all reasons, removed from all chance and the Creator of all attributes, and is beyond all bounds and limits—if so, why do the majority of scriptures attribute to Him a multiplicity of attributes, names, and words that indicate limit and boundary? These refer only to the Sefirot. For the Simple One, in His essence and simplicity, these do not apply; they apply only in relation to His attributes, as will be explained in the Gate of Essences and Vessels. For through the attributes, the limits are defined.

<column-break/>

And the **Citron** <note>Etrog</note>, what is it? It is the Female. This is why it is written: "The fruit of a beautiful tree <note>Hadar</note>, branches of palm trees." What is this "fruit of a beautiful tree"? As the translation <note>the Targum</note> says: the fruit of the tree is the Citron. And what is "Beauty" <note>Hadar</note>? This is the "Beauty of All." This is the beauty mentioned in the Song of Songs: "Who is she that looks forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?"

**The Explanation:** First, the author wonders how we were permitted to attribute changing qualities to the root of the human soul, which is a hidden, inner Emanation. He says that from the revealed Emanation, what Sefirah does Man possess? He says they are "aspects of thought," as concluded later. When all things were of one kind, it was impossible for them to be sustained—meaning, in a revealed existence—without returning to be hidden in their source. These are the "Secret of the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> among the lower beings," which is a "High Necessity." 

From the "Nine" that were in His heart, He carved the Citron <note>Etrog</note> as the Female. For at the beginning, the Thought did not emerge into the power of the Male; through this, it "knew its kind." Therefore, it is not in the initial Unity, for it was emanated through the power of the Female who receives influence and becomes a channel for the revelation of existences.

And when it says "because she was arranged," it is as if to say: behold, she was arranged, or it means she was arranged with her "children" <note>the lower worlds or souls</note>. Were it not so, she would have remained with the other Sefirot in their Unity, in the secret of "also their children shall sit upon your throne forever." This is the secret of the "Assembly of Israel" <note>Knesset Yisrael</note>—"May she be your mate," according to the true explanations intended in these Gates. 

If we and our ancestors had not sinned, we would have all merited a soul from the World of Emanation <note>Atzilut</note>, and our bodies would have been like precious stones <note>Tarshish</note>, like the high angels, existing for generations upon generations like the body of Enoch. Our status would have been even higher than his, for "he dwells on high," whereas here [on earth] he did not merit that. However, God returned Man to the earth, and the "Essence of the Divine Presence is among the lower beings" when the body and soul are paired from below, and together they are "complete" to wipe away the "thick cloud" and the "mist"—that iron wall that separates Israel from their Father in Heaven. Then the "shadows" of the separate forces that block the Divine Presence will flee.

Behold, it was always in His heart that the "Males" should be nine, and the Citron <note>Etrog/Malchut</note> should be the tenth reality. However, before its "planting"—which is the separation required here—it was, as it were, "carried on their shoulders." They are the channels for the fixed abundance entrusted to them. This is what is meant by saying "it is from those nine." 

The Kingdom <note>Malchut</note> was being built continuously through the secret of "One, and One, and One" <note>A reference to the High Priest's count on Yom Kippur</note>, which the High Priest counts in the inner chambers on the Day of Atonement until the completion of the act in the secret of "A woman of valor is the crown of her husband." At that point, she is the "Beauty of All." "Many daughters have done valiantly, but you excel them all." 

Afterward, the "few" <note>the forces of impurity</note> grew strong in all the works of Creation, from the time the Serpent came upon Eve and cast "filth" into her, until His anger subsides and He comforts us. Then "the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun," and she will return to be the "Beauty of All," perfumed with myrrh and frankincense from the "Mother of Children" who is joyful. By this power, we read of her: "Who is she that looks forth as the morning?" in the awakening that rises from her to the above, and in her elevation to be the "fourth" to every "three" <note>referring to the four legs of the Divine Throne</note>. 

Or, she is "fair as the moon" next to the lower Sefirot <note>Netzach, Hod, Yesod</note>, "clear as the sun" next to the middle Sefirot <note>Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet</note>, and "awesome as an army with banners" next to the intellectual Sefirot <note>Chokhmah, Binah, Da'at</note>.

It says there: his students asked him, "What is the meaning of the letter *Dalet* <note>Numerical value 4, often associated with Malchut</note>?" He told them: "To what is the matter comparable? To ten kings who were..."

Likewise, he intended to remind us not to mistakenly include in the count the Prince of the Presence, Metatron <term>Metatron: The highest archangel in Jewish mysticism, often called the "lesser YHWH" because his name shares the same numerical value as Shaddai (Almighty)</term>. And similarly, "Ten and not eleven," and his intention was to prevent this [false] counting of ten, and to remove from it any subtraction or error of "increasing" (which actually) diminishes from ten.

# Chapter 3: Furthermore

In the explanation of the sixth Mishnah and our Teacher [Moses Cordovero] of blessed memory, who said: "The ten shall not increase." The intention is that one should not include [others so that it] increases beyond ten, as it was said in the Book: "Ten Sefirot of Nothingness <note>original: *Belimah*</note>, ten and not eleven." And it shall not decrease—the righteous one shall not decrease from ten, as it says "Ten and not nine." Therefore, he said we must first introduce the matter of the Sefirot, for there are ten from above to below, and ten from below to above, like the image of a sunbeam hitting a polished mirror in a window and reflecting back toward its source. 

(So too is the matter of the Sefirot: they are "vessels" from above to below until Malchut; from there, the light strikes and returns to the place of its source.) In the way of the "Surrounding Light" that descends to its end—just as there are ten from top to bottom, so there are ten from bottom to top. This is the refined secret of the form of the letter *Aleph*, which has a *Yud* above and a *Yud* below, and a *Vav* in the middle, totaling ten from above, ten from below, and the *Vav* in the middle in the system of the Names. (There are also upper waters and lower waters, and the firmament <note>original: *Chulia*</note> in the middle. The letter *Yud* of the Name *Yah* is the "opening" that unifies the upper and lower waters. This is the secret of "Taking the Shekel," which mediates between the three levels of the Shekel—the *Yud* in its fullness [10+6+4]—which is) twenty *gerahs* <note>a biblical unit of weight</note>. There are two *Yuds* (Y-H) and three [letters] in the word *Yad* (Hand) on this side and *Yad* on that side.

**And** with this, the explanation of the *Nectar* will come: "It shall not increase," etc. The intention is to say that it is unnecessary to mention the other Sefirot, for even *Tiferet* (Beauty), which is "rich" in its spread and generality more than the other Sefirot, should not have its generality added to more than ten Sefirot, because the rule is "Ten and not eleven." If so, we should not add to its generality more than ten, because it is a "Tenth" <note>original: *Asiron*, a play on "Rich" (*Ashir*)</note>. Rather, its richness lies in the abundance of flow, returning to the fact that it is composed of ten many times over, but it never increases beyond the general ten. 

Furthermore, "it shall not decrease" refers to *Yesod* (Foundation). Even though it is called "poor" <note>original: *ani*</note>, as it is written "The righteous one eats [to satisfy his soul]," it should not have less than a generality of ten. Despite its poverty, it must not be less than them, because the rule is "Ten and not nine." Its poverty is only in the reduction of its flow or its generality of ten—meaning it does not multiply the generality ten times ten. However, it should not decrease from the mentioned ten, so that there is no separation between the ten. It is impossible to say that it is a place of separation (rather, they are always ten).

And if she is not flawed in her essence, even though light increases in the other emanated ones, she is equal to them in every single way except for what we mentioned. 

*Yesod* (Foundation) is also called "poor," having nothing of its own, because the light of *Malchut* is a "deposit" with him. **Pomegranate Slice: Gate of Ten and Not Nine — Pomegranate Nectar**

<margin>Kingdom (*Malchut*). And the secret of the number 60, for it is twice 30 <note>original: *S"L*, numerical value 30</note>. The key to faith below: It is stated there that all the powers of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are layered one upon the other and they resemble a tree. It is Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), and it is the souls of the righteous that fly from the Spring to the Great Channel, ascending and clinging to the Tree. And by whose merit do they fly? By the merit of Israel, for when they are righteous and good, the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) dwells among them and dwells within their deeds, in the "bosom" of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

...and He makes them fruitful and multiplies them. **And in the *Tikkunim*** <note>The *Tikkunei Zohar*</note> they said: The root of the four letters <note>The Name YHWH</note> and the ten letters is Kingdom (*Malchut*), which is comprised of all ten Sefirot. One must include her in the whole, for whoever takes Kingdom without the nine Sefirot is "cutting the shoots" <note>A Talmudic metaphor for heresy or separating the Divine attributes from their source</note>, and whoever takes the nine Sefirot without Kingdom is a denier of the Root. **Furthermore**, the Sages of the Mishnah were careful not to count the Infinite (*Ein Sof*) or the Choice among the two Sefirot <note>Meaning, among the ten</note>. For the Crown (*Keter*), despite its great stature, is counted with them, while the Infinite (*Ein Sof*) is vastly beyond it. Similarly, it is not proper to count Crown (*Keter*) and Knowledge (*Da'at*) together in the count of ten in a single "tree." For the Crown alone is a Sefirah from the World of Nothingness (*Belimah*), whereas Knowledge **is** a new entity that was renewed through the "Balance" <term>The Balance (*Matkala*): A Zoharic concept referring to the equilibrium of Divine forces during the process of emanation</term> and emerged into actuality from what was previously only potential. The obligation to distinguish between two "negations" <note>The hiddenness of Keter vs. the emergence of Da'at</note> is minimal, but every detail is significant.

**Understand** with wisdom and contemplate the tradition of our Rabbis: "He brought forth one thing from another." Establish supports for your understanding through what you have received; this is being "wise in understanding." However, when you lean upon this and your springs burst forth outward, then investigate and know, and afterward calculate and establish. Similar to this, in the book *The Spring of Wisdom* (*Ma'ayan HaChokhmah*): "Know, understand, investigate, restore, and establish... and join one thing to another," etc. This will be explained clearly through the secret of the "Evaluations" <note>original: *Bechinot*</note> occurring two or three times, which we will explain in Gate 11.

In this way, Understanding (*Binah*) becomes for him the "Beginning of Knowledge" (*Reshit Da'at*), and she will be like a listener to Wisdom. This is within the secret of the Higher Wisdom and the Wisdom influenced by the "Flow" <note>original: *Mazzal*</note>, the secret of Science <note>original: *Mada*</note>. Investigate through the "funnel" of trade-offs, and establish every inquiry upon its clarity and truth. Then "Restore the Creator" <note>original: *Hashev Yotzer*</note>—who is the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), Blessed be He—over the totality of the Emanation (*Atzilut*) which He established. In the count of the emanated ones, He should only enter as the One who is "Exalted above all" as their Head. This is hinted at in the Alphabet, where we count ten letters and afterward combine them to find "King" (*Melekh*). **Or** one might say: Establish the "Word of the Lord"—which is Kingdom (*Malchut*)—upon its clarity and its support, which is the "Pillar of the World." After she is awakened toward them, "Restore the Creator," which is the Spark called "The Creator of the Beginning" <note>original: *Yotzer Bereshit*</note>, who designs the forms of all existing things within Kingdom, which is the beginning for the lower worlds. Then "Restore the Crown (*Keter*)"—which is the Creator of the Beginning, the secret of Wisdom—to its place; this is from top to bottom. This is the "Grafting of the Tree into the Tree" that we mentioned in Chapter Two to complete the Higher Union.

### Chapter 6 Explained

In the *Faithful Shepherd* <note>Ra'aya Meheimna, a section of the Zohar</note>: The masters of the secrets of the Torah and the masters of the Attributes inherit souls from the side of the Holy Kingdom (*Malchut*), which is comprised of ten Sefirot. For whoever inherits her, merits all ten Sefirot without separation. "Ten and not nine"—for if they inherited Kingdom alone, it would be nine in separation from her. Because there is no separation there, the *Book of Formation* says "Ten and not nine." And if you should say that it ascends above ten—the Explicit Name *Y-H-V-H* etc. that is unified with her—it does not ascend above ten. For this reason: "Ten and not eleven."

The truth is that all souls, even those drawn through the Worlds of Separation, are comprised of ten Sefirot in their full stature. From them, all the limbs and structures of a person spread out to complete his form, unless they were damaged by sin and returned to be clothed in a blemished body, or their corruption was within them during their lives—a blemish according to their wickedness. **However**, the "Masters of Attributes" who possess the merit of the Patriarchs and whose every deed is for the sake of Heaven—they draw a soul for their children from the World of Emanation (*Atzilut*). No being from the "Separated Worlds" <note>The lower worlds of Creation, Formation, and Action</note> has authority over it; rather, they are nourished from its essence as it passes. This soul is unified with all the Sefirot through the power of Kingdom in an essential union, for the Kingdom that breathes a "soul of life" into this righteous person breathes from her very essence. He uses the word "Inherit" based on the "Inheritance of Jacob our Father," for wherever it exists, it remains in the possession of the heirs. However, it cannot occur without a direct cause, which is why he said, "Whoever inherits her"—meaning he takes it by law through the merit of his parents who sanctified themselves at the time of union. "And he merits her"—for his own deeds assisted him in such a way that he merits the Ten Sefirot without separation.

**And if** you say the count ascends above ten, and even if they inherit Kingdom alone, the ones remaining above would not be less than ten—do not say this! For the "Explicit Name" is Beauty (*Tiferet*), who unifies with her by the power of the essence of the Will that shines through Wisdom. Its fullness has ten branches across a width of four, and Kingdom is the "Private Domain" <note>original: *Reshut HaYachid*</note>, her own domain, and she is included in its fullness. Because of them, Israel are called kings, righteous ones, seers, prophets, masters of Torah, mighty ones, pious ones, understanding ones, wise ones, and heads. The explanation of "Israel" is as clarified in the *Tikkunim*. Therefore it says there: The King's Daughter (*Malchut*) cannot be merited except by the King's Son, who is called "Israel, My firstborn son."

**And they said:** This Kingdom belongs to Emanation (*Atzilut*); she has below her the Kingdom of Creation (*Briah*), and she is the Kingdom for the angels of Creation. She is the "Adornment of the Matron" <note>The Queen</note> who serves her, and she is the image of her Mistress, comprised of ten. This level Israel can reach, but regarding the Kingdom of Emanation of the Holy One, Blessed be He, it is said: "I am the Lord, that is My name, and My glory I will not give to another." Nevertheless, whoever profanes the "garment" of the King is considered as if he profaned his Matron. They explained this profanation there as the wandering of the soul that is hidden in the Separated Worlds to be revealed...

# Pomegranate Nectar &emsp; Gate of Ten and Not Nine &emsp; Pomegranate Slice

The changes, the judgment, and the mercy do not exist within His essence to such a degree. The secret of this "falling of the outer [forces]" <note>Referring to the external manifestations or the lower emanations that interact with the world</note> is intended so that we do not deny the foundations of our faith regarding the principles of Divinity and the absolute simplicity required of the Cause of All. This absolute simplicity is infinite. Therefore, one must believe in the *Sefirot* so that the principles of our religion are not left open, God forbid, to those with wandering hearts. This is the reason we are compelled to accept the "falling" <note>The manifestation or descent into plurality</note> of the Torah and the recounted faith, and why there is a multitude of details within the secret of the Tradition (*Kabbalah*). **And from** the scriptures, a hint was clarified regarding the "thirty languages" <note>The Hebrew letter Lamed has the numerical value of 30</note> from the mandatory words of study and Tradition: "Words you shall speak" <note>original: *millin tamalel*</note>. For the power (*chayil*) of the letter *Lamed* points toward the Crown (*Keter*), which cannot be grasped by thought. Our sages' hint was clarified from the words of "Thirty" <note>The letter *Lamed*</note>, which teaches: "Yours, O Lord, is the Greatness (*Gedulah*), and the Power (*Gevurah*), and the Glory (*Tiferet*), and the Victory (*Netzach*), and the Majesty (*Hod*), for all that is in the heavens and in the earth... Yours, O Lord, is the Kingdom (*Mamlakah*)" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>. This "Yours" (*Lekha*) hints at the first three emanations. Understanding (*Binah*) is called a "treasure" (*segulah*), as the letter *Kaf* [in *Lekha*] relates to the "Twenty Gates of Understanding." For the phrase "For All" (*Ki Khol*) relates to the Foundation (*Yesod*) which receives and includes them—the twenty gates of Understanding. For all the letters of "Yours" (*Lekha*) and the secret of the Foundation receive the twenty gates through the chain of the five Sefirot called "All" (*Khol*). The Foundation also honors the connection between the six directions <note>the Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note> and the Kingdom (*Malchut*), which are detailed in the verse. "Yours, O Lord, is the Kingdom" points toward *Malchut*.

->### Chapter 9<-

Regarding those to whom the secret was not revealed, Heaven forbid that such a person be called a heretic, nor did they "cut the plantings" <note>A Talmudic metaphor for heresy or damaging the divine unity</note>. It is appropriate to weigh everything with insight, following the order of the commandments and principles, rather than being hasty, while also not concealing the secret. However, those to whom the secret was revealed, yet they revealed it further and then denied it because of their poor character—having become accustomed to "external sciences" <note>Secular philosophy or non-kabbalistic studies</note>—even they are not necessarily called heretics, but they are "those who cause others to sin" through their smooth-talking transgressions. They are called heretics only if they deny the Oral Torah's explanation, for then they are like the Karaites and heretics. As Maimonides wrote in the third chapter of *The Laws of Repentance*: The Blessed Creator comes to strip heresy away from faith. This is to establish the laws [of the Sefirot] as the "Simple One," so as not to contradict the principles of the religion, especially regarding the principles of prayer. For one who is not involved in Kabbalah and does not intend his prayer toward the Divine Might (*Gevurah*) is considered like one who "types" <note>meaning, acting mechanically</note>. For God forbid, in relation to the writing of His Simple Names, He is not subject to change—He does not shift from judgment to mercy or from will to will because of prayer. This change only occurs in relation to His "garments," which are the *Sefirot*. Through them, His providence and preparation are directed toward others, and through them, the two aspects of Judgment and Mercy are balanced without changing Him. This profound change will be explained in the Gate of Names and Titles. The end of the matter is that a person is compelled to believe in the *Sefirot* so that they do not damage the foundations of faith, for it is impossible to uphold the pillars of the Torah without this.

->### Another Chapter<-

The knowledge of the Sefirot and the recognition of their existence is chosen through their names. Know that the names are revealed and most famous as: **Crown** (*Keter*), **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*), **Understanding** (*Binah*), **Greatness** (*Gedulah*), **Power** (*Gevurah*), **Glory** (*Tiferet*), **Victory** (*Netzach*), **Majesty** (*Hod*), **Foundation** (*Yesod*), and **Kingdom** (*Malchut*). These Sefirot are the ten divine utterances, deep and hidden. The Sefirot and the Names are all one thing, for the spirituality of the Names is the essence of the Sefirot. The Names of the Crown are ***Eheyeh*** (I Will Be); for Wisdom, ***YHVH***; for Understanding, ***YHVH*** vocalized as *Elohim*; for Kindness (*Chesed*), ***El***; for Power (*Gevurah*), ***Elohim***; for Glory (*Tiferet*), ***YHVH*** vocalized as *Mah* <note>The name with a specific numerical value of 45</note>; for Victory and Majesty, ***Tzevaot*** (Hosts); for Foundation, ***El Chai*** (Living God); and for Kingdom, ***Adonai*** (Lord).

...who were in one place and all were wealthy. One of them was wealthy, but not like the others, even though his wealth was great. He was called "The Count" before the [other] wealthy ones, for even though he had less, his wealth was great in its own right. As they explained in the *Tikkunim* on the verse "I the Lord do not change" <note>Malachi 3:6</note>: "Truly 'I' refers to the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*)." This is what is written: "I will punish you, even I." "I" does not change, nor is "I" replaced by another. He does not change, and I am not hidden from Him. But regarding the guilty, the Holy One, Blessed be He, appears to change and is hidden from them. This is what is written: "I will hide my face from them." This is the ultimate flaw resulting from the "diminution" [of the moon/Shekhinah]: that the intention for the Glory to dwell in our land was not fulfilled. And since all the holy souls were engraved within her, the sinning soul damages its root, and the "river shall be wasted and dried up" <note>Isaiah 19:5</note> from the side of that soul, as stated in the *Tikkunim*. **And the truth is** that even when it is written from Above, she is called "poor." You were a "deposit" in the hand of another. This is from the language of "I will respond (*e'eneh*) to the heavens and they shall respond (*ya'anu*) to the earth." But with the diminution, she "lies in sorrow" because there is no righteous man in the land, and her soul is dry. It is bitter for her in the way we mentioned. For Jerusalem stumbled through the deeds of the wicked to provoke His glorious eyes. It is written "poor" (*ani*) because the Emanated Glory does not receive rebellion or flaw, God forbid; rather, the "Lower Glory," which is its likeness, is called "poor and riding on a donkey" <note>Zechariah 9:9</note> when the glory of the *Shekhinah* is clothed in the separate worlds to subdue the "Shells" (*Klippot*). These "separate ones" are themselves the "seven eyes of the Lord," to which rebellion truly reaches. With this, the scripture and the tradition are justified together.

## Chapter 5: To Lift

The stumbling block from the many and the good who were confused in the explanation of the words of Ramban <note>Nahmanides, 13th-century sage</note>. I will add and seek more from the clear "testing stone" to find the corner of their error; this is the fruit of removing their sin. They asked: What is the meaning of "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place"? This implies that no one knows His place. There is a parable of a Matron <note>A queen or noblewoman</note> who came from a distant place. They did not know from where she came until they saw she was a woman of valor, beautiful and fitting in all her deeds. They said: This one was surely taken from the side of Light, for her deeds illuminate the world. They asked her: "From where are you?" She said: "From my place." They said: "If so, the people of your place must be great. Blessed be you, and blessed be your place." Is not the Glory of the Lord one of His hosts? Is He any less? Why then do they bless "His place"? A parable: To what is this comparable? To a king who had a beautiful garden, and outside the garden, near to it, was a beautiful piece of field. If you irrigate the garden, at the start of the irrigation, the water flows over the whole garden. But that piece of field was not irrigated, for it was no longer attached to it. Even though everything is one, he therefore opened a place for it and irrigated it alone. **The intention** is that the emanation of the Kingdom (*Malchut*) from Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) is like a "land from afar," and its existence—this simple reality—is not grasped at all. The "people of her place" are great in the secret of the "Beings" (*Havayot*) which are in Wisdom. She is indeed included in the holiness of the Seraphim, but she has two aspects: The first is a "locked garden," in which she drinks at the beginning of the irrigation. The second is the aspect of the "field," which is the "root of the tree below" in the secret of the letter *Shin* <note>symbolizing the three branches of the Sefirot</note> through the power of Understanding (*Binah*). Sometimes it is breached, sometimes it is built—this is the secret of the letters *Dalet* and *He* <note>The letter *Dalet* means "poor/door" and *He* is the same shape but with an added leg, representing expansion</note>. # Gate One: Ten and Not Nine — The Pomegranate Orchard
### Section 21, Page 1
<meta>catchword: They shall fill</meta>

And for all the righteous of the generations who were before us, from the first man, Adam, until our father Abraham, peace be upon him: **And they are** likewise explained in the scriptures as the "Three Mothers" <note>The three foundational letters—Aleph, Mem, Shin—from the *Sefer Yetzirah* (The Book of Formation)</note> from the words of Job: "And wisdom, where shall it be found?" <note>Job 28:12. In Hebrew, "where" is *Me-ayin*, which literally means "from Nothingness." Kabbalists interpret this to mean Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) emerges from the Crown (*Keter*), which is called "Nothingness" due to its incomprehensibility.</note> for the hidden Crown, due to its proximity to its Source, is called "Nothingness" (*Ayin*), indicating its relationship to Wisdom and Understanding; and "Nothingness" is the place and source from which Understanding (*Binah*) issues. **And furthermore**, the seven lamps shall shine, and the Menorah and the doorposts <note>original: *mezuzot*</note> that the Lord spoke of to us—this is the secret of the expansion of the fifty Gates of Understanding in the surrounding world. This refers to the levels from Lovingkindness (*Chesed*) downward, when the Upper Gate is revealed at the top of the letter *Lamed* <note>The letter *Lamed* is the tallest Hebrew letter, often likened to a tower</note>, a tower flying in the air, which influences downward through the extension of the letter *Kaph* <note>The letter *Kaph* is shaped like a vessel or palm</note>. Their general forms are the vowel-points *Segol* and *Tzere*, comprising five *Yods* <note>The letter *Yod* has the value of 10; five *Yods* represent the five dimensions of the soul or the five primary Sefirot</note>, five attributes encompassing the ten, when the "Mothers" shine upon them. These are Greatness, Might, Beauty, Victory, and Splendor, and no more. This is because everything that serves as the foundation—the bolt <note>original: *tzir*</note> of Joseph <note>Joseph is traditionally associated with the Sefirah of *Yesod* (Foundation)</note>—encompasses the fifty gates behind him, "in heaven and on earth" <note>Aramaic: *bishmaya u-ve-ar-a*</note>, which is the "Land of Desire" <note>A term for the Sefirah of *Malchut* (Kingdom)</note> above Victory and Splendor. In Beauty (*Tiferet*), the Foundation and Kingdom are included, and she [the Kingdom] later proved her lower existence as a "lowly kingdom" with its legions. Even there, the Lord shared His honor with her, for the King and Queen <note>Metaphors for the Sefirot *Tiferet* and *Malchut*</note> draw from a single Crown. **And in the Tikkunim** <note>Referring to the *Tikkuney Zohar*, a classic kabbalistic text</note> it was expounded on the verse: "And David took five smooth stones from the brook" <note>1 Samuel 17:40</note>. These are the five Sefirot with which David praised the Holy One, Blessed be He, saying: "Yours, O Lord, is the Greatness, etc." <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>. He drew them from "The Brook," which is the Foundation (*Yesod*), the "Life of the Worlds." When he placed them in the vessel, which is the Holy Kingdom (*Malchut*), they became one and sank into the forehead of the Philistine [Goliath] and killed him. And in the *Ra’aya Meheimna* <note>The "Faithful Shepherd," a layer of the Zohar</note> they expounded that the "five stones" are the words "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord [is One]" <note>The *Shema* prayer</note>, which is the "Kortah" <note>Aramaic: perhaps meaning the selection or the calling</note> of the *Shema* reading, the "lip of the Divine Presence" (*Shekhinah*), through which they become one, and by this merit, he defeated the Philistine. As in the portion of *Bereshit* <note>The first portion of Genesis</note>, they said there are five firmaments written here, and the "Life of the Worlds" travels through them and leads them; they are all included one in another. Were it not for this "division" <note>The differentiation of the emanations</note> opened by the "Central Column" <note>The middle line of the Sefirotic tree (Keter-Tiferet-Yesod-Malchut)</note>, they would not be included or formed one within the other. The "five hundred years" <note>A classic measure in Jewish cosmology for the distance between heaven and earth</note> are the "Tree of Life" that clings to them to produce fruit and offspring for the world. All the "waters of creation" that flow and extend from the Beginning are divided beneath it, and David the King takes all and divides it for the "Crown" <note>original: *Keter*</note>, as it is written: "And he divided to all the multitude, etc." And it is written: "You give to them, they gather it up," and it is written: "She rises while it is yet night and gives food to her household and a portion to her maidens" <note>Proverbs 31:15, interpreted here as the Sefirah of Kingdom distributing divine energy</note>.

## Chapter 10: Spirituality
The Sefirot yearn for and shine upon the Names [of God] through the intention of the writer or the one who utters them with his lips in holiness and purity. For the Sefirot are nothing other than names and titles for the King of Kings according to His actions. However, there is a "Simple Being" without vowel-points that includes all the emanations in a hidden subtlety, and its branches are the ten Names (*Havayah*) with specific vowel-points for each and every Sefirah—except for the tenth, which is influenced by all of them. In it, the "fullness" of all the Sefirot expands; not one is missing from its place and their likeness. Each one of them includes ten Names that are never to be erased. **And behold**, the Names are the Sefirot; it is explained that these and those are the names of God according to His actions. Wherever the Name of Being (*Havayah* - Y-H-W-H) is described, as we will mention later, these ten names reveal the details of that Being and its generalities. For the "tip of the [letter] *Yod*" is a hint to the Supreme Crown, and there it is not enjoyed <note>i.e., it cannot be grasped or utilized</note>; behold, we call it by the name *Ehyeh* ("I Will Be"). The letter *Yod* itself, wherever it appears, has the essential name *Yah*. So it is for all of them. This is even more wondrous for us: for the praise, thanksgiving, prayer, and unification that we perform through these pronounced names might lead the listener to think they refer to only one or two Sefirot, God forbid, according to the specific quality indicated. But in truth, it is nothing other than the unification of all ten Sefirot and the ten Names (*Havayah*) that we will explain later in Gate 19, when that specific mention is revealed in our mouths and hearts, serving that particular limb within all ten Names. We find that the general requires the particular and the particular requires the general through the power of true unification, and it is a wonder. **It is clear** what this is: for the name *Ehyeh* is a hint to the existence of the Crown as it is revealed in the Sefirot from the perspective of Understanding (*Binah*), and not otherwise. For from the perspective of its own essence, it is very awesome—who can contain it? The name *Yah* is a hint to the existence of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) as it is revealed in all of them when it unites with Understanding. The name *Havayah* (Y-H-W-H) with the vowel-points of *Elohim* <note>Usually pronounced as 'Elohim' when pointed this way</note> hints at Understanding, which is Mercy, yet Judgments are awakened from her. In the *Sifra Detzniuta* <note>The "Book of Concealment," a core part of the Zohar</note>, it is "The Living Y-H-W-H" <note>original: *Y-H-W-H Chai*</note>. This appears to be the secret of Sustenance, where the Kingdom is not revealed there, or in the secret of *Ehyeh* by numerical equivalence, and we shall return to discuss it. The name *El* corresponds to Lovingkindness (*Chesed*); *Elohim* to Might (*Gevurah*); *Havayah* with the vowel-points of *Tzevaot* <note>Hosts</note> to Beauty (*Tiferet*). Or, some say with the explicit vowel-points of *Adonai*, but with an added *Patach* [vowel] at the end for the expansion of the guttural letter and to sweeten the judgments of the "Female" [Sefirah]. *Tzevaot* is shared by Victory (*Netzach*) and Splendor (*Hod*). However, "no two prophets prophesy in the same style"; therefore, when joined with *Havayah*, it is in Victory, and with *Elohim*, it is in Splendor. Some attribute *Tzevaot* to Victory, *Eloah* to Splendor, and *El Chai* to Foundation (*Yesod*), according to later authorities, for *El* is borrowed from Lovingkindness and *Chai* [Living] is unerasable, though it is only a title. Their core is in the words of Rabbi Abba in the portion of *Vayikra*: he said *El Chai* is as we say, "For there the Lord commanded the blessing, life forevermore" <note>Psalm 133:3</note>. This is the Righteous One (*Tzadik*), from whom all life issues. Rabbi Eleazar attributed the name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty</note> to the Kingdom (*Malchut*). **And it appears** in the Bible 134 times without any additional letters. The hint in this is the secret of the 134 <note>numerical value of *KL"D*</note> for its "branches," which are the actions drawn to the lower worlds from its power, specifically through the "Righteous One" (*Tzadik* / *Yesod*) in the secret of the Palm Tree (*Tamar*), male and female, for one does not rise without the other. "They shall turn their back to the neck" <note>original: *kodla* - Aramaic for neck</note>. Others wrote that the initials and the walls of East, West, and South also equal 134, and in the Greek language, *KL"D* <note>Greek: *kleis* or *kleida*</note> means "The Locking Key." They said that these three directions are locked by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, but the North is left open—in the secret of "the world is like an *exedra* [a porch open on one side]" <note>Babylonian Talmud, Bava Batra 25a</note>. The shape of the letter *He* [ה] proves this, as the world was created with it; in it, He made all directions closed except for the North side, which is open to good and evil. At a time when Israel does not do the will of the Place [God], "fire is near"; but when they do His will, the Attribute of Mercy rolls and surrounds it, as it is said: "He bears iniquity and passes over transgression." And they said it shall be fenced in the time to come.

# Gate One: Ten and Not Nine — The Pomegranate Orchard

In this world, of which it is written: "But the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot" <note>Genesis 8:9. In Kabbalah, the dove often symbolizes the Shekhinah (the Divine Presence) in exile.</note>, and these matters reach those who return to walk for their own sake alone, and there is
