## Chapter 7: The Commandment
To give the half-shekel in the sacred shekel. Rabbi Meir <note>A reference to a passage in the Zohar or related literature</note> asked: What is this "half-shekel"? It is like a half-*hin* <note>An ancient liquid measure</note>, and this is the letter *Vav*, which is centered between two letters *Heh* <note>Referring to the structure of the Tetragrammaton (Y-H-V-H). The Vav (6) stands between the two Hehs (5 each).</note>. The "stone for weighing" is the letter *Yod*. "Twenty gerahs shall be the shekel" <note>Exodus 30:13</note>—this is the letter *Yod* <note>The letter Yod has a numerical value of 10. Two Yods (one for the shekel, one for the half-shekel) or the dual nature of 10 up and 10 down equals 20.</note>. "The rich shall not give more" <note>Exodus 30:15</note> refers to the Middle Pillar; he shall not increase beyond ten, for so it was stated in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an early foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>: "Ten and not eleven." "And the poor shall not give less"—this is the Righteous One <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note>; he shall not decrease from ten, just as it was stated: "Ten and not nine." The "Half-Shekel" itself is ten. And the foundation of this inquiry we mentioned in Chapter 2: that the Emanation <note>Atzilut</note> descends ten degrees and returns back against them; and behold, "twenty" is the numerical value <note>Gematria</note> of *Keter* (Crown). The *gerah* <note>original: "גרה"</note> is a title for *Malchut* (Kingship), whose wings are spread toward Justice. The shape of the letter **Aleph** proves this: a *Yod* above, a *Yod* below, and in the middle is *Tiferet* (Beauty), which connects the "upper waters" of the Higher Shekhinah <note>Binah/Understanding</note> with the "lower waters" of the Lower Shekhinah <note>Malchut/Kingship</note>, which are in a state of unity without any separation at all. It is explained elsewhere that *Malchut* is also called "half-shekel" when she rises to *Tiferet* in the secret of the vowel point *shuruk*. Behold, the simple *Yod* is the "weight-stone" of the measure of ten, and its full spelling includes the complete shekel. *Tiferet* is called "ten" because it includes more abundance than its companions, being strengthened by many inclusions. The "Righteous One is lost" <note>Isaiah 57:1</note> in the exile of the Shekhinah because his inclusions are few and his light does not shine; however, he shall not lack nor exceed ten. The "Half-Shekel" is the median between the two *Heh*s and the complete measure, and it includes ten within itself. **And in the Tikkunim** <note>The *Tikkunei Zohar*</note> they said regarding the verse "But a mist went up from the earth" <note>Genesis 2:6</note> that *Malchut* shall rise up to *Chokhmah* (Wisdom), the upper *Yod*, because from there she was taken. This is the meaning of "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>. She was taken up to them and drank from above, in its upper tip, in its middle, and in its lower tip. And when she descends, she descends comprised of three drops, and she is called the letter **Yod** made of three *Yods*: the upper *Yod* is upon this head, which is the Supreme Crown (*Keter*) above all heights; and afterwards she descends into the middle and takes from there in the Middle Pillar; and afterwards she descends below to her place—the *Yod* which is below the **Aleph**. This is the secret of the *Segolta* <note>A Hebrew cantillation mark shaped like three dots</note>. From this it is proven that the "Half-Shekel" is also ten. Elsewhere they explained the Explicit Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> as being comprised within the letter *Aleph*—that "if your heart runs, return to the place," in the sense of "nullify your will before His will." The intentions of the Shekel should be [the name] *B-Y-T U-L-S-H-K-S-H* <note>A mystical permutation of names</note> to nullify the will of others.

## Chapter 8: However
<margin>The RaN <note>Rabbi Nissim of Gerona, 14th-century scholar</note>, of blessed memory: The first three [Sefirot].</margin> The Thirteen Attributes of Mercy shall not add to the number of ten. For in the opinion of the Gaon Rav Hai, of blessed memory, the first three—which are names that may not be erased—indicate the roots of the subtle existence of the Sefirot. This means the Sefirot are ten in their place; their emptiness is at the heads of the lines: Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding (*K-Ch-B*). The existence of the heads is in the *K-Ch-B* of the Crown, and their roots are in the "Hidden of the Hidden" heads, according to the path of the Sage, peace be upon him, in the *Sefer [Pardes]* and mentioned in a specific gate with Divine help. According to this, it is correct to explain the ten latter attributes: for "Merciful" <note>original: *rachum*</note>—of which it is said "I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy"—and "Gracious" <note>original: *chanun*</note>—"I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious"—both of these apply even if one is not worthy. Likewise, "Slow to Anger" <note>original: *erekh apayim*</note> for the righteous and the wicked is directed toward the first three, which are considered as one, for they are [pure] Mercy. "Abundant in Kindness" <note>original: *rav chesed*</note> is as it sounds. "Truth" <note>original: *emet*</note> is *Gevurah* (Might/Judgment) to verify its judgments. "Preserver of Kindness" <note>original: *notzer chesed*</note> is *Tiferet*, leaning toward the right. "Forgiver of Iniquity" <note>original: *noseh avon*</note> is in *Netzach* (Victory), "and Transgression" <note>original: *pesha*</note> in *Hod* (Splendor), "and Sin" <note>original: *chata'ah*</note> in *Yesod* (Foundation), "and Cleanser" <note>original: *nakeh*</note> in *Malchut* (Kingship), of which it is written "He will not cleanse" <note>Exodus 34:7</note>—this "Cleanser" refers to the World to Come, while "He will not cleanse" refers to this world.

<margin>The Sage, of blessed memory.</margin> **And Rav Hamai**, in the *Book of Contemplation* <note>Sefer Ha-Iyun</note>, brought a tradition attributed to Simeon the Just, which holds that the attributes exceeding the ten Sefirot are the three final attributes. The commentators thought he referred to three powers within *Malchut*, named *Malki-El*, *Aturi-Ya*, and *Nasi-El*. Their sign is the name *ADNY* <note>Lord</note>. Now, "Her ways are ways of pleasantness," and it seems they are the sources of actions within her, similar to the sources of the roots that will be explained in *Keter* (the Crown). It is possible they are the beginning of the "Worlds of Separation." But the opinion of the tradition refers to the World of Creation (*Beriah*). See the "Chest of the Son" <note>original: *chazeh ke-var*</note> in the fifth measure: "Fire, its height is the Curtain" <note>original: *Pargod*</note>. This is the Throne of Glory, a screen before the world of Emanation (*Atzilut*). And there is the place of the souls and the "Chambers of Grandeur," referring to the chambers of the Garden of Eden, the resting place of the souls. For indeed, their essence is in *Atzilut* in the secret of "Man" <note>original: *Adam*</note>; but in their expansion into *Beriah*, the form of Eden is renewed for them, which is a subtle conceptual form. There they are still "souls" <note>original: *neshamot*</note> and "desolate" <note>original: *shomemot*</note> in the secret of *Tohu* (Chaos), "Something from Nothing." Their form is their "hewing" in the image of the World of Formation (*Yetzirah*) in the "Garden of the Generations of the Day," in the secret of *Bohu*, "Something from Something." From there they find rest for the "Spirit" <note>original: *Nefesh*</note> in the secret of the World of Action (*Asiyah*); this is the thirteenth level mentioned by Rav Hamai, which is the secret of the Upper Array, referring to the spiritual entities in the height of *Asiyah*. According to this, the names that may not be erased are indications of the first three Sefirot, which are intellectual, not attributes. "Merciful" and "Kindness" and "Gracious" are in *Gevurah*—mentioning "Gracious" because it is a free gift. "Slow to Anger" is in *Tiferet*. "Abundant in Kindness and Truth" and "Preserver of Kindness" are in *Netzach* and *Hod* in the way we explained in the first path. And *Malchut* is "Forgiver of Iniquity." "And Transgression" is in *Beriah*, which is a thin curtain [separating] through transgression between Emanation and the separated beings; once the Emanation spreads to it, one "looks to his Maker." This is the interpretation of the word as a pleasant compound: *P-Sh* <note>transgression</note> and then *Sh-A* <note>looked/turned</note>. "And Sin" is in *Yetzirah*, for there the "purification" <note>original: *chittuy*</note> is like the River of Fire <note>original: *Nehar di-Nur*</note>. And "Cleanser" for those who return is in *Asiyah*, for "he shall not be cleansed" who touches her if they do not repent. **And the Sage** explained that the thirteen attributes are twelve "Beings" (*Havayot*) joining from the name *BaN* <note>A Divine Name with the numerical value of 52</note>, and the "Repair" <note>Tikkun</note> that includes and brings them out is hidden in *Keter* and spreads through *Binah*, *Tiferet*, and *Malchut*, as will be further explained. Others explained "The Lord, The Lord, God" as *Keter*, *Tiferet*, and *Yesod*, with ten titles/branches spreading from each of them... there are much deeper and more numerous systems in all this. However, what we have mentioned here will suffice for our purpose.

He is not "one" like a counted number, for He undergoes no change, variation, description, or multiplicity. Rather, He, may He be blessed, is simple and absolute, beyond every measure, description, and boundary. Yet He also supervises, rewards, and punishes. What did His wisdom decree to emanate the Sefirot, which were received from Sinai, after they were revealed to our holy forefathers...

From there, the limit is considered, for the place of the North is hidden, and from there it surrounds to the South. And if so, this will burst forth with the rescue of all corners of the land... against the right side. And the explanation is: "Mercy" is literally from below to above as explained. When it is chosen, it necessarily has a beginning, a middle, and an end. For if they had no end among the created things, they would go on without end. Since there is a limit and an end, there must be a "Head," for one cannot exist without the other. All these have a head, an end, and a middle. Because of these three, each of these directions is included in three, totaling nine, and they are the prepared place, making ten, etc. The intention is not the literal head and end of the physical spheres, for even a sphere has a house... the difference between the Cause and the caused.

The author of *Menuchat Yehudah* wrote another reason, writing that the life-force that spreads and includes all is the "Living One," and so forth.

Rabbi Shimon said: "O Lord my God, many are Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us." Rabbi Shimon gave three crowns: those designated for the Princes, for the High Priest, and for the King. To elevate the awe of them, we required—in the guidance of the Chosen Nation—a Deputy, a Second-in-Command, and a Head of the Court. Beneath them are three "flocks of sheep," the hosts of Israel: the priestly watches who are "lovers of peace and pursuers of peace," the military officers who rule the people, and the Sanhedrin <term>The high court of ancient Israel</term> who sit on the thrones of judgment. All of their eyes and hearts are toward the "Crown of a Good Name," the congregation of Jacob, the "Mother of them all." This is a sufficient and true reason, without a doubt.

### Chapter 2: The Tanna <note>A sage from the era of the Mishnah.</note> 
mentions this incidentally regarding the Creation of the World and the Giving of the Torah. Because of this, he teaches "Ten Sefirot." But there are many Hallelujahs! He refers to those where it is written: "Praise Him with the blast of the Shofar." Which are they? The instances of "And He said" in Genesis. But there are only nine! "In the beginning" (Bereshit) is also considered an Utterance, as it is written: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made." 

The simple meaning of the discussion proves that "Be fruitful and multiply" is not part of the count, because it is a commandment placed upon us, and a blessing for those who keep it and engage in it for its own sake; but here we are dealing with the Creation of the World, and this is clear. **However**, in the portion of *Vayikra*, Rabbi Shimon explained "ten, ten the spoon" <note>Numbers 7:14.</note>: ten for the work of Creation, and ten for the Giving of the Torah.

And if you should say: if we do not count Knowledge in the tally because it is the connector and is included within Wisdom and Understanding, then we should likewise not count Foundation <term>Yesod; the ninth Sefirah, which acts as a funnel for divine energy</term> in the tally, as it also serves as the connector for Beauty <term>Tiferet; the central Sefirah of harmony</term> and Sovereignty <term>Malchut; the final Sefirah, the manifest world</term>. And it is still difficult: why, in truth, did you see fit to remove Knowledge from the tally and yet count Foundation? To this, it answers: "Understand with Wisdom and be wise with Understanding." The explanation is: "Understand" (Binah) is within "Wisdom" (Chokhmah) because it is included in its potential; "Wise" (Chokhmah) is within "Understanding" (Binah) because it is included in it. For they are always included in one another, because they are "friends that never separate." Therefore, Knowledge is always "in concealment" <note>Hebrew: "itkassia"</note>. We cannot count it due to the hiddenness of its light, as it is written: "In that which is hidden from you, do not seek." This is not the case for Foundation, which connects Beauty and Sovereignty, which are called "beloveds" <note>Hebrew: "dodim"</note>; their union is not constant. For this reason, the text concludes: "Examine them and investigate them, and establish the matter clearly." And this is enough for the wise.

-># Gate Two: The Reason for Emanation<-

<margin>The reason for the emanations being ten. Called "Hidden." *Minchat Yehudah* <note>A commentary on the *Sefer Yetzirah*</note> wrote in the name of Rabbi Azriel <note>Azriel of Gerona, a seminal 13th-century Kabbalist</note>:</margin>

And it may be said that the reason is for everything to be a single point, like three axes <note>Original: "qutrin," diameters or dimensions</note>: length, width, and depth. In union and in action, this gives the "judge" and the number of the four... the aforementioned names... and with the encompassing space that contains them, it becomes ten. The intention is that although the Divine Words—heaven forbid—possess no body or form, nonetheless, we describe them through the metaphor of the body and form. Just as the masters of Kabbalah maintained that there are four elements hinted at in the Sefirot <note>Wisdom, Understanding, Beauty, and Sovereignty</note>, even though they are the root of the elements... and the elements are drawn from them, so too the matter is "enlarged" into a body. For heaven forbid that there should be an actual body above (nor that the categories of the body should be added), but rather because the body was created from them, and they are its root... as a description by way of metaphor for the categories of the body. Therefore, it requires "length, width, and depth" above—the intention being the Power through which length is made, the Power through which width is made, and the Power through which depth is made. And so these three powers perform three actions... a metaphor of nine, and as a parallel to the metaphor of the body... before all of them, the "tenth power" rises, which is the ten powers that are the ten Sefirot.

**Annotation:** Wisdom, Understanding, Beauty, and Sovereignty are the roots of the elements. Strength (Gevurah) is the root of Fire. Mercy (Hesed) is the root of Water. Beauty (Tiferet) is the root of Air. Sovereignty (Malchut) is the root of Earth. And in the end... between the "Chariot" and the elements... it seems to me that the order of the elements is from below to above... each one turns to its right... West, South, East, North... Mercy, Beauty, and Strength. And the decider is always in the middle. The "waters which are above the heavens" correspond to Mercy. The "waters beneath"... correspond to all of them which draw from Mercy. And so the foundational fire corresponds to Strength, and the fire of the firmaments... and the "firmament divides" is Beauty. And it says "in the midst of the waters" and did not mention fire, as it leans toward Mercy. Furthermore, it is sufficient that the name *Elohim* <note>The Divine name associated with Judgment/Strength</note> is mentioned 32 times regarding Strength... and its number is 32. (Explanation: that the elements are three according to the order... from which come water... and this is not according to the order of the elements which are Earth, Water, Air, Fire... for in the nature of the simple elements it is not so... but the elements are high above according to the order of their creation, as it was in the creation of man: first water, then earth, and afterward He breathed into him life... and He brought the spirit into him...)

### Chapter 1: Clarification

**Chapter 1** The commentators wrote that every point arrives with three dimensions: length, width, and depth. When these interpenetrate, they become nine, and the space that sustains their existence is the tenth. Therefore, the Sefirot were ten. The intention is that we were permitted to compare the Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah</term> to a point and its expansions, as related to the "ends of the earth" in the *Sefer Yetzirah*. The point is not truly physical; it is not divided, but rather unified in its powers. Your sign is the word *Yad* <note>Hebrew for "Hand," with a numerical value of 14</note> in its full spelling: point, line, and surface. When they are folded upon each other, "a house is built" through the tenth power that brings the body into actuality. Their use of the word "axes" rather than "lines" hints that the point pierces and spreads through the inner depths of the levels, not merely on their surface.

And they said that the point of Emanation has a beginning, a middle, and an end. For the "end" is the edge of the intended limit, and whatever is limited at its end is limited at its beginning, and between them is a middle state. In their total inclusion of one another, they shall be "perfectly joined" to the sustaining space, as mentioned. All of this is a parable and metaphor to recognize the superiority of the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), who is truly without end, over the emanated beings, despite their great value. For they are the cause of limitation through the divisions of aspects and their distinctions from Cause to Effect.

There are those who synthesized the abstraction of the "point" and its dimensions with the "end, middle, and beginning" to reach ten aspects. This was because it was difficult for him to understand why the manifestations of the point would be doubled—why one parable of the point would not suffice. If we are to double it, who is to say two times is enough? He thought to escape this doubling by changing the names as mentioned. But he struggled in vain; since the point is indivisible, it cannot be imagined that part of it expands to one dimension and part to another, but rather the whole point to every dimension. Thus, the total power is hidden within them in three distances to be multiplied once more. The dimensions, however, are divided, and therefore the expansion stops at the edge of the limit.

**Furthermore**, the commentators wrote that since the Emanation enters into number, it is required to have the "all-encompassing number," which is ten. In all these matters, there is no "speeding" <note>i.e., no logical contradiction</note> where the later would be the cause of the former. However, it never entered the minds of the perfected ones to believe in all we have said except as proofs and evidence to support the awakening of the intellect alongside the accepted Kabbalah. They said that one should not seek a reason for the Divine Will; for if so, we would be like Saul <note>likely referring to King Saul or a general "inquirer"</note> asking if there is a cause above that motivates His action. Even if we say there is a reason...

# Pital of the Pomegranate: Gate 2 on the Reason for Emanation, Essence of Pomegranates
<note>The title *Pelah HaRimon* (Slice/Pital of the Pomegranate) refers to a commentary on the *Pardes Rimonim* (Orchard of Pomegranates) by Moses Cordovero, a foundational work of 16th-century Kabbalah.</note>

## 2 2 / 2 2
<meta>catchword: And he explained</meta>

Behold, in any case, that logic <note>original: "ta'am" — literally "taste," but used here as "reason" or "logic"</note> is not something that can be tasted or felt by anyone else, for His knowledge is His very essence. From this, it follows that we cannot grasp anything of Him, for the Unique One is not divided; anyone who could grasp a part of Him would grasp the whole, and both of these are impossible. Rather, we have a tradition regarding the existence of the Blessed One, and our grasping and contemplation occur not within the One, but within the intermediary levels <note>The Sefirot</note>, which indeed differ in degree and intensity. **Truth and Faith**: the significance of number is great and well-suited to illustrate Emanation <note>original: "Atzilut"</term>, as it is measured by ten levels. For the wheel of number runs upon ten, and its cycle is **from a thousand thousands** <note>A reference to the infinite potential within the decimal system</note>; this is a wonder within the secret of Unity, multiplying beyond investigation. Emanation is also examined through three "knots": Lovingkindness, Judgment, and Mercy <term>Chesed, Din, and Rachamim; the three primary emotional branches of the divine attributes</term>. Each of these has a beginning, a middle, and an end: 
- Wisdom, Greatness, and Victory <note>Chokhmah, Gedulah/Chesed, and Netzach</note>
- Understanding, Power, and Splendor <note>Binah, Gevurah, and Hod</note>
- Beauty, Foundation, and Sovereignty <note>Tiferet, Yesod, and Malchut</note>
- And the Crown <note>Keter</note> encompasses them all. 

There are those who have written that the first three are intellectual faculties rather than moral attributes <term>Middot</term>. Indeed, Lovingkindness whitens sins, while Fear <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note> punishes the wicked. Beauty is the "attribute of the day," a judge and arbiter who pays back His enemies in kind. Victory <note>Netzach</note> was necessary to conquer the Accuser, and Splendor <note>Hod</note> to give thanks to God, who provides the strength to silence the enemy. Foundation and Sovereignty are male and female; the latter is the "attribute of the night." Aside from the specific objections one might raise—such as the fact that we have never heard of a specific attribute being required just to "give thanks" or to "conquer the evil inclination"—this entire line of reasoning does not truly satisfy the logic of Emanation.

**However**, what seems most plausible to us regarding the logic of this number is that which many have already merited to understand regarding the divine conduct. This is found in the short introductions of the Sage <note>likely referring to Maimonides or Cordovero</note> in the second introduction: that the "thought of Israel" preceded everything. This is the logic behind "Many are the wonders You have done, O Lord my God, and Your thoughts toward us." Rabbi Shimon taught: There are three crowns specifically for the Prince, the High Priest, and the King. Because of the exalted nature of their awe, we required—in the administration of the Chosen Nation—a Deputy, a Second-in-Command, and a Chief of the Court. Beneath them are three flocks of sheep, the hosts of Israel: the priestly watches (who are lovers of peace and pursuers of peace), the army officers who go down among the people, and the Sanhedrin <term>The supreme judicial council of ancient Israel</term> who sit on the thrones of judgment. All of them have their eyes and hearts set toward the "Crown of a Good Name," the congregations of Jacob, their great mother. This is a sufficient and undoubtedly true explanation.

### Chapter 2: It was taught

This refers to the creation of the world and how the Torah hints at it. For this reason, it teaches "Ten Sefirot." We learn in the Talmud, in the nineteenth chapter of Rosh Hashanah: To what do these ten "Kingships" correspond? Rabbi said: To the ten praises that David uttered in the Book of Psalms. There are many praises there, but these specifically use the phrase "Praise Him with the blast of the Shofar." Rabbi Yosef said: They correspond to the Ten Commandments given to Moses at Sinai. Rabbi Yochanan said: They correspond to the Ten Utterances <term>Ma'amarot</term> by which the world was created. Which are they? The word "And He said" <note>original: "Va-yomer"</note> appears nine times in Genesis, and the word "In the beginning" <note>Bereishit</note> is also considered an utterance, as it is written: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made." The plain meaning of our discussion proves that this is not merely a matter of a large number, but because it is a commandment placed upon us and a blessing to those who observe it and engage in it for its own sake. We are dealing here with the creation of the world, and it is clear. **Indeed**, in the portion of Vayikra, Rabbi Shimon explained: "Ten, ten is the spoon"—ten for the work of creation and ten for the giving of the Torah.

# Essence of Pomegranates, Gate 2: The Reason for Emanation — Slice of the Pomegranate
<note>The title *Asis Rimmonim* (Essence of Pomegranates) is a summary of Moses Cordovero’s massive 16th-century kabbalistic encyclopedia, *Pardes Rimonim* (Orchard of Pomegranates). A "Slice" (*Pelah*) refers to a specific sub-section.</note>

...they will fill. And it <note>Referring to *Da'at* (Knowledge)</note> acts as the connector for Wisdom and Understanding and is not a Sefirah <term>Sefirah: One of the ten divine attributes or channels through which the Infinite manifests</term> in its own right. And if you should ask: if we do not count Knowledge in the total because it is the connector and is included within Wisdom and Understanding, then we should likewise not count Foundation (*Yesod*) in the total, for it too is the connector for Harmony (*Tiferet*) and Kingdom (*Malkhut*), and "the body and the sign of the covenant are considered as one"? <note>This is a classic Kabbalistic problem: if *Da'at* (the bridge between the upper intellects) isn't counted as one of the ten, why is *Yesod* (the bridge between the lower emotions and the feminine) counted? The quote "body and covenant are one" refers to the anatomical/spiritual link between the torso and the reproductive organ.</note> To this, the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The "Book of Formation," the oldest known book of Jewish mysticism</note> says: "Ten and not nine." For if we did not count Foundation in the total, there would be only nine. And if it is difficult for you to accept counting Foundation even though it is a connector—and you think we should then count Knowledge as well—to this it says: "Ten and not eleven." For when we also count Knowledge in the total, there are eleven. We must strictly preserve the count of ten. Yet it remains difficult: why, in truth, did you see fit to remove Knowledge from the count and include Foundation? To this, it answers: "Understand with Wisdom and be Wise with Understanding." This means: *Understand* <note>original: *Havin* — related to *Binah*</note> with the Wisdom that is included within it, and *be Wise* <note>original: *Hakham* — related to *Chokhmah*</note> with the Understanding that is included within it. For they are forever included in one another because they are "friends that never part." Therefore, Knowledge is always "in concealment," and we cannot count it due to the hiddenness of its light—"Seek not what is too wondrous for you." This is not the case for Foundation, which joins Harmony and Kingdom, who are called "lovers" <note>original: "Dodim"</note> whose union is not constant. Regarding these, it concludes: "Examine them and investigate from them, and establish the matter clearly." And this is enough for the wise.

->**The Second Gate: The Reason for Emanation**<-

## Chapter 1: An Explanation
<margin>The reason for the Sefirot being ten: The author of *Minchat Yehuda* wrote in the name of Rabbi Ezriel <note>Ezriel of Gerona, a 13th-century Kabbalist</note></margin>
Ten <gloss>10</gloss> is the reason because everything began as a single point, comprising three dimensions: length, width, and depth, existing within one another. Just as in the way of a cubed number: 9 aspects <note>3x3</note>, and with the containing space itself, they are 10. The intention is that the ten Sefirot in their beginning were like "body and souls"—so far his words. They are like the extension of body and souls. The Kabbalists aimed to show how the four elements <note>Fire, Air, Water, Earth</note> are hinted at in the Sefirot of *Netzach, Hod, Tiferet, and Yesod*. This is because these are the "primary elements," the roots of the physical elements, which are drawn from them. This follows the order of the "Body" <note>The Sefirotic structure is often mapped onto a divine human form</note>, for it is not that there is a physical body Above (nor should one apply physical definitions to the Sefirot), but rather, since the physical body is built from them and they are its root, they are included in three "dimensions" <note>original: *Ma'aliyot* — elevations or dimensions</note> beyond physical limits. Therefore, we may precisely apply "length, width, and depth" to the realms Above, meaning: the power by which length is made, the power by which width is made, and the power by which depth is made. Since each of these three powers performs three other actions, there are nine "dimensions," and the interiority of the "Body"—which defines its totality—is the tenth name, as mentioned above regarding the ten intentions of the Sefirotic emanations.

### Annotation
*Netzach, Tiferet, Yesod,* and *Ananer* <unclear>possibly *Anan* or a variant of *Hod*</unclear> are the roots of the four elements. In creating the four lights: Earth is *Malkhut*. The relationship between the vessels and the elements... it appears to me that the order of the elements is from below to above. In any case, the "cornerstone" corresponds to the East, South-East, and North, surrounding the *Malkhut*, and from there *Tiferet* and *Gevurah*. The "Deciding Factor" is always in the middle. The "waters which are above the heavens" correspond to *Chesed* (Lovingkindness). The "waters which are beneath the earth" reflect *Chesed*. Likewise, the primordial Fire corresponds to *Gevurah* (Might), and the "fire of blood" and the firmament correspond to *Tiferet*. It is said: "in the midst of the water" twice; the name *Elohim* <note>The divine name associated with Judgment</note> is in *Gevurah*... (Meaning: the elements follow the general paths of the Sefirot: water, fire, light, earth. The order of elements is: earth, water, light, fire. For in the nature of simple elements we find: the smallest sphere is the element of Earth, followed by the sphere of Water, then Air, then Fire. The two [higher] elements are higher and higher in the order of their creation, just as in the creation of man: first flesh from earth, then [the souls] entered within...)
<meta>catchword: element</meta>

<column-break/>

## Chapter 1: [Continued] They Wrote
The commentators wrote that every point exists in three dimensions: length, width, and depth. When these are multiplied into each other, they become nine, and the space that sustains their existence is the tenth. Therefore, the Sefirot were ten. The intention is that we have inherited the level of Emanation as a "point" and its expansions, just as the "ends of the earth" are attributed in the *Book of Formation*. The point is not truly physical; it is not divided, but rather unified in its powers. Your sign for this is the letter *Yud* <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing a point</note>: when spelled out (*Yud-Vav-Dalet*), it represents the point and its expansion. When folded upon itself, a "house" is built by a tenth power that brings the "body" into actuality. They said "dimensions" (*ketarim*) rather than "lines" to hint that the point pierces and spreads through the inner depths of the levels, not just on their surfaces. They said that the points of Emanation have a "Beginning, Middle, and End," for the "End" is the intended limit, and whatever is limited at its end is limited at its beginning, with an intermediate state between them. Through their inclusion in one another, they become a complete whole within the "Sustaining Space" mentioned before. All of this is parable and metaphor to help us recognize the superiority of the *Ein Sof* (The Infinite), who is truly without end, over the Emanations—despite their great value—for the Sefirot are the cause of limitation, dividing the levels and distinguishing between the Cause and the Effect. There are those who mapped the expansion of the Point into its dimensions onto the "End, Middle, and Beginning" to reach ten aspects. This was because he found it difficult to explain why the limits of the point should be doubled, asking: Why is one metaphor of the point not enough? If we double it, what forces us to stop at two? He thought to escape this doubling: the point does not divide; one cannot imagine that part of it spreads to one dimension and part to another, but rather the *whole* of it to *every* dimension. Thus, the collective power is found in all three distances, multiplying once more. The dimensions, however, do divide, and thus the expansion stops at the boundary's edge.

## Furthermore
The commentators wrote that because Emanation (*Atzilut*) enters into the category of number, it must take the "universal number," which is ten. Yet in all these explanations, none are free from "strangeness"—for how can the later effect be the cause of the preceding? However, it never entered the minds of these perfect sages to believe literally in what we have said; rather, these are logical proofs to support the awakening of the intellect alongside the accepted Tradition <note>original: *Kabbalah*</note>. They said: one should not seek a reason for the Divine Will. For if so, we would be like one who asks if there is a cause above the Creator that motivates His actions. Even if we were to say there is a reason...

# Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 2: The Reason for Emanation — Essence of Pomegranates

<page-num>1a</page-num>

**Lebanon** refers to the trees of planting that the Holy One, Blessed be He, uprooted and planted in another place, and these trees are called the **Cedars of Lebanon**, as it is said: "The cedars of Lebanon which He has planted." This **palanquin** <note>original: "Appiryon" (Song of Songs 3:9). In Kabbalah, this refers to the structure of the lower worlds or the Sefirah of Kingdom being built by the higher lights.</note> was not built or perfected except through them, the "findings of Lebanon." These are the **six days of Creation**, for day by day, He arranged within this palanquin the order that was befitting to it. They explained three aspects regarding these six extremities <term>Six Extremities: The Sefirot from Kindness (Chesed) to Foundation (Yesod), corresponding to the six directions of the physical world</term>. First, an aspect like the **horns of grasshoppers**, where they were called the "Cedars of Lebanon" in a hidden state of existence. This word is derived from the language of "song" (*ron*), and its grammatical weight is like "the streams." Regarding these, it says "and the Lebanon shall grow great," and the Midrash *Genesis Rabbah* expounds: "The trees of the Lord are satisfied"—meaning they are satisfied with their lives. Second, the "Trees of Lebanon" refer to those trees that were uprooted from Lebanon and are now **planted in the House of the Lord**, which is the secret of the six extremities in their proper place. There they are truly called "Trees of the Lord." This word is derived from the language of "pride" (*ga’on*), which implies the planting itself. Regarding this, they said "they are satisfied with their waters," meaning the waters drawn to them from the River <note>The "River" usually refers to the Sefirah of Understanding (Binah), the source of the divine flow.</note>. Third, regarding the palanquin in its being built, it is said "they are satisfied from their hour," and of this it is said: "they shall flourish in the courts of our God." Rabbi Hanina said: "The world was not worthy to make use of cedars; why then were they created? For the sake of the **Temple**." And it is written: "And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone finished at the quarry," for the palanquin is called the secret of the **finished stone**, which is the number fourteen <note>The Hebrew word for "Hand" (Yad) has a numerical value of 14, often symbolizing the power of the Sefirot before they branch out.</note> before the branches spread out. 

**Furthermore**, we can explain the word "palanquin" (*Appiryon*) as "let the palanquin reach us," as the sages said: "My world, my world! Would that you find grace before me." They gave a parable: To what is this like? To a king who was marrying off his daughter and made her a wedding canopy (*Chuppah*) and arranged it for her. He said to her: "My daughter, would that this canopy finds grace before me at all times, just as it finds grace before me at this hour."

### Chapter 4: And Why 

Because the **first three** attributes were hidden, their actions were drawn forth through the **three Patriarchs** <note>In Kabbalah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob embody the Sefirot of Kindness, Might, and Harmony.</note>. "Let there be light" comes from the **Crown** (*Keter*) by way of **Kindness** (*Chesed*). From **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*) is drawn "Let there be a firmament" by way of **Might** (*Gevurah*). From **Understanding** (*Binah*) is drawn "Let the waters be gathered" by way of **Harmony** (*Tiferet*). This is what was intended in the passage from the *Tikunim* <note>Referring to the *Tikunei Zohar*, a classic Kabbalistic text.</note> that we transcribed above. Likewise, "and she shall go out" from that palanquin we mentioned in the previous chapter. There they further explained that "Let the earth sprout" was subsequently drawn from Kindness by way of Harmony on its day. From Might was drawn "Let there be lights" through Harmony, and it was handed over to **Victory** (*Netzach*), which is the fourth day, to bring it into action; however, they did not shine until the fifth day when the waters swarmed—this was the statement of Harmony by way of **Splendor** (*Hod*). When the statement of Mercy was completed, the statement of Judgment was finished, whose pride is the creatures [created] for its light. They were also assisted by it in their creation, for thus the natural processes were completed, as the living begets the living and the sun. And from Victory, Splendor, and **Foundation** (*Yesod*), [life] was drawn through Foundation on the sixth day: "Let the earth bring forth," "Let us make man," and "Behold I have given." From this it is explained that "Kindness and Favor" is not among the [Ten] Statements, but is a blessing mentioned on the sixth day so that it would be completed on the seventh, by the power of the statement "I will make him a helper," as a canopy over all honor, to leave a blessing in His house. 

**And in the *Tikunim*** they said: "In the beginning (*Bereshit*), in the beginning"—this is the **sixth day**, of which it is said: "And it was evening and it was morning, the sixth day." Here there are three craftsmen: one craftsman brings out lights on the fourth day, which were suspended on the [first] day...

<column-break/>

...and there will be **ten kingships**, for "Kingdom" (*Malkhut*) is included in the Sefirah and its count. (Our female) <note>Likely a reference to the Shekhinah, the feminine divine presence.</note> is appointed with the "kiss" of the water (*Mayim*) in the twenty, and it is said: "He is holy in His holiness" (Crown/Keter)... and eight in the firmament (Wisdom/Chokhmah)... in His might He brings forth those who wake and shall shut in the greatness of His cycle (Greatness/Kindness)... with the sounding of the Shofar (Might/Gevurah), the power is removed and the Shofar of atonement is merited... and the "Kinnor" <note>A biblical lyre or harp.</note> of Harmony (*Tiferet*) has **twenty types of melody** corresponding to the twenty movements within it, including eight simple rests... the tablets of Wisdom, which is called a "collection"... and the two simple rests... the first being called "hot and day," as explained above... inside and from the voice of those who are liable and the voice of punishment, and for every search there is a place. There are twenty types of melody to allow for each one of them **seven aspects**: the aspect of the days, the aspect of the miracles... and for the secret of the "Teruah" blast and for the completions... and this is according to the three witnesses of the three rests... a matter shall be established. There are ten rests... a general rule and a punctuation.

**Chapter 6: And also** 
The cantor begins to say "He who pardons" on weekdays... ten... and more simple... because the intention of "He who pardons" is to cause the Cedars of Lebanon to be forgotten... (meaning that "He who pardons" is found in every place, and the intention of "He who pardons" is in the world to come, and therefore they are there to be lost). And this secret explains the voices on the Festivals, that the generalities and levels shall be profaned, and they begin one level after another... to be separated and to return and to be refined... until there is a leaf... and in a night it perished. And now, how can one say a word to remember why it is thus and not thus? It is a pleasant melody in His wisdom... to establish the purpose of existence and destruction. For if the number of those included were ten, for if they were fewer than ten, they would be drawn toward destruction until there was no trouble in their destruction. And the reason they are included in the purpose and the end is so that the lower beings... if they were purposeful, there would be a lack in the world forever, and he would not receive punishment for his sins... and the legislation spreads in the world and the corruption would not be mended. And the righteous were like infants in the World to Come, and they would not see the good. And everything in the world was created for a purpose... as it is said, "Everything [God made] for His sake." For it could be shown that each one is made of ten, but rather to publicize and to give a good reward to the righteous on the day... as our Sages of blessed memory said in the Tractate *Avot*: "That by their being destroyed..." etc. It is not that the emanations have a limit and an end, but that the actions drawn from them act as purposeful actions in those that compose the world, because they [the worldly things] have an end. And thus the righteous sustain it (the world)... and if not for them, it would be destroyed. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, and furthermore the Master of the Universe, who is Mercy, the statement of Judgment was finished, and there was a need for many... to increase the creatures from it, they were assisted both for Judgment and for Mercy, to specify and to give reward for all... 

**However**, it is difficult regarding this reason, for if so, after the Resurrection—which is the essence of the world—the sinners will be removed from the earth. What then is the reason for the [existence of] "Other Sides" <note>original: "Sitra Achra," the demonic or impure realms in Kabbalah.</note> and the "Shells" (*Kelipot*)? This relates to the holy Halls (*Heikhalot*) that lead a person according to his deeds, as will be explained in the Gate of the Halls. And in the time of Rectification (*Tikun*), when there is no mention of punishment or the removal of all humans, it [the Shells] will be naked... and it is possible to say they will be brought to memory, and in the final times there will be no judgment or acquisition... and they are many in the abundance of peace...

# Essence of Pomegranates, Gate 2: The Logic of Emanation — Slice of the Pomegranate

And he explained: "I am [the Lord]" <note>The first of the Ten Commandments.</note> corresponds to "Let there be light" <note>The first saying of Creation.</note>. "You shall not have [other gods]" corresponds to "Let there be a firmament." "You shall not take [the name in vain]" corresponds to "Let [the waters] be gathered." "Remember [the Sabbath]" corresponds to "Let the earth sprout." "Honor [your father]" corresponds to "Let there be lights [in the sky]." "You shall not murder" corresponds to "Let [the waters] swarm." "You shall not commit adultery" corresponds to "Let the earth bring forth." "You shall not steal" corresponds to "Behold, I have given [you every herb]." "You shall not bear false witness" corresponds to "Let us make man." "You shall not covet" corresponds to "I will make him a helper against him." According to this arrangement, "In the beginning" <note>Hebrew: *Bereshit*</note> is not part of the count of the ten sayings, and the saying that completes the ten is the "helper" <note>Genesis 2:18</note>, even though it appears much later in the Torah portion. However, in the *Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkuney Zohar*, a classic Kabbalistic text.</note>, there is another way: they count "Be fruitful and multiply" among the crafts of the sixth day along with the other sayings, making ten without needing to include "In the beginning" or the "helper."

**And it is stated** there: Just as Abraham, who is the Right <term>Right side: The attribute of Kindness (Chesed)</term>, is the first day, and within him are included and suspended the 248 positive commandments; so too with Isaac, who is like the second day, in him are suspended the 365 negative commandments. The phrase "like the second day" regarding Isaac is understood from what was explained in the *Sefer HaBahir* <note>The Book of Brilliance, an early Kabbalistic work.</note> that Kindness is the attribute of Abraham, distinguished by its source, but not so the "Fear of Isaac" <note>Isaac represents Gevurah (Judgment/Strength/Fear).</note>. This will be discussed further with God's help. The third day includes everything; from it are suspended both positive and negative commandments "like grapes on a cluster." Regarding "In the beginning," some say Jacob is "a simple man" <note>Genesis 25:27</note> and this is the third day, for there were three times until here: the first day, the second day, and the third day. Each one brought forth its craft. The first day [represented by the letters] A-L-H <note>Elohim</note> is a wondrous and hidden craftsman. # Essence of Pomegranates, Gate 2: The Logic of Emanation — Slice of the Pomegranate

On the first day, of which it is said "Light," a second craftsman brought forth swarming creatures from the waters; this is what is written: *Let the waters swarm.* This was dependent on the second day, of which it is said "Water," as it is written: *Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters.* Here there is water, and there there is water. A third craftsman brought forth grasses and seeds corresponding to the third day, as it is said: *Let the earth sprout vegetation.* And it is said on the sixth day: *Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.* That which was dry land on the third day became, through its fathering, the sixth day—which is the Foundation <term>Yesod: The ninth Sefirah, acting as a funnel for all divine energy into the world</term>, which includes both right and left, like the letter *Tav*. 

Even though each of the first craftsmen brought forth their craft into the world, Rabbi Eleazar explains in the section on *Bereishit* <note>Genesis</note> that these were hidden and not revealed. It was the "fourth leg of the Throne," which is included in the third day to be one without separation, that revealed them. Afterward, three crafts spread out from the Building through the attribute of Beauty <term>Tiferet: The central Sefirah representing balance and harmony</term>: "Let it sprout" (similar to the dry land); "Lights" (similar to "Let there be light"); and "Let them swarm" (similar to the firmament). Even the sixth day is thus, for the latter days—Lights, Swarming, and Blessing—depend on the fourth leg, which is the Sabbath that is included in the sixth day. This was prepared for it as a "beautiful thing," as mentioned in the secret of the sixth from that "Palanquin above" in the section on *Terumah*. From it, three crafts also spread out: "Let the earth bring forth" (similar to "Let them swarm"), "Living soul" (and "Living soul"), "Let us make man" (similar to the sun and moon, small and great, male and female), and "Behold, I have given" (similar to "Let it sprout"). From this, the blessing is drawn, as we mentioned above regarding the statement "Be fruitful and multiply," which is the craft intended for itself. 

As for why those two Sages of the Tractate *Rosh Hashanah* and the section of *Vayikra* omitted it, it seems the reason is that the fulfillment of the statement depends on another. Therefore, it was said, *God said to them*, unlike *Behold, I have given*, where He alone is the giver. This is true of all other utterances, for *He commanded and they were created*. However, according to the system of the *Tikkunim* <note>Tikkuney Zohar</note>, it is correct to count "Be fruitful and multiply" among the Ten Utterances. With this, the "crafts" are established alongside the Ten Utterances, for the statement "It is not good [for man to be alone]" is not a craft in itself, since it is written afterward, *I will make him a helper*, and it appears as an exceptional case in the text and is not mentioned among the six days. However, the generations that follow from it are indeed the intended "craft."

### Chapter 5 Explained
From this, it is clear that the questioner's intent was this: their statement that "By ten utterances the world was created" implies that it refers to the tools of His craft. The craft of the Kingdom <term>Malchut: The final Sefirah, representing the physical world and God's sovereignty</term> is derived from the Foundation in the ninth utterance, which is "Behold, I have given." They answered him well that "In the beginning" (*Bereishit*) is also an utterance, in which the existence of the Crown <term>Keter: The highest Sefirah, Divine Will</term>—which includes all of Emanation—is hidden. In most of the utterances, the inclusion of the "ten" is also clear. From the Crown is drawn "Let there be light," which is the emanation of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>, as we have mentioned. 

**In the Sefer Ha-Bahir**, Rabbi Bun said: What is the meaning of the verse *I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was*? What is "from everlasting" (*me-olam*)? It refers to a matter that must be hidden (*le-ha'alim*) from the whole world (*olam*), as it is written: *He has also set the world [olam] in their heart*. Do not read it as "the world" (*olam*), but as "hiddenness" (*he'elem*). The Torah said: I preceded to be the head of the world, as it says, *I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning*. And do not say perhaps the earth preceded it, for it says, *before the earth was*, as we say: *In the beginning God created*. And what did He create? The needs of everything, and afterward, "God" <note>Elohim</note>...

<column-break/>

<margin>(To mention and to punish... to judge man according to his deeds)</margin>
The Palaces <note>Heikhalot</note> (in the minority of the Zohar 52), meaning that the essence of Emanation was not initially for this purpose <margin>(Reward and punishment... was not the only purpose)</margin> but rather to reveal and make known His parts. The revelation of these parts is more appropriate after the world has descended from its [original] voice... as it is written: *And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; in that day the Lord shall be one, etc.* For through the connection and foundation of the Sefirot, His secret will be revealed, as well as the taste of knowledge and blessing, as it is written: *And they shall teach no more every man his neighbor... for they shall all know Me, etc.* 

**Furthermore**, there is another reason, which is that He, blessed be He, desired to distinguish Himself and to do good for those included in Him, and to be a head to do good to the created beings... to show and reveal the eyes of the created beings to His greatness, so that He might be recognizable and known in His unity through His actions. This is what is meant by "His goodness was to His desire to reveal His loftiness to the lowly." Since the revelation of His loftiness to the created beings—from the height of His loftiness in His hiddenness—would still not be possible for the created beings to grasp, it proceeds to Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), and from Wisdom to Understanding (*Binah*), and down to the Kingdom (*Malchut*), for that is where the grasp of the King's loftiness resides. 

**A parable** for this: A person enters a house through a long hallway, and the sun shines through the window. No person in the house can look directly at the sun's light because it is too powerful for the darkness. While the sun is at its greatest, it is [too] clear and will strike their faces. When they sit in the house, they benefit from the light and are not harmed by its clarity and strength. But if the light were hidden and concealed, the inhabitants of the house would still need additional lamps to see. Now, when the light comes into the house to benefit them from the light that shines through the windows, it is called a "benefit." These windows are like curtains before his eyes. In this light, the window is an opening... (His intent is to fix the matter of the light so it won't strike the eyes of the observers; even if the windows are reduced, he will still draw out the essence of the light through its revelation). He will draw out the light and not withhold it from those who see. The light is drawn through the windows. The intention is not [to block], but to fix the light so they can enjoy it as much as possible, and it won't be harmful in its intensity, but rather a clear light, a sweet light, a covered light.

### Chapter 7 Furthermore
There is another reason to be said, and to understand the matter, one must know that because the Sefirot are subtle and of simple spirituality, separate from body and soul, and are prepared so they do not divide into parts in any way... <margin>(From the occurrences, may He be blessed)</margin> but rather... and the matter was not because of the pride of their power, but for the perfection of those who are supported and included, Heaven forbid. Rather, for the sake of the created beings... they needed to descend to the openness of the "body" that thinks [in parts]. This is the matter: they mention His greatness and His power... the perfection is for the lowly... and one should not say that the guidance is added...

# Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 2: The Logic of Emanation — Essence of Pomegranates

And what is written after it? *The heavens and the earth* <note>Genesis 1:1</note> etc. And behold, the existence of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: The second Sefirah, representing the flash of intuition</term> was included in the Palanquin <note>Hebrew: *Apiryon*, a term for the structure of the lower Sefirot</note> through the attribute of Kindness <term>Chesed</term> by the command of the Crown <term>Keter: The highest Sefirah, representing the Divine Will</term>, and so all of them, as previously stated. **However**, the essence of the aforementioned question—regarding the ten "Kingships" <term>Malchuyot: The section of the Rosh Hashanah prayer emphasizing God's sovereignty</term>—is to know what these generalities point toward within the Sefirah of Sovereignty <term>Malchut: The final Sefirah, through which the divine light enters our world</term>. Rabbi <note>Judah the Prince, the 2nd-century redactor of the Mishnah</note>, who was the leader of his generation, replied that they correspond to the ten internal levels of *Malchut* itself. It was toward these that the mighty King, the "Sweet Singer of Israel" <note>King David</note>, aimed in the ten "Hallelujahs" <note>The final five chapters of Psalms, which contain ten mentions of "Hallelujah" in the Hebrew liturgy</note>, the rectifications of *Malchut* in the order she sings her beauty at the conclusion of the Book <note>The Book of Psalms</note>. For there they were gathered, five "Hallelujahs" corresponding to five, in the mystery of the "Full Hallel" <note>The special prayer of praise said on festivals</note> which transforms intentional sin into merit. This was for the sake of the Name and the praise due to the Torah, and it exists in the mystery of the "Renewal of the Work of Creation." Therefore, one who recites this *Hallel* every day has a portion in the World to Come. This is not the case with the "Egyptian Hallel" <note>Psalms 113–118, which recount the Exodus</note>, which exists in the mystery of exile and "foreign service" <note>slavery/idolatry</note>; one who says it every day is like a blasphemer and a reviler, for he appears to be complaining. If he does not desire his current state, why does he not nullify it? As the Elders were asked about this in the Mishnah in its proper place: it was only permitted during the "sweetening of the Moon" <note>The sanctification of the new month</note> and the "filling of her defect" <note>full moon/festivals</note> on days when miracles were performed for our ancestors. Even on the New Moon, it is recited in "leaps" <note>skipping sections</note>, and it is not a "Full Hallel," for it requires a sin offering <note>referring to the temple service of the New Moon</note>; an individual recites it without a blessing. Similarly, on the last six days of Passover, when Israel was in great fear, even the most zealous among them—on the final holiday—witnessed the "work of His hands" <note>the Egyptians</note> drowning in the sea; therefore, the "Full Hallel" is not recited on those days, but only as a "leap" following general custom. However, regarding the ten "Hallelujahs" we mentioned, the last was the most beloved of the ten types of psalms. Rabbi spoke at length about the Book and its author to awaken the questioner to what was previously said: that the entire book is a rectification for the attribute of David <note>Malchut</note>.

**Afterward**, the discussion in the Talmud was completed in order from bottom to top. The response of Rav Yosef was prioritized, for the Torah was beloved to him; he held that the world was created only for its sake. Therefore, he replied that the ten Kingships correspond to the "Radiance of the Countenance" <note>Divine favor or revelation</note> of all the Sefirot within *Malchut*, just as it was at the Giving of the Torah, where the ten Sefirot bestowed the Ten Commandments upon *Malchut*—which is Sinai, the "Mouth of Power" that revealed them below. Rabbi Yochanan, however, held that "Today is the conception of the world" <note>a liturgical phrase from Rosh Hashanah</note> is what causes the flow into her, following the mystery of the "Ten Utterances" <note>The ten times "And God said" appears in Genesis</note>. The intention refers to the generalities she possesses within all the Sefirot in their respective places, through which the world was created. Behold, in the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei Zohar</note> it was explained that the hint within *Malchut* regarding "Remembrances" and "Shofars" refers to the Sefirot of *Tiferet* (Beauty), *Binah* (Understanding), and *Malchut* (Sovereignty). We have learned regarding all of them that the intention is towards the three "faces": whether from the generalities of the ten Sefirot in *Binah*, *Tiferet*, and *Malchut* (corresponding to the ten Hallelujahs), or the "Radiance of the Countenance" toward them (corresponding to the Commandments), or the generalities of *Binah*, *Tiferet*, and *Malchut* in the ten Sefirot in their places (corresponding to the Utterances). This is rectified and accepted.

->**Crown**<-
->**Wisdom** | **Understanding**<-
<note>original: כתר, חכמה, בינה</note>

### Chapter 6: We have learned
In the Tractate *Avot* <note>Ethics of the Fathers</note>: "With ten utterances the world was created." And what does the verse teach us? Why did it lengthen the story and mention them one by one? It could have simply said: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made* <note>Psalm 33:6</note> and nothing more! But "it is the glory of God to conceal a matter." This is why it teaches: "Could it not have been created with a single utterance?" It answers that by mentioning the utterances individually, He punishes [the wicked] and gives reward [to the righteous]. This comes to teach us, however, that the intended purpose...

<column-break/>

...is more known and recognized. His Cause is without body or form, being simple and without limit or the deficiency of lowly physical matter. It is far from any doubt. If we were to compare Him—for in this sense, any comparison is entirely false—what is this [world], and what are the angels who are [relatively] corporeal? For although souls are subtle, they have a slight tendency [toward form]. Similarly, an effect cannot have the power to bestow spiritual light upon its cause. Because He is subtle, He cannot be divided; rather, He acts by Will in the spiritual realm, where primary perfection lies in His unity and His being indivisible. It is also not a "deficiency" that there are beings greater than these; for there is no [comparison] between the Emanator <term>Ma'atzil</term> and the Emanated <term>Ne'etzal</term> except that which exists between a Cause and its Effect. And all that was possible for the Emanated to be was achieved in the great kindness of the Emanator within the perfection of the Crown <term>Keter</term>, until no power remained for the Emanated to be "missing" between the Crown and the Emanator. There is no room to say, "Why was there not another level between them?" for the Crown was attached [to the Source], since no power was lacking. It was necessary for the Emanated to be the "end" of the Emanator; this is not due to a deficiency in the Emanator, but due to the intent that there remains within [the creation] a choice—that it is "emanated" and "caused," and its Cause is above it. Many things are above the secret, for it is an effect of its cause to bestow upon its cause. And because it is emanated from an effect, it is forced to descend from before His presence and His ways. Just as there was no difference between the Emanator and the Crown except the relationship of Cause and Effect, so too was the matter between Crown and Wisdom, and between every Sefirah and the Sefirah emanated from it, down to the ten Sefirot and that which was drawn from them. And just as it was impossible for the Crown to be anything less than the Emanator [intended], so it was impossible for there to be any "gap" in the Emanated between the Emanator and the Crown. Thus, no room was left for there to be any "missing" level between one Sefirah and another. From what we have explained, the matter of the "Three Aspects" within every single Sefirah will be clarified. It is covered by two aspects: its aspect in relation to what is emanated from it (which is its essential aspect) and its aspect in relation to its Emanator. In this aspect, it must possess the "Aspect of Longing"—meaning, it yearns for and seeks its Emanator (the Crown), which does not separate from it at all. After this, it descends itself, and Wisdom had its own "depth upon depth" until it reached the point of being the aforementioned Cause... [the text becomes complex here discussing the nested levels]. And behold, also the aspect of "Cause to Effect" must be within it. The ascent from Understanding <term>Binah</term> to the aspect of the Crown-like formation that instructs Understanding, which receives its power from the aspect appointed over the Crown, was an ascent to the aspect of the Essence. And Understanding's own essence was the Cause for the aspect appointed over Understanding. And so it is in every single aspect: there were three internal aspects. Thus, from level to level and point to point, there was a difference between Cause and Effect, for there is no "limit" to the descent of the Light. The further it removes itself from the Emanator, the more the Upper beings are revealed [to the lower], branching out from their Supernal lowliness and becoming "clothed." This is the mystery of "Cause and Effect," the secret that "every deficiency is included and made ten," and the mystery of the descent of the levels within the essence of the Sefirah itself. For the "Crown of the Crown" is the aspect that clings to the Emanator, may He be blessed, and the "Sovereignty of the Crown" is the aspect that stretches toward Wisdom. In the "Crown that is within Wisdom," it is an effect [of the Crown above it]. The "Sovereignty of the Crown within the Crown" and the "Sovereignty within Wisdom" is the aspect that stretches toward...

<meta>The text cuts off here, with the catchword "toward" (אל) indicating the start of the next page.</meta>

# Juice of Pomegranates, Gate 2: The Reason for Emanation — Hermon Slice

The Palaces <note>Hebrew: *Heikhalot*, referring to the divine structures or "rooms" within the spiritual realms</note> (and it is known etc. in the second part) — it appears that the primary purpose of Emanation <term>Atzilut: The highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, where the divine light is still unified with God</term> was not originally for this matter (to mention and gather the thoughts of the darkness to search for the revival of those who merit His kindness according to their deeds, which would be unnecessary) nor was it derived from it (for reward and punishment in the upper pleasure alone). Rather, it was to reveal and make known His divisions <note>The distinct attributes or Sefirot</note> and for the beauty of those divisions. It is more fitting that the world should thus praise Him and view the "arrangement of praise" <note>Hebrew: *Tikun Mekulas*</note>. Therefore, as it is written: *And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be one and His name one* <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>. For through the binding and unification of the Sefirot, goodness, kindness, and the flow of knowledge and blessing will be revealed, as it is written: *And no longer shall each man teach his neighbor... for they shall all know Me* <note>Jeremiah 31:33</note>.

**Furthermore**, one can say the reason for "limiting and ending" <note>The creation of boundaries in the infinite</note> is that the King (the Holy One, Blessed be He) desired to bestow influence and do good to "the other" <note>The created beings</note>, and to be a King over the small creatures, to influence them from the attributes of mercy, to bequeath the inheritances, and to reveal to the eyes of the creatures His greatness. This is so that He might be recognized and proven to His creations through their needs. This is the meaning of "Kingship": occupying Yourself with His intention to aggrandize His majesty manifoldly.

However, because the revelation of His majesty toward the creatures—due to the magnitude of His hidden heights—would be too much for the creatures to grasp, He had to bequeath the "Reception" <note>The Kabbalah</note> and the Wisdom of God down to the Understanding <term>Binah</term> until the Sovereignty <term>Malchut</term>, for it is there that the perception of His majesty is available to others.

**A parable** for this: A King who is beneficent and enters a ruined path to walk, and out of his great piety provides bread in a house so that those who are hungry may come and be sustained. The King returned, for he had great power to make a very large "cloak" <note>OCR reads *Atitit*, likely *Atifah*—a covering or veil</note> to better the search, and he lives across the expanse. Those standing in the house look out, and they are not harmed by the intensity of his clarity and his encompassment. And even though the light <note>OCR *Kur*, likely *Or*</note> was sweetened, hidden, and concealed, nevertheless, the voices are still far from those standing in the palace of the King, etc.

And now we come to the Ten Sefirot within the "House" <note>The manifest world</note> to strike from the light that shines through the "cloak." And why was the matter of the cloak necessary? Because at the edge of goodness, if not for the "garments" <note>The Sefirot acting as filters</note>, out of the abundance of its simplicity, the light would overwhelm the gazer. Therefore, there are "rectifications" <note>Tikunim</note> for the light so that it may be sweetened to the eyes of the beholders. If these filters were diminished, the eye of the beholder would be damaged by the intensity of the light; if they were increased, the light would be darkened and the sweetness of the light would not be felt. The intention was thus to "sweeten" the light so they could benefit from it most effectively—not so bright that they cease to exist, but a light within a light within a light, established.

### Chapter 7
**Furthermore**, one may give a reason for this limitation. To understand the matter, one must know that because the souls are thin and simple spiritualities <note>De-void of physical matter</note>, they could be damaged if they were to be entirely absorbed into the Divine. They must be contained within "vessels." According to this, when one asks why the Emanator did not emanate the Sefirot all at once, the answer is that He emanated them in a specific order—to be three Sefirot first, so that later they could be divided into "faces" <term>Partzufim: Divine personas or configurations</term>. Because of this, it was impossible for them to be [completely] revealed <note>Blessed be His Name</note> all at once. This was not due to any lack in the Emanator, but due to the limited capacity and perfection of those who receive and are influenced. It was for the benefit of the recipients; to make them "vessels," they needed to descend into the "vessels of the body" that receive. This is the greatness of the deeds: that the greatness of the Creator is revealed through the creation of worlds to bestow upon another.

<column-break/>

On the first day, of which it is said "Light." The second Craftsman <note>Original Aramaic: *Omana*</note> brought forth swarming things from the water, as it is written: *Let the waters swarm* <note>Genesis 1:20</note>. This was dependent on the second day, of which it is said "Water," as it is written: *Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters*—here is water and there is water. The third Craftsman brought forth grass and herbage corresponding to the third day, as it is written: *Let the earth sprout vegetation*. And it says on the sixth day: *Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth*. That which was in the "third" on the "sixth" is the "living being" <note>Chayah</note> of the sixth day, which is the Foundation <term>Yesod</term>, including right and left like the Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>. And even though the first Craftsmen were one, each brought out his craft. Rabbi Eleazar explained in the section on *Bereshit* <note>In the Zohar</note> that they were hidden and not revealed. The "Fourth Leg of the Throne" which was included in the third day to be one without separation—he revealed them. Afterwards, three crafts of the building spread out through the attribute of Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>: "Let the earth sprout" like the "dry land"; "Lights" like "Let there be light"; "Let the waters swarm" like the "firmament." And even the sixth day is so, for the latter days—Lights, Swarming, and Blessing—depend on the Fourth Leg, which is the Sabbath that is included in the sixth day. He prepared for him "beauty," as mentioned in the mystery of the "Sixth" from that "Palanquin" above in the portion of *Terumah*. Three crafts also spread from it: "Let the earth bring forth" like "swarming," "living soul" and "living soul." "Let us make man" like the "lights"—small and great, male and female. "Behold I have given" like "sprout vegetation." And thus the blessing is drawn out, as we mentioned above regarding the statement *Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth*, which is the craft intended for its own sake.

As for why these two Sages of the Tractate *Rosh Hashanah* and the portion of *Vayikra* omitted it, the reason seems to be that the fulfillment of the "Utterance" <note>Ma'amar</note> depends on another. Therefore it says, "And God said to them," but not so regarding "Behold I have given," for He alone is the Giver. So it is with all other Utterances, for *He commanded and they were created* <note>Psalm 148:5</note>. However, according to the six rectifications, we rightly count "Be fruitful and multiply" as part of the Ten, and with this, they are considered ten crafts corresponding to the Ten Utterances. For the "Utterance of the Helper" <note>Genesis 2:18 "I will make a helper for him"</note> is not a craft in itself, since it is written after it *I will make him a helper*, and furthermore, it appears separately in the text and is not mentioned within the six days of creation. However, the generations that follow from it are the truly intended craft.

### Chapter 5
It is explained from this that the intention of the questioner was: "What are they?" <note>Referring to the Ten Utterances</note>. For when they said "With Ten Utterances the world was created," it implies that they refer to the "tools of His craft." The craft of the Sovereignty <term>Malchut</term> is derived from the Foundation <term>Yesod</term> in the ninth utterance, which is "Behold I have given." And they answered him well: "*Bereshit* (In the beginning) is also an utterance." In it is hidden the existence of the Crown <term>Keter</term> which includes all of Emanation. In the majority of the utterances, the inclusion of the Ten is also explained. And from the Crown is drawn "Let there be light," which is the emanation of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>, as we have mentioned.

**And in the Book of Clarity** <note>Hebrew: *Sefer HaBahir*, one of the earliest kabbalistic works</note> Rabbi Bun said: What is the meaning of the verse *I was sovereign from eternity, from the beginning, from the earliest times of the earth* <note>Proverbs 8:23</note>? What does "from eternity" <note>Hebrew: *Me-Olam*</note> mean? It refers to a matter that must be "hidden" <note>Hebrew: *He'elem*—a pun on *Olam* (world) and *He'elem* (hiddenness)</note> from the whole world, as it is written: *He also put the world (ha-olam) in their hearts* <note>Ecclesiastes 3:11</note>—do not read it as *ha-olam* (the world) but as *ha-elam* (the hiddenness). The Torah said: I preceded to be the "Head" of the world, as it says *I was sovereign from eternity, from the beginning*. And do not say that perhaps the Earth preceded it, for it says *from the earliest times of the earth*, as we say: *In the beginning God created*. And what does "created" (*Bara*) mean? He created the needs of all, and only then "God" (*Elohim*)...

It also reconciles the "Ten Utterances" of creation with the structure of the Sefirot, drawing on the Zohar and Sefer HaBahir.</summary>
