# Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 2: The Reason for Emanation — Juice of Pomegranates

<margin>
He tells the end from the beginning <note>original: "maggid mereshit," a reference to Isaiah 46:10</note>, and the imitation [of the light], and not its separation, and the hiding of the light through the descent of the levels until the lowest aspect. And even in a narrow window, the opening and the hole within its navel exists, and its path reaches seven windows, the opposite of the order of the open pestles (of which the number is to give a level to a window, which are 20, 3, and instead of a "Vav," the seat of the earth, and if you investigate the earth, the thickness of the altar is 7, instead of a "Vav," and a mile). And the order of all generations was written through the channels, which are the ten great and inclusive ones, which because of their greatness and loftiness (and the power) and the ability of their servant, there will be the level of an additional window.
</margin>

"A firmament is a journey of 500 years" <note>A traditional Talmudic measurement (Chagigah 13a) used here as a metaphor for the spiritual "thickness" or distance between different grades of divine reality</note> is the secret of the inclusion of the "sisters" <note>Referring to the interconnectedness of the Sefirot</note>, and it is equal in all levels in their essence and in their relation to others. **And in the Tikunim** <note>The *Tikunei Zohar*, a foundational Kabbalistic text</note> they said: The level of "washing" <note>original: *archisu*</note> with water, this is **Kindness** <term>Hesed: The Sefirah of expansive love and benevolence</term>; and the "heavens in a span" <note>Isaiah 40:12</note> refers to the Olive, which is **Strength** <term>Gevurah: The Sefirah of judgment and restraint</term>; and "comprehended in a third" <note>Isaiah 40:12</note>, this is the **Middle Pillar** <term>Tiferet: The Sefirah of Beauty and Harmony that balances Kindness and Strength</term>, which is the third; and "weighed the mountains in scales," this is **Victory** <term>Netzach</term>, and "the hills in a balance," this is **Splendor** <term>Hod</term>. And these are the creation of the letter *He* <note>The second letter of the Divine Name Y-H-V-H</note>, for this Point <note>the Sefirah of Wisdom</note> dwells within them as five points, which is the letter *Yod* that emerged from the "Pure Air" <note>original: *Avira d'khia*</note> which is the **Supreme Crown** <term>Keter: The highest Sefirah, representing the Divine Will</term>. And because these five measures are the creation of the Higher *He*, it is the one that "travels through them five hundred years" between each one. And the secret of the matter is that the "Tree of Life is a journey of 500 years" <note>A midrashic description of the vastness of the spiritual Tree of Life</note>, meaning between each one there are five hundred years, and in the "thickness" of each one there are 500 years, for they all rise in the balance of "five and five" for each side. And the secret of the matter is: *And you shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the planks of the first side of the Tabernacle, and five bars for the planks of the second side of the Tabernacle, and five bars for the planks of the Tabernacle for the rear side westward* <note>Exodus 26:26-27</note>. The "rear sides" are the thighs of truth <note>Netzach and Hod</note>. And what is the "Westward" <note>original: *Yamah*, literally "to the sea"</note>? This is the Higher Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: The immanent aspect of God, here associated with the Sefirah of Binah</term>.

**He said** that the essence of **Understanding** <term>Binah: The Sefirah of divine intellect and "The Mother"</term>, which includes in the subtlety of its existence fifty gates, because of which it is called "Who" <note>original: *Mi* (מ"י), which has a numerical value of 50</note>, and it is also called "To You" <note>original: *Lakh* (ל"ך), which has a numerical value of 50</note>. It spreads through them by way of the five bars of the Tabernacle for the building of the "Side" <note>referring to the creation of the feminine aspect</note> of which it is said, "ten cubits shall be the length of the plank." "Cubits" <note>original: *Amot*</note> are "hundreds" <note>original: *Me'ot*</note> in reverse, as they explained there. And in another place, they explained "Plank" <note>original: *Keresh*</note> as the reverse of "Connection" <note>original: *Kesher*</note>; they said that the connection of existence rises in the Air until the Infinite and descends until the end of all things, including 500 years twice—that is, the fifty gates of Understanding included in ten in "Direct Light" and "Returning Light." And all of this is through the **Foundation** <term>Yesod: The Sefirah that channels all divine energy to the world</term>, which is one bar that includes them all. It is written as "Bars" and the whole combination is called *Lakh* ("To You"), and **Kingship** <term>Malchut: The final Sefirah, our physical reality</term> is the "Final Sea," the combination of *Mi* ("Who").

**And in the Zohar** they explained the verse "A man of measure, five cubits" <note>1 Chronicles 11:23</note> as referring to Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him. Its explanation above is as follows: And if you say, is it not written "five cubits"? It means from the end of the world to the end of the world. It is known that the "edge of the heaven" above is Understanding (*Binah*), as in "To You, O Lord, is the greatness" <note>original: *Lekha Hashem HaGedulah*</note>, and the "edge of the heaven" below is Kingship (*Malchut*), as in "To You, O Lord, is the kingdom" <note>original: *Lekha Hashem HaMamlakhah*</note>. And "five cubits" is directed exactly in the middle. And when you multiply the number of five firmaments by the number of five hundred years, you get fifty by fifty, like the measure of the Courtyard of the Tabernacle before the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, which are the "two *Lakhs*" <note>Two sets of 50</note> we mentioned: Direct and Returning.

**And in the chapter** "One may not expound" <note>Talmud, Chagigah 11b</note> regarding the verse *Ask now of the days that are past... since the day that God created man upon the earth, and from one end of heaven to the other* <note>Deuteronomy 4:32</note>, and it is written *You have hedged me behind and before* <note>Psalm 139:5</note>, which is from East to West—they said that both are the same measure. And similarly, in the chapter "They would not bind," the Sages say these and those are equal, meaning from East to West is equal to from Heaven to Earth. The commentators said that when Adam stood, his height was from heaven to earth, and when he lay down, it was from East to West. There is no doubt that this speaks of before his "diminution" <note>The midrashic idea that Adam was originally cosmic in size but was shrunk after his sin</note>, for it is written afterward, *And You laid Your hand [kappekhah] upon me*. We read this as *Kaf* (20) and *Tav* (400) <note>suggesting a measure of 420</note>. Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: He diminished him. And Rabbi Eleazar added and stood him at one hundred cubits, and all is explained in the verse. Behold, "before the diminution" indicates that he is **Beauty** <term>Tiferet</term> shining in the secret of the Fiftieth Gate, the "edge of heaven" above. And "West" is **Kingship** (*Malchut*), influenced by him through the **Foundation of the World** (*Yesod*). She is called "Bride," included in all the gates through the "All" <note>Yesod</note> that grasps the heaven and the earth. She herself is the letter *He*, an abbreviation for *Hod* (Splendor), which is the House of Kingship at the time of favor... it is the secret of "when he lies down." And "his standing" is the secret of the "Measure of the Stature" <term>Shiur Komah: A mystical concept regarding the anthropomorphic visualization of the Divine</term>, the line of the measure, the "Hope [Mikveh] of Israel is the Lord."

<column-break/>

### Gate Three: If the Infinite (Ein Sof) is the Crown (Keter)

#### Chapter 1
It has already been clarified from what we learned in the Mishnah: "Ten and not nine" <note>Sefer Yetzirah 1:4</note>, that the **Supreme Wisdom** <term>Chochmah: The second Sefirah, but the first point of conscious intellect</term> is not the Emanator, as is the opinion of some who infer from the end of the phrase, "ten and not eleven." It is a widespread rule among them that the Sefirot are the essence of the Godhead according to their system. In the fourth gate, we are destined, with God's help, to open blind eyes in this inquiry to understand and contemplate what is desired according to the truth in understanding these two words: **Essence and Vessels** <term>Atzmut and Kelim: One of the great debates in Kabbalah—whether the Sefirot are God's actual self (Essence) or just tools (Vessels) He uses to act</term>. And what is the intention of the Sages of Truth and Justice regarding them—whether we take each word and its meaning on its own, or whether we use both together in our studies. For us, the emanated beings are undoubtedly "renewed" <note>meaning they were created at a point in time, unlike the Eternal Creator</note>; the Emanator is exalted far above the greatest among them. **The Sage** <note>likely referring to Moses Cordovero</note>, may he rest in peace, elaborated on this inquiry in the book *Pe'at Yamah*, until he explained and said that even though we assume the Crown (*Keter*) is close to the Infinite (*Ein Sof*)...

#### Chapter 1: Explaining
The level of the Crown is lofty and higher than Wisdom; it is the Infinite, and it is the numerical equivalent of "Crown" and its existence, to add to what we said regarding the *Book of Formation*: "Ten and not nine, ten and not eleven." This is our rule: that this is the second matter and its explanation. And what was written as being from the intellects and from the writings, and similarly the scriptures, and from the intellects—Wisdom was clarified in general. From the first aspect, it was clarified; however, it was already prepared there, they were separate, and the Infinite was besides it, as before the Emanation. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is paired in existence in an inseparable way... for He is set apart... and He is the first without a beginning and the last without an end. For if one were to imagine the existence of the Supernal, and it is not the "Necessary Existence" <note>a philosophical term for God, whose existence is mandatory and depends on nothing else</note>—according to our words, there are many who say that the Crown (*Keter*) was prior to all the emanated beings and closest of all to the Emanator forever. And to add to this what they said in the chapter of Rabbi Eleazar: "Before the world was created..."

# Juice of Pomegranates, Gate 2: The Reason for Emanation — Slice of the Pomegranate

to the Understanding <note>Hebrew: *Binah*</note>, and the Crown <note>Hebrew: *Keter*</note> that is within Understanding is caused by and clothed within its aspect. This is likewise true for all the Sefirot. In this matter, it should be said that every single part is composed of ten, so that one does not say, God forbid, that there is a defect—as if only a partial birth occurred. Rather, every part and every point that emerged into the law of its perfection comes from Him, and its inclusion is according to what is above it. They rose to that which they were formed into, completing for Him the "Yod" <note>The letter Yod has the numerical value of 10</note> of every Sefirah, every part, and every point, in the aspect of ten levels. This was done to bring out what is within the part and to teach from it. 

And so it was in (all) parts and levels (and this is simple). The level of "Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge" <term>Chabad: An acronym for Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at, representing the intellectual faculties of the divine soul</term> exists in every level, even in the external aspects, and likewise in the worlds of Creation, Formation, and Action <note>The three lower worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah</note>. For the matter of Chabad is that they include all levels, from the Cause of All and from the first point in the external realm, down to the lowest point at the "navel of the earth." 

For when one looks into this investigation, every level will be divided into thirty levels, and every level will have the power to be divided into four levels, and every part to return to ten parts, until it is divided into fine subtleties. This is until these ten Sefirot serve as the life-force for the World of Creation <note>Beriah</note>, which is a specific cause for the ultimate purpose of its external expression. So it is according to this order for all levels and all parts, until the entirety of all worlds is found in a connection of individual sections, uniting and clinging together. Between them, they are like **layers of onions** <note>original: "galdei betzalim," a classic Kabbalistic metaphor for nested spiritual spheres</note>; every emanated being draws sustenance from its superior and clings to it, until no judgment or separation is found between them at all. And this is—

->[A circular diagram containing ten concentric rings, representing the hierarchy of the Sefirot or the nested structure of reality.]<-

the place of the "ground." This is not in the sense of a physical place to be divided among them, but rather the ten Sefirot were more [expansive] because of the "living slice" <note>Referring to the title *Pelach HaRimmon*</note>. There is no void to divide the Mercy, and the mystery of the voids was given to us only to show the nullification of the part that exists between world and world. 

As the "Descent" goes down ten levels until the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note>, in order to be a distant tether, the "Ascent" of the face of the Descent goes up ten levels; it cannot spread further as the levels of the Descent until it becomes the level of the World of Creation. And behold, the Kingdom was the end of the Descent and the head of Creation, and its value to Creation is like the value of the "Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding" <note>Keter, Chochmah, Binah</note> to the Descent. There was nothing between the Kingdom and the beginning of Creation except the part that exists between world and world alone. Because the Descent went down ten levels, it was necessary for the levels of the World of Creation—the "Star"—to be formed. Such is the order of the descent of all other levels from Creation to Formation, and from Formation to Action, down to the celestial spheres and the foundations, reaching the central point at the "navel of the earth." All levels cling to one another and exist through one another. Who would be so lacking in foundation as to open their mouth and ask why the parts of the levels in the Kingdom were not more or less than they were? Or why the Creator did not create a larger or smaller world? To ask such a thing is a great foolishness regarding the nature of the world and its levels, which are set upon a perfect and praised existence and order. Everything is arranged in the order of levels, from the highest which is grasped in eternity to the lowest which is grasped in the physical appearance. They are balanced in purpose and in nature. In any case, the existence of the Sefirot was necessary; for if the order of the Sefirot did not exist within the nature of the world, it would never have been possible for the world to exist, because of God's simplicity. The world is conducted by the Holy One, blessed be He, through the levels of His power. For this matter, the Wise One chose the Sefirot. This intention is only to reveal the Emanation and the External.

<column-break/>

The intent behind them <note>the Sefirot</note> is to make known His divinity, may He be blessed, and to do good for those who are born. He knows and witnesses that no thought can reach Him at all, except through the ten "mirrors." Therefore, He restricted His Presence within them and created the world. Because the light of the King's face is the life of the world, the power to limit was not naturally imprinted in the World of Emanation <note>Atzilut</note>, except through the chaining down of the levels. This was prepared in Kindness <note>Hesed</note> according to a proper order, so that the deeds of the lower beings themselves might increase the light, or the opposite.

**And behold, the wicked destroy the world with those same Ten Utterances** <note>The ten phrases "And God said..." in Genesis chapter 1</note> from which they benefit in an excessive manner, trespassing by taking without a blessing. Is it not seen that they provoke anger? The utterance "Let there be light" becomes "the light of the wicked shall be withheld." "Let there be a firmament"—and they are washed away. "Let the waters be gathered"—and the waters prevail [as in the Flood]. And so it is with all of them; they are punished through the Ten Utterances. The language [of punishment, *par’u*] is derived from the phrase "Avoid it, do not pass by it" <note>Proverbs 4:15</note>, which implies revelation. And when, through their transgression, darkness covers the earth, He is found in the "Land of the Living" [the hidden realm]. But when sinners cease from the earth, and "behold, it is very good," there is pleasure for them and pleasure for the world; His kingdom is revealed, may He be blessed, and His glory shall be seen upon us. 

In contrast, **the righteous are uplifted through the success of their deeds to increase the strength of the Power above.** Behold, through their righteousness, they sustain the world through the Ten Utterances, which are unified and sweetened by them upon the earth. Their reward is through the Ten Utterances, whose ultimate purpose is the intelligence to know Him, may He be blessed. For "the glory of kings" <note>the Sefirot</note> is to "search out a matter," though the investigation of the Infinite <note>Ein Sof</note> is absolutely impossible. 

It was taught: "He made a condition with the Works of Creation: If Israel accepts the Torah, it is well; but if not, I will return you to chaos and void <note>original: *Tohu va-Vohu*</note>." He did not say "I will destroy you," for the earth shall not be sold into "permanent extinction," but rather He would return them to chaos by hiding the individual forms and returning them to the general form. The parts of matter would also return to the Prime Matter, for total nothingness follows at its heels. 

In the merit of all that is called by His name and for His glory, He engraved them, hewed them, and refined them into Ten Hidden Utterances, which are the Ten Sefirot. He engraved their likeness in the Throne of Glory, hewed their branches in the World of Angels, and refined their actions in the lower world. Thus, existence consists of upper and lower beings without number to His legions. This is what the scripture means: "I have created it, I have formed it, even I have made it" <note>Isaiah 43:7, referencing the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah</note>.

### Chapter 7

The "Good and the Benefactor" <note>A name for God</note> returns with a generous eye to the Holy and the Near. In the law of an emanated being, there is as much subtlety and spirituality as possible. Therefore, from the Unique Emanator, only one single emanated being proceeds <note>Referring to Keter</note>. Likewise, the second emanation that chains down from the Crown (Keter) equals it in everything, except for the fact that it is its cause. So it is with all of them. There is no way or entry to place them in a number except in the aspect of Cause and Effect, until there is no empty space left to contain another emanated being. For there is no concept of "place" in the realm of richness, and there is no barrier or stationary point for the Light. 

Every point is composed of ten, and its foundation is the four worlds <note>ABiYa: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah</note>, "each joined to its sister." Every inclusion is a "chosen upper" and a "cause for the lower." There is nothing between Emanation and Creation except that which is between Cause and Effect, and so it continues to the end of all levels. Thus, all of existence is found to be like a lamp of sections and unified parts, like **layers of onions**. And as for what our Rabbis said, "that between every heaven and heaven is the thickness of a heaven"—

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of the Sefirot, specifically moving into Gate 3 of the text. It addresses the ontological status of the Crown (Keter) and whether it should be counted as the first of the Ten Sefirot or if it is part of the Infinite (Ein Sof), which would lead to Knowledge (Da'at) being counted as the tenth instead.</meta>

-># Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 3: Whether the Infinite is the Crown — Juice of Pomegranates<-
->### 3b<-
<meta>catchword: of the Crown, in... </meta>

Regarding the division of the wonders and depths of Wisdom intended by those who came to count the Crown <note>Hebrew: *Keter*</note> as one of the ten: according to the way of truth, the secret is that the "Cause of all Causes" <note>Hebrew: *Sibat kol ha-Sibot*</note> and its Builder, upon whom all causes depend, is not to be counted at all. It is not appropriate to count the Crown, as it has no end, beginning, or completion. It is the end of all. Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (Ramban), a 13th-century sage</note> warned of this in several places, intending that the Crown and the Foundation <note>Hebrew: *Yesod*</note> should not be included in the count surrounding the "Voice of Supreme Knowledge" <note>Hebrew: *Da’at*</note>—the voice hinted at in the verse, "By His knowledge the depths were broken up" (Proverbs 3:20). 

However, this reasoning is not entirely clear <note>original: "chaser" – missing or insufficient proof from simple logic</note> because it does not explain why the Crown is not in the sequence. If it is not part of the sequence, then it is like the First Cause itself. Why then should it not enter the count of the Sefirot, since the Sefirot are also its powers? We have not set ourselves to fully explain this now. 

Behold, after the Crown, one ascends to Wisdom <note>Hebrew: *Chochmah*</note>, and from Wisdom to Understanding <note>Hebrew: *Binah*</note>. There is a necessary distinction: just as the relationship of Wisdom to Understanding exists, so does the relationship of the Crown to Wisdom. Just as you included Understanding in the count of the Sefirot alongside Wisdom, so too should the Crown be counted with Wisdom. If so, what is the reason for elevating the Crown above the scale of the other emanated beings? 

Furthermore, they argued that it is the "Cause of Causes," but this is no argument at all. If it were truly the absolute Unity, it would be above and separate. However, once we have nullified the idea of it being the "Cause of all Causes" in its simple essence, it is not appropriate to distance the Crown so far, for it is not of a different degree, since it is created and caused. As they said in the Zohar, Wisdom is called "Holy," and if so, the Crown is the "Holy of Holies." Why then is it treated as the Cause of Causes? For the definition of the Cause of Causes does not apply to it in absolute truth, as it is beyond thought. 

Since the Crown is unified with all the emanated beings and is not the actual Cause of Causes, why should its standing be questioned? If you say it is not part of this count, then it must be the secret of the "Cause of Causes" itself, and if so, it would be the only one, and excluding the Crown would mean it is not part of the emanated world. 

Yet, we see that there is no separation between one emanated being and another except as cause and effect. Just as there is nothing between Wisdom and Understanding except the distinction of cause and effect, so too is the Crown between Wisdom and Understanding. Just as you counted Wisdom with Understanding, so too should the Crown enter with Wisdom. This is also proven from the *Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkuney Zohar*, a structural commentary on the Zohar</note>, which says: "These crowns, all of them are in the counting: the Head is the Crown; the Brain is Wisdom and Understanding; the two arms are Kindness and Strength; the body is the central pillar; the two legs are Victory and Splendor; the Foundation is the sign of the covenant; and Kingship is the mouth." Thus, the Crown is included in the Sefirot as their head, and Knowledge <note>*Da'at*</note> was not counted at all. 

Furthermore, it is mentioned in the Zohar's commentary on Genesis: "'In the beginning' (*Bereishit*)—this is Wisdom." It was established that "In the beginning" refers to His Wisdom, and "with Understanding" refers to the pillar called "Beginning." And this hidden Upper Crown has holiness within it. Therefore, it concludes that there are "two beginnings" (*Bet Reshit*). This was difficult for him because of the large letter *Bet* at the start of Genesis, implying that Wisdom was not the first.

<column-break/>

In the literal sense intended by the verse, the second level is "Beginning." Therefore, the letter *Bet* <note>The second letter of the Hebrew alphabet, with a numerical value of 2</note> in *Bereishit* implies that the second Sefirah is the beginning. Nachmanides wrote that the word *Bereishit* hints at Wisdom, which is the "First," and the Jerusalem Targum translates it as "With Wisdom" (*Be-chochmata*). The word is "crowned" by the Crown represented by the *Bet*. In the *Tikkunim*, they interpreted the "depth of the end" (which is Kingship) through the verse "I am asleep" <note>Song of Songs 5:2</note>, meaning "I am second" to Wisdom.

# Chapter 2: To know the difference between "First" and "Beginning." 
One must establish that the "First" is not an essential part that is attached and revealed to the latter. For the Upper Crown, due to the intensity of its hiddenness, is not revealed or spread downwards. Instead, Knowledge (*Da'at*) enters and serves in its place. However, the essence of Wisdom spreads through the Sefirot like a **drop from the brain** that serves the skeleton and becomes the "matter" for all the existences that follow from it. Therefore, it is called "Beginning" (*Reshit*), as it is attached and unified with the "End" in one subject, which is the revelation of the Emanation intended in the scripture.

## This is what we understand from what they said in the Zohar: 
"In the beginning... the hidden holy one carved a carving, a **lamp of darkness** <note>original Aramaic: *Botzina de-Kardinuta* – a paradoxical term for the powerful, blinding light of creation</note>, which pricked a point... that carving was carved and hidden within it like one who hides everything under one key. And that key hides everything in one palace. And even though everything is hidden in that palace, the root of everything is in that key, and that key closes and opens."

## It says that the Upper Crown was engraved and revealed in the essence of Wisdom 
within its interior, in the secret of Knowledge (*Da'at*) which breaks through it. It says regarding Wisdom that it is "hidden in a point that is pricked," meaning a reality that is also hidden like the Crown, except this is fashioned as a "pricked point" while the Crown is a "non-pricked point," meaning it is not attached to the latter as "Beginning" is to "End." 

Rather, the reality of Knowledge is a simple letter *Vav*, acting as a line of mercy performing its mission like a key. The "Palace" is Understanding (*Binah*), in the secret of the "chambers" mentioned in the *Idra* <note>A section of the Zohar</note>, where the "waters" are the secret of Knowledge, the interior of the body (which is Beauty / *Tiferet*). 

It is also hinted that Wisdom has three aspects within the inclusion of the ten Sefirot, which are hinted at in the shape of the letter *Yod* and its spelling out. The **upper tip** of the *Yod*, which is like a small *Yod*, includes the first three Sefirot; in this, it is equal to the Upper Crown, and thus it is not an essential revelation of the Crown since its aspect is also hidden. The **middle body** of the *Yod*, which is like a *Vav*, indicates the expansion of the essence of Wisdom; this is from Knowledge, which "closes and opens" the expansion of the six directions. The **lower tip**, which is like a *Dalet*, indicates the Kingship within it, in an aspect equal to Understanding. 

In the *Tikkunim*, they said that the **Musical Tropes** <note>Hebrew: *Ta'amim*</note> come from the side of the Crown, the **Vowels** <note>Hebrew: *Nekudot*</note> from the side of Wisdom, and the **Letters** <note>Hebrew: *Otiyot*</note> from the side of Understanding. Behold, the Vowels are "pricked" into the letters; one cannot imagine their pronunciation without them. Not so the Tropes, which are also subtle and hidden points, and they are the beginning of everything—for the Tropes are the beginning of thought and the ultimate expression in speech. However, they are not necessarily "pricked" into the letters like the vowels themselves. And their saying "from the side..."

<meta>This page continues the discussion from Gate 3 of "Asis Rimmonim" (The Juice of Pomegranates), a summary of Rabbi Moshe Cordovero's kabbalistic system. It explores the profound ontological distinction between the Infinite (Ein Sof) and the emanated Sefirot, specifically focusing on whether the Crown (Keter) is identical to the Infinite or a separate, first creation.</meta>

# Juice of Pomegranates, Gate 3: Whether the Infinite is the Crown — The Slice of the Pomegranate

Before the world was created, "He and His Name were alone." <note>This is a famous midrashic phrase meaning that before creation, only God's essence and His potential expression existed.</note> The meaning of "His Name" hints at the **Crown** <note>Hebrew: *Keter*</note> which preceded the process of **Emanation** <note>Hebrew: *Atzilut*; the process by which the divine light unfolds into the universe</note>. His Name is unified within His essence and hidden within it. The matter is thus: it is not appropriate to give life to all of Emanation as a whole during the time of Grace, just as the Crown is part of the collective of emanated beings. For all of them, "absence" preceded their existence—meaning they were created from nothing—which is not the case for God, the **Cause of All** <note>Hebrew: *Ilat ha-Kol*</note>, may He be blessed.

The **second difference** is that the emanated beings and their persistence depend on something outside themselves—on the **Cause of all Causes** <note>Hebrew: *Ilat kol ha-Ilot*</note>, may He be blessed. Nothing exists that is not dependent on Him. But the Emanator, the **Infinite** <note>Hebrew: *Ein Sof*</note>, may He be blessed, is self-sufficient and does not need anything else. Therefore, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai calls Him in the *Zohar* "That which does not stand on a hair," <note>original: "da-la kayma b-belora"; an Aramaic idiom meaning He is not suspended or dependent on any external support or doubt.</note> for He is the source of light and the Cause of Causes. He is called the **Cause above all Causes** <note>Hebrew: *Ilat al kol ha-Ilot*</note>. This has two aspects: first, from the language of "ascent" <note>Hebrew: *Aliyah*</note>, meaning He is higher than all high beings. This does not mean a physical place, as there is no space in the realm of Emanation, but refers to the "Cause of Causes" in terms of supreme rank, loftiness, and power. The second aspect is from the language of "Cause," meaning He is the reason and cause for all existing effects.

The **third difference** is that all emanated beings have names, titles, descriptions, and relationships. But for the Emanator, may He be blessed, there is no name, title, description, memory, or comparison. We only use terms to point toward Him, like the "Crown," or other hints from the world, but we do not count Him among things except as the **Cause of all Causes**. <note>The text here contains parenthetical notes discussing the philosophical necessity of God's existence vs. the contingency of the Sefirot.</note> Sometimes He is called the **Ancient of Ancients** <note>Aramaic: *Atika de-Atikin*</note>, the **Hidden of all Hidden** <note>Aramaic: *Temira de-Temirin*</note>, and the **Secret of all Secrets**, all of which imply that He preceded all things and remains concealed. Therefore, logic dictates that the Emanator should not be included in the count of the ten emanated Sefirot.

## Chapter 2: Explaining His perfection as the Cause over all
He is hidden and concealed within the Crown. This indicates that the **Infinite** is not the Crown itself. Furthermore, He is the unique Ruler over all, wondrous and covered by the Crown. <note>The author means that God's divinity is only revealed through the "garment" or "vessel" of the Crown, which then rides upon the other Sefirot.</note> Even though He is the Primal Light, the Pure Light, the Most Polished Light, He is still called the Cause of Causes. In the *Ra'aya Mehemna* <note>A later layer of the Zohar</note>, it says the Cause of Causes is wondrous and covered within this Crown.

## Chapter 3: Even according to the opinion that the Crown is not the Infinite...
...and that it is included with the rest of the Sefirot. It is written in the *Book of the Dove* <note>Hebrew: *Sefer ha-Yonah*, a work by Rama mi-Fano</note>, Gate 4: "All Kabbalists have agreed to count these ten: 1. Crown, 2. Wisdom, 3. Understanding..."

<column-break/>

Whatever is possible for an "effect" to get close to its "Cause," there must still be an immense and vast distance between the first effect <note>The Crown</note> and the absolute **Primal Cause** <note>The Infinite</note>. This distance is beyond measure—far greater than the distance between the lower causes and their effects. It is correct to say that the distance between the Crown and the Infinite is much greater than the distance between us, lowly beings, and the supreme Crown. For even though the Crown is Primal Light and Pure Light, it is still dark compared to the Cause of Causes.

### It suffices for our purpose here to know that the First Existent, may His name be exalted, is the **Necessary Existence**.
He is absolutely eternal, for "His name alone is exalted." However, the emanated beings were all renewed after "absence" <note>Meaning they were created *ex nihilo*</note>. In the *Tikkunim* <note>Tikkunei Zohar</note>, it is explained that the **Supreme Crown** <note>Keter Elyon</note> is the first of the count of ten, and it is called **Nothingness** <note>Hebrew: *Ayin*</note>. 
*   **A** = Crown (*Keter*)
*   **Y** = Wisdom (*Chokhmah*)
*   **N** = Understanding (*Binah*)
<note>The word *Ayin* (Nothingness) is spelled Aleph-Yod-Nun, here used as an acronym for the first three Sefirot.</note>
Regarding the Infinite, it is said: "Before Me no God was formed" (Isaiah 43:10). This means the Infinite was not "formed" by letters or "will," whereas the Crown is the first "Will" and is thus "formed" or emanated. After the Crown, there are no more "backwards" degrees because of its high rank. In the *Tikkunim*, it describes the **Divine Stature** <note>Hebrew: *Shi'ur Komah*; the metaphorical body of God composed of Sefirot</note>:
*   The Head is the **Crown** of all crowns.
*   The Brain is **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*).
*   The Heart is **Understanding** (*Binah*).
*   The two arms are **Kindness** (*Chesed*) and **Strength** (*Gevurah*).
*   The body is the **Central Column** (*Tiferet*).
*   The two legs are **Victory** (*Netzach*) and **Splendor** (*Hod*).

->The **Foundation** (*Yesod*) is the sign of the covenant, and the **Divine Presence** (*Shekhinah/Malchut*) is His sign. Thus it is clear that the Supreme Crown<-
is the first of the Emanation, and Wisdom is second to it. We mentioned in the order of the "Ten Utterances" <note>The ten phrases by which the world was created in Genesis</note> that the Supreme Crown is the first utterance and Wisdom is the second, as proven in the *Sefer ha-Bahir*. The word *Bereishit* ("In the beginning") hints at Wisdom through the power of the Crown hidden within it. This is seen in the letter *Bet* <note>The first letter of the Bible, which has the numerical value of 2</note>, which acts as a "house" <note>Hebrew: *Bayit*</note> for the other Sefirot. The *Bet* revolves around the *Aleph*, which represents the "Faithful Crown," wondrous and covered. In the *Zohar*, they say *Bereishit* means "Two Beginnings." The first is Wisdom. In the Jerusalem Targum <note>An Aramaic translation of the Bible</note>, it is translated as "With Wisdom." Because Wisdom is second in the count, the Crown—which is hidden and primal—is not included in the count, making Wisdom the "beginning" of the count. That is why the Torah starts with *Bet* (2) and the word *Reishit* (Beginning).

The letter *Bet* alone hints at Wisdom; therefore, it is written large in the Torah. Rabbi Akiva taught that the "crown" or "point" at the back of the letter *Bet* points toward the *Aleph* that precedes it. That upper point hints at the power of the **Infinite**, as will be explained. Thus, Wisdom is the second of the emanated beings, and the *Aleph* (the Crown) is the one that preceded it.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the nature of the Crown (Keter) and its relationship to the Infinite (Ein Sof). It specifically moves into the mechanics of how the first Sefirot—Wisdom (Chokhmah), Understanding (Binah), and Knowledge (Da'at)—interact to form the "Central Column" of the divine structure.</meta>

# Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 3: Whether the Infinite is the Crown — Juice of Pomegranates

And in this, these extremes will be equal—**Beauty** <note>Hebrew: *Tiferet*</note> and **Sovereignty** <note>Hebrew: *Malkhut*</note>—in the delicacy of the higher attributes, for they are intellectual and not merely emotional qualities. And we have learned: "Ten and not eleven," <note>original: "Eser ve-lo achat esreh"; a foundational rule from the *Sefer Yetzirah* stating there are only ten divine emanations.</note> because the hiddenness of the **Crown** <note>Hebrew: *Keter*</note> is but a single hidden aspect, called the **Unattainable Air** <note>original: *Avira de-la Itpas*; a state of pure potentiality that cannot be grasped by thought</note>. Yet at the conclusion of its stages, it is called **Attainable Air**. Behold, we have investigated this: it is a sixth aspect toward the end, and it belongs to **Wisdom** <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</note>. From there, the drawing forth of **Knowledge** <note>Hebrew: *Da'at*</note> toward **Understanding** <note>Hebrew: *Binah*</note> begins. This is called the **Order of Times**.

This reality of Knowledge, situated between Wisdom and Understanding, was explained in the *Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkuney Zohar*, a classic kabbalistic text</note>. They said: "In the beginning" <note>Hebrew: *Bereshit*</note> refers to two—Wisdom and Understanding. The third is "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of Knowledge." <note>A play on Psalm 111:10</note> Regarding this Knowledge, it is said: "And Adam knew Eve his wife," for there is no union except through Knowledge, which is the **Central Column**. Insofar as it is the Central Column, it is the union of the **Father** and **Mother** <note>The divine personae representing Wisdom and Understanding</note>. Likewise, below, the **Righteous One** <note>Hebrew: *Tzadik*, referring to the Sefirah of *Yesod* (Foundation)</note> is the union of the Central Column and the **Lower Presence** <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*</note>. Regarding the Body and the Covenant, <note>The physical manifestations of the central and foundational energies</note> it is said: "For the Lord is a God of Knowledge," <note>1 Samuel 2:3</note> and both are witnesses, for there is no testimony with fewer than two. And this is "In Him, blessed be He"—this refers to Wisdom and the Mother [Understanding]. This concludes the quote.

Behold, the meaning of the word "In the beginning" <note>Hebrew: *Bereshit*</note> as "Rise Up" <note>likely a reference to a specific Zoharic interpretation</note> is appropriate to explain that the Sefirot and Knowledge are the beginning of the "Fear of the Lord," as we learned: "An ignorant person cannot be a sin-fearing person." It is also written: "For in the Lord [YH], the Lord [YHVH] is the Rock of Worlds." This is a matter learned from its context, for the lower world is the "Image" taken from Man—which signifies Wisdom and signifies Knowledge. Thus, it is fashioned with two names: Wisdom and Eve. These—the Body and the Covenant—witness to each other. One "knows" through Knowledge, which is elevated above the "Mother of all living."

Behold, the Body and the Covenant testify to one another; just as Beauty <note>*Tiferet*</note> unifies through the Foundation <note>*Yesod*</note>, so too Knowledge unifies Understanding. Regarding both, it is said "For the Lord is a God of Knowledge," meaning the knowledge of both is equal in the act of Union. It is known that in capital cases, two witnesses do not join together unless they testify as one; therefore, it was necessary to interpret what was said about this regarding that.

It was further explained in the *Tikkunim* that there is no union for the world except through the Foundation, and Beauty also unifies above in the secret of the hidden "Covenant" that is with it, like the Crown. "These are the chronicles of Jacob: Joseph." <note>Genesis 37:2; in Kabbalah, Jacob represents *Tiferet* and Joseph represents *Yesod*</note> Similarly, "And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him," like the manner of male and female in the world of Formation, where the two are not united in all their limbs, but only in the Covenant of Circumcision. This concludes the quote.

All this provides great support for the opinion of the Sage <note>likely referring to Rabbi Isaac the Blind or another early authority</note> who considers the Crown to be in a state of ultimate hiddenness, and there it is not counted among the Sefirot, but is considered their Root and the place of Absolute Will. Another Sage considers the Crown as an existing Sefirah. Here, it is not far-fetched to call it "Knowledge" according to the way of these Sages and according to what we are currently explaining.

There is another opinion regarding the essence of Knowledge in the "Pomegranates" <note>Referring to Cordovero's *Pardes Rimonim*</note> above: that it is the partnership of the opposing attributes, **Kindness** <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note> and **Severity** <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note>, in their roots hidden within Wisdom and Understanding. Things are called "equal" because the Crown, called the **Cause of Causes**, is what binds and partners them. Beauty is also a blend of these opposites as they manifest in the attributes in their place. The general rule of the matter according to this: Knowledge is not counted for itself in the World of Nothingness <note>the *Sefirot* of the mind</note>, and the Crown is not counted in the revelation of the Emanation below. This is sufficient for the intended purpose. Behold, the words of the Sages are heard in tranquility, and there is no need to confuse the sections further.

<column-break/>

...than Knowledge, which is a Sefirah encompassing every aspect and the perfection of the collective Sefirah, being the inclusion of the tenth from its place and below. Behold, the emanation of the Crown is in the **Vast Countenance** <note>Hebrew: *Arich Anpin*</note>, which is the first world to the Emanator. The second world is the **Lesser Countenance** <note>Hebrew: *Zeir Anpin*</note>, which includes all forty Sefirot generally, from Wisdom to the Foundation. This is the secret of the world.

Know also that every Sefirah is established in three aspects:
1. The aspect of what it receives from above.
2. The aspect of its own essence, which is its unique power.
3. The aspect of what it gives to the Crown <note>meaning the link upward</note>.

The aspect that receives and unifies is more delicate and spiritual than the other aspects. The second aspect is its actual essence. <gloss>And this is what they said in their riddle: the explanation of "Kindness" which is the overflow of your Wisdom, that its qualities should be clarified in the place of revealed things.</gloss> The third aspect is the very beginning of the emanation from the Crown, which is the Vast Countenance with the Name [YHVH]. It is hidden and does not reveal itself to the world.

The beginning of the revelation of Emanation is in its first aspect. Therefore, some want to say that the intent regarding the Sefirot is that they were the beginning of revelation. And Knowledge was not counted as a separate Sefirah, but rather as something included in the Crown. This is why they say Knowledge is "born" from Understanding—because its power was canceled [merged] within the Crown. The Wisdom within the Crown is the "Brain of the Holy Ancient One," and it gives life to the Vast Countenance.

Thus, the Crown is composed of three "heads" or roots:
1. The root of the **Right Line** (Wisdom/Kindness).
2. The root of the **Left Line** (Understanding/Severity).
3. The root of the **Central Line** (Beauty/Foundation/Sovereignty).

Our teacher, Rabbi Eliyahu Nachman <note>possibly Eliyahu de Vidas, author of *Reshit Chokhmah*</note>, called the first three "Three Straight Paths," which are Mercy and Grace. In his prayer, he called them **Knowledge**, **Knower**, and **Known**. <note>A concept borrowed from Maimonides' *Mishneh Torah* to describe God's unity</note> The matter is that the Crown is hidden because it is the first beginning, and the powers are still concealed within it so that one cannot judge it as a "Knower"—which would imply the birth of the revelation of Wisdom. Rather, it is "Knowledge," for it is a simple, unified power, and nothing has yet been revealed from it. Wisdom is the "Knower" because it is the cause through which all powers are fashioned. The "Known" is the totality of Wisdom and Understanding together, included in the term "Knowledge," because the existence of all powers is within the Higher Knowledge.

<insert>Knowledge and this reality includes three</insert>

### Chapter 8: And this reality
...of Beauty within the Crown is called the "Order of Times," as I wrote at the beginning of the portion of *Phinehas*. We shall explain this: the roots of the Foundation <note>Beauty with Understanding; look into this, for the roots are in Understanding and they are the six hidden directions within Understanding</note>. They are the root for the seven directions of the Sefirot of the "Building" <note>the lower seven Sefirot</note>. They are the "House," and everything is a "Body" to Knowledge, for Knowledge is the reality of the three directions from Wisdom and above, and Wisdom is contained within Understanding.

# Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 3: Whether the Infinite is the Crown — Pomegranate Slice

...with letters. And the word **Beginning** <note>Hebrew: *Reshit*</note> seems to me to be an allusion to the internal aspect <note>original: *bechinah*</note>, and likewise there are two allusions to what was well-noted regarding the three transformations in their order. The **Beginning of Wisdom** <note>Hebrew: *Reshit Chokhmah*</note> encompasses the letters, and the **Crown** <note>Hebrew: *Keter*</note> is first. This is like the **Beginning of my Desire** <note>original: *Reshit Cheftzi*</note>, for the Crown is called the **World of Liberty and Freedom**, and this is the resting place of the Levites <note>In Kabbalah, the Levites represent the power of "elevation" and "rest" within the divine structure</note>. This is a state of rest alongside the chosen Sefirot in the number of one hundred and ten, for no thing is recognizable due to their great number and the depth of their matter and their ability to extend without end.

### **Chapters 4 and 5**

And as he explained in the *Book of Formation* <note>original: *Sefer Yetzirah*</note> regarding the words **Ten that have no end**, the word <term>Beli-mah</term> <note>Literally "Without-what," used in early mysticism to describe the Sefirot as abstract or beyond substance</note> can be divided into three parts: a vessel of beauty, and he explains what "what" means—namely, measures. The intention is that the ten Sefirot are without measure because their cycle is not attainable by us, and they do not have—that is to say, this one is "Judgment" and this one is "Mercy" and so on—rather, such traits arise out of their actions, while within their own essence they are "without what." Furthermore, the word is from the language of **bridling** <note>original: *belom*</note>, as it is written: "to bridle his mouth" <note>Psalm 32:9</note>, meaning that one should restrain his mouth and not speak of them in excess, because of the limitation of the one who perceives and the depth of that which is perceived. Or it may be from the language of **hiding and concealment**, as in the matter of bridling, which is a covering of the mouth and its concealment. And the Sefirot are "bridled/without what," meaning the Sefirot of the world which are hidden. All three interpretations follow one rule <note>The author argues that whether "Beli-mah" means "no substance," "silence," or "concealed," the theological point remains the same</note>. After the measure of **ten**, it explains that although we have spoken grandly of their loftiness, at any rate, that which we perceive of them is to give them a measure and the number of ten. And lest one think they have a boundary, it says clearly: **they have no end**. Even though we have assigned them a defined number, they still have no end. This is a matter of a thing and its opposite: in terms of their essence, which contains all levels of inheritance, they have no boundary; but in terms of their entry into action and their activities found among us, all their actions have a boundary according to our capacity to receive, as we are beings of boundary. This is the power of the greatness of our Creator: that within a boundary He reveals Himself and brings us into existence for the benefit of the lower beings who possess boundaries and ends. This is something that an enlightened brother, though far from these matters, should not be confused by. Therefore, it is written: "He was a scribe," <note>referring to the act of recording divine emanations</note> and by the power of my understanding between two other vessels. And the clarity of the matter is the explanation of the levels of the Crown in the count of the Sefirot.

### **Chapter 6 and What**

The difficulty that arises on this is what he said in the *Holy Assembly* <note>original: *Idra Rabba*, a section of the Zohar</note>: The "White Head" <note>original: *Atika Kadisha*, the most hidden aspect of the Crown</note> sought to provide and to influence, and the rest for his palate is like a bird that spreads its wings and goes out from the nest.

### **Chapter 7: To Understand**

My words emphasize the **Holy Precedence** <note>original: *Kadesh ha-Kadmah*</note> to Grace <note>Chesed</note>. For since the ten Sefirot are included in their actions, they are drawn toward the hole of the priestly drop. At any rate, He clothes Himself in the Crown and makes the Presence of Joy and Rest dwell there. This is what attaches and binds in the *Holy Assembly*, the Kingdom of attachment and story, and the end by way of the Crown—the hiddenness and the holes of concealment like His mercies. Because of this loftiness, the levels of the Crown are revealed through the "Cause of the Sefirot" and yet are not revealed or included among them, just as we are forced to include within Him the higher Sefirot. Thus, the one who is enlightened in the Sefirot will, by means of **Knowledge** <note>Da'at</note>, be joined inwardly. And because it is so hidden in its clarity, it is the praise of the external ones, for the praise of the internal ones is only from **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> downwards, where they are included in the ten aspects of Knowledge, which completes the place of the Crown.

<column-break/>

...of Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding. The intention is that the revelation of their existence is below in **Sovereignty** <note>Malkhut</note> through the power of the three highest ones that influence her through the lines of **Grace, Judgment, and Mercy**. And thus it is concluded there: they clothe themselves in water, fire, and wind <note>original: *maya, isha, ve-rucha*</note>, which are **Greatness** <note>Chesed</note>, **Strength** <note>Gevurah</note>, and **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>. And likewise they clothe themselves in **Victory, Glory, and Foundation** <note>Netzach, Hod, Yesod</note>, which are the vessels for the whole, for **Sovereignty** is the completion of them all.

---

### **Chapter 3: We Have Seen**

Those scholars who maintain that the **Crown** <note>Keter</note> precedes the other Sefirot and that it has always been a "garment" for the Emanator <note>the Infinite/God</note>. They base their words on what the Sages said: "Before the world was created, there was only the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Name." And Rabbi Shem Tov, in the *Book of Beliefs* <note>original: *Sefer ha-Emunot*</note>, supports this view, writing on behalf of the most wondrous and deep of the wise men that one should not count the **Supreme Crown** among the Ten, for it is within the **Infinite** <note>Ein Sof</note>, and there, there is no name, beginning, or end. This is also precise according to the text of the *Book of Formation*: "Ten and not eleven." The "Palace of the Gate" is **Knowledge** <note>Da'at</note>, and regarding this they said in the *Book of Brilliance* <note>original: *Sefer ha-Bahir*</note> that it is the **Holy Palace**, and the essence of the Unique Name <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> is intended in the letters of the Name in the middle, in **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>, for it is a palace for the Higher Root.

**The Sage**, peace be upon him, explained that Knowledge <note>Da'at</note> is nothing other than **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note> in its higher existence, which is entirely "delights." The proof is from the portion of *Pinchas* on the verse "For there is no deed, or reckoning, or knowledge" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:10</note>: this is the secret of the **six sides** that depend on Thought and are called the "World of that Thought." In the *Tikkunim* they said: The soul is the "breath of life," which is **Understanding** <note>Binah</note> that takes from **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>. The lower soul <note>Nefesh</note> is from **Sovereignty** <note>Malkhut</note>; the spirit <note>Ruach</note> is from **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>, and that is **Knowledge** <note>Da'at</note> which includes both of them. Regarding this it is said: "And through Knowledge the rooms shall be filled" <note>Proverbs 24:4</note>. And in the *Faithful Shepherd* <note>original: *Ra'aya Meheimna*</note> they said: "In a vision" <note>Numbers 12:6</note>—this is the **Higher Mother** <note>Binah</note>; "To him I make myself known" is through **Knowledge**, the son of *YH* <note>Wisdom and Understanding</note>; "In a dream I speak with him"—this is the latter stage. Thus, Knowledge is Beauty, and it should not be counted twice under any circumstances. Regarding the precedence of the Crown, he challenged this based on what has been clarified: that there is no difference between Crown and Wisdom except for the difference between a Cause and its Effect.

**To reconcile** the opinion of these scholars according to their system, it is possible to say that the emanation of the **Supreme Crown** in its simple existence is the **Exalted Light** mentioned by Rabbi Nehunia ben ha-Kanah. There is much to be said for its precedence according to everyone, in an absolute sense far removed from the concept of time—for even the order of times cannot be imagined regarding it. However, it does not add anything to the levels that descend except as a "Cause to an Effect." Rabbi Shem Tov intended this when he said that it is the Infinite; he did not mean it *is* the Infinite, but rather that it is *like* the Infinite. To it, this is a third aspect of the six accepted aspects in the expansion of every effect, as will be explained in this Gate. Whoever understands our words there will see through the "salvation of God" that it is not meant to be counted—even according to the Sage of blessed memory—except with the "strike of the hammer upon the completion of the work." Regarding this, they interpreted in the *Tikkunim*: "Sanctify to Me every firstborn"—this is the **Supreme Crown**; and **Wisdom**, which is **Israel**, "arose in Thought," as it is said: "And God said, Let there be light." We have already mentioned the partnership of the phrase "Let there be light" with the Crown and Wisdom. "And the Torah is light" refers to **Beauty**, which is **Knowledge**, which is **Israel**. For Knowledge is not a Sefirah in its own right, but rather it is the aspect of the **six extremities** hidden above in the first Sefirot.

# Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 3: Whether the Infinite is the Crown — Pomegranate Juice

...Water—He engraved and carved in it the Throne of Glory, the Wheels <note>Hebrew: *Ophanim*</note>, the Seraphim, the Holy Living Creatures, and the Ministering Angels. From His dwelling place, He established His habitation, as it is said: "He makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire." **Five:** He sealed the Height <note>The upward direction</note> with three letters from the simple ones and fixed them in His Great Name, **Y-H-W** <note>The three-letter version of the Tetragrammaton used in mystical sealing</note>, and with them He sealed the six extremities. He turned upward and sealed it with **Y-H-W**. **Six:** He sealed Below, turned downward, and sealed it with **Y-H-V**. **Seven:** He sealed the East, turned forward, and sealed it with **H-Y-W**. **Eight:** He sealed the West, turned backward, and sealed it with **H-W-Y**. **Nine:** He sealed the South, turned to His right, and sealed it with **Y-W-H**. **Ten:** He sealed the North, turned to His left, and sealed it with **W-Y-H**. These are the Ten Sefirot of "Nothingness" <term>Beli-mah</term>: The Spirit of the Living God, Spirit from Spirit, Water, Fire, Height, Depth, East, West, North, and South. Thus far [the quote]. **And behold**, the commentators said: "One" is the Spirit of the Living God, which is Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>; "Spirit from Spirit" is Understanding <note>Binah</note>; "Water from Spirit" is Lovingkindness <note>Chesed</note>; "Fire from Water" is Strength <note>Gevurah</note>. According to this, it is possible to explain the extremity of "Height" as the Crown <note>Keter</note> or Knowledge <note>Da'at</note>, as mentioned previously. It appears that the letter *Yod* which rules in the Height and Depth is the secret of "from the beginning to the end." In the extremity of the Height, the Higher *He*—the world of Mercy—prevails over the *Waw*, the world of the perimeter which is conducted by Judgment. In the Depth, it is the opposite. And the *He* rules in the East and West... and in the East, simple Lovingkindness prevails over blended Mercy, while in the West it is the opposite. The *Waw* rules in the North and South, which are its branches; in the South, the *Yod* prevails, and in the North, it is the opposite.

...to include Knowledge <note>Da'at</note>, which must be withdrawn and hidden within His Essence and His Wisdom. However, the line of conduct is given to compromises for their preservation and the guidance of the world. For out of His piety in the world, He carved a path for His holy conduct... and the extra perfection in Understanding <note>Binah</note> is the preparation of the attribute of the "Virgin" <note>A kabbalistic reference to the Sefirah of Malkhut/Shekhinah in its potential state within Binah</note> in the foundations... but there is no comprehension, for there is no knowledge to attain its beauty, and the hiddenness is added to its closeness. Understanding is not disqualified by this. All of this is understood through another distinction between the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> and Understanding <note>Binah</note>, for the name is what is called "to him" already, which in its deep contemplation cannot be grasped... <gloss>and enjoying what he understands</gloss>... so that no additional understanding is born at all. In the Creator, may He be blessed, one understands through His contemplation. Here it is understood <gloss>and the repair of the "Holy Day" <note>Yom Kippur</note> which was not there until now</gloss> and it shall be strong, drawn into His Wisdom. And from Understanding—meaning the distinction of the details in the worlds within Understanding—this is the voice that emerges from the foundation of the scribe, and this is the "still small voice." This is enough for the discerning.

### The Gate

**Indeed**, we have seen in the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei Zohar</note> that they attributed His seals to Greatness, Strength, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, and Foundation <note>The six lower Sefirot</note>, as will be explained in the next chapter. Therefore, we are obliged to explain the beginning of the Mishnah <note>The passage from Sefer Yetzirah</note> in another way that agrees with them. This is because "One" is the Crown, in the secret of "One, One and One" which we recite regarding the entry into the inner sanctum on the Day of Atonement <note>Referring to the High Priest's counting of the blood sprinkles: "One, one and one, one and two..."</note>, which are Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding. Here, too, most of what we contemplate regarding the Crown is through Understanding, due to its great hiddenness. **Even** so, we say: the Rabbi taught immediately after this "Spirit from Spirit" regarding Wisdom, as we shall explain; it too is from the side of Understanding. For the three highest [Sefirot] are considered as one before You. We consider the Crown and the Wisdom within Understanding, which are the heads of the known Emanation... and with this, take "Spirit of the Living God" in its plain sense as referring to Understanding. This matter is very clear in the words of the Sage [Moses Cordovero], may his memory be a blessing, at the beginning of the book *Alima*. From him, it will be verified what we explained above: that the Crown counted among us in the general tally of the Sefirot is not the "Wondrous Crown" <note>The Infinite/Ein Sof</note> which is not counted by others. Thus, the dispute is nullified.

**Chapter 6: And behold**, here "Spirit of the Living God" will be explained as referring to this Crown, which is the spirit for Wisdom, from which the "Source of Life" flows. Likewise, "Blessed and Praised be His Name" is attributed in the *Book of Brilliance* <note>Sefer HaBahir</note> to the Supreme Crown. The word **Blessed** <note>Hebrew: *Barukh*</note> fundamentally belongs to the Crown, which is influenced by the source of all life. In the *Tikunim*, regarding the letter *Bet* of the name *Avgitatz*... they said that "In Yah, the Lord is the Rock of Worlds," and where is the letter *Bet*? "Blessed" is my Head, the head and source of all blessings. Because of this, there is no [visible] Wisdom, and it points to the Crown which is the head and fountain of all blessings. Therefore, the *Bet* equals two in numerical value <note>Representing the duality of the hidden source and the first revelation</note>. The secret of the permutation of "Blessed" (*Barukh*) is explained by the acronym: "He rides the heavens to your aid," for He sits upon the wheels of His chariot, as in the words of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah. And this is the same: saying "it is Wisdom and points to the Crown" is the same as "Blessed and Praised be His Name." **Or**, the Teacher may be hinting at the totality of the Emanation in the secret of "There is none holy like the Lord": the letter *Kaf* is the Crown <note>Keter</note>, the *He* is His Name, and He is the "Life of the Worlds" hidden in Wisdom. They are the voice of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> which includes the six extremities, and the Spirit of Understanding <note>Binah</note>, the "still small voice" that is not heard. And the matter of the Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note>, where the hidden *Y-H-W* are in the *Yod* in the secret of "a flame bound to a coal." There they are the Holy Spirit, nursing from the Crown itself. He preceded with the "Voice," which is the essence of the worlds, and the two *He* letters are His dwellings.

**Two:** "Spirit from Spirit"—these are the two repairs of Understanding, as mentioned. Or it may mean "Wisdom from the hidden Wisdom," and by its power, the letters were influenced into Understanding. Or he may mean [Understanding] herself in her paths, which are the physical mass of the earth. **Three** "Mothers" in the letters **A-M-S** <note>Aleph, Mem, Shin</note>, an acronym for Air, Water, and Fire, which are Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding. In the beings of **Y-H-W**, they are Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge, which were unified in Wisdom and its paths, and with them the world was created. Knowledge <note>Da'at</note> is the foundation and the radiance of Mercy and Judgment in their roots—that is, the internal aspect of the line of Mercy, in the secret of the letter *Waw*, a palace for the supreme Holy Air. Then "Holy" shall be said of it, as explained in the book *The Faithful Shepherd* <note>Ra'aya Meheimna, a later layer of the Zohar</note>. **Seven** "Doubles"—**B-G-D K-P-R-T** <note>The seven Hebrew letters that can take a 'dagesh' or dot to change their sound</note>—whose pronunciation is soft or hard, besides the "strong dot" <note>Dagesh Hazak</term> which also exists in the simple form. These are the seven Sefirot of the surrounding world, whose actions are sometimes "Intermediate Judgment" and sometimes "Mercy," besides the "Hard Judgment" hinted at by the strong dot. And the **Twelve** "Simple" letters, whose pronunciation is always the same if they have no dot. They are also called "Simple" because they are the twelve boundaries of the diagonal, extending from Him—not the primary Sefirot. These are composed of Judgment and Mercy, unlike the words of some commentators who say they are simple [free] from Judgment. The spirit for each of them is the "vowel point" drawn from Wisdom to the letters in Understanding. The spirit of the Sefirot is their very essence, which spreads through them to give them life, as explained in the nearby gate. **Three:** "Water from Spirit" is...

It focuses specifically on the role of Da'at (Knowledge) as a bridge and the prohibition against investigating the highest three Sefirot too deeply.</meta>

# Juice of Pomegranates, Gate 3: Whether the Infinite is the Crown — Pomegranate Slice

Understanding is the palace of Wisdom, just as the Name clothes the voices to divide them into thousands <note>original: חלפי אלפים, likely referring to the differentiation of Divine speech into distinct powers</note>. Knowledge <term>Da'at; the mediating principle between Wisdom and Understanding</term> is the palace of the intellect, and from Knowledge the Torah issues forth. It is the source, the foundation, and the shoulder of all transitions. The unique properties of Knowledge allow it to bind Wisdom and Understanding together. This is because Knowledge flows down from the Crown <note>Keter</note> and is purified through it until it reaches the dwelling place of the indwelling presence <note>Shekhinah</note>. Through Knowledge, the Sefirot are held dear and receive from one another. By means of Knowledge, their "two depths" are split—this one receives and that one bestows. It flows and arms them from the emanations of Knowledge, which is hidden forever within the "body," as explained in the *Kuzari* <note>A famous philosophical work by Judah Halevi</note> and by our Sages of blessed memory.

This means that Knowledge extends into the "Ten Extremities," forming a trunk from above to below, resembling a body in relation to the upper realms (just as the upper realms serve as the "knowledge" for the lower ones). There, the chambers and separations are found, as explained by our Sages in the *Kuzari* cycle. This is the secret of Knowledge: it is the flow of the Holy of Holies that descends. It is not (as Rabbi Moshe Cordovero wrote) a separate, independent Sefirah. By understanding this, the words of the Zohar regarding the "Three Crowns" become clear. They reside in the "Small Face" <term>Zeir Anpin; the emotional Sefirot centered around Beauty</term>, which is Harmony <note>Tiferet</note>, and it gives rise to the "Six Children," the six extremities of the spiritual structure. 

It is difficult to grasp because this is the root of all color and form, and it is the most hidden aspect of the soul. The essence is that the unification of Wisdom and Understanding occurs through Knowledge, which is the flow of Harmony <note>Tiferet</note> before its full manifestation. This manifestation is the reception of Knowledge. Just as it is not proper to assign specific counts to the various facets of the soul <note>original: כנפי ענינין</note>, or to the many manifestations of the "Six Directions," so too it is not proper to count Knowledge as a Sefirah standing entirely on its own. 

Furthermore, one whose intention is focused on the ultimate goal of creation and the ascent of the soul must look toward the most ancient and holy source, which is the Supernal Crown <note>Keter Elyon</note>. It is hidden and fortified, called the "Fortress" <note>original: מעוז - Maoz</note> in its specific spelling, which hints at the "Light of Knowledge." This is the support of Understanding within the Supernal Crown, which bestows upon the Small Face strength and vision. Every beginning of revelation is found within the "Measure of the Spark" <note>original: בוצינא דקרדינותא - Botzina de-Kardinuta; a Zoharic term for the primordial spark of creation</note> which expands into the thirty-two paths of wisdom. 

Know that there are two Wisdoms: The first is the Crown in its hidden state, which is the source of all existence. Its paths are unknown to Understanding. The second is the manifest Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, which spreads through all its paths toward Understanding, as explained previously; this is its root. Sometimes, these qualities are combined and the term "Wisdom" is applied to "Understanding" (meaning that Wisdom is sometimes called "lower" when it acts through the vessel of Understanding). This occurs when the light of Understanding is dominant and clings to its source, like a child nursing from its mother. In the Torah portion *Terumah*, Understanding is called "Mother," a term for the human soul. 

(The author brings this as proof that one may inquire about Understanding, though we will establish later in Gate 9 that there are limits, as explained in *Pardes Rimmonim*). 

After speaking of the first three Sefirot, we must clarify the prohibition regarding them. As it says in the portion *Yitro* regarding the verse "Lest they break through to the Lord to gaze": one's mind should not be settled on staring into them. One must turn away three times before looking <note>original: וכאסתכלתא ביה - an Aramaic phrase regarding mystical contemplation</note>. It is written that "you shall see only that which is after," meaning you may look at the "lower" manifestations, the six extremities, but you are forbidden from inquiring into Understanding. The general rule for all three "Firsts" <note>Keter, Chokhmah, Binah</note> is that looking into them is forbidden. For who can grasp the thought that spreads through their purity, or the way God is wise in His Wisdom, or the way He understands through His Understanding? Rashi warns us on the verse "Lest they break through to the Lord" that this alludes to these three crowns...
<meta>catchword: to include</meta>

<column-break/>

...more than this measure: **Chapter 4: We have learned**, "Ten Sefirot of Nothingness—their measure is that they have no end:
A depth of beginning and a depth of end;
A depth of good and a depth of evil;
A depth of height and a depth of below;
A depth of east and a depth of west;
A depth of north and a depth of south.
The singular Master, God, the faithful King, rules them all from His holy dwelling place forever and ever."

# The Intention

According to the commentators, the "depth of beginning" refers to Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> and the "depth of end" refers to Understanding <note>Binah</note>, in the secret of the Jubilee <note>The 50th year, symbolizing the return to the source in Binah</note>. The term "depth" is applied to all of them to indicate they are "without end." Although the text mentions "good and evil," this is not meant literally, but rather in terms of the flow of actions resulting from the powers of Greatness <note>Chesed/Mercy</note> and Strength <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note>. 

"Depth of height and depth of below" refer to the Crown and the Kingdom <note>Keter and Malchut</note>, or Knowledge and the Kingdom, depending on various opinions. There are six adjacent directions: height, below, and the four winds (directions). This aligns with everyone’s view: East is Harmony <note>Tiferet</note>, West is Foundation <note>Yesod</note>, North and South are the Victories <note>Netzach and Hod</note>. North is mentioned before West, and South returns to East. The relationship of West to Foundation is because all spiritual influences gather there to pour out upon the Earth, which is the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note>. 

It is also possible to interpret "West" as the Kingdom when it is directed toward the "East" before its "diminution" <note>A reference to the moon/Malchut losing its original light</note>. In that case, Foundation is the "depth of below," which does not rise above the Kingdom except through the "Sign of the Covenant" <note>the procreative aspect of Yesod</note> when the "Beloveds" <note>the male and female aspects of God</note> unite to emanate souls. Even in a time of Divine favor, this only happens at appointed times. We have already mentioned that the Kingdom comes from the power of the "Female" from the very beginning of Thought, wherein all powers are mixed to take action.

**The Singular Master** is the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), blessed be He. He is called "God, faithful King" <note>original: אל מלך נאמן - El Melekh Ne'eman</note>, even though He cannot be defined by any name, to indicate the necessity of His existence and His eternal providence. The acronym of this phrase is **Amen**. The first "Amen" is an acronym based on the names *Adonai* (Lord) and *Y-H-V-H*, representing Harmony and Kingdom in total unity with the whole of Emanation. There is a *Yod* (numerical value 10) above and a *Yod* below, representing the ten Sefirot. Then the Unity returns to be revealed in detail. Through the name *Adonai*, the hand <note>original: יד - Yad, also meaning 14</note> is revealed in the second "Amen," including the center—for everything is powered by the "Soul of Souls," as mentioned in the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei Zohar</note>.

According to this, it is not far-fetched to focus one's intention when answering "Amen" on the length of its melody. First, on its numerical value, which contains the combination of 14 and the name *Adonai*, encompassing the six directions and the Kingdom. There is also another acronym based on the "Three Mothers" <note>the primary letters Aleph, Mem, Shin</note>: "One, Singular, and Unique" for the Crown; "King, who reigned, who reigns" for Wisdom; "He was, He is, and He will be" for Understanding (which is the letter *Yod* and the letter *Heh*, as is known). Behold, it is good that we hold onto this, and from that also let us not withdraw our hand. For who is it that brings everything close and unifies everything? It is the Cause of Causes. Regarding this, the text says He "rules them all from His holy dwelling place"—this is the Supernal Crown. "I am the Lord, the first," and "until forever and ever" refers to the lack of a "depth of end," implying Understanding is the end of the hidden realm, Foundation is the end of the "body," and Kingdom is the end of all Divine leadership—"and with the last, I am He."

**Chapter 5: Furthermore,** we have learned: "Ten Sefirot of Nothingness: One is the Spirit of the Living God, blessed and praised be the name of the Life of the Worlds. Voice, Spirit, and Word—this is the Holy Spirit. Two: Spirit from Spirit; He carved and engraved within it twenty-two letters—three 'Mothers,' seven 'Doubles,' and twelve 'Simples'—and one Spirit is from them. Three: Water from Spirit; He carved and engraved in them chaos and void, mud and clay; He carved them like a garden bed, set them up like a wall, and covered them like a ceiling. Four: Fire from Water..."

It emphasizes the role of Da'at as a bridge and the mystical significance of the word "Amen" in unifying Divine names.</summary>
