--- Page 44 ---
<meta>This page continues the investigation into the nature of the Sefirot (Divine Emanations), specifically debating whether they are "vessels" (tools) or "essence" (part of God Himself). It builds on the previous discussion of Knowledge (Da'at) as a bridge between the Infinite and the finite.</meta>

-># Pomegranate Slice, Gate 4: Essence and Vessels — Juice of Pomegranates<-

<gloss>The Sefirot are truly like a space <note>original: "challal," referring to a vacuum or vessel</note>. Let the power of the potential be like the power of the actual. And just as the words "pardon" and "justify" are used by our Sages, here too they are justified. Know that the Sefirot are like visionary tools which a worker uses for his work to distinguish between different actions. The Sefirot are prepared for every thing and its opposite. To bring this closer to the intellect, the Sages compared them to the "Will of the Soul," which is the source for all the many powers and thoughts that spread out from it. Even though they are many, their essence is only one. The soul does not change despite the changes in the body that bring the soul's thoughts into action. We are forced to say that they are equal things and their opposites, for if not, there would not be power in it for every individual thing. Therefore, they compared them to the soul's will. Just as the soul spreads through the body, so the Creator—may He be blessed—from His great light, prepared these vessels. Our Sages called them "Sefirot" and "Jewels." These Sefirot emanate from Him; they receive flow <note>term: "shefa" - Divine influence or energy</note> from Him more than all other created beings. They are like a body and soul to one another, but they are not like physical bodies. Rather, they are like light issuing from the eye, which is not a tangible object that can be grasped, for it is nothing but the light seen by the smallness of the heart and formed through the power of imagination. This is the intended meaning of his words in the pamphlet.</gloss>

# Chapter 2
Others have written that the Sefirot are actually parts of the Essence <note>original: "atzmut," referring to God's own being</note>. They argue that the distinction of names, titles, and attributes that we attribute to Him are only from the perspective of those who receive the light, according to their varying capacities.

# Chapter 3
According to the view of Nahmanides <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, 13th-century scholar</note>, who was the first to say they are "vessels" and not "essence," a question arises: If this is so, it would imply that the Blessed One is "wise" only through the Wisdom <note>the Sefirah of Hokhmah</note> that issued from Him. And where did that Wisdom come from? He is the Knower with a knowledge that is inherent to Him. He is the Knower, the Knowledge, and the Known—all are one. This is not the case with other created beings, for when they know something, the knowledge is separate from their essence. <note>The author uses a philosophical proof: in humans, the person (knower), the information (known), and the act of knowing are three different things. In God, they are perfectly unified.</note> For example, when a man knows something, he forms an image in his mind, and three things exist: 1. The intellect that is separate from the object, 2. The Knower who recognizes the object, and 3. The Known object itself. These are three distinct things. But with the Holy One, He is the Knowledge, the Knower, and the Known. His knowledge does not come from observing things outside of Himself; rather, by knowing His own Essence, He knows all the affairs of the world, since their existence is found within Him. He is the "form" <note>or blueprint</note> of all created things. They exist within Him in a subtle, hidden state, like a book that is closed. All created things are like drawings within the Sefirah, and the Sefirah is the vessel. All existing things depend on Him. Thus, He is the Knowledge, the Knower, and the Known. This is the secret of Knowledge. This is what is meant by "By His hand the earth was founded"—through the hand of the Sefirot, which are the vessels and tools of creation. If this is so, our prayers should be directed to the Sefirot? Heaven forbid! Rather, the prayer is directed through the "Infinite" <note>Ein Sof</note> which is hidden within them. If we pray only to the vessels, there would be a change in His will, heaven forbid.

<column-break/>

# Pomegranate Slice
All thoughts, whether good or evil, and the multitude of actions and their differences are carried out through the body, which brings thoughts into action. Despite this, there is no physical "body" in the Sefirot, heaven forbid, nor any of the occurrences or limitations of a body. All these descriptions are merely metaphors and allegories. They are types of light, like the light that comes from the eye, which is not a tangible thing. The sight achieved after the light is emitted is captured by the thought-image of the heart and formed in the imaginative faculty. Some have compared this to a spark of the sun and its light; the light is a property of the sun, not the sun's essence itself. So too, the Emanation <note>term: "Atzilut" - the realm of the Sefirot</note> is a property of the Emanator. He added that the "Curtains" <note>term: "Parsaot" - spiritual barriers or extensions</note> mentioned in the books of the Chariot <note>Hekhalot/Merkavah literature</note> regarding the Sefirot refer to "spreading out," as in the verse "He spreads His wings to the south."

# But
It must not be imagined that He, blessed be He, is "Wise" through a newly created wisdom, heaven forbid, or that He "understands" through an external understanding. Nor should one think that He rewards and punishes in a way that suggests He has "abandoned the earth" to the conduct of the vessels. Heaven forbid that the holy ones in the land should think so; not one of the scholars of truth and justice would err in this. However, others have insisted on the legal opinion that the Sefirot are the very Essence of Divinity. They say that the change in names and the number of Sefirot does not imply multiplicity in the Emanator, because these names are not attributed to Him except in relation to the "receivers" <note>humanity</note> and their varying perspectives. We shall debate and judge this together.

# Let Them Say
Let those who fear the Lord say: if they are just one essence, what then is the need for unifying "measure with measure" <note>referring to the balance of Divine attributes</note>, such that this one receives and that one bestows? Who placed "capacities" within a single essence that are affected by one another? And where is the "unification" that is completed through our prayers and the intentions of our commandments? From where does this unity awaken, and where does it go when the Indwelling Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> is in exile? Where does it return when it "knocks for its beloved"? And what of the plumbing of the "channels" <note>spiritual conduits</note>? How would we establish the many bodies of Torah law? Furthermore, regarding the existence of the attributes themselves: who forces us to attribute a "number" to them in a place where we ought to cease counting, for there is no number there? The truth is what the Sages explained in *Exodus Rabbah* on the verse "And they shall say to me, what is His name?": His titles and names change according to His actions. This is the transition from His creatures. Open the "First Gate" and you will find the "Faithful Shepherd" <note>Ra'aya Meheimna, a section of the Zohar</note>; hear it and know it for yourself.

# Chapter 2
It is clearly explained in the *Zohar* and the *Tikkunim*, and it is simple among all the wise, that even the "Supernal Crown" <note>Keter Elyon</note> is "black" <note>unfathomable</note> before the "Cause of Causes." It is not an attribute or a name. There is not a single letter or vowel point in the entire Torah capable of containing or even hinting at His glory and greatness. Even the first letter of the Name <note>the 'Yud' of the Tetragrammaton</note> is attributed to Wisdom <note>Hokhmah</note>, as is known; it only hints at the Crown through the "upper tip" of the letter. This is like the story of the two children who were tested by their teacher to see if they knew to whom they were praying: one pointed to the roof and one pointed to the sky. From this premise, a great difficulty arises: what will the Sages of Israel answer regarding calling Him by the Four-Letter Name, the Great and Awesome Name that is not pronounced—the "Proper Name" <note>Shem HaEtzem</note>?

# And Every
Wise-hearted person will admit the truth: there is no way to turn right or left in answering this difficulty except by what we are accustomed to learn and teach—that the Name belongs to the *essence of the Emanation*, not the essence of the Emanator, heaven forbid. It refers to the inner part of the Emanation, which is the soul...

<summary>This page debates whether the Sefirot are God's actual essence or merely "vessels" He uses to interact with the world. It concludes that while God is unified, the names and attributes we use refer to the system of Emanation (Atzilut) rather than His unknowable, infinite self.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the discussion of the Infinite (Ein Sof) and the Crown (Keter) in Gate 3 into the specific mechanics of the Sefirot through the permutations of Divine Names, concluding with the start of Gate 4 regarding the debate of Essence versus Vessels.</meta>

->עסיס רמונים (Juice of Pomegranates) — Gate 3: Whether the Infinite is the Crown — פלח הרמון (Pomegranate Slice)<-

She is Understanding <note>the Sefirah of Binah</note>, to which the verse "Let the waters be gathered" (Genesis 1:9) refers. These waters receive the form of existing things more than the Spirit <note>the Sefirah of Ruach/Tiferet</note>. Therefore, within them were engraved "Chaos and Void" <note>original: "Tohu va-Bohu"</note> and "Mire and Clay," which correspond to the four letters of the Divine Name <note>Y-H-V-H</note>. In the Midrash *Bereshit Rabbah*, they asked: What is *Bohu*? It is the thing that clothes the *Tohu*. They said that *Tohu* is the "green line" that encircles the world from above, for the circle relates to the form of a simple letter *Yod* in its thinness. "Mire" <note>original: "Refesh"</note> refers to waters that thicken through the revelation of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> more than Understanding <note>Binah</note>. Thicker than both is "Clay" <note>original: "Tit"</note>, an allusion to the final letter *He* <note>the Sefirah of Malchut</note>. In each of these is included the reality of the "six extremes" <note>the six spatial directions/Sefirot from Hesed to Yesod</note>, which are like a garden bed, a plaster floor, and four walls. **Four** are fire, water, wind <note>or spirit</note>, and Sovereignty <note>Malchut</note>. Lower Strength <note>Gevurah</note> is influenced by the waters of Understanding and preceded the secret of the Sabbath, which existed before the world. This is also because of their existence and the kinship she has with Understanding <note>Binah</note>, which is composed of all the worlds, and Sovereignty <note>Malchut</note> is also her offspring. To wake us to this, he mentioned them near her, and from their rule He founded His dwelling, as it is written: "Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters, who makes the clouds His chariot, who walks on the wings of the wind... who makes spirits His messengers, flaming fire His ministers." What is written afterward? "He established the earth on its foundations, so that it should never be moved." We shall speak of this further with the help of Heaven.

### Chapter 7
It is stated in the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei HaZohar</note>: *Ehyeh* <note>Divine name meaning "I Will Be"</note> is *Y-H-V*, and it includes the six sides with which He seals the six directions. These are: **Y-H-V, H-V-Y, V-H-Y, V-Y-H, H-Y-V, Y-V-H.**
**Y-H-V** is taken by the Right, which is Kindness <note>Hesed</note>, and with it He seals Wisdom; through it, "He who wishes to become wise should turn South."
**H-V-Y** is taken by the Left, which is Strength <note>Gevurah</note>, and with it He seals Wealth; through it, "He who wishes to become wealthy should turn North."
**V-H-Y** turns toward the East and is taken by the Middle Pillar <note>Tiferet</note>, and He seals with it.
**V-Y-H** is taken by the Right Thigh <note>Netzach</note>; it looks upward and He seals Life with it.
**H-Y-V** is taken by the Left Thigh <note>Hod</note>; it looks downward and He seals Sustenance with it. It looks upward toward Wisdom and is bound to the Right Thigh, and with it He seals Sustenance.
**Y-V-H** turns toward the West, toward the Righteous One <note>Yesod</note>, which is the "Mixture" where all the hosts are mixed. It is completed in the eight letters <note>an allusion to the combination of YHVH and ADNY</note>. These are the eight letters through which He is called "Eight Worlds," and the Righteous One <note>Yesod</note> is called "Living of the Worlds" <note>original: "Chai Alamin"</note>. All these existences hang from the Supernal Mother <note>Binah</note>, who is Life; the Righteous One is called "Living" after her name. The "Living Creatures of the Chariot" <note>Chayot HaMerkavah</note> are named after her because the Supernal Mother is Life, as it is said: "She is a Tree of Life to those who hold fast to her." She is the Chariot for Wisdom. Sovereignty <note>Malchut</note> is there the letter *He*, and through her He is called *Y-D-V* in completion. **The intention** is that the name *Ehyeh* <note>A-H-Y-H</note> is the clothing for the first three letters of the Essential Name <note>Y-H-V of YHVH</note>, and *Adonai* <note>A-D-N-Y</note> is for the final *He*. The order of the Kingdom is straight: Greatness <note>Hesed</note>, Strength <note>Gevurah</note>, and Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>. It then returns in Victory <note>Netzach</note>, Splendor <note>Hod</note>, and Foundation <note>Yesod</note>, for Foundation also emerges from the lower world in the secret of Benjamin. Note that Kindness <note>Hesed</note> causes the Supernal *He* <note>Understanding</note> to prevail over the *Vav* <note>Beauty</note> and Foundation. Conversely, the "Fear of Isaac" <note>Gevurah</note>, whose judgment is strong, causes the "Blended One" to prevail over simple Kindness. Splendor <note>Hod</note> is the opposite; Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> inclines toward Kindness and is aroused toward it to strengthen its action, and they subdue Judgment with their labors in the secret of "Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel," and likewise "I will remember My covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham." Victory <note>Netzach</note> overcomes with Kindness and Mercy against Splendor <note>Hod</note>, and the occupation with this is for the completion of the Union. Therefore, the "seals" <note>permutations</note> differ from the order of the Mishnah, as we are dealing here with the Emanation <note>Atzilut</note> in pairs, and their inclination toward Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy—each according to his gift. **In any case**, we have learned that the essence of the "seals" is in the World of Surrounding, and not otherwise. According to this, "Height and Depth" in our Mishnah are explained as Victory <note>Netzach</note> and Splendor <note>Hod</note>. This is also implied by their statement regarding "This is the book of the generations of Adam": four letters are clothed in four colors—White for *Yod*, Red for *He*, Green for *Vav*, and Black for the final *He*. This Name refines the colors in every place, and it is what draws the lines of the forehead in this likeness: *Y-D-V*. These four marks of the lines are the Depth of Height, Depth of Below, Depth of East, and Depth of West. The Teacher also placed the Victories <note>Netzach/Hod</note> before Greatness, Strength, and Beauty, whether speaking in the language of men regarding "Up and Down" and the "Four Directions," or whether looking toward Wisdom and Understanding. **In this way**, we shall also explain the Mishnah of "Depths": Beginning and End <note>Keter and Malchut</note>, Good and Evil. This is not literal, but refers to their rooting in Wisdom and Understanding. Furthermore, do not read "Evil" <note>original: "Ra"</note> but "Friend and Companion" <note>original: "Re'a"</note>, for it is known that "Will" <note>Re'uta</note> and "Heart's Desire" are both in Understanding. The kingship in the seals of the letter *Yod* over Victory and Splendor is the secret that "the matter depends on the filling." The letter *He* is the chamber of their conception with East and West, and the letter *Vav* is the body and the essence of the arms, North and Right <note>South</note>. They have already explained that "South" <note>Darom</note> means "Dwells on High" <note>Dar-Rom</note>, for the reality of Kindness is at the head, above; this is the relationship between "Height" and "South" according to all explanations. "North" <note>Tzafon</note> means "Hidden" <note>He'elam</note>, for the perfection of Judgment is in its being hidden from the lower beings and its contention in the Supernal roots, the Lands of the Living.

# Fourth Gate: Essence and Vessels

### Chapter 1: Because the Creator, may He be blessed, is One in absolute simplicity, multiplicity, change, and boundary do not apply to His Essence.

And souls, and the Torah is interpreted through the Sefirot in Judgment and Mercy, Right and Left.
And the like. Some commentators have established and received that there is no aspect of divinity in them.
The Emanator, blessed be He, despite the power of the Emanator being in the emanated—behold, the Sefirot
are like equal vessels for every thing and its opposite, which the Craftsman acts through
by His will, and their actions are without end. The analogy is to the Will of the Soul
which is in everything...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Divine Name and its relationship to the lower worlds, specifically transitioning into Gate 4 which addresses the fundamental Kabbalistic debate: are the Sefirot (Divine emanations) the actual essence of God or merely tools/vessels used by God?</meta>

# Slice of the Pomegranate &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gate 4: Essence and Vessels &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Juice of Pomegranates

His letters are not [mere] letters, Heaven forbid, but He is the Root and the Beginning of all existences and sources in their various aspects. Within them are the branches of the Absolute Will to be called by a Name—to benefit "the other" <note>referring to created beings outside the Divine essence</note>. This is what is called the **Infinite** <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note> in truth, for the Possessor of the Name obviously has no end, just as He has no beginning.

**Therefore**, Maimonides <note>The 12th-century philosopher Rabbi Moses ben Maimon</note> did not mention the eternity of God, blessed be He, among the "Principles of Faith," because it is obvious that He is eternal since He is Primordial <note>original: "Kadmon"</note>. It is well known that every primordial being is eternal, but not every eternal being is primordial, for many created beings will be eternal by the Will of the Creator. These matters are simple in themselves and self-evident, even though those who disagree with Maimonides did not descend to their depths, and not out of wisdom. Here too, His Name and His Will are the beginning of [the Sefirot]. We need to make known that they have a beginning from Him, which is a "willed" beginning and not a "temporal" one, but they have no end or essence <note>limitation</note> at all.

**And** with what we have explained, you will not find difficulty in the fact that the **Crown** <note>the highest Sefirah, Keter</note> is often described as the "Infinite." Behold, we do not describe the Absolute Primordial One in any way at all, and we refrain from this to teach ourselves that it is impossible to contemplate or seek Him out except through His Name and His Will alone. Even in this, we have chosen [to speak] only from the perspective of Him being the Infinite, with all warnings set and guarded, Heaven forbid, regarding His loftiness. Even though it is appropriate for the "Supreme Crown" due to its [closeness], we seek out whatever is possible for us in the heights of the heavens regarding the "Contraction of the **Divine Presence**" <note>original: "Tzimtzum Shekhinah"</note>. The word *Shekhinah* is the numerical value <note>Gematria</note> of *Rakia* (Firmament) when adding the word itself and its four letters, which was hinted at in *Midrash Rabbah* regarding the departure of the Divine Presence to the seven firmaments and its return through the merit of the righteous. All such matters, wherever they appear, are "ancient things" <note>profound secrets</note>. Heaven forbid that we should speak, or even contemplate, these matters regarding the Possessor of the Absolute Will, who is exalted above all blessing and praise. The term "Infinite" in each of the inquiries we are permitted to describe Him with requires interpretation upon interpretation. Wisdom rests in an understanding heart; "chapter headings" <note>concise summaries</note> will suffice for such a person. For as much as the intellect rises, we must all the more keep a muzzle on our mouths. In these deep inquiries, brevity is beautiful.

**Behold**, the four-letter Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, YHVH</note> is called the "Name of the Essence," blessed be He. It is the source for all the Names; it is the Essence and the Soul to them, while they are "vessels" for it. When we mention "Essence" (*Atzmut*), even in the heights of the world, it is not the Absolute Essence, but rather the Will—which is the "hiddenness of the Name" and nothing else. The intention is the absolute hiddenness of the Great Name in its Root, regarding which we have learned: "He and His Name are One" <note>original: "Hu u-shmo echad"</note>. This is not grasped by us, nor even by Michael the Great Prince <note>the Archangel</note>, even in the meditation of the heart, let alone in the movement of the lips or the visualization of letters. Behold, the "Vessels" for Him are the hidden souls of the Sefirot and the essence of all the worlds, which are not grasped even in the heavens above. The totality of these awesome Vessels—which are not "vessels" except in a very distant, metaphorical sense—is nothing other than the intellectual recognition in which the four letters are prepared to move. From this recognition are drawn the "fillings" <note>original: "miluim," the spelling out of letter names</note> that arose in Thought. The filling that precedes its companion in level and hiddenness—which are the same thing—is considered the soul to its companion.

<column-break/>

*...coloring according to its action: this one white and that one red. Your sign for this is: "the changer returns." This refers to the cycles of change that spread through His essence. For [the Infinite], Heaven forbid that there should be "color" at all, for they are simple, without change or affectation. He does not act through the change of the Vessels that are distinct in their actions. In a way, there is no change in the Essence that spreads through the [Sefirotic] essence, except in its source regarding the "outpourings"—meaning, according to the receivers and the power relative to itself.*

**Further**, another parable: consider the sun mentioned [shining] through a window. If its path passes through ten glass lamps <note>term: "Ashashiyot" - colored glass vessels</note> of different colors, even though the pure radiance has no color, through its passage it will imitate the appearance of the changing glass lamps. In truth, there is no change in the sun at all. Understand the Essence's relationship to the lights through the change of the glass lamps. So is the matter with the Sefirot: (there is no color in the spreading Essence at all, neither Judgment nor Mercy, but through its spreading into the Sefirot—which are the glass lamps blended with their colors—Judgment and Mercy will drip from them), just as was explained in the parable of water. According to the Kindness <note>Hesed</note>, the glass lamps or Vessels will be completed, and thus their light will increase according to their likeness and their internal Sefirah.

Behold, the "Limit" exists only from the perspective of the Vessels receiving Him. We do not intend "limit" except regarding the limit of the actions as they are perceived by us; but there is no limit in their power relative to us. The change of thought regarding them—from the perspective of the order of action perceived by us—is not from their actual essence, but through our refinement in Creation, Necessity in Formation, and Knowledge in Action <note>referring to the four worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah</note>. It is the difficulty of the change and the limit and the praise that we perceive in thought, to "lessen" or "enlarge" them and to understand and judge as He wills, blessed be He. When we say "lessen" or "enlarge," we mean to elevate that which is at a level of "one tenth" <note>referring to Malchut</note> so it is explained at a higher level, such as the Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> and the "offspring of the world" like the secret of Knowledge <note>Da'at</note> reaching up to the Crown; or to "lessen" in the sense of [the moon being told] "Go and diminish yourself," and so on. Study this carefully.

**Behold**, now according to what has been explained, there are two types of Sefirot, containing "arrangements" and "vessels." The foundation of their order is like a Body to a Soul.
1. The Internal: This is the Intention; it is the Spiritual Sefirah. it is like the active force in [physical] chemistry, and it is the Light that spreads through the Essence of the Infinite, blessed be He.
2. The External: These are the Vessels. They exist so the Intention can perform its actions. For the essence of beneficial action depends on the Soul, even though it is filtered through the Vessels.
Parable (Heaven forbid [the comparison]): The Intention spreads through the limbs of the body. An action of the hand does not depend on its physical source alone—for many have hands but cannot do good—because the vitality of the Intention does not spread through it. Rather, the essence of the action depends on the Soul traveling through the living hand. Nevertheless, their actions are not equal; this one performs a refined action and that one a different one. The change in actions comes from the change in the external limbs that carry out the actions. For when the Soul is filtered through the limit of the limbs, it acts through holy governance and contemplation. In the power of a limb... [text continues regarding the soul and body metaphor].*

# Juice of Pomegranates &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gate 4: Essence and Vessels &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Slice of the Pomegranate

...within the **Sefirot** <term>Sefirot: the ten divine emanations or "numbers" through which the Infinite interacts with creation</term>, and they are to Him like vessels for the actions that flow from Him into the world of separation and below. And because the Sage <note>referring to Rabbi Moses Cordovero</note>, may his memory be a blessing, in his book *Pardes Rimmonim* <note>original: "Sefer Pardes Rimmonim" or "S.P.R."</note>, Gate 19, Chapter 1, distanced the association of the Great Name <note>the four-letter Name of God, the Tetragrammaton</note> even from the essences of the world of **Emanation** <note>original: "Atzilut"</note>, I must caution the reader. He spoke correctly according to his own method in every place throughout this inquiry that we are explaining. This is famous throughout all his books, and in this Gate specifically, one should look at what he explained in Gate 5, Chapter 19: that the name of the Essence is called such because this Name includes and encompasses the entire world of Emanation in a complete, true, and established unity. 

**However**, for one who is not satisfied by this—since the emanations are "renewed" <note>meaning they have a beginning in time or logic</note> while the Name is "primordial" <note>original: "Kadmon," meaning existing before all else</note>, as we have learned: "Before the world was created, there was only He and His Name alone"—even though many explain this statement in different ways: you too should say to him that we do not attribute the Great Name except to the **Will** <note>original: "Ratzon"</note> insofar as He desires to bestow good. This Name, too, is nothing other than the source of all existences and names, as will be explained in the upcoming chapter. It is not a name that any other being can grasp at all, not even the emanated beings, except through a distant example, similar to how He performed wonders of kindness with us by depicting it in the Torah. The Torah comes to hint to us about the "grasping" of one of the emanated beings, such as **Beauty** <note>original: "Tiferet," often abbreviated as T"T</note> with the vowel points of the Name, or **Understanding** <note>original: "Binah"</note> with the vowel points of the name *Elohim*. This is sufficient for now.

**And here** I am instructing and proceeding: for in every place where the Sages taught "Essence and Vessels," the intention is the **Essence** of the attribute <note>Middah</note> we are discussing, and its **Vessel**. It is accurate to say that what is "Essence" for one attribute may be a "Vessel" and "Garment" for the attribute above it. I have been accustomed to this from the day I reached intellectual maturity with my colleagues, both old and young, to sweeten the secret of Essence and Vessels: call them "Will and Utterance," or "Sephirah and Utterance." These are "Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us" as King David, peace be upon him, said. "Wonders" are the Sefirot, and "Thoughts" are the Utterances. The intention in all this is the hidden and the revealed aspects of Emanation. I have spoken well; if you wish, say it is a logical explanation, or if you wish, use the verse: "Then He saw it and declared it; He established it and searched it out, and He said..." (Job 28:27-28). "Declaring" <note>original: "Sippur," related to "Sephirah"</note> comes first, then "Saying" <note>original: "Amirah," related to "Ma'amar" or Utterance</note>, and between them is preparation and limitation. Thus, even the "declaring" in our context is not prepared or limited. We are destined to explain this further in Gate 11 with God's help. This is the essential difference between the "Ten Sefirot" and the "Ten Utterances" which the Sages taught in the language of the Mishnah in *Sefer Yetzirah* and *Ethics of the Fathers* <note>original: "Masechet Avot"</note>. Everything is corrected and received with Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge—not as a metaphor or a shared term, but as specific words for specific inquiries; and the word of the Lord in our mouth is truth.

### Chapter 3: And What 
Even now, I have not come to obscure but to explain and to show the precious glory of the greatness of the Name of the Essence that preceded all worlds, as we mentioned. For indeed, "His Name" <note>original: "Shmo," Shin-Mem-Vav</note> in numerical value <note>term: Gematria</note> equals **Will** <note>original: "Ratzon," Resh-Tzadi-Vav-Nun. Both equal 346</note>. This is calculated with the number emerging from the Name itself: **Y-H** times **Y-H** is 225, and **V-H** times **V-H** is 121, which together in numerical value equal "His Name" <note>15x15 + 11x11 = 346</note>. It is known that "He and His Name are One," and "His Will is One." This Name, which is His Will, is unified in His thought, blessed be He. Not only does it have no vowel points—for we do not know how the thought spreads through it—it does not even have [standard] letters.

...in our hope for the "Living, Living" <note>original: "Chai Chai," referring to the source of life</note>. ### Chapter 4: And the Truth
The Infinite <note>original: "E.S." for Ein Sof</note>, blessed be He, is in absolute simplicity, such that it is impossible to attribute or depict in Him any boundary, or... or impression, or change. It is impossible to grasp Him... not even through letters or vowel points... and not in the writing of His existence... what is known is that when the emanation was emanated, the Infinite, blessed be He, emanated ten Sefirot which are of the Essence unified in Him. He and they are one, like the flame bound to the coal. These Sefirot are the Soul and the thoughts... the vowel points in the names which are like vessels. It is as if one said that the Infinite, blessed be He, is the Essence... and they are the vessels. An analogy is made to the celestial spheres <note>original: "Galgalim"</note>, but the Sages agreed that they are bodies, even though they are spiritual... and they have a soul... and the sphere is the body that covers it, and the light is its soul... as it is known from the memory of the Sages. And behold, according to this, they are like the "Eyes of the Spheres"... the physical spheres and the Divine Intelligence that spreads within them. This is the way to imagine the Sefirot. In the **Zohar**, it distinguishes between the essence and the vessels with this language: "He made in it many forms and carved in it all engravings." The Essence is the "spreading" which is like a soul, using the language of "blowing" and "form." The vessels are described with the language of "carving." And according to the vitality, the Wisdom <note>Chochmah</note> will be divided... the first Sephirah which is a garment for the inner one... which is called Wisdom... and the middle one is a garment for it, and so on for the rest of the levels of the Sefirot. And then there would be change in the attributes... so that it would be accurate to say He is divided into parts... but the change and the division are only in the external Sefirot. (And we can support this matter so it will be accepted by those who contemplate).

->**Analogy**<-
Consider a spring of water that spreads into vessels (which are) colored: this one red, this one white, and this one green. Even though the water is simple and devoid of any color, it will be divided in the vessels, each one according to its color. Thus it will appear to the observer as "red water" due to the change in the appearance of the vessels, but not in reality. But in the spring itself, there is no change of appearance at all, only in the vessels. So too with the Sefirot: the vessels are the Sefirot that conduct the world—Kindness, Strength, Beauty, etc.

# Juice of Pomegranates &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gate 4: Essence and Vessels &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Slice of the Pomegranate

Its letters are not [mere] letters, God forbid; rather, He is the root and the beginning for all existences, manifested in various forms. Within these forms are the branches of the Absolute Will, which desires to be called by a name in order to benefit "the other" <note>referring to created beings outside of God's simple unity</note>. This is what is truly called **Ein Sof** <term>Ein Sof: literally "Without End," referring to God as He is in Himself, beyond all human comprehension</term>, for it is obvious that the Master of the Name has no end, just as He has no beginning.

**Therefore**, Maimonides <note>original: "the Rambam"</note> did not list the eternity of God (Blessed be He) among the essential principles of religion. It is self-evident that He is eternal because He is Primordial <note>original: "Kadmon," meaning first and uncaused</note>. It is well known that every primordial being is eternal, but not every eternal being is primordial—for many created things will be eternal by the will of the Creator. These matters are simple in themselves and established in their place, even if those who challenged Maimonides did not reach the depths of his wisdom. Here too, His Name and His Will—which are the beginning for them <note>the Sefirot</note>—must be understood as having a "willed" beginning from Him, not a temporal one, and having no end or essence of conclusion at all.

**And** with what we have explained, we leave no doubt as to why the **Keter** <term>Keter: "Crown," the first and highest of the ten Sefirot, representing the Divine Will</term> is often described as the **Ein Sof**. Note that we do not describe the Absolute Primordial Being with the term "Forms" <note>original: "Panim," literally "Faces"</note>. We avoid this to teach ourselves that it is impossible to contemplate or seek Him except through His Name and His Will alone. Even in this, God did not choose [to be known] except from the perspective of being the **Ein Sof**, with all the lights arranged and preserved—God forbid [we should think otherwise] regarding His loftiness. Even the "Supernal Crown" <note>original: "Keter Elyon"</note> is only worthy of seeing a "Yod" <note>the smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing a point of beginning</note> of His. All that is possible for us in the heights of the heavens is to seek the **Tzimtzum** <term>Tzimtzum: the Divine "contraction" or "withdrawal" that allows space for a finite world to exist</term> of the **Shekhinah** <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence as it dwells within the world</term>. The numerical value <note>original: "Gematria"</note> of *Shekhinah* equals that of *Rakia* <note>original: "Firmament"</note> [when calculated] with the word itself and its four letters, as hinted at in the Midrash Rabbah regarding the withdrawal of the *Shekhinah* to the firmaments and its return through the merit of the righteous. These are "ancient things" <note>a phrase used to denote deep, hidden mysteries</note>, and it is forbidden for a mortal to even contemplate these matters regarding the Master of the Absolute Will, who is exalted above all blessing and praise. The term **Ein Sof** used in every inquiry we are permitted to describe requires explanation upon explanation. In the heart of the understanding person, wisdom shall rest, sufficing for these main principles; for as the intellect rises, we must all the more guard our mouths from speaking, and in these deep inquiries, brevity is beautiful.

### **Behold**, the Four-Letter Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, Y-H-W-H</note> is called the **Essence-Name**. It is the source of all names; it is the essence and the soul to them, while they are vessels to it. When we mention "Essence," even in the highest heights of the world, the "World" is not the Absolute, but rather His power—which is the hiddenness of the Name and nothing else. The intention is the absolute hiddenness of the Great Name in its root, where we have learned that **"He and His Name are One."** This is not grasped by us, nor even by Michael the Great Prince, even in the thoughts of the heart—certainly not in the movement of the lips or the drawing of letters. Behold, the "vessels" for Him are the hidden souls of the **Sefirot** and the essence for all the worlds, which is not grasped even in the heavens above. The totality of these awesome vessels—which are only called "vessels" in conjunction with the light—is nothing other than the conceptual expression in which the four letters are ready to move. From this flow the "fillings" <note>original: "Milluyim," a method of expanding a name by spelling out its letters</note> that arose in the Thought. One filling precedes another in rank and hiddenness, for they are one thing, distinguished only by the change of the letters themselves.

### **Chapter 4: One** word of the Supreme God, that in His Will, may He be blessed...

<column-break/>

<gloss>Protected according to His action. Therefore, it is explained that the Sefirot are the lights spreading from His hiddenness, may He be blessed. They are like water that has no inherent color, for they are simple and without change or affectation. They do not act with the change of the vessels that the vessels engage in through their actions. At their root, there is no change in the spreading Essence, but only at the core of the thought—meaning, according to the recipients and not according to Himself. **Another** analogy for the subject: like water passing through ten differently colored glasses. Even though the change [of color] is seen in this one or that one, the water itself does not change its nature through the change of the glasses. Since the truth is that the change is not found in the Essence itself, but only relative to its connection to the vessels. All the changes of the Sefirot (for in the spreading Essence there is no "Judgment" and no "Mercy," but through its spreading into the Sefirot—which are like glasses of different colors—it is judged as Judgment or Mercy) are like the water descending. According to the glass, the glasses or vessels will be called "red" or "white," but their inner simple nature remains. Behold, the color is only from the perspective of the vessels that contain it. The intention regarding the "Glory" <note>the Divine manifestation</note> is only regarding the limit of the actions that reach us. But within themselves, they have a limit from our perspective—this limit and this change which shifts from one side to another is the total action that reaches us. This comes from their own essence through their being clothed in their vessels. Their shape and form are made, and through them, the change and the limit and the qualities are seen. These are placed for "repair" <note>original: "tikkun"</note>, or to distinguish them, or to direct them, or to diminish them as He wills, blessed be He. The word "repair" or "distinguish" means to elevate that which is at the level of the "Ten" to be at a more hidden level (as in the matter of the Foundation <note>original: "Yesod"</note>, the T, the M <note>mystical letter references</note>) and the inclusion of the world in the secret of Knowledge <note>original: "Da'at"</note> up to the Crown <note>original: "Keter"</note>. This "repair" is like [the teaching], "Go and diminish yourself," and similar things. **And behold**, now according to what has been explained regarding the two types of Sefirot: the primary ones are the vessels, united as a person is with his body. The inner part is the "Neshama" <note>the highest level of the soul</note>, which is the internal Sefirah, the power that acts within them. This is the spreading light of the Essence of the **Ein Sof**, may He be blessed. The second part is the external, which are the vessels, and they are drawn from the aforementioned Neshama to perform its actions. For the core of the action is not dependent on the soul alone, even though it is distinct from all vessels. An analogy: the light of the soul spreading through the limbs of the material body. If there were no action of the hand, it would not be dependent on the temperament of the hand, for how could hands act if the life-force were not spreading through them? Yet, the core of the action is in the soul that necessitates it. Nevertheless, there is no change in the soul—the soul of the eye is not [different from] the soul of the hand, even though their actions are not equal. This one is for seeing, and that one is for touching. For the change of actions comes from the change of the external limbs that originate the actions. When the soul changes with the vessel and remains, the limbs act according to the power of the soul. Behold, if one were to move the power of life from the hand to the leg, it would not act correctly because only the power of the soul that flows to the hand has the power of grasping. And so is the comparison to the Sefirot: they are like the comparison of body and soul. The soul is the Essence spreading in the Sefirah, and it is the intention within them to act. Its form is that if it were to stand alone without the Sefirot, it would be called by one name; but through all the changes of the Sefirot, they are like a body without a soul, and from [their union] are drawn the actions of the internal soul.</gloss>

It references the seminal work of Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (the Ramak) and his commentary, *Pardes Rimonim*.</meta>

# Juice of Pomegranates &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gate 4: Essence and Vessels

In this summary, it is proper to provide you with a lesson according to his view, for the whole matter is like a book of measurements and laws—the law of those who do good and the law of those who do evil, a fortiori <note>original: "kal v'chomer"</note>. Through this, the philosophers would [mistakenly] remove the Blessed Truth from the world. This is the opinion of the philosophers, and in their folly—Heaven forbid—they differ from the view of the Ramak <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (1522–1570), a leading kabbalist in Safed</note>, of blessed memory, as is known to all who see his books and sources. Therefore, he takes the form of the hand <note>a metaphor for the Sefirot</note> and calls it "the hand of His gaze." Regarding the opinion of the book that forbids [associating] the Essence with anything else, neither light nor feeling—this man <note>the philosopher</note> does not feel, etc. In his haste, he replies that there is no need for **Malchut** <term>Malchut: "Kingship," the final Sefirah</term> to receive from **Tiferet** <term>Tiferet: "Beauty/Harmony," the central Sefirah</term>, nor is there any additional end to be taken from another, just as our physical matter would not be ignited as a flame... and this is the reason for the levels of the worlds and the order of the emanations and their unification. This is the goal and the secret that Israel labors over: what do we occupy ourselves with? (This section speaks of the foundation of the Sefirot). Furthermore, according to his view, even the form of the Sefirah only exists at the time of action, and when the action is withdrawn, the Sefirah is withdrawn, a fortiori. The end of the matter, according to his words, is that the Sefirah has no true existence in reality, etc. However, we shall not let this diminish our speech, for we have already established the crown of this knowledge: that "these and those are the words of the living God" <note>a Talmudic phrase meaning both conflicting views have spiritual validity</note>, and through Him, the simple shall live.

**Chapter 4: And the Truth** regarding the Infinite <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note> is that He is absolutely simple, to the point that we cannot establish or recognize in Him any boundary, measure, affect, or change. We cannot praise Him with any name, nor with any attribute, letter, or point—not in writing, nor in His presence prior to emanation, nor in the hiddenness of His existence before the emanation of Atzilut <term>Atzilut: The World of Emanation, the highest of the four worlds</term>. However, what we must know is that at the beginning of the Emanation, the Infinite (Blessed be He) emanated ten Sefirot in which His Name and Essence are unified. There, everything is a complete unity. These Sefirot are there like a drop within the sea (as is written). The points in the names there are the "vessels" in Man; it is said that their essence is spirit and soul. The "vessels" are a parable for the celestial spheres; all the sages agree that they are bodies with living, spiritual souls—spiritual power and vitality within each one. This was his labor, and it atones for the honor of God. Behold, according to the truth, there are two types of unique spheres: the first part are the spiritual spheres, and the second are the "souls" that spread within them. Such is the way of the metaphor for the Sefirot. **In the Zohar**, the emanation of the Essence and the Vessels is described in this language: "He carved in it many carvings, and engraved in it all bodies." Thus, the Essence that spreads out is the likeness of the soul (in the language of "carving"), and the Vessels are the language of "engraving." In truth, the Vessels—meaning the known Sefirah which is a garment for the inner light—only occur because the inner light, which is called its father in vitality, and the engraving is a garment for it. So too for the other attributes of the Sefirot. This does not cause a change in the Emanator, nor a division within Him that would justify saying He is divided into parts—for there is no change or division except in the internal Sefirot. (And this is included for the sake of understanding and is founded in God so that it may be accepted by the mind of the seeker). **A Parable:** Compare it to a source of water spreading into vessels that are colored: one red, one white, one green, and the like. Behold, though the water is simple and devoid of all color, it is divided among the vessels, and each appears according to the color of the vessel. The change is seen in the water due to the change in the appearance of the vessel; it is not a change in the water's actual substance, but only in its appearance. It happens that there is a distinction regarding the water only from the perspective of the colors of the vessels. So it is with the Sefirot: the Vessels are the Sefirah designated for us as **Chesed** (Kindness), **Gevurah** (Strength), **Tiferet** (Beauty), etc. Therefore, it is said: color...

**Chapter 3: And What**

<column-break/>

# Slice of the Pomegranate

...within the Sefirot, and they are to Him like vessels for the actions that flow from Him into the separate world and below. Because the Sage <note>referring to Cordovero</note> (may peace be upon him) in *Pardes Rimonim*, Gate 19, Chapter 1, distanced the association of the Great Name even from the Essence of the Emanation, I must warn the reader: he spoke correctly according to his system in every place in this inquiry which we are explaining. It is well-known in all his books, and in this Gate specifically. Look at what he explained in Gate 5, Chapter 19: that the "Essential Name" <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> is called such because this Name includes and encompasses the entire world of Atzilut in a complete unity—true, firm, and established. However, for one who is not satisfied with this—since the emanations are "renewed" <note>created/emanated in time</note> while the Name is "primordial," as we have learned: "Before the world was created, there was only He and His Name alone"—even though many explain this statement in different ways, you too should say to him: We do not attribute the Great Name to anything but the **Will** <note>original: "Ratzon"</note>, insofar as it desires to do good. This Name is also nothing but the source of all existences and names, as will be explained in the next chapter. It is not a name that anyone else can grasp at all, not even the emanated beings, except in a distant likeness—similar to how He wonderfully bestowed His kindness upon us by depicting it in the Torah, hinting to us how one of the emanated beings, such as **Tiferet**, is grasped with a specific vocalization, or **Binah** <term>Binah: "Understanding," the third Sefirah</term> with the vocalization of *Elohim*. This is sufficient.

**And here**, I am teaching and demonstrating that whenever the Sages taught "Essence and Vessels," the intention is the essence of the specific attribute (Middah) we are discussing and its vessel. Thus, it is correct to say that what is "Essence" for one level can be a "Vessel" and "Garment" for the level above it. I have been accustomed since I reached maturity—the day of all the companions, old and young alike—to sweeten the secret of "Essence and Vessels" by saying to them: "Will and Speech," or "Sefirah and Speech." For these are "Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us," as King David (peace be upon him) said: "Your wonders" are the Sefirot, and "Your thoughts" are the Utterances <note>original: "Ma'amarot"</note>. The intention in all this is the hidden and revealed aspects of the Emanation. I speak well: if you wish, it is the logic with which you began; if you wish, it is the verse where it is written, "Then He saw it and declared it; He established it and searched it out" <note>Job 28:27</note>. He "prepared" it and "searched" it out first, and then "said" it. Between them is preparation and limitation. Thus, the "declaration" <note>Sipur</note> itself, in our context, is not prepared or limited, as we are destined to explain later in Gate 11 with God's help. This is the essential difference between the "Ten Sefirot" and the "Ten Utterances" which the Sages taught in the language of the Mishnah in *Sefer Yetzirah* and *Ethics of the Fathers*. Everything is established and received with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge—not as a metaphor or a shared term, but as specific words for specific inquiries. The word of the Lord in our mouths is truth.

**Chapter 3: And What** even now, I have not come to obscure but to explain and to show the precious glory of the greatness of the Essential Name that preceded all worlds, as we mentioned. For indeed, "His Name" <note>Hebrew: "Shmo"</note> in **Gematria** <term>Gematria: Hebrew numerology where letters have numerical values</term> is "Will" <note>Hebrew: "Ratzon"</note>—this and that, including the number resulting from the Name itself: *Yud-He* [15] times *Yud-He* [15] is 225, and *He* [5] over *Vav-He* [11] is 121, which together in Gematria equal "His Name." It is known that "He and His Name are One," and "His Will is One." This is His Name, which is His Will, unified in His thought and blessed. It is not just that it has no vocalization—for we do not know how thought spreads within it—but even the letters...

The previous page introduced the debate regarding whether the Sefirot are the Divine Essence itself or merely instruments. This page specifically addresses the concept of Divine Will (Keter) and uses a famous analogy of sunbeams passing through spheres to explain how the Infinite can interact with a finite, changing world without changing Its own nature.</meta>

# Gate 4: The Essence of the Vessels — Juice of Pomegranates

The wonder and the rectification occur when it is known that the **Crown** <term>Keter: the highest Sefirah, representing the Divine Will</term> is called "Will." The "Chooser" <note>the Infinite Source/God</note> desires through it. Thus, the Chooser is capable through its power, as is known from the tradition. He is "Known through the Known" <note>a phrase suggesting God is understood through His emanations</note> in the level of **Knowledge** <term>Da'at: the bridge between the upper and lower Sefirot</term>, for He is known through it and rectified by it. This Knowledge is the Sefirah of **Beauty** <term>Tiferet: the central Sefirah of the heart and harmony</term>, as explained in the book *The Orchard* <note>original: "Sefer ha-Pardes," referring to Pardes Rimonim by Moshe Cordovero</note>.

This Crown and the choice of **Kindness** <term>Chesed: the attribute of love and expansion</term> is the foundation of the **Sovereignty** <term>Malchut: the final Sefirah, through which the Divine interacts with our world</term>, for "from love and below" <note>an idiom for the lower emotive Sefirot</note> they turn in their ways, and "sin crouches at the door" <note>Genesis 4:7</note>. This relates to the reception of choice, also called "Evaluation." This is a portion of Knowledge before Kindness ascends, even though it is destined to act. The choice that He chose—before the action—was the Knowledge hidden within the "Voice" of Knowledge.

However, the "flaw" above has not yet ceased. Regarding the "Additional Offering," <note>Musaf</note> before its action with its "mouth," it is known above that there is no flow of influence or forgiveness until he is crowned. This is what the verse means: "For now I know that you fear God" <note>Genesis 22:12</note>. For "Knowing" refers to that knowledge which has moved from potential to actual through the deed of the "Voice," which is the union of **Beauty** and **Sovereignty**. This is why the word "I knew" <note>yada'ti</note> is used, a term for knowledge and connection, as in "And Adam knew Eve" <note>Genesis 4:1</note>. 

Sometimes "Choice" is mentioned in place of "Knowledge," just as **Sovereignty** is sometimes mentioned in place of **Beauty**. For example, in the Book of Creation <note>Sefer Yetzirah</note>, the activities of the sixth day are mentioned as male aspects, preceding the letters which are female. Conversely, in the name *David*, the female aspects are mentioned before the male. While the Infinite remains unified <note>original: "he-cha-i s," likely referring to the Hayyei Ha-Atzmut or the Living Essence</note>, the judgment is not far from mercy. Even as the Sovereignty is mentioned, the Choice remains upon the Beauty (which is Knowledge). This is appropriate for a teacher to explain. If Israel were not worthy, they would be in sin, and so too David was not worthy, and he was stoned, etc. This occurred because they placed Choice before Knowledge; this is the secret of the Kingdom.

Despite all this, one must investigate and ask: Since the Infinite/Sovereignty is removed from all attributes, opposites, changes, and boundaries, how is it possible that the "Choice"—which is a concept within the Sefirot—can exist? For opposites like "Kindness" and "Judgment" ultimately result in opposition and various boundaries and changes. All these attributes and their dependencies would then be attributed to Him as contradictory things! 

The path to answering this doubt has eluded some commentators, to the point that they said the matter of His connection and His unity is a mystery, like the hidden connection and foundation of spiritual names within physical, material, and bodily frames.

**And it is possible** to say that the matter of attributes, boundaries, and changes found in the holy Sefirot are not boundaries in relation to the Infinite Essence Himself, but only in relation to the created beings. For it is known that He is "Wise by Himself" and "Bounded by Himself," but without an end for the sake of the created beings; therefore His actions are called such for the sake of "the other."

**And after** this, it was necessary to emanate the world of Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four spiritual worlds</term> and to act in a way that there would be boundaries and actions in this world. For this reason, it was necessary for the "Emanated" to exist specifically through Him and not through another. Thus, the light proceeds to include the "Vessels" so that they may be unified. The lack of Sefirot and boundaries corresponds to His boundary-less nature, and Judgment corresponds to His role as Judge. Therefore, all matters of lack or deficiency are attributed to the "Vessel," whereas the "Essence" remains simple and hidden. The Vessel proceeds toward the Essence, and the Essence toward the Vessel, and so it is with all the other attributes. This is unified in the ultimate foundation: the light "dresses" itself in its "garments." We can prove that the garment without the light is like a silent corpse, and the light without the garment has no existence or reality within its actions in the worlds. This was not due to a need on His part, Heaven forbid, but was intended for the sake of the "other" who was created—to bestow good upon the other. It was not by necessity, but by Will. Therefore, the statement "He emanated and created the lower worlds" means it was to reveal His glory, to be unified in them, to cling to them, to sustain them, and to direct them toward their purpose.

There is yet another doubt regarding the Sefirot. After we have explained that their source is from the Blessed Essence, and that they are not created in a way that they were non-existent before, we are left with the problem: they are composite, limited, and finite. How can we attribute such things to God, who is the Simple One in absolute simplicity? Some commentators answer that the "Light of Emanation" is not separate from the Emanator; rather, the Emanation itself was hidden within His essence in an extremely subtle potential. Now they have been revealed and moved from potential to actual. In relation to the created beings, they are "new," but not in relation to the Emanator. This explanation suffices to say that the Sefirot are not "attributes" in relation to the Emanator (who is the hidden Infinite), but rather the spreading of His own essence. As the sages said: "He and His life-force are one; He and His vessels are one." This spreading/expansion did not exist [in this way] previously, and if so, there would be change and composition—this is a difficult problem!

The resolution of the matter is to compare it to the light of the great Sun. Imagine a clear, polished sphere that can receive light. It does not receive it until the sun is positioned directly within its circular boundary. These boundaries/spheres act upon the light in various ways. Although the sun's strength is one, the light it grants is received through these spheres and does not separate from the sun. Because the spheres are placed one inside the other, the light from the great Sun descends through the inner spheres until it reaches the end of the expansion, surrounding all things. This light and heat that is drawn inward is like the essence of the light and heat in the sun itself. The "sweetness" or "variation" found within the light is not from a change in the sun's essence itself, but from the filters and spheres standing before it. Thus, the light and heat spreading within the spheres is not the same as it was before it entered the spheres. However, we should not confuse them; the Great Sun is the source of the heat and light. The only "new" things are the spheres and the vessels that limit His light relative to their capacity. Indeed, before this, His light reached a reality that was even more revealed, but the "Spheres" clothed it and hidden it. When we look at the reality of the Emanations through the lens of this metaphor, the aforementioned doubt is beautifully resolved. For the Great Sun is a hint at the Infinite (**Ein Sof**), and the spheres are the Sefirot (meaning, the "Vessels"). The light and heat spreading within them is His Blessed Essence, the Hidden One who spreads through the Sefirot, giving them life, managing them, and directing them according to His Blessed Will.

### Chapter 10
All these matters and designations we have mentioned until now are to clarify and teach that the Sefirot are both Essence and Vessels, etc. In all these things, the details are found. What Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (may peace be upon him) said regarding every single matter of the "Goodness" includes the "Essence and Vessels." He spoke of nothing else, especially in one passage in the *Tikkunim* <note>Tikkuney Zohar</note>, where Elijah opened and said: "Master of the Worlds, You are One but not in the sense of number..." Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explained this as a "Hidden Form" that is not established, but is revealed and goes out through the "Will" and the "Wills," and changes within them, etc. Furthermore, in the books of Rabbi Moshe <note>Moshe Cordovero</note> regarding the "Imaginary Form," at the end, before He created the "Image of the World," He was alone without form or likeness... and also in the *Ra'aya Mehemna* <note>a section of the Zohar</note> on Commandment 13, it is explained...

It uses the metaphor of sunlight passing through colored or limiting spheres to explain that while the Divine Essence remains one, its manifestation through 'Vessels' (Sefirot) allows for finite attributes like Kindness and Judgment.</summary>

# Juice of Pomegranates, Gate 4: Essence and Vessels — Segment of the Pomegranate

The interior of <unclear>SAT</unclear> these vessels is the **Crown**, as previously mentioned. **And from what** is worthy to be known is that the **Crown** <term>Keter: the highest Sefirah, representing Divine Will</term> is divided into the category of "Inner Light," and there is no more in the Sefirot. At the heights of grace, it contains all the lower ones that are drawn out and nurtured from it until the very end. These are the "facings" that are atop one another, up to ten ascents; each Sefirah within them is distant yet aligned one against the other. Through this alignment, the light of the sun will be good and its path is learned by all. <unclear>SAT</unclear> It is good that [light] moves from the highest to one of the sides, and that light is purified because it does not receive anything except through change. Behold, the power of light will be like a flock in the light; thus it will be absent from each of the ascents beneath it as we pass through. And behold, this absence does not stem from a withdrawal of the light itself, but rather from the poor preparation of the receivers <note>This is a classic Kabbalistic analogy: the Sun (God) shines constantly, but if a window is dirty or a vessel is opaque, the light appears dimmed or absent. The fault lies with the vessel, not the light.</note>. So too is the matter with the Sefirot: the Supernal Light descends from above through the "channels" from one Sefirah to the next. And if, God forbid, a Sefirah is "blemished" <note>Referring to human sin or spiritual blockage affecting the flow of blessing</note>, the light is lacking and cannot be fully rectified above. This is because the Infinite does not add light to a flawed or defective place. Regarding the depth of the lower Sefirah, it may turn its face away without looking toward the place of light, and because of this turning, the paths become like stains and the lamps like shrouds; the light departs and becomes distant, and judgment <term>Din: the attribute of restriction and severity</term> comes into being. Behold, this is not because the light itself is divided or absent, but because the "face" of the Crown's light has withdrawn from the depth of that Sefirah, and it becomes cloaked in the aforementioned Judgment, even though its nature is Kindness and Mercy.

### Chapter 5: And Behold
->As mentioned, the matter of the Sefirah: Light with Poverty<-
->And Vessels designated by the power of the Infinite<-
Which hovers over them until a single name arrives, which is **"A-D-O-N-A-I"** <note>The Hebrew name for Lord, often associated with the manifestation of God in the world</note>, a name that indicates Unity. All the attributes and the prepared movements and the "colors" that are drawn out will be like the internal "burnished ones"—meaning the Vessels that contemplate the light of **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah: the first flash of intuition or divine intellect</term> which spreads through the Essence of the Infinite, blessed be He.

### Chapter 6, 7, 8: And With
->The existence of these "burnished ones" and the Sefirah<-
->Is not the reason for the variation in actions<-
Because an action occurs only from the power of the Governor and the Essence that spreads within them. This is similar to the actions of the limbs of the body: the actions are powered by the Soul, while the changes [in the type of action] are due to the different organs of the body <note>The soul is one, but the hand grasps while the foot walks; the "change" is in the instrument, not the life-force</note>. Even though these "intellectual ones" are not subject to change, the variations come from the vessels, which are "Wills," not from the Governor. If the student thinks that some changes originate from the essence of the Sefirot and the vessels themselves, it would be an error, God forbid! For since the Infinite is not subject to any change at all, so too the primary emanated Sefirot—which are vessels and Wills—bow before the Soul that spreads from the Essence of the Infinite. Due to their closeness to Him, they are not subject to change at all. Rather, there are "secondary garments" in the way of **Creation** <term>Beriah: the second of the four worlds, the realm of the Divine Throne</term> in which they are clothed and warmed. These changes are generalities within the "Throne of Glory," and they are called "Throne" and called "Creation." **Emanation** <term>Atzilut: the highest world of pure divinity</term> in relation to Creation is like the Soul spreading from the Essence of the Infinite into the primary vessels. Furthermore, there are "third garments" in which they clothe themselves; these are generalities within **Metatron** <note>A high angelic figure often associated with the governance of the lower worlds</note> and are called **Formation** <term>Yetzirah: the third world, the realm of angels</term>. The level of Creation is to Emanation as a soul within a body. The relation of Creation to Formation is like the relation of Emanation to Creation. Through the level of Formation, specifically, there are changes, cycles, clothing, and purpose. All actions are evolved there, yet the actions are not fully completed until they clothe themselves in the fourth levels called **Action** <term>Asiyah: the lowest world, including our physical reality</term>, which are solidified into physical and material things, as will be explained in the gate of "ABYA" <note>An acronym for the four worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah</note>. Even though the relationship of Emanation to Creation is like the Infinite to the Sefirah, and similarly the relation of Creation to Formation, nevertheless the matters are not identical. The Infinite is not called by the name "Sefirah," but the "Governor" is called "Sefirah," and the Sefirah is called "God." Action exists in the form of Creation, but not so in the Infinite. For He cannot be called "Mighty" in Himself, as He possesses no attributes. From this, I will move to the letters and Action, which are not in a "place," for the Sefirah and the emanated ones are called by one name because they are garments of a Name or a Place. But in the Infinite, there is no "where" and no "name" revealed—neither in the aspect of His existence before Emanation nor after it. For even in the Essence that spreads within Emanation and the Sefirah, in the aspect of His simple Essence, there is no "where," no name, no title, no letter, and no vowel-point that could encompass or clothe Him.

### Chapter 9: And After
We have truly explained the matter of Essence and Vessels and that there are no changes in the Infinite despite the unfolding of His Sefirot. We have provided a beautiful and pleasant hint toward the Holy Ladder that leads to the knowledge of Him, blessed be He, which extends to all perception, neither good nor evil; through it is His knowledge. And you shall contemplate the word:
<meta>catchword: The Holy</meta>

<column-break/>

the sum total of His Will is what is called the **Infinite** <term>Ein Sof: "Without End," God in His absolute, unknowable state</term>, as we have explained. The Infinite is the "First Cause" of all existing things, for there is no cause above Him. We are not permitted to attribute the title of "Cause" to anything above His Will, except by associating it with His Will, which is described as the "Cause of all Causes" and everything similar. And the truth is that He and His Will are one. **And behold**, we have heard of this "Ten," but these are the Wills—meaning the interior of the Sefirot—where number exists only in their absence <note>Meaning they are so unified that they cannot be counted as separate entities</note>. Whoever knows the difference between absolute negation and the "absence" that sits at the head of natural beginnings will descend to the depth of this intent, and this is in its simplicity. **However**, regarding the "Ten Utterances" <note>The ten phrases by which the world was created in Genesis</note>, number is attributed to them in the existence of "something from nothing" <term>Yesh me-Ayin: Creation ex nihilo</term>, which is not a complete number. These are like vessels for the inner essence. In these vessels, **Kindness**, **Judgment**, and **Mercy** are described—not in the vessels themselves, but through their clothing in Creation, Formation, and Action. For **Kindness** <term>Chesed</term> is the essence in the **Creation** of a world that is entirely good; **Mercy** <term>Rachamim/Tiferet</term> is in **Formation**, for "the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Beauty" <note>original: "HKB"H v'Tiferet"</note> nest there; and **Judgment** <term>Din</term> is in **Action** <term>Asiyah</term>, as is known. The "Ten Levels of the Throne" are the true number of "something from something" <term>Yesh me-Yesh</term>, and this exists only in the lower worlds, about which it is written, "and from there it was parted" <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. **Hold** this principle in your hand: whenever we mention "Essence" and "Vessels," the **Essence** is the specific **Soul**—that is, the Inner Light that gives life to that specific vessel wherever it may be. We do not mean that the Divine Essence itself is seen there, God forbid, but rather the essence of that specific vessel. For example, the soul of a human is the true "human," while the body is the "flesh of the human." For the Hidden Essence gives life to everything, and He is the **Soul of Souls** <term>Nishmat ha-Neshamot: the ultimate divine spark within all levels of soul</term>. But this is a general principle that does not require this specific detail we are explaining. Remember this fundamental rule always, for then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have success.

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of the transition from the "Infinite" into the structured world of the Sefirot. It should attach to the space through a small matter, a portion of the flow; as for the vacuum upon it, it is drawn over it. This does not mean it is unmixed, but nonetheless, the Intellect improved it until it emptied everything onto it, like the **Crown** (*Keter*) <term>Keter: the highest Sefirah, representing the Divine Will which is almost identical to the Infinite</term>, which does not contain even a portion of the flow. For in the lower aspect, the end is hidden in total concealment. Because of this, the "Lines" were not able to be revealed until His Wisdom (blessed be He) was known, to bring out the "hollows" <note>This refers to the "Empty Space" or vacuum created to allow for a finite world</note>. This is the secret of the number 18 (*Chai*): 8 for the **Crown**, 10 for **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*), and 20 for **Understanding** (*Binah*), as explained in the *Zohar* (The Tikunim) according to the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. The "Gathering" was hollowed out in relation to the **Crown**, which is called *Chai* (Life). This does not mean it was void of existence, but rather it required a "Hollow" to act from it. Even though the "Gathering" was a hollow aspect, it was still subtle and divided within the Supernal Source until it was called a "portion of a secret." Even the number 19 does not apply to **Wisdom**, except when compared to its expansion. Therefore, even though the "Living Beings" (*Chayot*) <note>High-ranking angels or divine forces</note> could not be revealed, it does not mean they could not be emanated at all, for they were already hidden in the **Crown**. Rather, the point is that the powers of **Judgment** (*Din*) and **Might** (*Gevurah*) could not emerge from potential into action because of the extreme proximity of the emanated to the Root. For in the light of the King's countenance, there is only life <note>A common Kabbalistic theme: God's immediate presence is so "merciful" and "bright" that the restrictive power of Judgment cannot function there</note>. The powers of Judgment rose in thought but not in action. This is the secret of what is written: "These are the kings who reigned in Edom" <note>Referencing the "Kings of Edom" from Genesis, which Kabbalists interpret as early, unbalanced attempts at creation that "shattered" because they were pure Judgment without Mercy</note>, as stated in the *Idra*. The essence of Divine Providence comes from the side of Judgment, as our Sages said: "The Holy One intended to create the world with Judgment, but He saw it could not stand, so He partnered it with Mercy." Therefore, in these three levels—**Wisdom**, **Crown**, and **Understanding**—the powers of Judgment were not revealed at all. Because of this, Judgment was considered "sweetened," for it had a good disposition of Mercy, being in the first emanation. This is why the first world of Judgment is in the second "hollow," and the **Crown** and first two are the "earlier ones" mentioned in the "Sabbatical" hollow. Because of their proximity to the Source, the Infinite, Judgment cannot perform its actions or judge its laws, for in the light of the King's face there is life. Therefore, the Emanator required the "hollows" and all the forms of Judgment until the third level. In short: because the first Sefirot are subtle and hidden, the powers of Judgment and all the actions of the "Extremities" <note>The six directions/Sefirot that govern our physical reality</note> could not be revealed or act through them.

...in this, because the waters, which are the secret of **Mercy** (*Chesed*), are not the cause for the darkness, which is **Might/Severity** (*Gevurah*). Rather, it is a "proximate cause," like a mother <gloss>1</gloss> to the embryo formed in her womb. The "distant cause" is the drop of the father from his very brain. And the truth is this: because **Severity** is from the essence of **Understanding** (*Binah*), then it is called the "distant cause." Similarly, **Greatness** (*Gedulah/Chesed*) is formed from the **Understanding** adjacent to it, and **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*), which is exalted, is its root. Likewise, **Wisdom** is a proximate cause for **Understanding**, and the **Crown** (*Keter*) is its root. And the **Crown** is a proximate cause for **Wisdom**, while its strength is the **Infinite** (*Ein Sof*).
