### Gate 6

## Chapter 5: The Essential Point

The governance of the lower realms and their life-force is through the "Extremities" (*Ketzavot*) in the **Crown** and the **Will** of the "Cause of All Causes." The matter of these six Extremities is like a tree that requires planting and watering. The "planting" refers to the roots planted within **Understanding** (*Binah*), in such a way that the six Extremities are three mentioned entities, which are the "entities of planting." The "watering" refers to the branches of the tree, and the "fruiting" refers to the place where the influence of actions happens.

Behold, for the existence of emanation, these three things were necessary. When it arose in His mind (blessed be He) to plant them—had they been in the **Crown** or **Wisdom**, they would not have endured, because they would be too attached and close to their source. Even though the powers of Judgment were visible in them for the needs of providence, when the Extremities reached **Understanding**, they were satisfied with powers. These attributes of Mercy would be nurtured and find joy in their "masters" <note>The higher sources</note> which they have in **Understanding** and **Crown**. There, **Understanding** holds the first place for the Extremities, through the attributes of Judgment and Mercy. Afterward, **Understanding** spreads to its own place, which is the second attribute for the Extremities—its actual location. And there they are built like a tree that is nurtured. Afterward, the tree produces its fruit, which are the actions of the Sefirot performed through the **Kingship** (*Malkhut*).

The matter of these six Extremities is that they are divided into six of Judgment and six of Mercy, which are the "three lines"... You should know that at the time of the emanation of the **Crown**, the ten Sefirot were within it, hidden one inside the other. They were not revealed within it at all, except for the essence of **Wisdom** and **Understanding** in the form of "points" <term>Nekudot: concentrated sparks of light before they expand into vessels</term>... like a "Primordial Secret"... Light within Light... and within these three points were all the rest of the Sefirot... and these are the three "Appointed Ones" through which Thought spreads.

Afterward, the intention was to emanate **Understanding** as a whole within the three points... Not that at the time of the emanation of **Wisdom** they saw **Understanding**... but rather in the manner of the emanation of each and every Sefirah from these first three, there were ten paths:
1. The aspect of concealment before its revelation...
3. The aspect of revelation in its essence in its proper place...
9. Giving it the power to be able to emanate the higher Sefirah...
10. The aspect of the revelation of their nurturance as is fitting for them...
And the matter is that when the Infinite emanated the **Crown** at the beginning of its emanation, it was...

# The Fifth Gate: The Order of Emanation

---

## Chapter 1 and Chapter 2: Explaining the Order of Emanation
Know that the order of the <term>Emanation (Atzilut): The highest of the four spiritual worlds, where the Divine Light is perfectly unified with the Divine Attributes</term> is as we have explained in many places. Some say that the <term>Ten Sefirot: The ten dimensions or attributes through which God interacts with the universe</term> are included within one another. For example, **Kindness** (*Hesed*) of the first is included in the **Crown** (*Keter*). From the **Crown** comes **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*); from **Wisdom**, **Understanding** (*Binah*); from **Understanding**, **Greatness** (*Gedulah*); from **Greatness**, **Power** (*Gevurah*); from **Power**, **Beauty** (*Tiferet*); from **Beauty**, **Victory** (*Netzach*); from **Victory**, **Voice** (*Kol*); from **Voice**, **Foundation** (*Yesod*); and from **Foundation**, **Kingdom** (*Malchut*). The reason for this specific order is the transition between the General and the Particular, in the way of "Cause and Effect." (For it is impossible for two effects to come from a single cause and be identical, as they would then be one; they must separate, for that which is a body cannot be divided in space). This is the opinion of <note>Rabbi Azriel of Gerona: A foundational 13th-century Kabbalist</note> the Gaon Rabbi Azriel, of blessed memory, the author of the *Book of Faiths*, in Gate 1, Chapter 14. However, he placed **Foundation** (*Yesod*) before **Victory** (*Netzach*), and the secret of this is included in the reasoning. The transcriber says: "Here, the seventh opinion is missing."

## Chapter 3: This is the opinion of the Gaon Rabbi Joseph Caro, of blessed memory.
He perceives **Kindness** (*Hesed*), **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*), and **Understanding** (*Binah*) as being within **Power** (*Gevurah*). This will be clarified through the triad of **Beauty** (*Tiferet*), **Foundation** (*Yesod*), and **Kingdom** (*Malchut*). There is also a third opinion: that the first three (**Crown**, **Wisdom**, **Understanding**) are included in the **Crown**. From the **Crown** comes **Wisdom**, from **Wisdom** comes **Understanding**, and **Understanding** includes **Kindness** and the final seven Sefirot as one. These three opinions will be clarified through the words of <note>Rashbi: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai; therefore, it is necessary to establish a compromise between them.

## Chapter 4:
Therefore, one must say that the World of Emanation is so "simple" <note>In philosophy, "simple" means non-composite or pure</note> that the Sefirot are the ultimate hiddenness of the hidden. Their distinction was not revealed to others because the beings were hidden; the Sefirot were concealed in the "Worlds of the Void," within the subtle and refined Emanation. They were not yet Sefirot as they are now, but rather they were unified in their "White-Hot Coal" and the foundation of their vitality, without description or separation. Consider the metaphor of a white-hot coal: the flame is bound to it, and it contains various colors, yet no specific color is visible until it spreads out. These colors exist within the essence of the coal, but they are hidden and combined. (The flame is hidden within the coal in a way that there is no distinction or separation between coal and flame at all. So it is with the Sefirot before their expansion; they were unified in the Infinite, the foundation of their life, in the ultimate hiddenness). From this unity, the three Sefirot emerged from the Source, which is called the "Root of the Sefirot" in the Kabbalah.

->**And when** it arose in the Simple Will to reveal<-

His hiddenness, he brought forth from the Void into existence. He emanated from that Simple Will the first Sefirah, called **Crown** (*Keter*). The existence and distinction of this Sefirah were not visible at all, even after the emanation, until it was called <term>Ayin (Nothingness): A term for Keter, signifying that it is beyond human comprehension, not that it doesn't exist</term> "Nothingness," signifying the absolute absence of grasp. Even this name does not truly fit it. (In our explanation, we wrote that regarding its names, it is not called by any name, as is explained in many places. The term *Keter* means that even though it is one, it is not Wisdom; it is the "Pre-existent Wisdom," and this is the secret of our words). It was only occupied with the "Thinkables"...

<column-break/>

## Chapter 1: Various opinions have been stated regarding the Order of Emanation.
Some explain the chain of attributes as emerging one by one in order. Among them are those who placed **Foundation** (*Yesod*) before **Victory** (*Netzach*) and **Splendor** (*Hod*) to indicate that **Beauty** (*Tiferet*) also has a conceptual priority over **Kindness** (*Hesed*) and **Power** (*Gevurah*). This is because the "Middle Line" <note>The central axis of the Sefirotic tree, representing balance</note> is entirely rooted in the **Supernal Crown** (*Keter Elyon*), though it appeared later in the emanation for the purpose of "Deciding" <note>Mediating between the right side (Mercy) and the left side (Judgment)</note>. This eventually caused **Foundation** to also be later than its two companions in reality.

**And there** are those who say concerning the **Crown**: "It is a single light that includes three" (Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge). Each of these includes others. From **Wisdom**, a single light emerges that includes two: **Kindness** and **Victory**. From **Understanding**, a single light emerges that includes two: **Power** and **Splendor**. And from the point of the **Crown** itself, a single light emerges that includes three: **Beauty**, **Foundation**, and **Kingdom**. Some say that **Crown**, **Wisdom**, and **Understanding** were emanated from one another, and from **Understanding**, the "Seven Lamps" <note>The seven lower Sefirot</note> emerged all at once.

**All these** views are true. Before the emanation of the Sefirot, everything was hidden in the "Root of Roots" in a state of existence that was the ultimate hiddenness and unity, where no image or "point" could be ascribed at all. Yet all were unified in Him. Afterward, He emanated from Himself a single point, a single emanation—the **Crown**, called *Ayin* ("Nothing") due to the extreme subtlety of its point and its attachment to its Source. From it, a second point was emanated into revelation—**Wisdom**, called *Yesh me-Ayin* ("Something from Nothing"). However, "Absence" was still attached to it, so a third point was required to reveal actualized beings—this is **Understanding**. Thus, "Wisdom is the beginning and Understanding is the end," either because she completes their form or because they return to her in the secret of the "Jubilee" <note>The 50th year in Jewish law, representing a return to the source</note>.

**These** three points were all included in the **Crown** initially. There, the three "Lines" were included, each within the root of its source in the **Crown**. After the **Crown** brought the point of **Wisdom** to light, it first flowed into it **Understanding**, and then **Beauty**, **Foundation**, and **Kingdom**. Afterward, **Kindness** and **Victory** were discerned within its essence. Within the **Understanding** that was in it, **Power** and **Splendor** were discerned. **Wisdom** emanated **Understanding** and first flowed into it the "Middle Line," and then **Kindness** and **Victory**. Then **Power** and **Splendor** were discerned within her essence. **Understanding**, through the power of **Wisdom**, emanated **Kindness**, and **Victory** was included in it. Through it, she emanated **Power** by her own power, and **Splendor** was included in it. Through both of them, she emanated **Beauty** last, to place "Conflict" <note>The divergence of Right/Kindness and Left/Power</note> before "Decision" <note>The balance of Beauty</note>. Despite all this, **Beauty** is sometimes counted first, as its "Body" is within its core essence. **Afterward**, **Kindness** revealed the way of **Dread** (*Pachad*), and **Beauty** revealed **Victory** through the power of **Wisdom**. **Dread** revealed through **Beauty**, and **Victory** revealed **Splendor** through the power of **Understanding**. **Beauty**, through **Victory** and **Splendor**, revealed **Foundation**, and through him revealed **Kingdom**. All of this was through the power of the **Crown**. (The Sages of the Secret said... the intention in this...)

## Chapter 5: The Principle
The governance of the lower realms is dependent upon the "Seven Edges" <note>The seven lower Sefirot</note> within the **Crown**, and the Will of the Cause of all causes. The matter of these "Seven Edges" is like a tree that requires planting and transplanting. The intention is that the "first blessing" and the hidden powers of His hand are the providence of this "Tree." These are the "Roots" planted within **Understanding** (*Binah*), in a way that the Six Edges in the **Crown** have two necessary existences: the existence of the "Planting," which are the hidden roots, and the existence of the "Transplanting," which are the branches of the tree. The "Tendrils" of the Sefirah are below, in the place where actions are influenced. 

Now, since the distant Emanations require these two matters—while still in His Mind (blessed be He)—if their "planting" were in **Crown** or **Wisdom**, they would not endure because they are too subtle and close to their Source; the powers of Judgment would not exist in the way necessary for governance. Therefore, when the "Edges" reached **Understanding**, they expanded into specific powers. The existence of this "Transplanting" allows them to "suckle and draw" <note>A common metaphor for receiving spiritual sustenance</note> from the hidden powers they have in **Understanding** and **Crown**. Through the emanation of His Will from **Understanding**, the Judgment and Mercy are revealed. 

Afterward, they are drawn and "sown" into their essential place—that is, from the emanation of **Understanding** to the "Edges," which is their actual location. They are like the leaf of a tree that draws from the roots, and afterward, the tree produces its fruit, which are the actions of the Sefirah performed through the "Tendrils." The matter of these Seven Edges consists of the actors: one for Judgment and six for Mercy. These are the twelve "Living Creatures" (*Chayot*) in the **Crown**, which are twelve Severities... seventy to the [unclear]... twenty-six of the Name <note>Refers to the Tetragrammaton, which has the numerical value of 26</note>... which are the three existences of the Edges included in these three places.

With what has been explained (that the existence of the Edges could not be revealed through **Crown** and **Wisdom** until the order of emanation reached **Understanding**, followed by drawing down and sowing), know that at the time of the emanation of the **Crown**, the Ten Sefirot were within it, one inside the other, hidden in their essence. Therefore, within the **Crown**, the **Crown** and these other Sefirot were not revealed at all. Rather, the primary things revealed within it were **Wisdom** and **Understanding**. The existence of the **Crown** is in the "Mystery of the Point," comprised of three points revealed within it, from which three lights were made. These are the hidden roots of the Sefirot:
1. **Ancient Light** (*Or Kadmon*)
2. **Clear Light** (*Or Tzach*)
3. **Polished Light** (*Or Metzuchtzach*)

Within these three points were the entire order of the Sefirot. (Behold, the **Supreme Crown** emanated the Edges and flowed into them all the Sefirot). These correspond to the three aspects of the Soul (which correspond to the First Three Sefirot) and the "Three Brains" through which they spread. Afterward, in the second emanation of **Wisdom**, they were included in three points... 

However, at the time of the emanation of **Wisdom** or the emanation of the **Crown**, the Sefirot within them were like the emanation of every single Sefirah. From these first three Sefirot, there were ten aspects:
1. The aspect of **Concealment** before revelation in the Sefirah that births it.
2. The aspect of **Revelation** as it is seen within the birthing Sefirah.
3. The aspect of **Ascent** to its proper place.
4. The aspect of **Power** given so the Upper Sefirah can shine within it.
5. The aspect of **Receiving** the light.
6. The aspect of **Bestowing** power to emanate further.
...reaching ten aspects of revelation in their proper rectification. The matter is this: when the Emanator emanated the **Crown** at the start of its emanation, it was in the **Crown**...

## The Fifth Gate: The Order of Emanation

### Chapter 1 and Chapter 2: Explaining the Order of Emanation
<margin>Know that the order of emanation in the tradition...</margin>
The sages disagreed in several ways. Some perceived the **Sefirot** <note>The ten creative powers or attributes of God</note> as streams flowing one from the other: Kindness from Wisdom, as Wisdom is to Crown. From the **Crown** (*Keter*) comes **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*); from Wisdom, **Understanding** (*Binah*); from Understanding, **Greatness/Kindness** (*Gedulah/Chesed*); from Greatness, **Severity** (*Gevurah*); from Severity, **Beauty/Harmony** (*Tiferet*); from Harmony, **Victory** (*Netzach*); from Victory, **Splendor** (*Hod*); from Splendor, **Foundation** (*Yesod*); and from Foundation, **Kingship** (*Malchut*). The reason for this specific order is that, according to their understanding, there is no distinction between the whole and the parts except by way of "cause and effect." Thus, if there were two primary roots for Wisdom, there would be two effects of the same level and they would be equal. This is the opinion of the great master, the author of the *Book of Intervals* <note>Likely referring to a specific chronological or kabbalistic work</note> in Gate 30, Chapter 10, though he placed Foundation before Victory and Splendor; the reason for this will be explained later. The copyist notes that one of these follows the third opinion:

### Chapter 3: This is...
...the opinion of the sage Rabbi Joseph Karo, of blessed memory <note>The famous 16th-century author of the Shulchan Aruch, who was also a mystic</note>. His view is that Wisdom, Kindness, and Victory are aligned like streams of a single light. From the Crown come Beauty, Foundation, and Kingship. There is yet a third opinion: that the Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding were emanated first. From the Crown comes Wisdom, from Wisdom comes Understanding, and from Understanding, all the other lower Sefirot emerged at once. These opinions find their ladder of support in the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar</note>; therefore, a structured order must be established between them for everything.

### Chapter 4: And Therefore...
It must be said that before the emanation, the **Infinite** (*Ein Sof*) was a simple, absolute Unity, the ultimate pinnacle. His Divinity was not revealed to any other being because there were no "existences." The potential for the Sefirot was hidden within Him like the hidden potential within a flame <note>A common kabbalistic metaphor: the colors of a flame exist potentially within the fire before they are visible</note>. They were not actual Sefirot as they are now; rather, they were unified in their perfection, without multiplicity or separation. Remember this: like the sparks within a coal, they are many "intermediaries" that do not even arise in thought, just as the powers of the soul exist within a person's essence. These intermediaries are like a single entity within the flame, such that there is no division or separation between the master and the flame at all. So it was with the Sefirot before their expansion; they were unified in the Infinite—the True Foundation—hidden in the ultimate pinnacle. The existence of these Sefirot is the source of the emanation called "Points" (*Nikudot*). **And when** it arose in the Simple Will to reveal His Divinity, He brought forth "existences" and "effects" from that Simplicity. First, He emanated the one called **Crown** (*Keter*). Because of its extreme subtlety and its attachment to its Source, this Sefirah was not revealed at all. It is even called "Nothingness" (*Ayin*) to indicate that it is a Sefirah of absolute concealment. These names are not literal <note>The text warns against taking "Nothingness" too literally as a lack of existence; it refers to being beyond human comprehension</note>. Indeed, to think otherwise is an error, for the emanation is explained in many places as a subtle light. He is the "Cause of Causes," and to say otherwise contradicts our traditions. It is only called "Nothingness" when compared to the things that follow.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 1: On the Order of Emanation, various opinions were stated.
There are those who explained the chain of the Divine Attributes as emerging one from another, one by one in a linear sequence. Among them are those who placed **Foundation** (*Yesod*) before **Victory** (*Netzach*) and **Splendor** (*Hod*) to indicate that **Beauty** (*Tiferet*) also has a precedence in thought over Kindness and Severity. This is because the entire "Middle Line" is rooted in the Higher Crown and was unified with them during emanation for the purpose of "arbitration" <note>The Middle Line balances the Right (Kindness) and Left (Severity)</note>. This later caused Foundation to also be placed after its two companions, according to the truth of the matter.

### And there are...
...those who say regarding the **Higher Crown** (*Keter Elyon*) that "He is the light that includes three": Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding. Each one of them includes others. From Wisdom, a single light sparkles forth, including two: **Kindness** and **Victory**. From Understanding, a single light includes two: **Severity** and **Splendor**. And from the point of the Crown itself, a light sparkles forth including three: **Beauty**, **Foundation**, and **Kingship**. And there are those who said that Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding were emanated one from another, and from Understanding, the "seven lamps" <note>The seven lower Sefirot from Kindness to Kingship</note> emerged all at once.

### And all...
...is the truth. For before the emanation of the Sefirot, everything was hidden in the **Root of Roots** in a hidden existence—the ultimate concealment and unity where no form or "point" could be discerned at all. Rather, they were all unified in Him. Afterward, He emanated from Himself a single point, a single emanation: the **Crown** (*Keter*), which is called **Nothingness** (*Ayin*) because of its extreme precedence and subtlety within its Source. From it was emanated a second point in revelation: **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*), which is called **Being from Nothingness** <note>Hebrew: *Yesh mi-Ayin*; the first point of "somethingness" emerging from the incomprehensible</note>. Yet, "absence" still clings to it. Therefore, a third point was required for the revelation of existences: **Understanding** (*Binah*). Wisdom is the "beginning" and Understanding is the "end"—either because she completes their forms, or because they return to travel within the mystery of the Jubilee <note>A reference to the 50th year/Sefirah of Binah where all things return to their source</note>, as is known.

### And these three...
...points were all included in the Crown at first. There, the three "lines" <note>The Right, Left, and Middle pillars of the Sefirotic tree</note> were included, each one within the inclusion of its root in the Crown. After He chose to bring the point of Wisdom to light, He first flowed into it Understanding, then Beauty, Foundation, and Kingship. Afterward, Kindness and Victory were established within its essence. Within the Understanding that He built, Severity and Splendor were established. Wisdom emanated Understanding and first flowed the Middle Line into it, then Kindness and Victory, while Severity and Splendor were established within her essence. Understanding, through the power of Wisdom, emanated **Kindness**, in which **Victory** was included. Through her own power, she emanated **Severity**, in which **Splendor** was included. Through both of them, she emanated **Beauty** last, to bring the "dispute" <note>The tension between Kindness and Severity</note> toward "arbitration" <note>Balance</note>. Despite all this, Beauty is sometimes counted first, as its "body" is rooted in the Crown. **Afterward**, Kindness was revealed by way of "Fear/Dread" <note>Gevurah</note>, and Beauty revealed Victory through the power of Wisdom. Fear revealed Splendor through the power of Understanding. Beauty revealed Foundation through Victory, and through Foundation, it revealed Kingship. All of this was done through the power of the Crown. (And the Rabbis said, "the waters were pregnant and gave birth to darkness..." the intention in this is...)

# Juice of Pomegranates: Gate 5 — The Order of Emanation

To examine the form of Kindness (*Chesed*) and subsequently Understanding (*Binah*) in all its external essence, and Severity (*Gevurah*) with all its light; for the light is a branch of Severity, and Understanding acts with the power of the external Crown (*Keter*). There are 136 "faces" <note>original: "partzufim" — divine configurations or personas</note> to decide between the right and the left, between Kindness and Judgment. Because there are 136 configurations in Understanding, Kindness and Severity are revealed more prominently. Before their emanation, the Crown was hidden; therefore, they have a presence above Kindness and Severity. This is the reason why Beauty (*Tiferet*) sometimes inclines upward toward the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) <note>original: "shekhinah" — the indwelling presence of God</note> to indicate the "Segol" vowel pattern <note>three dots in a triangle, representing the balance of three Sefirot</note> over Kindness and Severity in the secret of this Eight-fold structure—which is hidden in Understanding on every side. Below Understanding, it moves from side to side and from below to above. This means it is situated below Kindness and Severity, as is now clear regarding the fifty small Sefirot, which act with the power of the thirty Sefirot: Kindness from the totality of Understanding, Severity opposite Understanding, and Beauty corresponding to the Crown, all acting through Understanding.

Subsequently, the built Kindness was revealed so that the power of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) would be included within it. Afterward, Severity and Splendor (*Hod*) were revealed so that the power of Understanding would be included within them. Then, Beauty and Foundation (*Yesod*) were revealed so that the power of the Crown would be included within them. In the writing of the extension of every Foundation within Beauty, it is sometimes found on the "wing" of Splendor—though this was not fully investigated due to the reason of the "chariot of Beauty." <note>referring to the complex interweaving of divine attributes</note> 

Afterward, the "Greenery" <note>a symbolic color for the Sefirah of Tiferet/Beauty</note> wrapped itself and moved from its place in the Kindness of Beauty, descending to become the tenth Sefirah below Foundation. Thus, Foundation became the ninth, as the writing states regarding the diminishing of the Greenery. This is as Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai (may his memory be a blessing) said in the *Tikkunei ha-Zohar* <note>a foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>: "Open to the thirty paths... as in the first day of the Ancient One, He opens the paths of Judgment," etc. "The Beloved did not go to the seat of the oppressed," etc. The Sage, Rabbi Isaac Luria <note>the Arizal, though the text attributes this to the source material used by Ramak</note>, wrote the "Order of the Tree" in this language, as transcribed by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (Ramak) in the *Book of Gleanings*, Gate 30, Chapter 14. This provides the reason for what we have mentioned.

Rather, they placed these signs as markers for the order of their emanation, their nourishment, and their flow. In the *Tikkunim*, it says: "Come and see the skull of this...

Since everything is conducted through the two paths of Kindness and Mercy, Heaven forbid that a seeker or one who meditates with a wicked heart should taste this for themselves by imagining a physical seal or form, Heaven forbid! They must not fall into the trap of physical imagination, which would conversely obscure the vision of the "Thorn" <note>a reference to the tip of the Hebrew letters, signifying the highest, most subtle points of divinity</note> and entangle the vision of what they are capable of receiving and bearing.

<meta>This page continues the transition from Gate 5 (Order of Emanation) to Gate 6 (Order of Arrangement). # Juice of Pomegranates: Gate 5 — The Order of Emanation

<margin>The Crown</margin> (It is hidden and not revealed in the diagram before us, just as the soul is hidden within the body. Within it, the Secret Wisdom <note>original: "Ha-Chochmah ha-Sstumah" — the Hidden Wisdom</note> is contained, and its void is revealed within it; therefore, it belongs there.) When the Hidden Wisdom struck it and its void in its proper place, it produced within it a "fifty." Then, when the Hidden Wisdom struck it and its void again, it produced the power to receive the Sefirah <note>one of the ten divine emanations</note>, resulting in a "four" within it. When the Hidden Wisdom struck it and its void a third time, it produced the power for the Sefirah to be seen, resulting in a "five." Afterward, it struck it and its void to produce the power to bequeath the Sefirot to their proper places—that is, in the final aspect of humility. Through this "striking," these aspects that were included in the Crown of the King, the Infinite (*Ein Sof*) <note>The Infinite, the most primordial state of God</note>, became the emanation of the dwellers of Wisdom, the King of the Crown. These last three aspects within the Crown are the three traces <note>original: "reshimot" — the impressions left by divine light</note> in Wisdom. So it was in the emanation of Understanding (*Binah*) from Wisdom, just as it was in the emanation of the five "extremities" and the "ship" <note>an obscure metaphor for a vessel of light</note> together. The three traces in Wisdom are: one joined to the Crown—not revealed, but rather its existence is there (this is the "four" in the Crown mentioned as the power to receive the Sefirah, which is hidden); the second in Wisdom was joined to the essence within the Crown (this is the "five" in the Crown, which was the power for the Sefirah to be seen); and the third of Wisdom, which was revealed in its own place (this was the power in the Crown that allowed it to bequeath the Sefirot to their proper places). <margin>And thus you shall judge for the three to separate to</margin> the three traces of Understanding. The matter of these aspects is certain and without any doubt at all; they are all within the "Orchard" (*Pardes*) <note>A reference to the *Pardes Rimonim*, the foundational work this text summarizes</note>. As it is written: "One acquired and one built," may he be filled with the depths of his words.

**The existence** of these acquisitions in a hidden way within the Crown and Wisdom is what is termed "Nalips," "Kikika," and "Krisa" <note>These are obscure, non-Hebrew terms used by medieval Kabbalists like Recanati to describe states of non-existence or potentiality</note>, according to the words of Rabbi Isaac of blessed memory in *The Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer* and in the words of Recanati <note>Menahem Recanati, a 14th-century Italian Kabbalist</note>. The intention is not that there was any doubt before the Blessed One until He had to decide and act, but rather that all things are drawn from the Absolute Will into the form of His Wisdom, to teach the existence and sources of the Sefirot hidden within Wisdom and the Crown. It follows, therefore, that the existence of the totality of the Sefirot consists of five systems:
1. One in the Crown (*Keter*)
2. Two in Wisdom (*Chokhmah*)
3. Three in Understanding (*Binah*)
4. Four in Beauty (*Tiferet*)
5. Five in Kingdom (*Malchut*)

The last four systems are all hinted at in the four letters of the Name <note>original: "Y-H-W-H", the Tetragrammaton</note>, for in each and every letter, all the Sefirot are included. The first system, which is in the Crown, is hinted at in the tip of the [letter] *Yod*. Due to its extreme subtlety, it is not described in detail except through the other systems. These first systems were explained in the *Zohar*, in the portion of *Bereshit* <note>Genesis</note>. And in the portion "When you make known" regarding the verse "May it be Your will," and "O Lord, You have made them all" <note>Psalm 104:24</note>. This is a language of "totality"—meaning it was not yet essentially structured in Wisdom, but only in the way of totality. In Wisdom, it was in the first rank, which is the language of "rectification" (*tikkun*) that was established in Understanding. It is fitting that in Beauty, it extends through "nursing" <note>original: "yanikut" — a stage of spiritual development</note>. "And the Earth" is Kingdom (*Malchut*), which receives that fullness, and there they "fled life" <note>referring to the distribution of life-force</note>. This is the meaning of the verse.

->### Chapter 6 and Afterward<-

Since the essence of the Crown itself has been explained as being included in three traces, like three dots as mentioned above, we must know how they were included in one another. In the point of the essence of the Crown itself, Beauty (*Tiferet*), Foundation (*Yesod*), and Kingdom (*Malchut*) were included, which relate to the Middle Line, the Line of Mercy. In the point of the essence of the root of Wisdom, Greatness (*Gedulah* / *Chesed*) and Victory (*Netzach*) were included, which relate to the Right Line, the Line of Kindness. In the point of the root of Understanding, Strength (*Gevurah*) and Splendor (*Hod*) were included, which relate to the Left Line, the Line of Judgment. This matter is brought in the secret of the "Actions," as will be explained in the Gate of Strikes and Governance. This is hinted at in *The Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer*: "With ten sayings the world was created, and with three they were included: Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge." The reason he said "Knowledge" (*Da'at*)—which is Beauty (*Tiferet*)—will be explained in the sixtieth gate.

**And when** it arose in His Blessed Will to emanate Wisdom from the Crown and to emanate within it the rest of the Sefirot, He first emanated and revealed within it the Crown and the Father <note>Wisdom is often called "Abba" or Father</note>. Then he revealed Beauty and the traces of his structures. They had arranged "configurations" <note>original: "partzufim" — divine personas</note> and were unified as one through the Foundation (*Yesod*), but they were not revealed like Understanding. The beginning of emanation and the formation of configurations were received in Wisdom. Even though their essence is from the Crown, they were not called by the name "emanation" until they reached Wisdom, because there they were revealed to have a name and a first utterance.

We now open with a portion of the five levels in emanation. The first is in Understanding, which was more visible because even in the Crown, there was power in one point of the three included, which is the "double-faced" configuration <note>original: "du-partzufin" — two entities joined together</note> corresponding to the "fifty." But in Understanding, more were added as the hidden things were clarified. Now, only a portion of the three levels—the "covering" and the "enclosure"—was revealed, which are more hidden than the "double-faced" configurations that are not yet found in their places. The fourth is the level of Strength (*Gevurah*) and Splendor (*Hod*), which have no recognizable revelation at all because they lack their source, as Understanding was still hidden in Wisdom and not yet revealed. Therefore, Wisdom emanated Understanding by the power of the Crown. At the time of Understanding's revelation, the hidden Line of Judgment was inherited and revealed within its essence, as is fitting for their origin and root. Immediately upon the emanation of Understanding, Wisdom emanated power from its essence, Kindness and Wisdom, and placed before the Crown "double-faced" configurations corresponding to Understanding. Within it were three levels of emanation: the first, the "double-faced" configuration, which is the most revealed because the Crown emanated it into Wisdom, and Wisdom, by the power of the Crown, emanated it into Understanding. Thus, the Crown is the actual emanator, and from it, the emanation was forced to be more revealed than the rest of the emanations within Understanding, because this involves a dual process from Wisdom to Understanding. The second is the level of the Line of Kindness (Greatness and Victory), which is hidden and "double-faced" because it only has one point of contact from Wisdom to Understanding. It is revealed more and more in the Line of Judgment, because that has only one point, and the Line of Judgment is still within its root in Understanding and has not taken its place at all. These things will also be explained—why Judgment only comes from Understanding and is hinted at there, because Understanding is the root of Judgment. Even in Understanding, it has no revelation. [It will also be explained] why Beauty and Kingdom rise up to the Crown, while Kindness and Wisdom only reach Wisdom and no further, and Strength and Splendor only reach Understanding and no further. As it is written in the *Tikunim*: Beauty and Kingdom rise to Understanding, and there they have a revealed source; they further rise to Wisdom, and there their head has a revealed source; and their root is in the "free gift" <note>likely referring to a higher level of grace</note>, not in their order in Understanding, which is higher. They further rise to the Crown, for there is their hidden root... and not Understanding, for those that are higher have no root except the root of Kindness, and so too for every place... in a very great concealment. The matter of the departure and ascent of these... will only happen through the awakening of the Sefirah to its root... but at the time when all the lines are refined in their root, all will be precious as one, and they will all rise as one, higher and higher, even to the Infinite (*Ein Sof*). All the points were distributed in Understanding according to the order I mentioned. Behold, Understanding, by the power of Wisdom, emanated Kindness... because the branch of Kindness entered. The reason they called Kindness to Understanding... to emanate the rest of the Sefirot in its way to the Infinite, because Beauty is the decider between the extremities, and the way of the decider comes after hearing the words of the contenders. Therefore, it was necessary to emanate...

# Slice of the Pomegranate: Gate 6 — The Order of their Standing (Juice of Pomegranates)

...whose name is like the name of his Master <note>A reference to the angel Metatron, whose name is numerically equivalent to Shaddai</note>, and whose wisdom in its value is like a female that brings forces into action. Understanding (*Binah*) is between the two of them, in the secret of the "Hidden Knowledge" (*Da'at*) contained within it. This is the secret of the three names revealed to Moses at the Burning Bush. Therefore, it is said that if a specific virtue is desired, one should first say "I Will Be" (*Ehyeh*) sent me, and then "I Am That I Am" (*Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh*). It seems more likely to explain that the designer of this specific diagram thought there was "Judgment" (*Din*) within Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), which is why he drew it on the left—but this does not bring satisfaction to the mind.

**Truthfully**, there is a semblance of proof from what we learned in the *Faithful Shepherd* <note>original: "Ra'aya Meheimna," a section of the Zohar</note>: "And I was among the exiles"—this refers to the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, the final Sefirah</note>, within which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is One. The letter *Vav* (ו) represents an addition, and "I" (*Ani*) is the "River," the "Righteous One" (*Tzadik*), the foundation of the worlds. A river flows out of Eden to water the garden: What is "Eden"? It is Understanding (*Binah*). The river flows out from it, and this is the *Vav*, the "Son of YH" <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton, representing Father and Mother/Wisdom and Understanding</note>, the rank of the "River." Nevertheless, it emerges from the Supernal Mother (*Binah*) and spreads through the six Sefirot until the "Righteous One" (*Yesod*), and from him, it waters the Garden, which is the *Shekhinah*. What is the meaning of K-B-D <note>original: ככ"ד</note>? *Kaf* is the Crown (*Keter*); *Bet* is Understanding (*Binah*); *Resh* is the "Beginning of Wisdom" (*Reishit Chokhmah*). The Crown is on the right, Wisdom is on the left, and Understanding is in the middle. It is a "chariot" to ascend the ascents. All ten Sefirot are included in this River, which extends to the "Righteous One," who includes everything. Because of him, the "Righteous One" established a "great and strong tree," providing food for all, and upon him, everything depends.

**However**, these words prove that the prophecy of Ezekiel was an exception necessitated by the circumstances of the hour. The intention was that he saw [the divine] within the exile for the protection of Israel—where Understanding (*Binah*) and Beauty (*Tiferet*) were together, in the secret of "the hand did not move from the hand of Moses." This remained while enemies entered Jerusalem and until they departed—meaning, throughout the duration of the exile, they would together "sweeten the secret" to save the children and find a way to appease their iniquity. This occurred by the river *Yesod* (Foundation) which flows from *Eden* (Understanding), below which no eye can see. The "Inner Knowledge" (*Da'at*), which includes the extremities, emerges and spreads through them in a hidden way. The "poured river" of their foundation is the extension of the River, and from it comes the watering of the Garden. It is explained in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar</note> that this was a vision Ezekiel had in a dream—meaning, through the Sefirah of Kingship (*Malkhut*) and with "eyes closed" from the side of *Yesod*. Therefore, there were ten Sefirot included in the River in the secret of K-B-D. This refers to the "Female Tree" where *Yesod* is the deciding factor. In the "Male Tree," the arrangement would be different. Thus, Ezekiel's prophecy was a temporary instruction for that time, and one does not derive general laws from it.

**Chapter 3: Behold**, Rabbi Isaac of Acre, the student of Nachmanides, in his book *Enlightening the Eyes* (*Me'irat Einayim*), thought to draw the Right and Left of the Tree relative to the writer and reader. This is similar to the way one gives the greeting of "peace" after prayer <note>referring to the bows at the end of the Amidah prayer</note>. This follows the plain meaning of the verse, "I have set the Lord always before me" (Psalm 16:8). He said that the "Face" of God seeks us, and we see the "Back." Even if it were as he said, it is written "And you shall see My back." Furthermore, we find that our father Abraham traveled "toward the South," which is the right side of the world and the "Right Hand of the Most High." Regarding the *Tefillin* <note>phylacteries</note>, of which it is written "And all the peoples of the earth shall see," the reader reads them in their proper order according to the agreed-upon arrangement of the parchment we mentioned in the previous chapter: the right of the parchment corresponds to the right of the reader.

**However**, the giving of the "peace" greeting is an exception to the rule. Abaye did not know this and thought to say "his own right and left," but Rabbah taught him that one ought to show himself as one who is certain his prayer has been accepted...

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A Kabbalistic diagram depicting a right hand held vertically. Specific Hebrew letters are assigned to parts of the hand: the fingertips are labeled (from right to left) ח (Chesed/Mercy), ג (Gevurah/Strength), ת (Tiferet/Beauty), נ (Netzach/Victory), ה (Hod/Splendor). The thumb contains the letter י (Yod). In the center of the palm is an א (Aleph), with a ו (Vav) below it, and a ה (He) at the base of the hand, spelling out the Tetragrammaton and other divine names. The letter מ (Mem) is positioned next to the wrist. This diagram represents the mapping of the Sefirot and Divine Names onto the human hand to aid in meditative prayer.</image-desc>

...as a sign for the world. For the scale of merit and the scale of guilt will be according to its value, not according to the value of those who receive it. One acts according to His actions and His creatures. Afterward, "His right" is "our right" and "His left" is "our left." He is the "Head" who oversees them in all His limbs. This is the view of all the masters of this diagram who wrote it in the likeness of a "female" arrangement. Regarding the "male" arrangement, "His right" is opposite the divine Right. Thus, His right will be opposite the Right of the Supernal ones, and His left opposite their Left. Furthermore, since in truth there is no "above," nor "five fingers of the hand of God," nor "five fingers of the foot," nor right, nor left, nor back, nor front—as all these descriptions prove—they are actually five of the "branches" of the Tree that were spread and planted for the honor of Israel. Our Sages said that there were ten things created at twilight, and from them, everything was created. Do not be confused by this: there is no "right" or "left" there. Everything is "Right" and everything is "Left" in the Blessed One. How much more so for the "Cause of Causes" who is exalted above all perception—may He be blessed and exalted—for He has neither right nor left, neither front nor back.

**To understand** the matter of the order of the Sefirot properly: know that in the realm above, there is no right, left, front, back, separation, or division. Rather, the matter involves the "Cause of Causes." Their existence is a chain of emanation (*hishtalshelut*), one from the other, from the Cause to the Effect.

**And behold**, it is known that every "Cause" encompasses its "Effect," and every cause encompasses that which was caused by it. In this way, all existences are chained together, cause after cause, from the first until the "navel of the earth." This one is the effect of that one, and this one encompasses that one like circles within circles. This whole sequence is within the Infinite (*Ein Sof*)...

<image-desc>A complex geometric diagram consisting of a central square containing the letter מ (Mem). The square is surrounded by multiple ornamental borders and architectural-like patterns. This represents the Sefirah of Malkhut (Kingship) as a container or "palace" that receives and holds the divine light from the higher Sefirot.</image-desc>

...and it is blessed in the "Hidden Wisdom." It is written around it "The North," and so on, until the end of the Sefirah of *Malkhut* (Kingship), which is the "Conclusion." It is written "The Conclusion of the Encompassment." It is written "The Atmosphere of the World of Action" <note>the physical realm</note> until it is found "in the center of the Earth," "in the middle of the Palace." It is written "Seven Lands," as explained in the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in the portion *Vayakhel*. Let the reader not mistakenly think that when we say the Sefirot encompass one another, we mean it in terms of physical space or circles. Rather, grasp it in your wise soul: despite this, there are qualities of "high" and "low" in terms of cause and effect, as in a chain or a wheel...

**Chapter 5: In this way**, they will be explained regarding the matter of the "Ten," but not in another way. For they are distant from the "Complexities of the Body" <note>physical limitations</note>. The author of *Ma'alot ha-Binah* also proves this and explains that everything is founded upon the Infinite (*Ein Sof*). It is written that the Crown encompasses Wisdom, and so on, each one within the other. Also in the Zohar, portion *Terumah*: "From the time that the seven heavens were created, the *Shekhinah* includes them all," and so on. Similarly, the Tabernacle hints at the *Shekhinah* being comprised of the ten Sefirot...

And many followed after him.

<meta>This page continues the discussion from Gate 6 of *Asis Rimmonim* regarding the visual arrangement of the Sefirot. # Slice of the Pomegranate: Gate 6 — The Order of Their Standing | Juice of Pomegranates

Whose name is like the name of his Master <note>A common reference to the angel Metatron, though here applied to a specific Sefirotic configuration</note>, and Wisdom in its value is like a female that brings forces into action, while Understanding lies between them in the secret of the "Knowledge" <term>Da'at; the third "hidden" Sefirah that balances Wisdom and Understanding</term> hidden within it. This is the secret of the three names revealed to Moses at the Burning Bush. Therefore, some explain that if we require the virtue of the *Segolta* <note>original: *segolta* — a triangular cantillation mark</note>, one should first say "I Shall Be" <note>original: *Ehyeh*</note> hath sent me, and then "I Am That I Am." However, it seems more correct to explain that the creator of this diagram thought there was Judgment in Wisdom, and therefore depicted it on the left; but there is no satisfaction in this approach.

**Truly**, there is a semblance of proof for this from what we learned in the book *The Faithful Shepherd* <note>original: *Ra'aya Meheimna* — a later layer of the Zohar</note>: "And I was in the midst of the exile" <note>Ezekiel 1:1</note>. This refers to the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>, in which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is One. The letter *Vav* (ו) is an addition, and "I" (*Ani*) is the River, the Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds. "And a river goes out from Eden to water the garden" — what is Eden? This is Understanding <term>Binah</term>. A river goes out from it, and this is the *Vav*, the "Son" of the letters *Yod* and *He*. It is the level of the forty-eight <note>likely referring to the 48 prophets or 48 qualities of Wisdom</note>, and the forty-eight comes out from the Supernal Mother and spreads through the six Sefirot until the Righteous One <term>Yesod; the Foundation</term>, and from him, he waters the Garden, which is the Divine Presence. What is the meaning of the acronym *KaBaR*? *Kaf* is the Crown <term>Keter</term>, *Bet* is Understanding <term>Binah</term>, *Resh* is the Beginning of Wisdom <term>Reshit Chokhmah</term>. Crown is on the right, Wisdom is on the left, and Understanding is in its fingers. He rides to ascend the ascents of the ten Sefirot; they are all included in this River which spreads until the Righteous One, who includes everything. Because of him, the Sages established the Righteous One as "the tree that is great and strong, and food for all is in it" <note>Daniel 4:9</note>, and upon him everything hangs.

<image-desc>A woodcut diagram depicting a left hand. Five Hebrew letters are inscribed on the fingers from thumb to pinky: ח (Chokhmah/Wisdom), ב (Binah/Understanding), ג (Gedulah/Greatness), ד (Gevurah/Power), ה (Hod/Splendor). The palm contains the kabbalistic letter combination גלתהג, and below it, the letters נ (Netzach/Victory), ה (Hod/Splendor), מ (Malchut/Kingdom).</image-desc>

**However**, these matters are brought regarding the prophecy of Ezekiel, which was an exception to the rule for a specific time and purpose. He saw it "in the midst of the exile" for the protection of Israel. The Divine Presence and the Beauty <term>Tiferet</term> were in a unique union, in the secret of "this did not descend from the hands of the secondary authorities." This was necessary because enemies had entered Jerusalem, so throughout the duration of the exile, they [the divine forces] would counsel together in secret to save the children and find a way to atone for their sins. This occurs through the River of Foundation <term>Yesod</term> which comes from the Eden of Understanding, for there is no "Eden" lower than it. This is Beauty <term>Tiferet</term> in the secret of Knowledge, which includes the extremities, going out and spreading through them in the path of "Gold" <note>original: *Ketem*</note>. "A river pours out their foundation" refers to the flow of the River, and from it comes the watering of the Garden. It is explained in the *Tikkunim* <note>Tikkunei ha-Zohar</note> that this was Ezekiel's vision "in a dream," meaning in the Kingdom <term>Malchut</term>, and with "eyes closed" from the side of the Foundation. Therefore, the ten Sefirot were included in the River in the secret of *KaBaR*, which is the female aspect of *AShM* <note>Fire, Peace, Water - a kabbalistic acronym</note>, where Foundation is the deciding factor in the "Female Tree." In the "Male Tree," however, Beauty would be the deciding factor in *AMS* <note>Air, Water, Fire</note>. The arrangement of the letters of the River is *KaRB* [Cherub]. Thus, Ezekiel's prophecy was a "temporary instruction" <note>original: *Hora'at Sha'ah*</note> and we do not derive the standard rule from it.

<image-desc>A rectangular diagram containing nested squares. The innermost square features the Hebrew letter 'מ' (Mem, representing Malchut or the Center). Decorative hatch marks surround the inner border.</image-desc>

### Chapter 3: Behold,
Rabbi Isaac of Akko, the student of Nachmanides <note>original: *Ramban*</note>, 
in the book *Illumination of the Eyes* <note>original: *Me'irat Einayim*</note>, thought to depict the Right 
and the Left of the Tree according to the perspective of the verse and the reader. This is similar to the way one bows "Peace" after the prayer <term>Amidah</term>. This follows the literal meaning of the verse "I have set the Lord before me always" <note>Psalm 16:8</note>. He said that the "Face" belongs to the Divine, and we see the "Back." If it be as he says, then "You shall see My back" <note>Exodus 33:23</note> is written. Furthermore, we find that our father Abraham was "traveling toward the South," which is the "Right" of the world and the "Supernal Right." Regarding Phylacteries <term>Tefillin</term>, of which it is written, "And all the peoples of the earth shall see," the reader reads them in their order, according to the order of the accepted parchment we mentioned in the previous chapter: that the right of the parchment aligns with the right of the reader. **However**, the giving of the "Peace" greeting is an exception to the rule. His father did not know this and thought to say "His right and his left," but his teacher taught him that it is proper to show oneself at the best, so that his prayer may be accepted.

<column-break/>

Therefore, in the general world, even Merit and Guilt are judged relative to us, according to the subtle and hidden spirituality, even in the way of His blessed actions—not like His usual ways. And thus His right is our right and His left is our left. Furthermore, he began to be added upon us in all its words. 
And all this is the Supernal that spreads out, a form in its supernal power, righteous according to the order of the *Vav* and the order of his right, a voice like the right. 
In our arrangement, the right will be opposite the Right of the Supernal ones, and his left opposite their left. Furthermore, according to the truth, there is neither Right nor Left above, but everything is the five fingers of the Hand of the Lord and the five fingers of the Foot. 
Right and Left are all the holiness of His right, which were thirty, and His supernal deeds that spread the spirituality. With wings for extra honor, the Sages of blessed memory achieved this, for there are Ten Commandments in the Assembly; from them, everyone receives, and for one person it ceases. He is protective of their money in the Palm, which has no right or left. Everything is Right and everything is Left. This is certainly true for the subtle spiritual beings who oversee every creature and providence. He is exalted, having neither right nor left, neither front nor back.

**And to understand** the matter of the order of the Sefirot well: know that above there is no right or left, no front or back, and no separation or division. Rather, the matter we shall mention exists only so that we may grasp how one level is derived from another in the world. 

**And behold**, it is known that every Cause which encompasses an effect draws it in, and every creature encompasses itself. Thus, all created things descend in a chain, linked together. The Supernal is engraved upon the sphere of the Earth, one atop the other, and one strengthened by the other, like the layers of an onion <note>original: *galdei galgalim* — literally "layers of the spheres"</note>. In this way, all are placed within the Holy Center: Wisdom is within the Crown, Understanding is within Wisdom, Grace is within Understanding, and so on, until the bottom of the Kingdom <term>Malchut</term>. Within the Kingdom is the Shell <term>Klipah</term>, and within the tenth "Yod" <note>likely referring to the physical world/Asiyah</note>, until the sphere of the Earth is found in the very center of everything, like a mustard seed. 

This began with the "Four Winds" <note>Directions</note> in their placement, as the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, of blessed memory, in the Torah portion of *Vayikra*. The student should not be mistaken by our saying that the Sefirah "encompasses" and that this one is "beneath" that one, as if to attribute to them the physical surrounding of a high place. Rather, in the soul, everything refers to the supernal holiness and Providence, in the manner of the world where there is a Giver <term>Mashpia</term> and a Receiver <term>Mushpa</term>, as explained.

### Chapter 5: And in this 
way they arrange the matter of the "Crown" <term>Atarah; another name for Malchut</term>, and not in any other way. For the physical husks of the body are far removed from this. (Also, the author of *Illumination of the Eyes* agreed to this, and it is necessary that everything is founded in the Infinite <term>Ein Sof</term>, and within the Crown is Wisdom, etc., and so they are all one within the other.) In the Zohar, portion of *Terumah*, (it implies there are nine "runnings" <note>referring to the Sefirotic flows</note> and the Divine Presence includes them all... and so too) in *Juice of the Pomegranate* <note>original: *Asis ha-Rimmon*</note>, the Divine Presence is included...

# Chapter 2: And some...
<margin>They drew them far apart like a *segol* <note>A Hebrew vowel mark consisting of three dots in an inverted triangle</note>, and others far apart in the likeness of a *segol*, and for the signs of their openings like a *segol*, in this manner:</margin>

->Crown<-

->Beauty<-
->Victory Splendor<-
->Foundation<-
->Sovereignty<-

<margin>And in this we follow the rule for the drawing of the Right Line being to the right of the scribe, and the Left Line to the left of the scribe. However, there is one who wrote the opposite <note>original: *le-hefekh*</note>, according to the way they said regarding the three steps at the end of the Standing Prayer <term>Amidah</term>: first one bows to their left, because that is the "Right" of the Holy One, Blessed be He; and after that to their right, which is the "Left" of the Holy One. One should not worry about his words (for his intention was to see the Face, where the Face's right is opposite our left, and the Face's left is opposite our right; therefore, one should not see the Face, as it is said: "You shall see my back, but my face shall not be seen" <note>Exodus 33:23</note>. Therefore, his words do not hold water). Furthermore, his view is the opposite of the matter of the Tefillin <term>phylacteries</term>, etc., for the three sections are to the right of the reader and the left of the wearer, and the section of "And it shall be if you obey" <term>Gevurah/Strength</term> is to the right of the wearer and the left of the reader. Consider also the ascents of the Altar, for there the Foundation of the world is, ascending to the South-East horn, which is the "Right" of the world. The matter of the steps is because (even though) in my prayer I established the upper worlds in a "backwards" manner <note>looking from behind</note>, nevertheless the Sefirot are linked to Him in a "frontal" manner. Since the three steps are to the right of the Holy One, which is our left. And to show also that his words are not his own, but rather from our intention and from the little we heard of his words. From the general rule of the "Backs" it follows that the Right comes from Water <note>original: *yamin mi-mayim*</note>. And according to the truth, above that which the princes of life and joy arrange. And the whole spirit of the secret and the one who exists and establishes the Foundation of my life, and the Holy One... let His days be sanctified and purified and spread out for merit; therefore, draw them in the way that was explained to be correct.</margin>

Below it are the letters "T-T" (Tav-Tav). Below those is a horizontal line with "N-H-Y" (Nun-He-Yod) followed by "M" (Mem).</image-desc>

<column-break/>

In the nineteenth Gate, their existence is in the "Skull" <term>Karkapta</term> in the secret of Understanding <term>Binah</term>.
And there is one who indicated in the upper *Yod* <note>The Hebrew letter י</note> that the "tip" <note>the small stroke at the top</note> refers to the Crown, and its body's right and left to Wisdom and Understanding. Its "pregnancy" <note>the middle bulge</note> is from Knowledge <term>Da'at</term>, which we understand from the lower tip of the upper *Yod*. Corresponding to it is the "Eternal Covenant" <note>the phallic Sefirah, Yesod</note> in the upper tip of the lower *Yod*, in its existence above Splendor, as we mentioned in the previous Gate. In the "roof" <note>the horizontal top stroke</note>, Greatness is to the right, Strength to the left, and Beauty in the middle; and upon their ends are the fingers of the hands. In the lower *Yod*, Victory is to the right, Splendor to the left, and upon their ends are the toes of the feet, with the Covenant in the middle. Do not ask why we do not interpret the upper *Yod* this way, for there is no "deciding factor" <note>mediator</note> at all between "Father" and "Mother" <term>Abba and Imma; Wisdom and Understanding</term>, except between the roots of Greatness and Strength; and it is enough to stretch Knowledge to the lower tip. And here in the lower *Yod*, the tip that points downward shall be Sovereignty.

**Others** drew right, left, and middle in the "roof" alone. In the upper *Yod* they placed Wisdom, Understanding, and Beauty; and in the lower, Victory, Splendor, and Sovereignty, one above the other. At their heads is a small path above to hint at the nourishment the Crown receives from the "Solitary Tree," and below in Sovereignty, where the "spoil" is divided among its "wings." Others imagined them in a circular form, "their end wedged in their beginning" <note>A famous phrase from the Sefer Yetzirah describing the Sefirot as a cycle</note>.

**However**, the beloved drawing agreed upon according to our system in this book is the likeness of the first letter *Aleph* (א). The first three Sefirot are like the *Segolta* accent; the second and third triads are like two *segol* vowels; and Sovereignty receives from them all. And Rabbi Shem Tov <note>original: ה"ר ש"ט — likely Shem Tov ibn Shem Tov, a 15th-century Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory, changed only the first three, drawing them one on top of the other, led to this by a different opinion he had read; even if he did not choose it, he did not wish to argue against it, and we shall speak of it soon. Many followed after him.

# Chapter 2: They Said
In the *Book of the Faithful Shepherd* <note>original: *Sifra De-Meheimna*</note> it says: Wisdom, Kindness, and Victory are to the right of their structure; the right side is the "Right hand of the Lord that does valiantly, the right hand of the Lord is exalted." And three are bound as one on the left: Understanding, Strength, and Splendor. And three levels are in the Middle Column: Crown, Beauty, and Foundation. And others are between them and the left. And in the *Tikkunim* <note>original: *Tikkunei Zohar*</note> it says: Nine Sefirot are tripled in the Middle Column in this manner: Wisdom, Kindness, Victory; Crown, Beauty, Foundation; Understanding, Strength, Splendor. Sovereignty is the tenth to them and the fourth to them.

**And they** said: Beauty <term>Tiferet</term> consists of three vowel points: *Chiriq* (ִ), *Cholam* (ֹ), and *Shuruq* (ּ). The tip of the *Yod* above is *Cholam*; the tip below is *Chiriq*; and the middle body is *Shuruq*. When these three are as one, they are the *Segolta* accent, the *Shalshelet* <note>a zigzagging accent</note>, the *Shuruq*, and the *Segol*. The Crown over Wisdom and Understanding is the *Segolta*; *Cholam* is over the letter *Tzadi*. *Segol* is the point under the *Tzadi*. Kindness, Strength, and Beauty are below. Victory, Splendor, and Foundation in the middle are the *Shuruq*. And these—when Beauty is in the middle—are the *Shalshelet* accent. Thus far. Note carefully that he first mentioned *Segolta*, *Shalshelet*, and *Shuruq* regarding the existence of Beauty and Foundation above their ends and within Understanding, and then he explained the two *segols* in terms of the "deciding" <note>balancing</note> aspect. **There is** another way that draws a *segol* and above it also in the place of the *Segolta*. Rabbi Shem Tov wrote that this does not conflict, and it contains a very deep secret, for he counted the ten Sefirot from the Supernal Crown whose name is...

### Segment of the Pomegranate: Gate 6 — The Order of their Arrangement — Nectar of Pomegranates

In all the levels, and thus wrote Rabbi Abraham <note>original: *ha-Rav Avraham*; likely Abraham Galante, a prominent disciple of Moses Cordovero</note> of blessed memory, the student of the Sage <note>original: *he-Chakham*; referring to Moses Cordovero, author of *Pardes Rimmonim*</note> may he rest in peace: **And the clear truth** is that the emanated beings <term>Sefirot: the ten creative powers or attributes through which the Infinite reveals itself</term> are not drawn into a physical place. Rather, it is according to our saying, "Blessed is the Place" <note>A traditional Jewish epithet for God, implying He is the "space" in which the world exists, rather than the world being His space</note>, for He is the "place" of the world. For the Infinite <term>Ein Sof: the Boundless or Infinite Godhead prior to any emanation</term> is the "place" for the Crown [Keter], and the Crown is the place for all that is beneath it, and Wisdom [Chokhmah] is the place for what is beneath it. Likewise, Sovereignty [Malkhut] is the place for the World of Creation [Beriyah], and Creation for the World of Formation [Yetzirah], and Formation for the World of Action [Asiyah]. This continues until the central point. Thus, the element of Earth is found within the element of Water, which is within the Air, and the Air is within the element of Fire, and all of them are within the celestial spheres. In this way, every effect is encompassed by its cause, until the conclusion of the levels.

<margin>
And the explanation of the intent of the Sefirot according to the Rama <note>Rabbi Moses Cordovero</note> in the writing of the book *Galui ha-Sodot* [The Revealment of Secrets], and the memory of the writing of the Sefirot above. What was written above concerning the order of their standing: that which was written is the way of the intention in the Sefirot. For just as when they went at the beginning, the Blessed Creator willed and influenced the Wisdom which is the second level, so too it joins together. This is the secret of the "standing," which can be explained and joined as it was at the beginning. Wisdom is the second level. From this perspective, the quality of their inclusion is shown in the likeness of their birth, to be in this: Crown, and then the Crown influences Wisdom and Understanding. Therefore, Wisdom is joined to the right and the crowns associated with Understanding to the left, so that Understanding is the "bride" and receives through her. And with this, since Wisdom is influenced like a King and Understanding as Might, it is joined.
</margin>

->The Gate<-

<image-desc>The names of the ten Sefirot are arranged in a textual diagram reflecting the Tree of Life layout: Keter (כתר) at the top; followed by Binah (בינה) on the left and Chokhmah (חכמה) on the right; then Gevurah (גבורה) on the left and Gedulah (גדולה) on the right; Tiferet (תפארת) in the center; Hod (הוד) on the left and Netzach (נצח) on the right; Yesod (יסוד) in the center; and Malkhut (מלכות) at the bottom.</image-desc>

As a metaphor, Greatness [Gedulah] is under Wisdom, and Might [Gevurah] is under Understanding, to indicate that its influence and nourishment will be "Good" <note>The Hebrew word for "Good" (Tov) is often associated with the right-side attribute of Lovingkindness/Greatness</note> from Wisdom, while the other [Might] has its root and nourishment from Understanding. Similarly, from the right side, the Crown influences Beauty [Tiferet], which is necessarily placed beneath it, between Lovingkindness and Might, facing the "opening" <note>the central channel</note> to receive its influence and nourishment. Its uniqueness is that it serves as a "mountain" <note>or "fortress"</note> for its aforementioned hosts, meaning it extends slightly below Lovingkindness and Might, as mentioned—that is to say, "below." In this manner is the order of the "Standing of the Ten Sefirot" <note>original: *K.S.* for *Eser Sefirot*</note> for the service of the second *segol* <note>Referring to the triangular arrangement of the lower Sefirot</note>. Beneath Foundation [Yesod] are the three branches spreading from the three general categories. Each branch is for Wisdom and Understanding to enter (and look beneath the first "mountain" for its nourishment, which is under Greatness, from where the essence of its nourishment comes; and Foundation is under Beauty, from where its nourishment comes. Because it is the ninth of them all, it extends downward). The order of the "chains" [Sovereignty] will be under Foundation, because it is the tenth level and only receives through it. This is the order of the standing of the Sefirot in their levels. Everything is a metaphor for its rank, level, and excellence as they were emanated. Similarly, what was mentioned in the Zohar <term>Zohar: The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</term> regarding the Sefirot—sometimes as "above" and "below" and sometimes returning to their inclusion—is in this way. For the "Arms" <note>the Sefirot of Chesed and Gevurah</note> will be like the arms, the torso, and the thighs. This is more their "reception" of the spirit of influence and help from the Infinite and the upper Sefirot, as explained many times in the Zohar. Specifically in the section of *Pekudin* <note>a section of the Zohar</note>, "a command for Might," etc., until it becomes a "trench" and becomes more established to be a source and cause for the "eyes" of the Sefirot... the moon [Sovereignty] which receives from the Sun [Beauty]... and sometimes it influences not through the center but only to one side alone, like the "intentions of the prayer" <note>original: *kavanot ha-tefillah*</note> to receive influence from above... and it will also be purified until it becomes the "Seventh" <note>a title for the Sefirah of Sovereignty/Shekhinah</note>. The matter of its "descent" is moving toward a lowering of excellence and thickness, and a coarsening due to the withdrawal of the upper influence from one of the attributes, until its "falling" from its excellence... as if "hiding the Face," as when one falls from God... and the "descent" of the attributes to be in the level of "hosts" <note>angels or lower spiritual forces</note>... as was explained regarding the ten Sefirot in their own right. And according to what we have written, all these matters will be opened. For the "standing" and "thickness" and the levels being one under the other depends on these two paths and the foundations mentioned above. From this it is clear that sometimes it will be in the secret of the "Tree" [the vertical array] and sometimes in the secret of "Lovingkindness" [the horizontal/triangular array]. Everything is according to the influence and the general state, with the aforementioned agreement: that the "standing" is a metaphor for the rank of their nobility, their nourishment, their influence, and the unfolding of their actions—this one to Judgment and this one to Mercy. And until the end of the "Throne" <note>the World of Creation</note>... as is found in the Zohar, Rabbi Mark on the verse "And I was in the midst of the exile" <note>Ezekiel 1:1</note>: The word *ba-tokh* [in the midst/center]—the letter *Bet* is Crown [Keter], *Bet* is Understanding [Binah], *Tav* is Beginning, and *Khaf* is Wisdom [Chokhmah]... the "eyes" are Wisdom and the "encompassed" is Understanding... (this implies that Understanding is between the Crown and the Crown, and this is explained according to our general words). This is the secret of the "Straight" [Yosher] arrangement, which is not talking about "clothing" <note>metaphysical layers</note> but rather its purpose is to show its strength over Israel... and from the Holy Vision, which is the "Foundation of the King" [Yesod], and in this secret the influence was drawn... and since the Shekhinah <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence, associated with the Sefirah of Sovereignty</term> is known as the "Land of the Living" [Eretz Ha-Chayim]... above for the unique "Tzaddik" <note>the Righteous One, a title for Foundation</note>... then Foundation, and then Beauty and Sovereignty over the Foundation in the way of "diminishment" <note>referring to the moon's diminishment</note>... and this "Exile" [Golah] goes above, which is Understanding [Binah] (Understanding is called "Pleasure" [Eden] and also from there and above it belongs to the "Days of Pleasure"). And Foundation receives from Understanding and Foundation to water the "Beast of the Garden" [Chayat ha-Gan], which is Sovereignty. This is what is meant by "the support in the Crown and its head in the Crown"... so too when this attribute is from Foundation... Wisdom is on the right... and the Shekhinah is on Wisdom... (and see later where it says the letter *He* will be over *He*, meaning Understanding and Wisdom).

After his heart has understood how to unify the worlds through the "Back" <note>original: *achorayim*; referring to the hidden or external aspect of divinity</note> which is visible, his ear will then listen to the "Face" <note>original: *panim*; referring to the inner, luminous aspect of divinity</note> which is awesome. Regarding what King David said, "I have set the LORD always before me" (Psalm 16:8), it is in the sense of: "I do not listen to those who would have me remove the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven from myself." This is the secret of the "Love of Kindness" <note>original: *ahavat chesed*</note>, and this is why the verse continues, "because He is at my right hand, I shall not be moved."
