### Chapter 5: Understanding (Binah)
It is explained in many places in the Zohar that she <note>The Sefirah of Binah is grammatically feminine</note> is Mercy. Even though she is not Judgment herself, judgments emerge from her side and are strengthened within her, and they "hang" from her. The explanation of "emerge from her side" is that they were emanated from her power, not from her essence. "Strengthened within her" means that without her, there is no sadness, as will be explained shortly. "They hang from her" means to be heard by her and to be transformed into Mercy at her will. In the Zohar's commentary on the Song of Songs, after Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explained the song that the lower beings sing to adorn the Kingdom (*Malchut*), they said via the mouth of Elijah: "It was decreed in the Supernal Beginning, a song of the praise of praises to the King to whom peace belongs." This is because she is a place that requires joy, for there is no anger or judgment there, as the World to Come <term>Olam Ha-Ba: The spiritual realm of reward, associated with Binah</term> is entirely joy and is a joy to all. Likewise, it sends happiness and joy to all levels. Just as an awakening of joy is needed to arouse this world from above, so too is it necessary to arouse joy and happiness from the "World of the Moon" <note>referring to the Sefirah of Malchut</note> toward the Supernal King. Likewise, the worlds stand in a single moment of anger, and the awakening only ascends from below to above. **He said** that there is another aspect in Understanding (*Binah*), which occurs when the Kingdom (*Malchut*) sings toward Understanding because Beauty (*Tiferet*) is her "Peace," and the Kingdom longs to be united with him. She sings forever for the continuation of the friendship between Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) and Understanding (*Binah*). However, the union of the generations occurs in the morning, and He scatters those songs. Understanding is a place that requires the awakening of joy so that she may bestow the abundance of her goodness; for when the children nurse, the milk increases in her breasts. Blessings, which are an addition of goodness, only rest in a place of male and female, so that the recipient may further bestow from them to his partner. He said that in Understanding there is neither anger nor "weak judgment." The emanation of her essence to all levels is joy. For when Strength (*Gevurah*) prevails from her power through a specific channel—for which reason she is called "the worker of strengths"—it is like a mother who disciplined her son and stirred his strength alone by ceasing the flow of her mercy from the extremities. The analogy is to a lamp that is always lit but is only used in the dead of night and darkness; only then is it aroused to lead the world. However, her emanation in a single glance to all the extremities, according to their nature, is Mercy in its essence, and the lamp is not extinguished—or rather, the light prevails over it and it serves no purpose <note>i.e., its "judgment" is swallowed up in its "mercy"</note>. There is another aspect to Understanding: that from the powers of the pillars of fire, it becomes sweetened and perfumed by one of the sparks of the sun. And what of it? It too is in Mercy. This was explained in the Torah portion of *Mishpatim*, where they said that when Strength (*Gevurah*) spreads out and the eyes blaze within the redness, the Holy Ancient One <note>the highest level of Keter</note> shines his whiteness, and it blazes into the Mother <note>Binah</note>, and she is filled with milk and nurses everyone.

### Chapter 4

### Chapter 5 and Chapter 6: The Sefirah
The second Sefirah is Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), and she is called "Beginning" because she was the first in revelation relative to the hidden Crown, which is the ultimate height. Until one finds her from her hiddenness, she is called "a hundred and sixty" in her elevation and the renewed "kneading." This Sefirah is also called "Thought" (*Machshavah*) to indicate that she too is hidden. Even though she is not as hidden as the Crown, she is nevertheless hidden in the depth of the concealed thought until there is no substance to it. And some say that Wisdom is also entirely exalted in the Crown. And some say that relative to the Crown, she is exalted Judgment, but relative to Understanding, she is exalted Mercy (and some have written that she is simple Mercy) and the Judgment is not aroused but rather extinguished and "clothed." And some say the opposite: that Understanding is Mercy and Wisdom is Judgment, and the Mercies of Understanding are "paired Mercies"—meaning that the Crown is simple Mercy, Wisdom is Judgment, and Understanding decides between them. For this reason, Understanding is precisely "the sweetness of sweetnesses." This means that these "sweetnesses" are Kindness (*Chesed*), and Strength (*Gevurah*), and Beauty (*Tiferet*). So too is his judgment in his movement: Crown corresponding to Kindness, Wisdom corresponding to Strength, and Understanding corresponding to Beauty. And they did not feel this in the "Deciding Mind" between the Supernal Wisdom and Understanding. The matters of this division are clarified in the *Addition of Judah* <note>original: *Tosefet Yehuda*</note>, who wrote that this is to decide between these orders and to say that Wisdom has some aspect of Judgment, and therefore called it the "Enduring Kindness" of the ten, and its sign is in the change and the reversal, etc. For since every cause and effect—the Cause bestows and the Effect receives—it must be that Judgment is bestowed and received. Therefore, the simple Wisdom is the beginning, and therefore it has a bit of Judgment...

The last <note>referring to the lower Sefirot</note> is linked according to our path. It is placed there because our intention is for the lower ones to relate to the upper ones, just as the upper ones relate to the lower. For above, they are not uniquely designated by a fixed name and attachment of Judgment and Mercy, as they are simple in the ultimate degree of simplicity and subtlety, requiring an ultimate unity in the essence of the "Shalitim" <term>Shalitim: Ruling powers or primary emanations</term>, as will be explained in the Gate of Places. Likewise, the "division of the lightning" <note>an allusion to the flash of emanation</note> mentioned in the general rules. And the sense of "feeling" also points toward this: being so close to the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), blessed be He, they are also Mercy. For according to the subtlety of His "countenance," so shall they be revealed; and according to their proximity to the source, so shall they be hidden.

In any event, the attribute of the Crown (*Keter*) will be complete Mercy, and the influence drawn from it will be according to the recipient. All the classes of Judgment <note>Gevurah</note> within the Crown exist to tip the scales against the forces of Judgment. This is proven by the fact that when the "heads of the horns" of Judgment are sweetened, they are neutralized, as Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, 13th-century scholar</note>, peace be upon him, explained regarding the night of the Passover. 

If one wonders how an action of Judgment can proceed from the Crown if it is absolute Mercy—how can the action of Judgment be secured from the Crown? Heaven forbid! But the essence is this: the action of Judgment is carried out through the ten Sefirot. Even what we call Mercy, it is because the Crown "hides its face" <note>original: "mastir panav"</note> (from the lower realms so that Judgment may act). This is the aspect of their reception, and at its end, it is an act of Judgment. This matter settles the action of Judgment as being also from the Blessed Infinite. For we are mindful to say that since He spreads through all the Sefirot, there is no place void of Him. Thus, He is Mercy, but by hiding His face, He consents to Judgment.

If one wonders further: if He removes His face and is hidden from the attributes, then the actions of the attributes would remain as they were when He was revealed. For according to His beauty, the actions of Judgment occur through the hiding of His face. One must say that regarding the "diminishing" <note>katnut</note>, different aspects are settled. When the attributes prevail and the "face of Mercy" spreads and is revealed, the actions and the Supernal light are revealed and unified in the Sefirot—manifestations of the Essence—until they are all unified as one in the ultimate refinement of the world. But when sins prevail and the conduits are blocked, the "light of joy" is removed and withdraws from the Sefirot. Yet, if it were removed entirely, the light would not manifest at all. Rather, it is a "minimizing" through which the light is hidden from all the Strength (*Gevurah*) within it. This is the "diminishing," and the influence adds up until the forces of Judgment prevail and perform their action without hindrance. Regarding this it is said: "Why, O Lord, do you stand far off? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?" (Psalm 10:1). He turns His back, and the Mercy is hidden. This is the cause of the existence of Judgment and its action in truth. There will be no remedy for this matter until the lower beings return from their evil way, and the light of the Infinite returns to be revealed through the Crown to all the Sefirot. Then the "eyes of Judgment" mentioned will be distanced by the flow of Supernal light, and all will be mended, as will be explained.

They are included and paired, side by side and one above the other; this one surrounds that one, and that one is surrounded by this one, just as every Cause surrounds its Effect. In truth, there is no "above" or "below" or "prior" in space or vacuum. All are a totality and a unity because they are unified and refined as one, becoming a single chain as explained in the books. # Chapter 4: General Principle
The root of movement that prevails over the "Five Strengths" (*Gevurot*) is the source of the emanation of everything, only to bring everything into the completed work upon the "heels" of the Crown (*Keter*). ...to action except through "Male and Female" <note>the polarity of active and passive forces</note>. The Crown alone is the exception to this rule, to teach about itself that it was brought into being from the Absolute Will without any [external] need at all. Concerning it, the sages said: "In what is too wondrous for you, do not investigate." However, Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) and Understanding (*Binah*) were only emanated from the power of the roots of Male and Female that were imprinted in the Crown. Indeed, the secret of "Face and Back" generally applies to the levels of subtlety and spirituality, not to the distinction between Kindness and Judgment. 

It is a vain falsehood to try and find the source of Judgment [elsewhere], for its existence is not absent even in the "Exalted Hiddenness" <note>Keter</note> as we mentioned. ...the sea of the Torah, and he separated it from the waters because it is the root of the faith of Israel. This reason also suffices for the intention of the *Kedushah* <note>The "Sanctification" prayer, where "Holy, Holy, Holy" is recited</note> which they found a root for in the *Ra’aya Meheimna* <term>Ra’aya Meheimna: "The Faithful Shepherd," a specific section of the Zohar</term> to explain the first "Holy" as the Crown (*Keter*) bound to Greatness (*Gedulah*); the second as Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) bound to Strength (*Gevurah*); and the third as Understanding (*Binah*) bound to Beauty (*Tiferet*). The *Book of Formation* (*Sefer Yetzirah*), the *Zohar*, and the *Bahir* all prove that Wisdom possesses thirty-two hidden paths. However, let us contemplate their inner nature slightly—not the "pillars" <note>the structural supports of the Sefirotic tree</note> from which we only recognize the outer surface, nor the "gates" which are open to every person of understanding.

### Chapter 5: Understanding (*Binah*)
It is explained in many places in the *Zohar* that Understanding is Mercy (*Rachamim*), and even though it is not Judgment (*Din*), Judgments emerge from her side and are strengthened within her, and they depend on her. This means "emerging from her side" implies they are emanated from her power, not from her core essence. And they "are strengthened within her" because without her, there is no sadness <note>original: "עציבו" (Aramaic), referring to the gravity or harshness of judgment</note>, as will be explained shortly. And they "depend on her" to be heard by her and to be turned back into Mercy according to her will. 

In the *Zohar* on the *Song of Songs*, after Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explained the song that the lower beings sing to adorn the Kingship (*Malchut*), they said regarding the "Mouth of Elijah" <note>A common introductory phrase for mystical revelations</note> that it was decreed by high permission: A song that is the praise of praises for the King to whom peace belongs <note>original: "למלכא דשלמא דיליה," a play on King Solomon's name, referring to the Sefirah of Tiferet</note>, because it is a place that requires joy, and there is no anger or judgment there. For the World to Come <note>a title for the Sefirah of Binah</note> is entirely joy and a unification for all. Likewise, it sends joy and gladness to all levels. Just as an awakening of joy is needed to stir this world from above, so too it is necessary to stir the "Moon" <note>The Sefirah of Malchut</note> with gladness and joy toward the Higher King. And when this is not so, the worlds exist in a state of anger, and the awakening does not ascend from below to above. 

He stated that there is another aspect within Understanding, which occurs when the Kingship (*Malchut*) sings toward Understanding because Beauty (*Tiferet*) is her "Peace," and Kingship desires to be united with him. She sings forever to maintain the friendship between Wisdom and Understanding. However, the union of the "Parents" <note>Wisdom and Understanding, known as Abba and Imma</note> is in the morning, and the "light for us" belongs to the time of songs. Understanding is a place that requires an awakening of joy so that she may overflow with the abundance of goodness; for when the "children" <note>the lower Sefirot</note> nurse the milk, her blessings and joy increase. For blessings, which are an addition of goodness, only dwell in a place where male and female are united. 

He added that the receiver continues to bestow from them to his mate. He stated that in Understanding, there is neither anger nor "weak judgment" <note>Din Rapheh</note>. The influence of her very essence to all levels is joy. For when Strength (*Gevurah*) prevails through her power in a specific channel—for which she is called "the worker of strengths"—it is because "his mother disciplined him" <note>A biblical allusion to Proverbs 31:1</note>; she awakens his Strength alone by ceasing the flow of her Mercy from the extremities. This is compared to a lamp that is always lit but is only used in the middle of the night and darkness; only then is it awakened to lead the world. However, her influence in a single glance toward all the extremities to provide for their work is, by nature, Mercy. A "Stranger" <note>original: "גר"</note> is only built when the vitality of the light overcomes him and he is not used for anything. 

Understanding has another aspect: from her power, the pillars of fire are sweetened and perfumed by one of the sparks of the Sun. What is this? It too is within Mercy. This was explained in the Torah portion of *Mishpatim*, where they said: "When Strength (*Gevurah*) spreads out and the eyes burn within the redness, the Ancient Holy One <note>Atika Kadisha, the highest aspect of the Divine</note> shines his whiteness and it burns into the Mother <note>Understanding</note>, and she is filled with milk and suckles everyone."

(Bottom of the Page) ...And how does it bestow? Every one of the extremities... <unclear>added from the words of the verse</unclear> and it will be as if it were a tithe. And all the aspects that exist will be like reflecting mirrors. And every female, meaning the receiver, and every male, meaning the giver, thus it shall be: every leaning and support, and every single point in these lower levels, the upper one bestows to the one beneath it. And the precision of this is that the Kingship (*Malchut*) receives and includes, and every part is called "male" in relation to the level below it, and "female" in relation to the level above it.

**Chapter 4:** And just as the transition of the verses occurs, where Kindness and Judgment are reversed from beginning to end and from end to beginning, and they are gathered at their end, so it will be in these pillars. And when the lights of the pillars are reversed, they will add to the beginning from its end to its beginning, or they will mix the directions of their attributes... in the way of inclusion and transformation. And the awakening that is explained in the Gate of Permutations will cause the paths of existence to ascend... and the pillars will be like essences and generalities in the two aspects of their actual existence. And they will be from the beginning to the end, ten attributes that are included in five places as mentioned above... as will be explained in the Gate of Details.

**Chapter 5 and Chapter 6:** The second Sefirah <term>Sefirah: A divine attribute or emanation</term> is Wisdom (*Chokhmah*). He began with Wisdom because it is the beginning. Its greatness in relation to the Crown (*Keter*), which is hidden in its aspects of action, until the end of its action, will be called "Living" (*Chai*), which points to the action and the refined influence. He began with this Sefirah and contemplated the lights until today, for it was in existence. This is according to the principle that it is not as hidden as the Crown; nonetheless, it is hidden in the depth of thought which was contemplated until it existed within it. 

Some say that even in Wisdom, there is absolute Mercy as in the Crown. Others say that in relation to the Crown, it possesses Judgment. But in relation to Understanding, it possesses Mercy. (Some write that it is "simple Mercy.") And let it not be said that Judgment only awakens from Understanding and Strength (*Gevurah*). 

Others say the opposite: that Understanding is Mercy, while Wisdom is Judgment. (The Mercy of Understanding consists of variegated colors of Mercy, whereas the Crown is "simple Mercy," and Wisdom is Judgment, and Understanding mediates between them.) Perhaps the reason for this is to clarify these three "Holies": the first head is the Crown against Kindness; the second is Wisdom against Strength; the third is Understanding against Beauty. And if they have the Mind (*Da'at*) that mediates between the upper extremities of Wisdom and Understanding, the words of their groupings are clarified in the *Wisdom of Judah* <note>Likely a reference to a specific commentary or the author's own insights</note> (who came to mediate between these opinions and say that Wisdom contains Judgment within it, since it is the first point that was separated from the "Nothingness" and it contains all change and transformation etc.). For since it is all creation and the strength of the cloud <note>original: "עננ'"</note> is bestowing, and the recipient adds, and every giver is Mercy and every receiver is Judgment. Therefore, all of Wisdom is simple Mercy, and for this reason, there is no Judgment in it as there is in others. And he came to reconcile this matter from the "Sanctifications": some explain that the first "Holy" corresponds to Keter with Gedulah; the second corresponds to Chokhmah with Gevurah; the third corresponds to Binah with Tiferet. Furthermore, the Mazal <note>spiritual influence</note> which is in Wisdom... it must be linked with Gevurah...

The final matter is entirely according to our way of understanding; it is clearly determined that our intention is not that the "restful states" <note>original: "מנוחות" (menuchot), referring to the stable, balanced states of the Sefirot</note> above are like the restful states below. For above, a Mother <note>Understanding/Binah</note> does not uniquely join with a permanent attachment of Judgment and Mercy, as they are simple in the ultimate degree of simplicity and fineness, and they unite in the ultimate union within the essence of the Roots, as was explained in the Gate of Primordials. Likewise, the "voids" of the Crown <note>original: "חלילות הכתר" (chalilot ha-Keter), the internal spaces or circles of the first Sefirah</note> in the mystery of twenty-five <note>Hebrew "כה" (Kah) equals 25</note> within the inclusion of nine—it is also entirely directed toward the mystery of "until I did not know" <note>Aramaic: "עד דלא ידע" (Ad de-lo yada), the highest, unknowable level of the Crown</note>. Its mystery is so refined... likewise Mercy. For according to their descent from before His face, so shall they be revealed, and according to their proximity to Him, so shall they be elevated. 

In any case, the attribute of the Crown shall be absolute Mercy, and the branches extending from within it shall be like the palms of all the forces of Judgment. When a hidden Voice is aroused to subdue the forces of Judgment, it calls out "Cleanser" <note>original: "מנקה" (menakkeh), one of the 13 attributes of mercy</note> to forgive, for in its restoration, the coldness <note>stiffness of judgment</note> is prepared and neutralized, as the Ramak <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> explained regarding the Lulav <note>the palm branch used on Sukkot</note>. One should not doubt how, if the attribute of the Crown is absolute Mercy, the action of Judgment can be drawn from its intellectual side from all sixty? For the Crown is of the count of the Ten Sefirot, and there is no strength in the action of Judgment that could cancel the Crown. If it is not cancelled by the Crown, then the resulting action of Judgment would be performed by the other nine Sefirot alone, which would not be appropriate. It is because from the side of the Crown, He "hides His face" <note>original: "הסתר פניו" (hester paniv)</note> from the Sefirot so that Judgment may act; this is the mystery of their providence and their hiddenness in the act of Judgment. In His Presence, the actions of Judgment are not attributed to these two... 

(For we are forced to say this, because since He spreads through all the Sefirot, He must be in them and He is indeed Mercy, but by hiding His face, He consents to the Judgment.) And one should not doubt that since everything is a hiding of the face, and our grasp is from the attributes, that the action of the attributes is called "false" <note>original: "שקרי" (shikri)</note> because the agents of Judgment act through the hiding of His face. One must say that in the matter of branching out, there are different aspects. For in the time of the "restful states," the face of Mercy is clarified, and when the revelations cease, the Essence of the higher Union is filled and unified in the Sefirah as an essential revelation, until they all unite as one in the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), the ultimate bond in the Cause of all types of rest. There is an opinion that our light of perception... and it departs from these Sefirot, not from the vessel, and every part reveals the light within them through the aspect of the Crown which is drawn from the side of the Strength (*Gevurah*) within it. What is the sufficiency and the flow of its contemplation? Until the forces of Judgment prevail and perform their action without shaking. All this is as it is said: "Why, O Lord, do You stand far off? Why do You hide Yourself in times of trouble?" <note>Psalm 10:1</note> when the light is not revealed as it should be. Then the conclusion of Judgment and its action occur according to its distance, and there will be no remedy for this thing until the lower beings return in proper repentance and call the Light of the Infinite to reveal itself through the Crown in all the Sefirot. Then all the forces of Strength will be distanced by the flow of the Supernal Light and they will be sweetened, as will be explained. 

The masters of Kabbalah mentioned that this Sefirah has 620 pillars of light <note>Taryag (613) + 7 = 620, the numerical value of "Keter" (Crown)</note> in the station of the Crown. (The first tradition in this matter is from Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah in the "Prayer of Choice"). And this is the prayer of Emanation (*Atzilut*); they stand in the order of their attributes, one above the other and one against the other, like a soul within the body, in the way we explained the order of the standing of the Sefirot in their totality. It goes beyond the category of "living creatures," seven upon seven, and seven worlds, and seven... and eight issues from it, and this hovers with it just as every world serves its predecessor. In truth, they have no limit, nor priority of place, nor difference or separation, because they are not individualized, but they delight in the One, and they rise to thirty in light in the completion within the Crown. In this, everything is according to its count, and each Sefirah shall have thirty aspects, for in every single pillar there shall be three inscriptions: one in the return of the recipient, and eight in the essential issuance (which is...

# Chapter 4: General Rule

It is a great principle in Emanation (*Atzilut*) that no existence in the world for a higher purpose <note>original: "לצורך גבוה" (le-tzorech gavoah), for the sake of the Divine</note>, whether small or great, comes into actuality except from a Male and Female <note>the balancing of giving and receiving forces</note>. The Crown alone is the exception that proves the rule, for it was brought into being from the Absolute Will without any need at all. Regarding it, they said: "In that which is hidden from you, do not seek." However, Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) and Understanding (*Binah*) were only emanated through the power of the roots of Male and Female that were imprinted in the Crown. He is the "High One" who needs them—namely, the Wisdom and Understanding within Him. 

Regarding the essence of Wisdom and its governance: some say that in relation to the Crown, it possesses some Judgment, but in relation to Understanding, it is Mercy. **And some say** that the pillars of the Crown are white, the paths of Wisdom are red, and the gates of Understanding are blended in the order of the "Extremities" <note>the six lower Sefirot</note>. "Understanding" (*Binah*) is from the language of "the man between" <note>original: "איש הבינים" (ish ha-beinim), a mediator</note>. Some who lean toward this view said that Wisdom is on the right, above Kindness (*Chesed*), to flow Judgment upon it so that the "Husk" (*Kelipah*) outside its rest shall not be cancelled, and Understanding is on the left, above Fear/Dread (*Pachad/Gevurah*), to blend the intensity of its judgment with her mercy. The tradition of their reasoning is that since Wisdom is the first emanated effect, it is therefore the beginning of opposites, and deficiency is "attached to its heel." 

Others say that Wisdom is Mercy from the side of the "Face" which turns toward the Crown, but from the side of the "Back" <note>the rear/outer aspects</note>, which are its face looking toward Understanding, Judgment sparks forth. To this, a difficulty is raised: for the relationship of the "Back" of Wisdom in its aspect to Understanding has not been clarified, nor what the "Back" of Understanding is in its aspect to Kindness and Strength, or to Endurance (*Netzach*), or even to Michael—to the Michael of Kindness in the separated realms. For indeed, the mystery of Face and Back in general is appropriate for the matter of fineness and spirituality, not for the aspect of Kindness and Judgment. It is a vain lie to seek the source of Judgment there, for its existence is not absent even in the "High Hiding Place" as we mentioned. And He who said to the "Void" <note>original: "בלימה" (belimah)</note> that it should tell, and to the "Absolute Nothingness" (*Ayin*) that it should reveal—the Name from the hidden power into existence—spoke to Mercy, and the Judgment hidden with them descended and they revealed it below in the "Fear of Isaac" <note>a title for the Sefirah of Gevurah/Judgment</note>. 

**And the truth** is that the first three <note>Keter, Chokhmah, Binah</note> and Kindness and Strength—all three of them are Mercy. The sign for this is "A-H" <note>The letters Aleph and Heh, the start of the Name of God</note>, the "First Kindnesses." Wisdom is called a "White Tallit" <note>prayer shawl</note> from the whiteness of the brain. The order of the Extremities is directed toward Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge (*Da'at*), and the Supernal Crown is the root that includes them all. However, the mercy of Wisdom is not absolutely simple like the Supernal Crown, and its precedence over the mercy of Understanding is explained and agreed upon. In the *Tikkunim* <note>Tikkuney Zohar</note>, they mentioned the relationship that the Crown has with Kindness, Wisdom with Strength, and Understanding with Beauty (*Tiferet*). The intention there is that Wisdom "loads fire into the law" <note>original: "טמיל אשא לחוק"</note> so that the forms will not be cancelled in the intensity of the Mercy; this was through Wisdom in order to weaken the Judgment. And in the *Tikkunim* we say: "Evil Satan" is the "Tearing of the Sea" <note>Wordplay on Aramaic/Hebrew letters</note>, and through it, he tore the sea and separated the Satan from there, who is the "impure waters." Because of this, "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters"—this is the Name that uproots Satan from the sea...

# Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 8: Essence and Governance — Juice of Pomegranates

It is known but not revealed at all. He "stirred up one from the east" <note>original: "העיר ממזרח" (Isaiah 41:2), a reference to Abraham or a divine awakening</note> to reveal His glory, to make known that place called "East," for from there is the beginning of every mystery of faith and the light to be revealed. Afterwards, "Righteousness called him to his foot," for Righteousness <note>original: "צדק" (Tzedek), often associated with the Sefirah of Kingship/Malkhut or Judgment</note> reveals the supernal Might and the dominion of the Holy One, Blessed be He. This Righteousness has dominion over all worlds, to lead them and to establish them as is fitting. And concerning this, "He gave up nations before him and made him rule over kings," for all the nations of the world exist under the authority of this Righteousness, as it is said: "And He shall judge the world with righteousness" <note>Psalm 9:8</note>. Furthermore: "Righteousness called him to his foot"—who calls to whom? Rather, Righteousness calls constantly to the "Luminous Mirror" <note>original: "אספקלריא דנהרא" (aspaklaria de-nahara), a term for the Sefirah of Beauty/Tiferet</note> and is never silent. Righteousness stands constantly at His foot, never departing from there, calling and never quieting, for this is what is written: "I shall be what I shall be," and "O God, do not be silent, do not be still" <note>Psalm 83:2</note>. This concludes the quote. This is also discussed in the Gate of Principles regarding the phrase "Who created these?"

## Chapter 7: It is stated in the Torah portion of Noah: "And the Lord smelled the soothing aroma"

-> And it is written: "A fire-offering, a soothing aroma to the Lord" <-

Smoke and fire are bound together as one, for there is no smoke without fire, as it is written: "Now Mount Sinai was all in smoke, because the Lord had descended upon it in fire" <note>Exodus 19:18</note>. Come and see: fire emerges from within; it is subtle and grasps onto another thing on the outside which is not as subtle. When they appear one within the other, then smoke ascends. Why? Because the fire has taken hold of a tangible thing. The symbol for this is the nose, from which smoke emerges out of fire. Concerning this it is written: "They shall put incense before Your nostrils" <note>original: "באפך" (be-apekha), literally 'in Your nose'</note>, because the fire is returned to its place and the nose gathers that aroma inward and further inward until everything is bound together and returns to its place. All is brought near into the Inner Thought <note>The highest level of the Sefirah of Understanding</note> and becomes a single Will. Then it is a "soothing aroma" <note>original: "ריח ניחוח" (reiach nichoach)</note>, for the anger is calmed <note>The Hebrew word for "soothing" (nichoach) shares a root with "calm" or "rest" (nuach)</note> and it is bound and becomes a state of rest. For the smoke is gathered, enters, and is folded into the fire, and the fire is bound to the smoke, and both enter further and further inward until the anger is calmed. When all is bound to each other and the anger rests, then there is a state of peace and a single bond, called the "rest of all rests," the joy of all as one, the light of the lamps, the light of the Countenance. Therefore: "And the Lord smelled the soothing aroma"—like one who smells and gathers everything back into its place.

## The intention is that the fire is awakened from Understanding (Binah) into the state of a flame

...which takes hold of a tangible thing. The smoke represents the external forces, the messengers of Judgment <note>original: "דין" (Din)</note> who stir up weeping and bring down tears from the eyes that burn with Judgment. The fire and smoke are joined, for the fire has no action except through the smoke; when they are separated from it, they are nullified, as it says: "As smoke is driven away, so drive them away" <note>Psalm 68:3</note>. At Mount Sinai, the Torah was given through Might <note>Gevurah</note>; therefore, the forces of Judgment were awakened. Come and see: fire emerges from within, from the midst of Understanding, to dwell in the Might that is within it. It is subtle and does not reveal itself until it grasps another thing—this is Might in its place, in the mystery of the "Nose of the Height" <note>A symbolic term for the passage of divine breath</note>. Here, this refers to the Beauty (Tiferet) within Understanding from its other side and its back, from which the warm breath comes, and in which "they shall put incense before Your nostrils." Therefore, the "Son of the Nose" <note>The breath or aroma</note> returns and is hidden deep within Understanding, and even further inward to the sense within the brain—in the reality of Wisdom (Chokhmah) which shines within Understanding to sweeten the Judgment. This occurs even on the side of Might, through the light of the Ancient One <note>original: "עתיקא" (Atika), the highest, most merciful level of the Divine</note>. This explains why it is written "soothing aroma" <note>nichoach</note> in a double sense: one rest for the revelation of the Ancient One, and one for the sweetening of the Altar.

<column-break/>

The reason is found in the *Tikunim* <note>The Tikunei HaZohar</note>: the revelation of the clashing of Judgment with Mercy is not constant; it passes and changes at long intervals. The sign of the nullification of Judgment by Mercy is not always present, for "He does not stir up all His wrath" <note>Psalm 78:38</note>, emitting much smoke and full of retribution. Therefore, in the Name of Mercy—the four-letter Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, YHVH</note>—the "shoulders" are far apart, and Judgment is revealed in it only at a distance. But in the seeing of the times, then our smoke <note>unclear reading in OCR</note> is constant. This is as the point of *Halamim* <note>A term for a specific vowel configuration of the Divine Name used in meditative kabbalah</note>. This is in the Name of Judgment that causes Mercy to flow, intermingling with it. This is explained in the Zohar, portion of *Emor*.

## Chapter 9: The 50th Sefirah is Strength (Gevurah), Understanding (Binah), and Crown (Keter)
It was explained above that the letters Y-H <note>Yah</note> represent Mercy and Y-H also represent Judgment. It is more correct to say that it is a powerful Mercy from all sides; that is, both from the perspective of its own essence and from what it receives from the Crown. From the Crown, it is a powerful mercy from the sources of Mercy, and from the perspective of what it influences. For the "Ends" <note>the lower seven Sefirot</note> draw from it. This is like "juice" <note>original: "עסיס" (asis), playing on the title of the section</note> compared to Mercy. All their hidden sources are within it, in Understanding (Understanding receives from them) and it bestows upon their branches the flow of Kindness and Mercy. All of them shall be directed toward the Judgments which are the yoke of Mercy. (Therefore, in the book *Reshith Chokhmah*, it is Mercy since it receives from the hidden points within it... [the text here describes complex interrelations of the vowel points and the Sefirot]). But nonetheless, it is Mercy from the side where Judgments are awakened from it. Therefore, it is called by the four-letter Name with the *Halamim* vowels. Since its core is Mercy, it comes in the hint of letters that indicate Mercy, but because Judgments are awakened from it, it comes with the hint of vowel points that indicate Judgment. To understand what we said about Judgments awakening from it, one must know how the essence of Understanding reveals Might (Gevurah), which is the "50th Gate" in the order explained in the Gate of the Order of Evolution. Know that even though Might is not clothed in the 50th Gate, everything descends... [text describes the relationship between the "Red" (Judgment) and "White" (Mercy)]. The Might that is elevated in Understanding will be included in the Mercy along with Kindness, the majority of the "Ends" being hidden within it... Nonetheless, because it "lies down" from Understanding, all its nourishment and influence come from it. It has no reality, power, or strength to cause harm, since it comes from her. Because the forces of Judgment are gathered in Might and are nourished and strengthened by their drawing from her name—that is, Understanding—Understanding is called by the four-letter Name with the *Halamim* vowels. Judgment is not constant, even though they themselves are then masters of Judgment; regardless, they are from her... as will be explained in Chapter 13. She is the "Prophetess" who bestows Kindness, though they adorn themselves as Judgment. They are the flame that raises the smoke... Know that when the sins of those below increase and the "sparks" are awakened, demanding Judgment from the Attribute of Judgment, the flow of blessing and Mercy departs and the connection from the side of supernal Kindness and Understanding is severed. Then... the flow in Understanding goes only to Might through the "pipeline" that nourishes it alone. At that time, she is awakened in Judgment and bestows upon him—meaning, through the power of that flow, Might is strengthened and clothes itself in its attribute, which is Judgment, and bestows from its essence to all the forces of Judgment so they can carry out the Judgment...

What was proven by the name "God" being for Judgment was a hint toward Mercy. (And it would be proper for them to understand that the name "God" is Judgment without the joining of Mercy, and likewise it would be proper for the four-letter Name to always indicate Mercy without the mixture of Judgment... even though the name "God" has a slight change toward Mercy, just as there is a revelation of Judgment in the four-letter Name). For behold, in the Name, there is no Mercy without Judgment, just as there is no Judgment without Mercy... "And you shall know today that the Lord is God" <note>Deuteronomy 4:39</note>, meaning that within the attribute of Mercy, Judgment is included. Therefore, do not wonder at retribution, and therefore it is not proper that the name "God" should be called alone, but rather together, in a way that Mercy is hinted at in it as well. # Juice of Pomegranates, Gate 8: Essence and Governance — Slice of the Pomegranate

And the truth is that sadness, which is the awakening of Judgment <term>Din: the divine attribute of justice and restriction</term>, has its primary root in Understanding <note>original: "Binah," the third Sefirah</note>, as was explained in the *Zohar* <note>The primary text of Jewish mysticism</note> on the Torah portion *Noach*, regarding the verse: "I will not again curse the ground anymore for man’s sake." In order that we should not mistakenly interpret the phrase "In secret places" as referring to the three upper Sefirot <note>Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah—the highest realms of the divine</note>, or at least to two of them, the author of the passage narrowed the scope of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> and said it refers only to one place. Its greatness indicates the inclusion of the three upper Sefirot. The Holy One, Blessed be He—who is Beauty <note>original: "Tiferet," the central Sefirah</note> and the possessor of the Name—comes with the vowel-point of Judgment by the power of Understanding <note>Binah</note>. **And the pride** of Israel is their sustenance from the Heart. "She was a keeper of the vineyards" <note>quoting Song of Songs 1:6</note> refers to the secret of "He who dwells with them in the midst of their impurity." This means the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> clothes herself within the ruling heavenly Minister of a nation in order to watch over us so that he does not bring us to total destruction. The Divine Presence did not descend only to Babylon or Elam or the other kingdoms for the community as a whole; rather, even if a single individual was exiled to Africa or to the islands of the sea, she sends one of her "glories" and "branches" to watch over him. This is like what we have learned: "If a student is exiled, his teacher is exiled with him." And it is written: "And seek the peace of the city where I have caused you to be carried away captive... for in its peace you shall have peace." "My own vineyard I have not kept" <note>Song of Songs 1:6</note> except through the elevation of their awe in purity—a nickname for the Divine Presence who clothes herself within the seventy Ministers <note>The guardian angels of the seventy nations</note> and influences them so that Israel may be nourished from the "leftovers." In this way, "her enemies became the head," according to what the sages taught. Its meaning is: one who becomes a "neighboring boundary" to Israel, who were originally enjoying an inheritance without boundaries. This is what David was pained by when he said: "They have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the Lord." And as our Sages of blessed memory said: "Since the Temple was destroyed, the taste of intimacy was taken away" <note>Referring to the secret of the Union of the inner Sefirot</note> and given to the transgressors outside the Curtain <term>Pargod: the celestial veil separating the divine realm from the lower worlds</term>.

**And the pride** of the Kingdom of Heaven is her aspect above with her husband <note>Tiferet</note>, for even there she finds no rest, but rather "He cast down from heaven to earth." Even though these verses require reconciliation without the specific saying of Rav Pappa, they do not contradict one another. We can generally explain "Strength and beauty are in His place" as referring to the usual state, while "My soul shall weep in secret" refers to times of exile. Now that Rav Pappa has said that absolute mourning is difficult, the verse about "secret places" presents a problem. One should not think to distinguish between "before" or "from before," as explained in the *Sfat Emet*. He thought to explain "before" as also referring to Understanding <note>Binah</note> which precedes the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>Tiferet</note>. The resolution is: "There is no sadness in the inner houses," and this is "before the Place." For regarding Bathsheba it is written, "And she stood before the king," and "secret places" refers to the innermost houses. **And he asked**: Is there no sadness in the outer houses? According to my view, it works well, for I say there is no sadness in the inner houses, but "He called for weeping and mourning" in the outer houses. Even the "secret places" would not be difficult for me, as it is possible to explain it as the "hiding of the Face" <term>Hester Panim: divine concealment</term> when the Divine Presence, which is the soul-level, clothes herself in the "Bird’s Nest" <note>A mystical realm where the Messiah or souls reside</note>. But according to your view, it is difficult, for "calling" implies making a voice heard outside. And who are those calling for weeping and mourning? It is Beauty <note>Tiferet, the name Y-H-V-H</note> and the Sefirot of Endurance, Majesty, and Foundation <note>Netzach, Hod, Yesod</note> which are the "Hosts" in "that day," which is the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note>. The resolution is that the destruction of the Holy Temple is different, for the pain was so great in the outer houses as if they were the source of the weeping. Even the forces of Mercy and Peace, and even their lower angels, "weep bitterly." This is compared to a King who was angry with his son; he said, "Until I expand his palace, I will not be reconciled with him, but rather I will vent my wrath on the wood and the stones." When his servants heard this, they said, "This is a relief; it is better that the palace be burned in a moment..."

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of how the Sefirot (divine emanations) respond to human conduct, specifically addressing the mechanics of how Judgment (Din) is either tempered by Mercy or allowed to manifest through the higher realms of Understanding (Binah) and Wisdom (Chokhmah).</meta>

# Juice of Pomegranates &emsp; Gate 8: Essence and Governance &emsp; Slice of the Pomegranate

When sins prevail, the light of Wisdom <note>original: "Chokhmah," the second Sefirah associated with pure intuition</note> withdraws and ascends upward, and the sources of Mercy become blocked. In this state, Understanding <note>original: "Binah," the third Sefirah associated with logic and processing</note> awakens Judgment <note>original: "Gevurah," the Sefirah of strength and restriction</note> alone. As it is written regarding the three vowel-points of the *Cholam* <note>a Hebrew vowel mark placed above a letter</note>, she [Understanding] provides for her [Judgment] from the side of Strength, which is established for them as darkness, wherein there is no peace, and the powers of Judgment are decreed to execute judgment. 

However, when the light of Wisdom is revealed, the sources of Mercy are opened, and Understanding influences all the extremities with power. Then, every flow of influence becomes Mercy. Because all the sources are then Mercy, the attribute of Judgment in the presence of the other sources becomes like **a candle at noon** <note>an Aramaic idiom meaning a small light is rendered invisible or insignificant by the great light of the sun</note>, unable to dominate or punish. Even Judgment itself becomes clothed in Mercy because it follows the majority of Mercy. This occurs when Understanding receives an abundance of Merciful influence from the Crown <note>original: "Keter," the highest Sefirah</note> through the channel established for her from the Crown. For when that influence is drawn from the Crown to Wisdom, all the channels are opened with Mercy. 

Conversely, Judgment will suckle from Mercy, and the "eyes" of Judgment will not distance themselves within the miracle, and the ascending forces will be satisfied by Mercy. In this way, our Sages of blessed memory explained that "the righteous transform the Attribute of Judgment into the Attribute of Mercy, while the wicked transform the Attribute of Mercy into the Attribute of Judgment" <note>A common Rabbinic teaching regarding how human behavior shifts the divine response</note>. (For by causing the sources to be blocked, Understanding is opened to enter the source of Judgment, and this influences judgment; the opposite is true for the righteous.)

**And according** to what has been explained regarding the intention of the "Face of Seventy" <note>likely referring to the seventy facets of the Torah or a specific divine configuration</note> concerning the "Visitation" <note>original: "Pekudah"</note> and its action in combination, you can conclude that the upper realms in Understanding act according to the influence bestowed upon them from above; she has no power to add, change, or diminish. This is compared to the eyes that awaken in a person: if there were no Divine Providence, they would not burn or emit smoke or shed tears, which prove her case. This relates to the first chapter [of Tractate Hagigah] on the verse: "In secret places my soul shall weep" <note>Jeremiah 13:17</note>. (And there is a chamber, a place that the Holy One, Blessed be He, has, where He weeps, and its name is "Secret Places" etc.) 

This follows the version of Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the preeminent medieval commentator</note> in the book: "In the inner chambers [it exists], but in the outer chambers it does not." However, Rabbi Todros HaLevi in the book *Explorer of Glory* <note>original: "Choker Kavod"</note> and Rabbi Yosef N. Kalatiny (?) in the books of the *N.L.K.* <note>possibly an acronym for a specific kabbalistic school</note> felt that "I have come to my rest" applies to our eyes. According to this, it is as if sadness and Judgment depend only on those "beauties" <note>referring to specific divine manifestations</note>, for then Understanding looks as if in a mirror. She acts according to the influx that enters her from the nearby higher source. For when Understanding does not receive the influx of Judgment from above, the powers of Judgment within Understanding do not have the opening to "smoke" except by the power of man. 

All of this is proven in the *Zohar* (Torah portion *Noach*) on the verse: "Now... we have been lacking everything," and the verse "I will not again curse the ground anymore..." which mentions a "sigh," but rather they [the attributes] prevail as one. The intention here is that Judgment is the opposite of Mercy, for the way of Mercy and influence is to protect and increase, as explained in the "Gate of Attributes." This is not the case with Judgment; if it is not influenced from above, it will not act or increase from below. This is what they meant by "In the outer chambers it does not [exist]," meaning there is no Judgment there unless they are empowered to add and increase (except according to the preparation from above). With this, we can understand the Sages' words: "The measure of Reward is greater than the measure of Punishment," for Reward continues to increase, whereas Punishment diminishes. These are the descents and falls into Mercy for the sake of the world's existence. Nevertheless, in truth, there is no Judgment above in Understanding, because Thought does not enact anything unless it is strengthened by the powers of Strength <note>Gevurah</note> and its mixtures.

<column-break/>

In the *Tikunim* <note>original: "Tikunei Zohar," a commentary on the first chapters of Genesis</note> they said: If a person does not raise up fragrances, incense, and the smoke of sacrifices and prayers in "awe and love," it is written: "Then the anger of the Lord shall smoke." And it says in the *Sefer HaBahir* <note>The "Book of Brilliance," an early kabbalistic text</note>: There is no "smell" except in the "nose" <note>original: "Af," which also means "anger" in Hebrew</note>, and there is no breath—which is the smell—except in the nose. And there is no "sweet savor" <note>original: "Nichuach"</note> except a "descent," as it is written: "And He descended," which the Targum <note>Aramaic translation</note> renders as "And He rested." The spirit descends and rests in those holy forms and is unified through the sacrifice. Therefore, the explanation of "Smell" <note>Reyach</note> is the letter *Yod* of the Name; "Breath" <note>Neshamah</note> is the letter *Heh*; and the "Nose" <note>Chotam</note> that is designated for this is the letter *Vav*. From the three of them, "Rest" <note>Manoach</note> is drawn to the final *Heh* <note>This explains the four-letter Name of God, Y-H-V-H, through the metaphor of scent</note>. Everything is through the spirit of the Single Master who is revealed upon them and brings them close. 

**And in the book *The Faithful Shepherd*** <note>original: "Ra'aya Meheimna," a later layer of the Zohar</note>, Rabbi Yehuda said: In the sacrifice, there is smoke, there is smell, and there is a sweet savor. Smoke comes from the side of Judgment; this is what is written: "For then the anger of the Lord shall smoke," and "Smoke rose in His nostrils, and fire from His mouth devoured." A sweet savor is Mercy, and "the smell of your nose is like apples." Rabbi Isaac said: Both are present; smoke and smell are both in the nose. The verses bear witness: one says "Smoke rose in His nostrils" and the second "and the smell of your nose is like apples." Why is one called "Smoke" (Judgment) and the second "Mercy"? Why Judgment and Mercy together? It is because in the nose there are two nostrils. Regarding "Smoke rose in His nostrils," what does "rose" mean? It rises from the heart, which is on the left, corresponding to Strength <note>Gevurah</note>. From the right, the spirit descends toward it to cool His anger and soothe it from the side of Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, for there is the Brain—Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> is on the right. "He who desires to become wise should turn south; he who desires to become wealthy should turn north" <note>A Talmudic mnemonic for the placement of the Temple vessels</note>. Understanding <note>Binah</note> alone is toward the left. 

Therefore, "Smoke rose in His nostrils" from Understanding toward Wisdom, which is on the right, and it receives it with joy through the song of the Levites. This smoke only rises through the fire that is lit in the "wood," which are the limbs filled with commandments. The "wood of the burnt offering" refers to the masters of Torah; the Torah kindles fire in them with the intensity of Strength, and smoke rises through them into Understanding—the smoke of the altar-arrangement. Since it ascends to the nose, it is called "Incense" <note>original: "Ketoret"</note>. This is what is written: "They shall put incense in Your nostrils." Nothing cancels death in the world like the Incense, for it is the "binding" <note>original: "Ketira," an Aramaic word for knot or bond</note> of Judgment with Mercy along with the sweet savor of the nose. The Aramaic translation of "binding" is *Ketiro*. Rabbi Yehuda said: Fortunate is the portion of the spirit! These are hidden matters revealed. Furthermore, the "Holy Lamp" <note>a title for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> said: After the prayer, which is like the sacrifice, whoever says the "Formulation of the Incense" after the "Tehillah Le-David" <note>Psalm 145</note> cancels death from his house. Thus far.

### Chapter 8: We read in the first chapter of Tractate Hagigah: "In secret places my soul shall weep..." 
-> Rabbi Shmuel bar Unya said in the name <-
of Rav: The Holy One has a place, and its name is "Secret Places" <note>Mistarim</note>. What does "because of pride" <note>Jeremiah 13:17</note> mean? Because of the pride of Israel that was taken from them. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: Because of the pride of the Kingdom of Heaven. But did not Rav Papa say: There is no sadness before the Omnipresent, as it is said, "Strength and gladness are in His place" <note>1 Chronicles 16:27</note>? This is not a difficulty: one refers to the **Inner Chambers** <note>Batei Guai</note>, and the other refers to the **Outer Chambers** <note>Batei Barai</note>. But is there no weeping in the outer chambers? Is it not written: "On that day did the Lord God of Hosts call to weeping and to lamentation"? The destruction of the Holy Temple is different, for even the angels of peace wept, as it is said: "Behold, the valiant ones [Arelim] cry without." Thus far. 

**This** is the correct version according to Rashi, may his memory be a blessing, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai stands with him, and not as Rabbi Todros HaLevi thought to correct it. Many followed him [Todros] in reading it this way: "Is there no weeping in the inner chambers? But it is written..." etc., meaning the angels of peace who are influenced from the inner chambers, for the *Arelim* <note>a high order of angels</note> suckle from the outer chambers. And the truth...

### Chapter 10: Rabbi Nehunia ben ha-Kanah said in his prayer that the first
->three are considered as one in the Mystery of Knowledge<-

The Knower, the Known, and the Knowledge <note>This triad, famously discussed by Maimonides and adopted by Kabbalists, expresses that in God, the subject, object, and act of thinking are a single unity</note>: we must understand and contemplate how they differ in their ascent toward the absolute Unity required of all emanated beings. Furthermore, one must wonder at what is said in many places in the *Tikunim* <note>The *Tikunei Zohar*, a classic Kabbalistic text</note> regarding the verse, "You shall surely send away the mother" <note>Deuteronomy 22:7</note>, which refers to two "sendings" or "divorces": the Mother is the Higher Divine Presence <note>Binah/Understanding</note>, and "the children" <note>represented by the word *Et* in Hebrew</note> refers to the Lower Divine Presence <note>Malchut/Sovereignty</note>. If so, what is the significance and unique status of Understanding?
->First, let us establish that the Unity of the Sefirot occurs in one of three ways:<-

**The First Unity** is the unity of the Sefirot in their very emanation. This unity is never withheld, for it is necessary for the continued existence of reality. The intention of the *Shema* prayer is to unite them all, one to another, and all of them within the Emanator <note>the Infinite Source, Or Ein Sof</note>, who is their King over all existing things and who gives life to them all. In this state, their existences remain below. However, this is not like the "Mystery of the Jubilee" <note>the 50th year, associated with Binah</note>, where one's spirit and soul are gathered back to Him. Our ultimate longing in this is to add perfection to them so that the damage caused by the Serpent may be repaired, and nothing else.

**The Second Unity** occurs when an additional flow of influence is renewed within them for a specific hour of need. For example, the service of the Name "Yah" <note>Yod and He, representing Wisdom and Understanding</note> is meant to draw down "Whiteness" <note>pure Mercy</note> from the Crown through Repentance. This is done by linking Thought <note>Wisdom</note> with it to influence Sovereignty <note>Malchut</note> to "whiten" sins. The unity of Understanding and Sovereignty occurs through the "Six Extremities" <note>the six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note> in the mystery of the Divine Names. One who wishes to become wise should draw influence from Wisdom through the "South" <note>the right side</note> to Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, where the Torah is found, and to Sovereignty, which is the "Lower Wisdom." One who wishes to become wealthy should draw from Understanding through the "North" <note>the left side</note> to Sovereignty. One who wishes to prevail should draw from Understanding through Strength and Majesty to Sovereignty—the "Sword that avenges the covenant"—and find aid from Victory to overcome enemies. All these aspects and their likes change according to the event within the Sefirot of the "Building" <note>the lower seven Sefirot</note>. But the first three are such that when one is revealed, its companions are brought with it. This is the mystery of the words *Asher*, *Rosh*, and *She'ar* <note>original: "אש"ר רא"ש שא"ר," permutations of the same letters meaning 'That/Which,' 'Head,' and 'Remnant/Kin'</note>. These three—Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding—are considered as one. As it says in the *Tikunim*: from the feminine side, the Supreme Crown is called *Asher*, and from the masculine side, it is called *Rosh* (the Head of all Heads). This also applies to Wisdom in its place, and Understanding...

<column-break/>

**The Third Unity** concerns Wisdom, Understanding, Beauty, and Sovereignty, which unite in pairs. No new emanation ever occurs <unclear>not</unclear> except through them. When this unity is lacking between Beauty and Sovereignty, it is also lacking between Wisdom and Understanding in their places, and the repair is directed toward all of them as one. As explained in the *Tikunim*, the "Small Letter He" <note>the last letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing Malchut</note> says, "I am asleep," in the mystery of "I was dumb with silence, I held my peace, even from good" <note>Psalm 39:3</note>. This is the withdrawal of the letter *Vav* <note>representing Tiferet</note> until the *Vav* is awakened toward her when our Messiah is revealed. Then, "the voice of my beloved knocks" <note>Song of Songs 5:2</note>, a knocking that ascends and descends. The letters of the Name that were in the mystery of *Yod-Dalet* <note>the numerical value 14</note> and the mystery of "so they two went" <note>Ruth 1:19</note>—meaning each of the two *He*s is far from its partner—then join as *Yod-He-He*. This is when the Lower *He* ascends to the *Yod* in the mystery of "The Lord by Wisdom founded the earth" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note> and "his father kept the matter" <note>Genesis 37:11</note>. Naturally, the Mother <note>Binah</note> accompanies her to awaken the Father's mercy. Then the Upper *He* descends to the *Vav* (the son of *Yah*), which is "By Understanding He established the heavens." This is the mystery of the Burnt Offering.

The day <note>original: "י"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א," spelling out the Name</note> in the mystery of "the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun."
->Move it to its place:<-

### Chapter 11: After the general nature of the Attributes and the way
->their traits, actions, and agreement are revealed in every<-

action as one, like the Crown through the connection and unity of the Sefirot—how is this? Know that the foundation of every Sefirah being composed of ten is an essential inclusion. Just as Kindness (Chesed) was explained, each one unites with every other one in equal aspects that sustain one another. For example, the Crown is connected with Wisdom as the totality of the Crown itself and as the essence of Wisdom. This is the way of the totality of Wisdom... and so it is connected with all other Sefirot and Kindness... and from these paths, the Sefirot can unite one with another... For example, the Kindness within the Crown unites with the Strength through the totality of the Crown in its essence and in the essence of Strength... and in the way the Sefirot are connected to one another, so too is the connection of the parts of the Sefirot... for there is no part in the whole that is not composed of ten... and this is the unity of the small and the great... and according to what I have written, the connections and inclusions of the Sefirot reach into the thousands and myriads... as explained in the Gate of Inclusions.

### Chapter 12: Know that the foundation of the Sefirot has three aspects
->The Sefirot being united (from what I mentioned<-
->in the previous chapter) from the start of their emanation in return and essential flow, and this is permanent<-

forever. For if the flow of all the equal inclusions to their source were withheld, the worlds would be destroyed and nullified. This unity is the end of power and will not be lacking or interrupted in any of the Sefirot, for it exists forever. This was His intention, blessed be He, for the foundation of all Sefirot, one in another and all in the beginning, and for His sovereignty over all existing things, great and small... and this is its importance and perfection. It is not to add or renew flow upon the "back" of the foundation... though in the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the traditional author of the Zohar</note> it is sometimes found that the foundation adds flow, the intention is an addition without the created beings being "complete in their name," as at the beginning of the fall of Adam the First, who "shortened the planting" <note>a metaphor for causing a separation in the divine realms</note>, and the flow of the land was called into question, the lights were diminished, and the beauty of things was lessened.

**The Second Unity** is the sanctification of the Sefirot to influence an additional flow of blessings to created beings, each one according to his righteousness, his situation, and his path, and according to the place and time. Sometimes there is a need for forgiveness, pardon, and atonement, and this draws the flow from the "Supreme Whiteness" of the Crown, which whitens the sins of Israel through Understanding, for she is the essence of Repentance... and Wisdom also influences this flow to Sovereignty, and Understanding and Sovereignty unite through Thought... and this is the Name *Yah* and a lesson for all the congregation of the Children of Israel.

# Asis Rimmonim / Gate 8: Essence and Conduct / Pomegranate Slice
### Page 119

The one who asks about the **Mystery of Judgment** and its proximity: for him, Wisdom was derived from the Book and he prides himself before the sages. However, for those whose inner intention grants them **Understanding**, they are more praiseworthy than the sages who merely pass over toward **Mercy**. (And from the mouth of the House of Judgment, merit is given to Wisdom and Mercy, through three stages until the rule of Mercy, which is the "Smallness" <note>Hebrew: *Katnut*, referring to a diminished spiritual state</note>, etc., like Saneivor <note>A technical name for a specific angelic or celestial configuration</note>). Many other doubts may arise in this matter.

And if he prepares his grave for the dead, for the "Face of Smallness" <note>Zeir Anpin, the "Short Face" or emotive attributes of God</note> in relation to Understanding is considered "Backwards" in relation to the **Crown**. This is specifically regarding the matter of **subtlety** and **spirituality**, but not regarding Judgment and Mercy. For the dependence of Judgment is not on subtlety nor on expansion like Mercy; rather, Judgment is included as a byproduct of Mercy. It is explained in the mystery of those who are led: there is no doubt that it is more Mercy than Strength <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note>. 

*This is analogous to a small branch compared to a massive and giant tree; the small branch is subtle in its extreme thinness... it is connected to the source... and is the secret that includes both... as explained in a different answer (and it is)... light from nothingness... and I found in the name of... that the reason is not in the Will, nor the limitation of His power, but He can do everything in the way that is for the benefit of the world. (And so is the matter with Judgment, for it returns and exists, but nevertheless, for us to be perfect in our qualities, we must align things to their proper nature). The matter is known: that the Crown is the absolute subtlety. Nevertheless, the root of Mercy and the root of Judgment are both in the Crown in the mystery of the "Three Points" included within it. For in the Crown, these three exist: Mercy, Judgment, and Compassion. But they do not exist as literal Mercy and Judgment; rather, they exist in a state of great subtlety, like the subtle potential of fire, spirit, water, and dust included in the elements. Mercy, Judgment, and Beauty (Tiferet) and Sovereignty (Malchut) would not exist as literal fire, water, wind, and dust, but from the purity of these elements—the subtle states between them. These are the "Three Points" mentioned above, which are contained, hidden, and unified in the mystery of the "Name"... (including all the hidden and subtle individualities to the ultimate degree of subtlety), as will be explained in the Gate of Emanations.*

(Nevertheless, after their emanation, they are revealed as "Grace" and "Eyes" in relation to the system of the attributes of action, which are Mercy, Judgment, and Compassion, which are affected in every place from their source. They are not called by the names Mercy, Judgment, or Compassion except in the way described in the "Roots" <note>referring to Cordovero's *Shorashim*</note>). For just as there are particular subtle details in the Infinite (Ein Sof), so too is the matter of the subtlety of the attributes and actions in every place. For the attributes (the actions) are drawn from the six particulars included in the Crown. The six included in the Crown are the cause for the lower attributes, and the Infinite (Ein Sof) is the cause for the six included in the Crown. Just as there are specific details in the Infinite, so too is there a change in the attributes and actions in the Crown. 

And just as the Sefirot were in their essence at their source, unified in the ultimate unity, and they had no separate qualities at all until they were emanated from the Crown—and when the upper particulars were revealed (which are the Wisdom and Understanding), a revelation of "Existence" appeared relative to the "Nothingness" and the hiddenness of the sources that were previously concealed in the First Order. Thus, even though the first three Sefirot were emanated, the attributes and actions were still hidden in great subtlety, until there was no sense of Mercy or literal action at all, until they were emanated and revealed in their own manifestation below, each in its source and the level appropriate to it. As we have crowned in its place... and this name—this question will not fall upon it: "From where does Judgment come?" For the root of everything is Mercy, but from the abundance of its subtlety, no Mercy is visible there, and it is like nothing...

<column-break/>

"...in a moment. You also bring wood, and I will bring coals; immediately the King will return and relent concerning his son." <note>This parable describes how human actions "below" can arouse divine compassion "above" to mitigate a harsh decree</note>

**Chapter 9: Alternatively**
It was heard well by the questioner: the meaning of "Before the Place" is before the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence, often called "The Place" in Rabbinic literature</note>. And the proverb "The native is on the earth and the stranger is in the highest heavens" <note>A phrase suggesting an inversion of the natural order</note>—consider it as you will: that "secrets" do not apply Above. That is certainly not true, for it necessarily means the "inner chambers" are for the Lord our God, and the negation applies to the "outer chambers," as we have said. He did not have enough time to cancel the decree of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and say "it is elevated" regarding the final sentence, until the questioner understood his intent and asked: "According to you, there is a difficulty with the verse 'And He called on that day' <note>Isaiah 22:12</note>, which certainly deals with a final sentence of judgment!" 

He replied: The destruction of the **Holy Temple** is different. For even the angels were terrified by the decree to hasten the atonement, as we explained. And do not say these were "Forces of Judgment," but rather "Angels of Mercy and Peace who weep bitterly" <note>Isaiah 33:7</note>. It is possible to explain "Angels of Peace" as the power of "Return," who in a time of favor are the angels who return to the Righteous One, who is called "Peace." And then they "weep bitterly." The verse's mention of "Hosts" (Tzevaot) is precise. Ultimately, the name of God (Tetragrammaton) punctuated with the vowels of *Elohim* <note>Judgment</note> is the source of the "Sorrow" for the Lord (Adonai) that was awakened toward Him and toward the "Hosts" who eulogized on that day. 

**Furthermore**, the mystery of the "Angels of Peace" together with the eulogy can be understood from the wonders of the **Cherubim** <note>The golden figures atop the Ark of the Covenant</note>. As the sages taught in Tractate Yoma regarding the verse "because they saw their nakedness": it was a new thing, a manifestation of the Absolute Will, that the Cherubim should be "intertwined" <note>embracing</note> at the time of the Destruction. This was the mystery of the "Angels of Peace"—so as not to terrify Israel. At that very moment, we read "They weep bitterly" in the House of the Sanctuary. "And He called" is a language of "Influence" <note>Shefa</note>, even for crying and eulogy. For even when it is desolate, it stands in its holiness. It is written: "It is a kindness (Chesed)" <note>Leviticus 20:17, interpreted here as a hidden mercy even in destruction</note>, yet they are "cut off." These two opposites appear "before the eyes of their people" from the power of **Understanding** (Binah), from which both Mercies and Judgments are awakened. 

**Therefore**, "Lord of Hosts" (YHVH Tzevaot) who calls for weeping and eulogy is joined to the Name of Havayah punctuated as *Elohim*—the mystery of Understanding. For regarding her it is written, "at a time of favor," and "she is not only my mother’s daughter, but my father’s daughter as well, and she became my wife" <note>Genesis 20:12</note>. Therefore, **Yom Kippur**, which alludes to her, forbids marital relations. These, then, are two garments for **Beauty** (Tiferet): the garment of Mercy in his love for **Rachel**, and the garment of Judgment because **Leah** was "hated." This is because at the time that "the Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one," a "shoot has already come forth from the staff of Jesse" <note>Isaiah 11:1</note>. His power is sufficient so that from now on the Cherubim will be intertwined. They should not despair of Mercy. The truth is that the King is "Complete" (Shalem) when He judges, for He judges for the good, even though His face is not "shining." This is argued *a fortiori* from its opposite as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach): the measure of Good is much greater than the measure of punishment. It is correct to believe that at the time of the Destruction, they were merely "intertwined" <note>in an embrace</note>, but in a time of favor, there are "coils all around." 

**And just as** during the Destruction of the Temple the decree of Yom Kippur was nullified for the reason we stated, so too during the **Dedication of the Temple** which Solomon built, they nullified ten days and seven days—fourteen days. This is a startling doubling! Rather, it is an allusion to the "Unification of the Personifications" (Partzufim), Male and Female, through the power of Wisdom and Understanding in joy and responsibility, never to be separated. This is what is meant by "Fourteen": the four letters of the Name (YHVH) and the ten...

# Pomegranate Slice / Gate 8: Essence and Conduct / Juice of Pomegranates
