### Chapter 11
After explaining the general nature of the Attributes <note>Hebrew: *Middot*, another term for the Sefirot</note> and the way their vitality, action, and establishment are revealed in every single deed—according to the way the Sefirot are linked and unified as mentioned—know this: because every single Sefirah is composed of ten sub-Sefirot <note>original: *asarah*</note> as has been explained, each one of them unifies with every other one until they are all unified across all equal levels.

How so? The **Crown** <note>Keter</note> within the Crown is linked with **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> through the general aspect of the Crown within itself and within the essence of Wisdom. Likewise, through the general aspect of Wisdom within the essence of Wisdom itself and within the essence [of the Crown]. In this manner, it connects with all the other Sefirot... in the essence of the Crown and its being. Aside from these paths, the Sefirot are included and unified with one another through the unification of the other nine parts of the Sefirot included within each Sefirah. For example, the Crown unifies with **Understanding** <note>Binah</note> through the inclusion of the Crown within her essence and within the essence of the Crown, and so too with all other parts and sub-parts across all the Sefirot. Every path of connection from one Sefirah to another occurs through the connection of these parts... according to what has been explained, the Sefirot are tied and included in their thousands and tens of thousands... and the reason they are linked, unified, and flow from one to another has been explained in the *Gate of Titles* <note>original: *Sha'ar ha-Kinnuyim*</note>.

### Chapter 12
Know that the matter of the unification of the Sefirot occurs in several ways. The [first] way involves the powers that branch out from the unity <note>from the side of the unification of the verse "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One"</note>. From the beginning of their revelation in their individual essence and status, they are forever linked. For if, God forbid, there was a gap in the flow... the worlds would be destroyed and nullified <note>original: *mitbattelim*, referring to the state before the world was rectified</note>. This [unification] is for the sake of the existence of the Sefirot... it was the intention of the Creator to unify the Sefirot... to show that He is the cause of their existence and this is His perfect structure. This is not to add or increase the flow beyond its nature, but to maintain the aforementioned unification... as Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the traditional author of the Zohar</note> said, when the "shells" <note>original: *Kelipot*, or forces of imbalance/evil</note> stand against it, we increase the flow... so that the [Divine] fleeing from the external forces is strengthened... and the beauty of the Crowns is not diminished.

->The Second Unification<-

This is the unification of the Sefirot to bestow an **additional flow** of bounty and blessings to bless the created beings, each one according to their righteousness and deeds, and according to the requirements of the place and the time. Sometimes there is a need for the "Kingdom" <note>Malchut, the lowest Sefirah</note> to receive more "Whiteness" <note>mercy and forgiveness</note>. When the flow is drawn from the supreme source, the **Crown**, it whitens the sins of Israel through **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, for she is the essence of **Repentance** <note>Teshuvah</note>. Through the unification of the aspect of Wisdom, this flow is channeled to the Kingdom, and the strict Judgments of the Kingdom are sweetened through the flow... this is to repair and bridge, etc., and this was [the secret of] "Forgive the entire congregation of the children of Israel."

<column-break/>

...the secret of "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" <note>Isaiah 30:26, a metaphor for the restoration of the Divine Presence/Malchut</note>.

### Chapter 10
Rabbi Nehunia ben ha-Kanah <note>A 1st-century sage to whom early Kabbalistic works are attributed</note> said in his prayer that the first three [Sefirot] are considered as one, in the secret of **Knowledge** <note>Da'at</note>: "The Knower, the Known, and Knowledge itself." We are obligated to understand and contemplate how they differ from the lower [Sefirot]... and we must wonder at what is said in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar</note> in many places regarding the verse "You shall surely send away the mother" <note>Deuteronomy 22:7</note>, that these are the two "divorces": the Mother is the **Higher Divine Presence** <note>Binah</note>, and "the [children]" includes the **Lower Divine Presence** <note>Malchut</note>. If so, where is the unique importance and unification of Understanding <note>Binah</note>? Let us first state that the unification of the Sefirot occurs in one of three ways:

->The First Unification<-

This is the unification of the Sefirot during their **Emanation** <note>original: *Atzilutan*</note>, which never ceases, for the sake of the maintenance of reality. The intention of the *Shema* prayer is to unify them all, one to one, and all of them within the Emanator <note>God</note>, declaring Him King over all beings, for He gives life to them all... and the goal we long for here is to add perfection to them, such that the damage caused by the Serpent <note>original: *nachash*, representing primordial sin/imbalance</note> is repaired, and nothing else.

->The Second Unification<-

This occurs when an **additional flow** is renewed within them for the need of the moment. For example, the service of the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note> is to draw "Whiteness" from the Crown through Repentance, when Thought <note>Chokhmah</note> unifies with it to bestow flow upon the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note> to whiten sins. The unification of Understanding and Kingdom occurs via the "Six Extremities" <note>the six emotive Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note> through the secret of the letters. One who wishes to become **wise** should draw from Wisdom via the South <note>associated with Mercy/Chesed</note> toward the **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note> where the Torah is found, and toward the Kingdom (the "Lower Wisdom"). One who wishes to become **wealthy** should draw from Understanding via the North <note>associated with Strength/Gevurah</note> toward the Kingdom. One who wishes to **overpower** should draw from Understanding via Strength and Majesty <note>Gevurah and Hod</note> toward the Kingdom—the "Sword that avenges the covenant"—assisted by Victory <note>Netzach</note> to defeat enemies. All these aspects change according to the events affecting the Sefirot of the "Building" <note>the lower seven Sefirot</note>. But as for the first three Sefirot, when one is revealed, its companions are brought with it... as they say in the *Tikkunim*: the Supernal Crown from the female side is called *Asher* <note>That/Which</note> and from the male side is called *Rosh* <note>Head</note>, the "Head of all heads."

->The Third Unification<-

This concerns Wisdom and Understanding, Beauty and Kingdom, which unify as **pairs**. Peace—and the renewal of emanation—only occurs through them. When this unification is absent from Beauty and Kingdom, it is also missing from Wisdom and Understanding in their place. The "Rectification" <note>Tikkun</note> is directed at all of them as one. As explained in the *Tikkunim*, the "Small Letter He" <note>the last letter of the Name YHVH, representing Malchut</note> says "I am asleep," in the secret of "I was dumb with silence, I held my peace" <note>Psalm 39:3</note>. This is the withdrawal of the letter **Vav** <note>Tiferet</note> until the Vav is awakened toward her when our Messiah is revealed. Then "the voice of my beloved knocks," rising and descending. The letters of the Name, which were in the secret of "Y-D-V," and the secret of "and the two of them went" <note>Ruth 1:19</note>—where each of the two letters **He** was far from its partner—now join as **Y-H-V-H**. This is when the "Lower He" rises to the "Yod" in the secret of "The Lord [YH] by wisdom [Chokhmah] founded the earth [Malchut]" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>... and the "Higher Mother" <note>Binah</note> accompanies her to arouse the Father's mercy. Then the "Higher He" descends toward the "Vav" (the son of Y-H), which is the secret of "Establishing the heavens with understanding." This is the secret of the "Ascending Offering" <note>original: *Korban Olah*</note>.

It categorizes three types of Divine Unification: one that sustains basic existence, one that responds to human deeds (like repentance or seeking wisdom), and a third that restores the cosmic balance of the Divine Name.</summary>

### Chapter 9: Or Alternatively

->The questioner understood the explanation well, meaning:<-
->Before the Omnipresent, which is the Shekhinah, and that—<-

"The native stays on the ground while the convert is in the highest heavens." <note>A Talmudic idiom (Yatsiva be-ara) suggesting a reversal of the natural order.</note> He replied: Whatever your perspective, it is certainly not true that "hidden things" do not apply Above. For by necessity, the meaning of "inner chambers" <note>Hebrew: *batei gawai*, referring to a place where God is said to weep in secret (Hagigah 5b).</note> refers to "the hidden things belong to the Lord our God," while the denial of weeping applies to the "outer chambers," as we have said. He did not merely cancel the logical inference <note>term: *Kal va-chomer* (a fortiori argument)</note> by saying it refers to the final decree, until the questioner understood his intent and asked: "But for you, there is a difficulty with the verse: *On that day...* <note>Isaiah 22:12</note> which certainly refers to the final decree!" He replied that the destruction of the Holy Temple is different, for even the angels were in a state of panic regarding the decree, rushing to hasten atonement, as we explained. Do not say these were only the forces of Judgment, but even the "Angels of Mercy and Peace shall weep bitterly." <note>Isaiah 33:7</note> It is possible to interpret "Angels of Peace" as the attributes of **Endurance** <note>Netzach</note> and **Splendor** <note>Hod</note>, which at a time of favor are the angels of unification for the **Righteous One** <note>Tzadik / Yesod</note> who is called "Peace." Or, "they shall weep bitterly," and the scriptural reference to "Hosts" <note>Tzevaot</note> is precise. Ultimately, the Name Y-H-V-H vocalized with the vowels of *Elohim* <note>indicating Judgment within Mercy</note> is the source of the sadness for the Name *Adonai* <note>the Shekhinah</note> that was awakened over it, and for the "Hosts" who eulogized on that day.

Furthermore, the secret of the "Angels of Peace" can be understood in relation to those who are atoned for, through the miracle of the Cherubs <note>term: *Keruvim* (the winged figures atop the Ark)</note>. As the Sages taught in Tractate Yoma regarding the verse "as they saw their nakedness"—it was a layman who innovated the idea that it was the Absolute Will that the Cherubs should be embracing at the time of the Destruction. This was the secret of the "Angels of Peace," intended not to terrify Israel. At that very moment, we read "they shall weep bitterly" regarding the Temple. The term "And He called" <note>Vayikra</note> implies an outflow of influence, even for weeping and eulogy; for even when the Temple is desolate, it stands in its holiness. It is written: "It is a kindness (*chesed*), let him be cut off"—two opposites in human terms derived from the power of **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, from which both mercies and judgments are awakened. Therefore, "the Lord of Hosts" who calls for weeping and eulogy is joined to the Name of Mercy <note>Y-H-V-H</note> vocalized as *Elohim*, the secret of *Binah*. Regarding her it is written: "at a time of favor," but she is not only "the daughter of my people" but "the daughter of my father" as well, "and she became my wife." <note>Alluding to the complex familial metaphors in Kabbalah where Binah is both Mother and 'Wife' to the central attributes.</note> Therefore, on Yom Kippur—which hints at her—marital relations are forbidden. Rather, they are two "garments" for **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>: the garment of Mercy in his love for **Rachel**, and the garment of Judgment because "**Leah** was hated." This is because "when Lebanon falls by a mighty one," a "shoot has already come forth from the staff of Jesse," and his merit is sufficient that from now on the Cherubs should be constantly embracing. This is the reason we stated: "so as not to terrify Israel," lest they despair of mercy. The truth is that the King is "Complete" even when He judges; He is clothed in Judgment for the sake of good, even though His face does not shine. This is an "all the more so" argument from its opposite as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach), for the attribute of Good is much greater than the attribute of punishment. It is proper to believe that at the time of the Destruction, they were in a state of "embrace" only, but in a time of favor, there is a "coupling all around." And just as at the destruction of the Temple the strictures of Yom Kippur were suspended for the reason we mentioned, so too at the Dedication of the Temple built by Solomon, they suspended seven days and seven days—fourteen days—which is a startling doubling. Rather, it hints at the unification of the "Personages" <note>term: *Partzufim* (Divine configurations)</note>, male and female, from the power of **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> and **Understanding** <note>Binah</note> in a joy of responsibility that shall never be separated. This is what is meant by "Four"—this is the Name Y-H-V-H—and the "Ten"...

...attained it as the study of Judgment and its proximity; the secret of the "One" of **Wisdom**. Look deeply: the beginnings of contemplative thought toward **Understanding** are sweeter because of their bluntness/dimness, while the diminutions toward **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note> (and because Understanding is second to Wisdom and Kindness is third to Understanding, until our simple mercies are like... as was seen). How many glorious doubts will fall in this matter! This is specifically regarding subtlety and spirituality. It was subtle in the ultimate subtlety... and the strengthening clings to the essence. (And so is the matter with Judgment, for it is unique... nevertheless, because its root is to be merciful and to do good, things are set on their proper foundation). The matter is known regarding the Crown: that all subtleties are included in it. Nevertheless, it is the root of Kindness and the root of Power <note>Gevurah</note> that exist in the Crown in the secret of the "King." The "Points" included in the Crown are the three lines: Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy. Not that there is actual Kindness and Judgment there, but they are there in an extremely subtle way... the power of the Foundation <note>Yesod</note>, and the Ox, and the Water, and the Dust, which are included in absolute Kindness... not that there is actual water, wind, and dust there, but the "Source of the Elements" is partitioned there in subtlety... as the three points of the Mind <note>vowels: *Segol*</note> that are included, hidden, and unified in the Crown... (including all the paths in hiddenness and ultimate subtlety), as will be explained in the section on the "Rectifications" <note>term: *Tikunim*</note>. (Nevertheless, the lack in the Rectifications is superior to the Foundation). So it is in relation to the three attributes of action: Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy. They are hidden in the Crown as "Sources," and there they are not judged as either Kindness, Judgment, or Mercy, except in the way described in the "Values." For regarding the matter of the subtle attributes and actions in the Crown: the attributes (actions) are drawn from the "tracings" of the Sefirot included in the Crown. For the "Realities" included in the Crown cause the rectified attributes. And just as the Sefirot were hidden in their source and unified in it with the ultimate unification—and were not "Sefirot" at all until after the Crown was renewed—so even though there was a merciful beginning, the attributes and actions were still hidden in great subtlety until there was no "perceived" judgment or action at all, until they were emanated and revealed in an essential revelation below... and when they were revealed in their place... His power of Kindness was in them... and this Name will not suffer exchange... the relationship of Judgment, for the root of everything is from above. Rather, from the abundance of their subtlety, no kindness was visible, and they are like...

Y-H-W-H <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> is "Day," in the secret of the verse: "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun." <note>Isaiah 30:26; a prophecy of future harmony between the masculine and feminine aspects of the Divine.</note>

# Chapter 10
Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kanah <note>A 1st-century sage and mystic to whom many early Kabbalistic works are attributed.</note> said in his prayer that the first three Sefirot are considered as one in the secret of Knowledge (*Da'at*). They are "the Knower, the Known, and Knowledge itself." We are obligated to understand and contemplate how they differ in their ascent toward the absolute Unity that is required of all emanated beings. Furthermore, one must wonder at what is said in many places in the *Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkunei Zohar*, a foundational Kabbalistic text.</note> regarding the verse, "You shall surely send away the mother" <note>Deuteronomy 22:7</note>—that these are the "two expulsions." The "Mother" is the Higher Presence (*Shekhinah*), while the word "the" (*et*) comes to include the Lower Presence. If so, what is the distinct importance and uniqueness of Understanding (*Binah*)? We must first establish that the unification of the Sefirot occurs in one of three ways:

## The First Unification
This is the unification of the Sefirot in their very emanation. This unity is never withheld, for it is necessary for the continued existence of reality. The intent of the *Shema* prayer is to unify them all, one to another, and all of them within the Emanator, crowning Him over all beings, for He gives life to them all. Their existence remains below, unlike in the secret of the Jubilee <note>A reference to the Sefirah of Binah/Understanding, where all things return to their source.</note> when "He gathers his spirit and soul to Himself." Our ultimate longing in this unification is to add perfection to them so that the corruption of the Serpent <note>A reference to original sin or the introduction of imbalance/evil into the world.</note> may be repaired, and nothing else.

## The Second Unification
This occurs when a supplementary flow of divine bounty is renewed within them for a specific hour of need. For example, the service of the Name Y-H <note>The first two letters of the divine name, associated with the higher Sefirot.</note> is intended to draw down "whiteness" (mercy) from the Crown (*Keter*) through Repentance (*Teshuvah*). This happens by joining Thought (*Machshavah*) with it to pour influence upon the Kingdom (*Malkhut*) to whiten sins. The unification of Understanding and Kingdom is achieved through the "Six Extremities" <note>The six emotional Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod.</note> in the secret of the "Sprinklings." <note>A reference to the Temple ritual of sprinkling blood, used here as a metaphor for directing divine energy.</note> One who wishes to become wise should draw from Wisdom (*Hokhmah*) through the South toward Beauty (*Tiferet*)—the place of the Torah—and toward the Kingdom, which is the "Lower Wisdom." One who wishes to become wealthy should draw from Understanding through the North toward the Kingdom. One who wishes to become powerful should draw from Understanding through Strength (*Gevurah*) and Glory (*Hod*) toward the Kingdom—the "sword that avenges the covenant"—assisted by Victory (*Netzach*) to defeat enemies. All these aspects and their likes change according to the event within the Sefirot of the "Building." <note>The lower seven Sefirot involved in the construction of our reality.</note> But regarding the "First Three" (the highest Sefirot), when one is revealed, its companions are brought with it. This is the secret of the words *A-Sh-E-R* (That), *R-A-Sh* (Head), and *Sh-A-R* (Remainder), which are "darkness and light alike." As they say in the *Tikkunim*: the Higher Crown from the feminine side is called *Asher*, and from the masculine side is called *Rosh*—the Head of all heads. This also applies to Wisdom in its place, and Understanding in relation to it, which are "the Remainder of the Flesh."

## The Third Unification
This concerns Wisdom and Understanding, Beauty and Kingdom, which are unified as pairs. New emanation never comes through them alone. When a lack occurs in Beauty and Kingdom, a lack also occurs in Wisdom and Understanding in their places. The repair is directed toward all of them as one, as explained in the *Tikkunim*. They said that the "Small Letter He" <note>The final letter of the Name Y-H-W-H, representing the Shekhinah/Kingdom.</note> says: "I am asleep, like a firstborn I have become mute, silent and still from good." <note>A poetic description of the Shekhinah in exile or diminished state.</note> This state lasts until the letter *Vav* <note>Representing the masculine aspect, Tiferet.</note> is awakened toward her when our Messiah is revealed. Then "the voice of my beloved knocks," and the flow rises and descends. The letters of the Name, which were in the secret of *Y-W-D-D* and *Y-H-W-D* <note>Permutations of the Name suggesting separation.</note>—"And the two of them walked" <note>Ruth 1:19</note>—meaning each of the two letters *He* was far from its counterpart, now join as *Y-H-H*. This means the Lower *He* rises to the *Yod* in the secret of "The Lord (*Y-H-W-H*) by Wisdom (*Hokhmah*) founded the earth," and "His father guarded the matter." Naturally, the Mother accompanies her to arouse the Father's mercy. Then the Higher *He* descends toward the *Vav* (the son of Y-H), which is "He established the heavens with Understanding (*Tevunah*)." This is the secret of the Burnt Offering (*Olah*).

->Which is to say, it takes its place:<-

# Chapter 11
After explaining the general nature of the Divine Attributes, the way their qualities and actions are revealed, and their agreement in every single action—as one, like the Crown (*Keter*) through the path of connection and the unification of the Sefirot—how is this? Know that because every single Sefirah is essentially comprised of ten sub-Sefirot, as mentioned regarding Kindness (*Chesed*), each one will be uniquely connected with all of them. They bond with one another through the "angles" of their aspects. How so? The Crown connects with Wisdom through the aspect of "the Crown within Wisdom," and in the world of Wisdom, it connects through the "Wisdom within the Crown." It connects with all other Sefirot through the part of itself within them. Thus, Wisdom connects to it through the part it receives from the essence of the Crown. And so it is with all other Sefirot. Aside from these paths, we could arrange the Sefirot toward each other and unify the other nine Sefirot included within Kindness. For example: Kindness connects with Strength (*Gevurah*) through the "Crown within its essence" and the essence of Strength, and so with all other parts. Through this path of inter-connection, the parts of the Sefirot connect to each other within themselves, part to part. Every part is comprised of ten, and so they are compounded... <note>The text here becomes highly technical, discussing the mathematical and geometric inter-inclusion of the divine forces.</note> as explained regarding the "Reciprocal Lights" and the "Chariots" of the Sefirot. For from every Sefirah, unique aspects are included, like a beam of light that is comprised of many colors. They become connected and unified as they travel from one to another, as explained in the "Gate of Sefirot."

# Chapter 13: Know
That the matter of the "Foundation of the Sefirot" has three aspects. The first is a unique perception <margin>from the perspective of the verse "The Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He"</margin> from the beginning of their emanation. This refers to their essential nature, which is eternal. Behold, this was the "Primordial Flow" of the lights... and the worlds were being created and canceled <insert>before their emanation</insert>. This foundation is the end of everything, and not one of the Sefirot shall be missing from it, for it is an eternal law. This was the intent of the First Unification: to establish the Sefirot as one, all of them in one state, crowning Him over all sources, great and small, to demonstrate their existence. This is their miraculous life-force, not intended to add or increase flow beyond what is required for existence. <insert>And also,</insert> if in the words of Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai <note>Traditional author of the Zohar.</note> it implies that unification sometimes adds flow, the intent is to add to the vessels so they can be perfect, for when they were first created, the "corruption of the Serpent" had not yet been removed... and the beauty of the "limbs" <note>The structure of the Sefirot</note> was diminished.

## The Second Unification
This is the bonding of the Sefirot to provide an additional flow of bounty and blessings for the sake of created beings, each according to their merits and needs, and according to the specific time and place. Sometimes there is a need for completion and drawing down from the "Higher Whiteness" of the Crown, which repairs the sins of Israel through Understanding (*Binah*), for she is the essence of Repentance. Through the study of the Oral Torah, Wisdom will pour that flow toward the Kingdom (*Malkhut*), and the Crown and Kingdom will be unified through the Names of Mercy. This is "Truth and Unity," and then there is peace for the entire congregation of Israel.

# Pomegranate Slice / Gate 8: Essence and Conduct / Juice of Pomegranates

The third point concerns the secret of Judgment <note>original: *Din*</note>. The Sages called this the "Hidden Wisdom" <note>original: *Hokhmah Ha-Mistabeket*</note> that arises from Kindness <note>original: *Hesed*</note>. When the qualities of Kindness are missing due to change and variation, Understanding <note>original: *Binah*</note> adds more to the flow. This is because the Kindness that remains within the attribute of Kindness is influenced by the fact that Understanding is the "progenitor" of Wisdom. Since Kindness is the third quality, it must endure the "smallness" of the Compassionate One <note>original: *Rahmana*</note>. Many hidden doubts may fall upon this matter.

If you ask why they are given a lower status, it is because the "face" of the Crown <note>original: *Keter*</note> relative to Understanding is considered "the back" in terms of its relationship to the Crown itself. This is specifically regarding the matters of subtlety and spirituality, but not regarding Judgment and Mercy. Outside of the manifestation of Judgment, which exists in a subtle state within the expansion of the Crown itself, the messenger can receive a branch of Kindness from below in the secret of the Angels. There is no doubt that this is more "Kindness" than the Strength <note>original: *Gevurah*</note> which is considered its "small" counterpart. 

This is like a great tree with a small branch at the very bottom. The root is extremely subtle and spiritual. It adheres to the "back" and assumes the burden of its bearer to restore this weakness to its perfect form. One must understand how one boundary transitions to another. From the perspective of the Crown, everything comes from its potential, and it is capable of doing everything in a way that aligns with the providence of the world. 

The same logic applies to Judgment. Though it is said, "He spoke and it was," we exist within lines of Divine Will that seek to return things to their proper form. It is well known that the Crown is the secret of the utmost subtlety. Nevertheless, the root of Kindness and the root of Strength exist within the Crown in the secret of the "three points" included within it. These are the three lines: Kindness, Awe <note>original: *Pahad*, another name for Gevurah/Judgment</note>, and Mercy. Wherever there is Kindness and Judgment, they exist there in great subtlety, like the subtle foundation of Kindness and its return. 

The essence of the inclusion of Kindness, Strength, Beauty <note>original: *Tiferet*</note>, and Sovereignty <note>original: *Malkhut*</note> is not that "Good" and "Day" exist there literally, but rather that the source of these foundations exists in subtlety within the life and blessings of the Ten Voices. These are the hidden and unified qualities within the Hidden Wisdom <note>original: *Hokhmah Setu'ah*</note>. They include all qualities and actions in the absolute peak of subtlety, as will be explained in the order of the Divine Conduct. 

Even though the Divine Might is revealed through the transition from Understanding to the level of the active attributes—which are Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy—they are all hidden within the Supreme Crown as their source. There, one judges neither Kindness, nor Judgment, nor Mercy, except in the way we described the "etching." <note>The author uses the metaphor of a scratch or etching (*Sertah*) to describe how these attributes exist as latent potentials before they are "drawn out" into reality.</note> Just as the point of etching exists in the Hidden Wisdom, so too is the subtlety of the attributes and actions in the Supreme Crown. The actions are like the internal "scratches" or lines included in the Crown. These lines become the causes for the expansion of the attributes. 

Even though Mercy was revealed in the Crown, the attributes and actions were still within the Essence in such great subtlety that they could not yet be called "good" or "evil" or even "action" until they were revealed. When they were revealed in their own essence below, it was according to their power and the level appropriate for them. Once they were received in their place, they emerged as actual attributes through the power that the King instilled in them. With this, the difficulty of "how Judgment emerges from the Source" is resolved; it is because everything exists above in potential, but due to its extreme subtlety, neither Kindness nor Judgment are visible.

<column-break/>

...at a moment, you too! Behold, I bring wood and I bring coals, and immediately the King relents and has compassion for his son. <note>A parable explaining how God's anger contains the materials for the eventual comfort and rebuilding.</note>

## Chapter 9
It was well understood by the questioner that "before the Place" refers to the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>. It is a common saying: "The native stays on the ground while the stranger is in the highest heavens." He replied: whichever way you look at it, "sorrow" cannot be attributed to the One Above. This is certainly true, for the verse "The hidden things belong to the Lord our God" <note>Deuteronomy 29:28</note> implies the "inner chambers," while the "outer chambers" are where the negation of sorrow applies. 

He did not manage to cancel the logical inference <note>original: *Kal va-Chomer*</note> or say that this refers only to the final verdict until the questioner understood the consolation and asked: According to your view, it is difficult to understand the verse "And on that day [the Lord] called [for weeping]" <note>Isaiah 22:12</note>, which certainly refers to the final verdict! He replied that the Destruction of the Temple is different. Even the angels were in a state of alarm over the verdict, hurrying to find atonement, as we explained. Do not say this refers only to the Angels of Judgment; rather, the "Angels of Mercy and Peace weep bitterly." 

It is possible to explain "Angels of Peace" as referring to the attributes of Victory <note>original: *Netzach*</note> and Splendor <note>original: *Hod*</note>. In a time of favor, they are the angels of unity for the Righteous One <note>The Sefirah of *Yesod*</note>, who is called Peace. Then, they "weep bitterly." The scriptural mention of "Hosts" <note>original: *Tzva'ot*</note> is precise. Ultimately, the Name Y-H-W-H vocalized as *Elohim* <note>The Name of Mercy written with the vowels of Judgment</note> is the source of the sadness for the Master, which was awakened toward Him and toward the mourning hosts on that day.

**Furthermore**, one can understand the secret of the "Angels of Peace" through the count of the wonders of the Cherubim <note>The angelic figures atop the Ark of the Covenant</note>. As the Sages taught in Tractate Yoma regarding the verse "they saw their nakedness": it was a new thing that the Absolute Will innovated—that the Cherubim should be found in an embrace at the time of the Destruction. This was the secret of the "Angels of Peace," intended not to terrify Israel. At that very moment, we read "they weep bitterly" in both sources. The word "He called" <note>original: *Va-yikra*</note> implies an outflow of influence, even for weeping and mourning, for even when the Temple is desolate, it stands in its holiness. 

It is written: "It is Kindness <note>original: *Hesed*</note>, and they shall be cut off." <note>Leviticus 20:17. In Kabbalah, this verse is interpreted to show how extreme Kindness can sometimes look like its opposite.</note> These two opposites appear before the eyes of their people through the power of Understanding <note>original: *Binah*</note>, for from her, both Mercy and Judgments are awakened. **Therefore**, "the Lord of Hosts" who calls for weeping and mourning is joined to the Name of Being <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> vocalized as *Elohim*, the secret of Understanding. 

It is written of her: "In a time of favor... but she is not the daughter of my mother, but rather the daughter of my father, and she became my wife." <note>A reference to Sarah in Genesis 20:12, used here to map familial relationships to the Sefirot.</note> Therefore, on Yom Kippur <note>the Day of Atonement</note>, which hints at her, marital relations are forbidden. These, then, are two garments for the attribute of Beauty <note>original: *Tiferet*</note>: the garment of Mercy in his love for Rachel, and the garment of Judgment because Leah was "hated." This is because at the hour when "the Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one," a "staff has already emerged from the stump of Jesse." <note>Isaiah 11:1; a messianic promise planted even during destruction.</note> His merit is sufficient so that from now on, the Cherubim will always be in an embrace. This is the reason we stated: "not to terrify Israel," lest they despair of Mercy. 

The truth is that the King is "Complete" when He judges, clothed in Judgment for the sake of good. Even though His "wings" are not shining, we can apply a logical inference from its opposite, as explained in the Zohar (Portion Beshallach): the measure of Good is much greater than the measure of punishment. It is proper to believe that at the time of the Destruction, they were in an embrace only, and in a time of favor, they are in a full union. 

**Just as** during the Destruction of the House the decree of Yom Kippur was suspended for the reason we stated, so too during the Dedication of the House that Solomon built, they suspended Yom Kippur. But that was for a different secret hinted at in the scripture, which says they celebrated for "seven days and seven days, fourteen days." This doubling is wondrous! It hints at the union of the "Faces"—masculine and feminine—through the power of Wisdom and Understanding in a joy and unity that shall never be separated. This is what is meant by "fourteen"—it is the Name **YHWH** plus the ten... <note>The text cuts off as it begins a mathematical/Gematria calculation of the Divine Name.</note>

# Pomegranate Slice / Gate 8: Essence and Conduct / Juice of Pomegranates

On the verse "A river went out of Eden" <note>Genesis 2:10</note>: This action is continuous and never-ceasing. The text attributes "eating" to the higher realms, even though "drinking" is considered more subtle and spiritual. This teaches us that the "edges" <note>the lower Sefirot</note> that manifest in their own place actually have a source above in Understanding <term>Binah; the third Sefirah, associated with the Divine Mother</term>, which is a "deep and calm stream" that waters them from above in a subtle and spiritual manner. It places "Will" <note>original: *Reuta*</note> before its importance, for it is right that "Unity" <note>original: *Achduta*</note> precedes "Joy" <note>original: *Chiduta*</note>, as Unity is more communal and inclusive, and naturally comes first. However, at first, it prioritized Joy from among the known qualities because it is the cause of Will; therefore, it placed them in close proximity.

**The Rule** that emerges from this is that Unity is constant and all-encompassing; there is never any separation within it, neither in the context of the Divine Attributes nor in our own context. Joy also never ceases among the Attributes, though it may seem to cease from our perspective. But regarding "Will," there are conditions even among the Attributes. In times of peace, they are never separated. This Joy exists even in the worlds of separation <note>the lower worlds</note> where the "Angels of Peace" and "Angels of Charity" reside. When "Righteousness and Peace kiss" <note>Psalm 85:11</note>, they also become unified as male and female, as explained in many places in the *Tikunim* <term>Tikunei Zohar; a classic kabbalistic text</term>. However, during the time of Exile, the Holy One, blessed be He, swore He would not enter the Heavenly Jerusalem <note>original: *Yerushalayim shel Ma'alah*</note> etc., as mentioned earlier. According to the first interpretation, the joys remain and there is no dispute. Nevertheless, it is written: "A friend loves at all times" <note>Proverbs 17:17</note>; even though they are not in a state of active union <note>original: *Zivug*</note>, the Divine Presence never leaves the Sanctuary, for "her impurity is not in her skirts" <note>Lamentations 1:9</note>, unlike the lower Presence <note>original: *Shekhintaa Tata'ah*</note>. Therefore, it is correct to say they are "friends who never separate," even when there is no active union, for there is—Heaven forbid—no strife or quarrel between them; rather, they both willfully grieve for those below.

**In the *Tikunim***, it is explained that there are three levels to the union of Wisdom <term>Hokhmah</term> and Understanding <term>Binah</term>. The union itself is hinted at in the Name "YA" <note>Yod-Aleph</note>, which is also "YH" <note>Yod-Heh</note> in their existence within the Crown <term>Keter</term> through the secret of Knowledge <term>Da'at</term> which is rooted there. This indicates that there was a "Palace" for the four-letter Name <term>YHVH; the Tetragrammaton</term>, which first expands into Wisdom, becomes a "vessel" in Understanding, and they unify in Knowledge which is revealed between them. They then expand a second time into Greatness <term>Hesed</term> and Strength <term>Gevurah</term>, unifying in Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>. A third time they expand into Victory <term>Netzach</term> and Splendor <term>Hod</term>, unifying in Foundation <term>Yesod</term>, and from there, they move into union with Kingship <term>Malkhut</term>. This is the "City of Four" where the Names *YHVH-Ehyeh* and *YHVH-Adonai* reside. Their numerical value <note>Gematria</note> equals "Lebanon" <note>138</note>, and likewise "Good Lesson" <note>Proverbs 4:2</note>. Their initial letters form the phrase "The Lord our God, the Lord is One" <note>original: *YHVH Eloheinu YHVH Echad*</note>. Their sign is *IAIA*, a holy Name whose letters represent Wisdom, Understanding, Beauty, and Kingship in the order of the words. The secret of "fair to look upon" <note>Genesis 29:17</note> is spoken of Rachel, and Onkelos translated "IAIA" as "in vision." Its numerical equivalent is *TR'HR*, which is the four-letter Name in the reversed "Tashrak" alphabet <note>a system where Tav=Aleph, Shin=Bet, etc.</note>, following the secret of "In you <note>original: *Bekha*</note> shall Israel bless" <note>Genesis 48:20</note>. For this reason, we mention "In You," referring to Your Name as expounded in the Zohar, portion *Shemot*. Behold, the existence of *YHVH* and *Ehyeh* is the light from Wisdom downwards, while *YHVH-Adonai* is the "Returning Light" from Kingship that turns upward through three levels. It unifies in Foundation with the Name *ADNVYH*. The one who answers "Amen" is greater than the one who blesses. *YHVH* expands in Victory and *Adonai* in Splendor; when they unify in Beauty, they expand into Greatness and Strength; and when they unify in Knowledge, they return and expand into Wisdom and Understanding. However, the names of the "Children" <note>the lower Sefirot</note> are not revealed in the Crown; they are hidden within their roots.

<column-break/>

The Divine Presence in the Lower Jerusalem precedes the Divine Presence in the Heavenly Jerusalem. Therefore, it was necessary for the "Son" of *YHV-H* <note>referring to the letters of the Name</note>—the first *Heh*—to be Kingship, which is in the "womb" with the people. Regarding this, the second *Heh* said "with the throne." But in the Burnt Offering <note>original: *Korban Olah*</note>, Understanding established the offering to Wisdom and Kingship, and established all of Beauty. Thus the Name is found in its proper order *YHVH*. This is the secret of "Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife" <note>Genesis 2:24</note>. (This means Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>, which separates from the first two and unifies with the final *Heh*, which is Kingship <term>Malkhut</term>). It has been explained that the union of Beauty and Kingship mirrors the union of Wisdom and Understanding. This is the secret of the Burnt Offering: it is a "sacrifice to the Lord," meaning a foundation for the sixth level of the four-letter Name, and a sacrifice in "uprightness," the Name of twenty-five <note>original: *Koh*</note>, following the portion of *Vayikra*.

### Chapter 14: And If

It is required of us: "And if you shall rejoice." For in the portion of *Vayikra* on the verse "I am..." etc., they received that it was from Wisdom and Understanding. For the "Beloveds" <term>Dodim</term> are Beauty and Kingship. It says that Wisdom and Understanding are "Friends" <term>Re'im</term>; the "Upper Friends" never separate... <note>original: *Lo Mitparshan*</note> (and this logic extends from Wisdom to Foundation). The minor point is that even during the time when the aforementioned union continues between Beauty and Kingship, there will be "Belovedness" between them. Beauty and Kingship only unify at specific intervals, such as the time of the "Standing Prayer" <note>the Amidah</note>. It is compared to this because it does not wake up constantly all day long, for the worlds must return to their watch to sustain the lower beings. Therefore they are called "Beloveds" <note>original: *Dodim*</note> who join sometimes, unlike the "Friends" who are constant as long as the Temple stands. Therefore, they are called "Friends" always, a sign of peace and strength, as explained in the portion *Lech Lecha*. In the law, it is written: "A river went out of Eden to water the garden." Do not say that they separate; rather, they are certainly connected (meaning they are unified by the word of the Lord, which flows from Wisdom to the "Buckle" which is Understanding). The whole reason for saying this is to suggest that the foundation of Wisdom and Understanding is periodic like the union of Beauty and Kingship—but no, they are certainly distinct, for the union of Beauty and Kingship is added in its proper season (but this is not so for the union of Wisdom and Understanding). The higher ones never separated in times of peace. However, they unify in Foundation first, and this is to say that the "drinking" flows in the House of Kindness <term>Hesed</term>, the foundation for the "children" <note>lower levels</note>, and it breathes upon them abundance and will, until the vitality of the world is filled... and it does not descend and stop the light and abundance for the great and the small. But at the time of the Sacrifice, it follows the proper order, even between Wisdom and Understanding, just as the order of the "Station" was between Beauty and Kingship. And that which the scripture attributed to Understanding above in the beginning, and "drinking" below to the Beloveds—when it should have been the opposite, as drinking is more subtle than eating—the reason is explained in the language of the Sages. It is a matter of "vision." The word "eating" refers to the Will, for the Sefirot are bound above in subtlety; they are the branches through which their nourishment flows. Their foundation and soul is the vitality of the Sefirot that expand and "consume" below, which is "eating." They rise to their source in the Emanation, and thus the Sefirot in their subtlety include also the Sefirot that are attached to them. Through this, the roots are honored in their activities by the ascent of the roots to the place of the roots. The end of these upper subtleties is a great and subdued movement of abundance and blessing... as the Divine Presence says in the *Tikunim*... and in that statement, they hint at the unions we mentioned in these three levels: Joy, Unity, and Will. Look there. (This refers to the first union, which is elevated by the rectification of Kingship).

And when the letters approach each other in a movement of rising and falling—which is not a complete proximity—and when the letters approach in their proper order as an "offering to the Lord," <note>original: *Korban l'Hashem*</note> that which was Y-H-H-V is restored to Y-H-V-H. The "Upper Aleph" <note>representing the source</note> reaches toward the *Yod* <term>the first letter of the Name, associated with Wisdom</term> and the "Lower He" reaches toward the *Vav* <term>the third letter, associated with the male principle/Tiferet</term>. At that moment, "the bones come together, bone to its bone" <note>Ezekiel 37:7</note>, in the mystery of "bone of my bones" (referring to the letters *Yod-He*) and "flesh of my flesh" (referring to *Vav-He*). Therefore, "a man shall leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife" <note>Genesis 2:24</note>. When the "Upper He" <term>Binah; Divine Mother</term> rises toward the *Yod*, it is said of her: "This is the law of the burnt offering; it is the burnt offering" <note>Leviticus 6:2; "burnt offering" in Hebrew is *Olah*, which also means "ascending"</note>. And when it descends toward the *Vav*, it is said of it: "and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning in it" <note>Leviticus 6:2</note> with the flames of love. Even though there is also a "rising and falling" here, it is only within the mystery of the "sin offering preceding the burnt offering." It is written: "and he came down from offering the sin offering" <note>Leviticus 9:22</note>, meaning that because of him, there is a repair for the "Lower He" <term>Malchut; the Divine Presence</term>. For the *Vav* first descends toward its own *He* <note>the Lower He</note> and afterwards it rises toward its *He* in the mystery of the "Ascending Offering" as we have said. Thus explained the Sage, peace be upon him, regarding the service of Yom Kippur <term>Day of Atonement</term> concerning the "Goat for a Sin Offering" which is performed outside, and "unto the people" which is a burnt offering. Both of these are from the "Additional Service" <note>Musaf</note> of the day. Behold, at that time, "the angels of God were ascending"—two, being the *Yod* in the *He*, one toward the other—"and descending"—two, being the *Vav* in the *He*, one toward the other. And the Sages established that the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: "I shall not return to the Upper He until I return to the Lower He," which is the secret of the words "I will not enter the city" <note>Hosea 11:9; a Talmudic reference to Jerusalem</note>. From this intended meaning, the "harvest" is like the "planting," and according to this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, mentioned here is described through Wisdom.

### Chapter 11: And it is Possible

To explain the discourse in *The Faithful Shepherd* <term>Ra'aya Meheimna; a later layer of the Zohar</term> on the verse "As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his place" <note>Proverbs 27:8</note>. He <note>Tiferet, the Divine Son</note> moves from his place, which is the "World to Come" <term>Binah; Understanding</term>, and goes after her <note>Malchut, the Divine Presence</note> into this world, and is sent away. He swore that he would not return to his place until she returns to her place. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Levite, of blessed memory, raised a difficulty: from here it implies that Tiferet <term>The Attribute of Beauty/The Son</term> afflicts himself voluntarily and separates himself from the enjoyment of the flow coming to him from the "World to Come." However, in the portion of *Acharei Mot*, it implies that the "Upper Mother" <note>Binah</note> withholds the "crowns" and the "streams of the rivers" from him, implying he is forced. He answered that indeed, the Upper Mother withholds the "crowns," which are the *additional* flow to make him king over the lower beings, and withholds the "streams of the rivers" that nourish them, as in the phrase: "Go, get thee down; for thy people have corrupted themselves" <note>Exodus 32:7; implying Moses only had greatness for the sake of Israel</note>. However, regarding the flow *allotted* to him for his own sake, which is renewed every day and never ceases, he "sanctifies himself with that which is permitted to him." Sovereignty <term>Malchut</term> is also like him; the flow proper to her will never cease, but by her own will "her soul is shortened" by the labor of Israel. **However, it is possible** that while the Holy Temple stood, Tiferet and Malchut would not unite to give birth to souls except at specific times, such as the day the Torah was given or at the end of the *Amidah* prayer. But at all other times, they would "delight in loves" in the Synagogues and Houses of Study, like lovers who unite in one house. This is not the case for Wisdom and Understanding <term>Chochmah and Binah</term>, for they are in constant union in the world, as it says in the Zohar on the verse "Eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>. The "Friends" above are found in "Will," in "Unity," and in "Joy," and they are never separated. Thus, he mentioned the first union in Wisdom and Understanding which we explained with the word "Unity," and the second he called "Joy," for every like-thing delights in its like and they rejoice in happiness. Regarding the third, he said "Will," meaning "Serenity," which is why they are never separated. And he was precise.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Divine Names and the dynamics of the Sefirot (Divine Emanations). The previous page explored how the arrangement of letters in the Name Y-H-V-H changes based on the movement of "rising and falling" during spiritual service, specifically comparing the union of the higher Sefirot to the relationship between husband and wife.</meta>

-># Pomegranate Slice / Gate 8: Essence and Conduct / Juice of Pomegranates<-

The verse **"And a river goes out from Eden"** <note>Genesis 2:10</note> describes an action that is eternally constant without interruption. It attributes "eating" to the higher realms, even though "drinking" is more refined and spiritual. This teaches us that the "ends" <term>the lower Sefirot</term> which are revealed in their place actually have a source above in **Understanding** <term>Binah</term>, which is a "deep and flowing stream" that waters them from below in a refined and spiritual manner. The text places "Will" <term>Re’uta</term> before its own importance, for it is right that **Unity** <term>Achduta</term> should precede the other, as it is more essential, inclusive, and primary in nature. However, at first, it prioritized "Joy" <term>Chiduta</term> because it is more well-known and significant, as it is the cause of "Will"; therefore, they were juxtaposed.

**The Rule** that emerges from this is that **Unity** is constant and inclusive; there is never any separation within it, neither in terms of the Divine Attributes nor in terms of our perception. **Joy** never ceases in terms of the Divine Attributes, but it may cease in terms of our perception. However, **Will** is subject to conditions even in terms of the Divine Attributes. For in times of peace, they are "never separated" <note>a Zoharic phrase describing the union of Wisdom and Understanding</note>, and then there is Joy in all worlds, even in the worlds of "separation" <term>the lower created worlds</term> where the Angels of Peace and the Angels of Charity reside. When "Righteousness and Peace have kissed" <note>Psalm 85:11</note>, they too are unified as male and female, as explained in the *Tikunim* <term>Tikunei HaZohar</term> in many places. But in the time of Exile, the Holy One, blessed be He, swore that He would not enter the **Jerusalem of Above** <note>the spiritual archetype of the city</note> until He enters the Jerusalem of below, as mentioned previously according to the first interpretation. Both views are true and do not contradict. Despite this, it is written: "At all times the Friend loves" <note>Proverbs 17:17</note>; even though they are not in a state of union <term>Zivvug</term>, the Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> does not depart from the Sanctuary, for "her impurity is not in her skirts" <note>a reference to Lamentations 1:9, implying the lower Shekhinah remains pure even in exile</note>. Therefore, it is correct to say they are "friends" <term>Re'im</term> and are never separated, even at a time when there is no union, for there is no quarrel or strife between them, Heaven forbid; rather, both of them willingly suffer for the sake of the lower beings.

**And in the Tikunim**, it is explained that in the union of **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term> and **Understanding** <term>Binah</term>, there are three aspects. The sharpening of their essence is in the Name **Y-A-A** <note>Yod-Aleph-Aleph</note>, or **H-H-V-Y** <note>He-He-Vav-Yod</note>. Their existence is in **Crown** <term>Keter</term> in the mystery of **Knowledge** <term>Da’at</term> which is concealed there. This indicates that "I Shall Be" <term>Ehyeh</term> shall be a palace for the Four-Letter Name <term>Y-H-V-H</term> which spreads out first into Wisdom, with its palace in Understanding. They are unified at the time of union when they blend together. They spread a second time into **Greatness** <term>Chesed</term> and **Power** <term>Gevurah</term> and are unified in **Adornment** <term>Tiferet</term>. A third time into **Victory** <term>Netzach</term> and **Splendor** <term>Hod</term>, unifying in **Foundation** <term>Yesod</term>, and from there in a union with **Kingship** <term>Malchut</term>. She is the "City of Four" <note>Hebron/Kiryat Arba</note> where the names "H-V-H A-H-Y-H" and "Y-H-V-H A-D-N-Y" reside. Their numerical value <term>Gematria</term> equals **Lebanon** <note>132</note>, and likewise "Good Lesson" <term>Lekach Tov</term>. Their initials are: "The Lord our God, the Lord is One" <note>Y-H-V-H E-lohenu Y-H-V-H E-chad</note>. Their sign is **Y-A-A**, which is a holy name, its letters representing Wisdom, Understanding, Adornment, and Kingship in the order of the words. This is the secret of "Beautiful of Appearance" <note>Genesis 29:17</note> which is written concerning Rachel. Onkelos translates **Y-A-A** as "fair to look upon," and its numerical equivalent is **T-R-H-D**, which is the Four-Letter Name in the *Atbash* alphabet <term>a cipher where A=Z, B=Y</term> in the mystery of "In this way shall he bless Israel." Furthermore, your name is mentioned as interpreted in the Zohar, portion *Shemot*. Behold, the existence of "H-V-H and A-H-Y-H" is "Direct Light" from Wisdom downwards, while "Y-H-V-H A-D-N-Y" is "Returning Light" from Kingship upwards in three aspects. For it unifies in Foundation with the name "His Lordship" <term>Adnutiah</term>, and "Great is the Iniquity" <note>Genesis 4:13</note>, "Amen" is greater than the one who blesses. It spreads as Y-H-V-H in Victory and A-D-N-Y in Splendor. In its unification in Adornment, it spreads into Greatness and Power. In its unification in Knowledge, it returns and spreads into Wisdom and Understanding. But the "Nicknames" <term>the lower aspects of the Names</term> are not revealed in Crown; rather, they are hidden in their roots.

<column-break/>

...He will enter the Jerusalem of Above before He enters the Jerusalem of below. Therefore, it must be so: the first ten is the first Kingship, and the eighth is the Daughter with Wisdom, and the five surrounds the Brain with the Iron <gloss>for the sake of every burnt offering</gloss> that rises and falls. Wisdom rises to Wisdom, and Kingship descends to Adornment, and from her flows the abundance in the order of the Name. This is the secret of **"Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife"** <note>Genesis 2:24</note>. <gloss>That is, Adornment, which connects from the first Kingship and unifies with the "Final He," which is Kingship</gloss>. They connect through the intention of Adornment and Kingship to be a permanent union. This is the secret of the "offering that rises and falls"—an offering to the Lord, which is the Foundation, the Tablets. So too, "Offering" <term>Korban</term> in numerical value is the same as the secret of the portion of *Vayikra*.

### Chapter 14: And If

This is spread through the names mentioned in the portion of *Vayikra* <note>Leviticus</note> on the verse "Eat, friends" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>. This implies that the "Beloveds" <term>Dodim</term> are Adornment and Kingship, and their sign is "at certain times," as they are friends. But Understanding and Wisdom are "Friends" <term>Re’im</term> <gloss>and this reaches the third Foundation</gloss> who never separate. Even when the absolute union is called between the Higher Father and Mother <term>Wisdom and Understanding</term> and the Son and Daughter <term>Adornment and Kingship</term>, the union of Adornment and Kingship is only "for a matter." For Adornment and Kingship do not unify constantly all day, like during the *Amidah* prayer <note>the standing prayer</note> or similar times. They do not remain aroused all day because Kingship must return to their foundations for the sake of the lower beings. Therefore, they are called "Beloveds" who connect occasionally for union. But it is written that it shall be "always, forever" as long as the Temple is built. Therefore, they <term>Wisdom and Understanding</term> are called "Friends," for they are always clinging and near to one another. Regarding this, the Zohar on portion *Lech Lecha* says: We have learned that all blessings... it is written: "And a river goes out from Eden" to water the garden. It does not mean "watering" literally, but that they are blessed and rested <gloss>meaning that when Wisdom gives to Understanding, it is like wine that brings joy</gloss>. The reason is that Wisdom and Understanding are occasionally in union with Adornment and Kingship, and the spirit connects <gloss>this is the union of Adornment and Kingship</gloss> becoming a female counterpart as is fitting for them <gloss>but this is not the case for the union of Wisdom and Understanding</gloss>. They are never separated in times of peace. From them, the connection begins; that is to say, a sublime body is unified in another "house" from the union, moving the eyes, and abundance and will shall flow upon them according to the purpose. "Smoke shall rise" <note>the smoke of the sacrifice</note> and "love shall descend," and it will distribute abundance to the great and the small. But the time of the sacrifice is sweet and orderly, just as it is between Wisdom and Understanding, as it will be in the proper order... **And** why did the verse attribute "Friends" to Understanding above and "Beloveds" below? It should seemingly be the opposite, since Understanding is more refined than "eating." The reason is in this style: Now, there is no way for Understanding to be filled according to her desire. The meaning is that the Sefirot which are above in refinement are the branches that were hidden within them, which are their foundation. It is similar when the Sefirot spread and are revealed below, which is the "revealed eating," translating their actions into refinement. For the Sefirot in their refinement also include the Sefirot after their revelation. Many are unified in the "branches" by the "rising of the leaves" to the place of the "Seraphim" <term>fiery angels/higher roots</term>. In this, these upper powers receive great benefit in abundance and blessing through the matter—meaning that she enters the lower ones for the need of "Power" <term>Gevurah</term>. As it was said in *Pelach HaRimmon* <term>Pomegranate Slice</term>, one can explain this with these three languages: their "Will" for the later ones, see there. <gloss>Meaning the first connection, where the Foundation of the Shekhinah prepares her food...</gloss>

<summary>This page discusses the constant vs. intermittent unions of the Sefirot, distinguishing between "Friends" (Wisdom and Understanding, who are always unified) and "Beloveds" (Adornment and Kingship, who unify based on human prayer and sacrifice). It explains the mechanics of Divine Names like Y-H-V-H and Ehyeh as they manifest through the levels of the spiritual hierarchy.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical dynamics of the Sefirot (Divine Emanations) and the permutations of the Tetragrammaton (the four-letter Name of God). The previous page established that "Unity" and "Joy" are constant in the higher realms but perceived differently in the lower worlds. This page applies those concepts to the liturgy of the Day of Atonement and the mystery of the Divine Union.</meta>

-># Pomegranate Slice / Gate 8: Essence and Conduct / Juice of Pomegranates<-
<meta>catchword: P'</meta>

<margin>6:19</margin>
This is the core of the **Day of Atonement** <term>Yom Kippur</term> service, as demonstrated in the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar</note> (on Leviticus, Chapter 8). Sometimes the Sages must labor in **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term> to become wise in the Torah, and sometimes Wisdom suffices even through a "path of loss" <note>original: "derekh hefsed"</note>. The spiritual weight of the Torah rests upon the Sefirah of **Beauty** <term>Tiferet</term>, while the Sefirah of **Foundation** <term>Yesod</term> rests upon **Kingship** <term>Malchut</term>, which is known as the "Lower Wisdom." This is also discussed by the Ramaz <note>Rabbi Moshe Zakuto, a 17th-century Kabbalist</note> (74:6). This **Foundation** is the basis for the eighteen Sefirot of the structural framework. It is revealed through the letter **Vav** <note>The third letter of the Divine Name, representing the male principle</note>. Sometimes the world requires the "Boundary of Judgment" <term>Gevurat Din</term> to strike out, and sometimes it requires the "Boundary of Kindness" <term>Gevurat Chesed</term>. According to the specific need, this flow of Divine energy increases within the first Sefirah upon which the world depends (more than the hidden intellects). However, there is no lack or division within the "higher three" <term>Gimel Rishonot: Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding</term>; they always stand in an abundance of kindness, flow, and blessing. Likewise, there is no division in their flow, except for what occurs in the letter **Vav**... and regarding the secret of this **Union** <term>Yichud</term> which stands in the "higher three" and is also found in the "lower seven," the lower ones are rooted in the higher ones. For all the Sefirot are founded upon the letter **Vav**, which acts as the foundation for the entire process of emanation. In this flow, the higher ones are primary, while the lower things are secondary and lack substance. This is the conclusion of the matter.

For there are four Sefirot: **Wisdom, Understanding, Beauty, and Kingship**. In certain matters, there is a kind of "coupling" between a man and his wife, but no human can truly grasp this without understanding the "Second Foundation," which is the secret of the **Union** <term>Yichud</term>—a literal coupling that joins the higher and lower realms. Through this Foundation, the holy Sefirot and all spiritual entities are aligned. However, this "Second Foundation" can be disconnected by sins. The success of the "coupling" depends on the union between the **Son** <term>Tiferet</term> and the **Daughter** <term>Malchut</term>. As long as there is no peace between the Son and Daughter, there can be no union Above. The absence of this union is like a "destruction," where the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah</term> is in exile. If her unions are only through a messenger, she is like a woman in a house by herself, sufficing for small matters but unable to provide for great ones. Regarding this, the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei HaZohar</note> say that during the time of exile, the "Higher Woman" <term>Binah/Understanding</term> is divorced along with the "Lower Woman" <term>Malchut/Kingship</term>, as it says, "a man who sends away his wife..." <note>original Hebrew quoting Isaiah 50:1 with a Kabbalistic expansion including the Shekhinah</note>. This absence of union is called **Exile** <term>Galut</term>. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explains that a "Burnt Offering" <term>Olah</term> is related to the word "Rising" <term>Oleh</term>, meaning a spiritual ascent. The letter **Vav** descends first to the "Lower Mother" <note>the Shekhinah</note>, and afterward the letter **Yod** rises to the letter **Heh** to draw down the hidden vitality... <note>original: "le-hamshikh de-ichi ityanut"</note>. The **Vav** with the "Higher Heh" <term>Binah</term> is the "Higher Jerusalem," until the **Zayin** <note>representing the seventh Sefirah</note> enters the "Lower Heh," which is the "Lower Jerusalem." (Regarding all this, Rabbi Shimon asked his father who was engaged with the verse "I sleep but my heart is awake..." <note>Song of Songs 5:2</note>. He explained that even in sleep, there is a rhythmic "beating" <note>original: "pifiku"</note> of the heart, which is the secret of the spiritual coupling for the Burnt Offering. The **Higher Heh** rises to the **Yod-Vav**, and the **Lower Heh** rises to the **Vav-Heh**. This is the secret of the Name **Y-H-V-H** <term>The Tetragrammaton</term> where the Father goes with the Mother and the Groom with the Bride). The meaning of the "Burnt Offering" <term>Olah</term> is the "ascent" of Wisdom to Wisdom and the "descent" of Kingship to Beauty, so that a "Complete Foundation" is formed. Sometimes the nine Sefirot of Mercy go with Wisdom, and the Bride goes with Man, as in the verse "The Lord by Wisdom founded the earth" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>. The order of the letters of the Name **Y-H-V-H** is thus: the first **Heh** is Kingship and the second **Heh** is Understanding, in order to draw down...

->Creation<-

<column-break/>

...ascending and descending, yet it is not a complete proximity. But when the letters are brought close, their order becomes "An Offering to the Lord" <note>original: "Korban l'Adonai"</note>. That which was previously ordered **Y-H-H-V** is restored to **Y-H-V-H**. The "Higher Heh" <term>Understanding</term> joins with the **Yod** <term>Wisdom</term>, and the "Lower Heh" <term>Kingship</term> joins with the **Vav** <term>Beauty</term>. Then "the bones come together, bone to its bone" <note>Ezekiel 37:7</note>, in the secret of "bone of my bones" (**Y-H-H**) and "flesh of my flesh" (**V-H**). Therefore, "a man shall leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife" <note>Genesis 2:24</note>. For this reason, when the "Higher Heh" rises to the **Yod**, it is called "This is the law of the Burnt Offering; it is the offering that rises" <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. And when it descends to the "Son," it is said, "the fire of the altar shall burn in it" <note>ibid.</note> with the flames of love. Even though there is "ascending and descending" here, it is only in the secret of "the Sin Offering precedes the Burnt Offering." It is written, "And he descended from performing the Sin Offering" <note>Leviticus 9:22</note>, meaning that because it is a restoration for the "Lower Heh," the **Vav** first descends to its own **Heh**, and afterward the **Yod** rises to its own **Heh** in the secret of the "Burnt Offering" as we said. This is also how the Sage <note>likely referring to Moses Cordovero</note> explained the Yom Kippur service regarding the "Goat for the Sin Offering" performed outside and the "Ram of the People" which is a Burnt Offering. At that time, "Behold, the angels of God were ascending"—this refers to the **Yod** and **Heh**—"and descending"—referring to the **Vav** and **Heh**. The Sages established that the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: "I will not return to the Higher Heh until I return to the Lower Heh," which is the secret of the verse, "I will not enter the city" <note>Hosea 11:9; interpreted as "I will not enter the Upper Jerusalem until I enter the Lower Jerusalem"</note>. This is compared to a plant, where the Holy One mentioned here is described through the attribute of **Wisdom**.

### Chapter 11: And it is Possible
To explain the teaching regarding the Sefirah of **Beauty** <term>Tiferet</term> according to what appears in the *Faithful Shepherd* <term>Ra'aya Meheimna, a section of the Zohar</term>: "Like a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his place" <note>Proverbs 27:8</note>. He moves from his place, which is the "World to Come" (**Understanding**), and wanders after Her <term>the Shekhinah</term> in "this world," guarding her. He swears that he will not return to his place until he returns Her to her place. The Rashba Ha-Levi <note>a commentator</note> questioned this, noting that this implies **Beauty** <term>Tiferet</term> suffers of its own will and separates from the pleasure of the flow coming from the World to Come. However, in the portion of *Acharei Mot*, it implies that the "Higher Mother" <term>Binah</term> withholds the crowns and the "flow of the rivers" from him by force. He answered that indeed, the Higher Mother withholds the "crowns," which are the *extra* flow used to make him king over the lower realms, and the "flow of the rivers" used to sustain them—similar to the phrase "Go, descend, for did I give you greatness for any reason other than for Israel?" <note>Exodus 32:7; Talmudic interpretation</note>. However, regarding the flow allotted to him for himself, which is renewed every day and never ceases, he "sanctifies himself with that which is permitted to him." **Kingship** <term>Malchut</term> is the same; the flow appropriate for her never ceases, but by her own will "her soul is shortened" <note>she restricts herself</note> by the labor of Israel. **However**, even when the Temple stood, **Beauty** and **Kingship** would not "couple" to birth souls except at special times, such as the day the Torah was given or at the end of the *Amidah* prayer. But at all other times, they would "delight in love" in the synagogues and study halls like lovers who unite in one house. This is not like **Wisdom** and **Understanding**, whose union is constant in the world, as stated in the Zohar (Portion *Vayikra*) on the verse "Eat, friends; drink and be drunk, lovers" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>. The "lovers" above are found in will, in unity, and in joy, never separating forever. Here, he chose **Wisdom** and **Understanding** for the "First Union," which he called **Unity**, and the second he called **Joy**, for like rejoices in like. Regarding the "Fifty Gates," he used the term "Wills," meaning they never separate forever.

It distinguishes between the constant, effortless union of Wisdom and Understanding versus the intermittent, effort-based union of Beauty and Kingship during the exile.</summary>
