<meta>This page continues the exploration of the "Deciding Factors" (the Middle Column of the Sefirot) and how they mediate between the polarized forces of Kindness (Chesed) and Severity (Gevurah). It specifically uses the archetype of the legal disputes between the Schools of Hillel and Shammai to illustrate how divine harmony incorporates opposing views.</meta>

# Pomegranate Nectar: Gate 9 – The Deciding Factors
## Pomegranate Slice

The essence of the **decision** <note>Hebrew: *Hakhra'ah*, referring to the mediation or "tie-breaking" role of the Middle Column in the Sefirotic tree.</note> is that it exists and is drawn out between two opposites until it establishes peace between them. Since a deciding mind cannot rule until its power extends over both extremes, and since the "Line of Mercy" <note>Tiferet, the central Sefirah</note> possessed all the strength and was ordered correctly, it was able to mediate. It was necessary to add to the "Deciding Factor" from the side of the Community of Israel <note>Malchut/the Divine Presence</note>, which is Mercy and simple expansion, so that it would possess all the **Kindness**. Therefore, **Tiferet** is called "the staff that leans toward kindness" for the sake of good. This is why [the Sages] returned to the practice of opening a legal case with a point of merit first. If the Sanhedrin <note>The high court of ancient Israel</note> had opened with a point of liability first, they would not have been able to judge the person at all, only to condemn the wicked. Because the dispute between **Kindness** [Chesed] and **Severity** [Gevurah] is intended to fulfill the will of God, they are sustained and established through the "decision"—meaning they are judged by the Middle decision, which is **Tiferet**, also called **Heaven** [Shamayim]. Regarding this, the Sages said: "Any dispute that is for the sake of Heaven will ultimately endure." However, the foundation of the dispute of the "husks" <note>The *Kelipot*, or forces of impurity</note> and the "Other Side" <note>The *Sitra Achra*, the demonic realm</note> is not for the sake of Heaven. Therefore, they do not accept mediation between them; they are destroyed and forsaken forever. This is why their end is destruction. Thus, the Holy One, blessed be He, distinguished between Holiness and the forces of the "husks," and woe to the one who dwells there without mediation, for they are brought down and lowered. To the realm of Understanding [Binah] is gathered kindness and darkness, as it is said: "And the wicked shall be silent in darkness." As it is written: "And God separated the light from the darkness"—the Light is Holiness, and the Judgment is the expansion through mediation. So too was the dispute of Korah and his assembly.

**The matter** of the decision is that it exists and is drawn out as a preparation between two opposites until peace is established between them.

And Shammai was a Prince, a man of kindness and humility, while the other <note>Hillel</note> was the Head of the Court, enlightened with **Severity** and fastidiousness. Yet both of them desired the Middle decision. Therefore, "these forbid and those permit," yet "both these and those are the words of the living God." For the one who declares impure, or disqualifies, or convicts, and the one who declares pure, or validates, or acquits—both are influenced *from the realm of Understanding [Binah], and behold, the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether.* Both sides of the dispute endure within the reasons of the Torah in the World of Unity. However, the School of Hillel merited that the practical law [Halakha] be established according to them; she is the **Divine Presence** [Shekhinah], *Esther who was "greenish" <note>Talmudic description suggesting paleness/humility</note> but a "thread of kindness" was drawn over her* to grant merit to the humble and lowly who are gentle in the law. For this reason, we do not say "the law follows the Messiah," for according to the practical awakening that our King Messiah will perform, so will he discern the judgment of the "decision" for every matter. **But** the dispute of Korah—who was a Levite and challenged the Priesthood—was for the sake of provocation. He and all his assembly clung to the fire of Gehenna [Hell], the hard "husk" of which it is written that it is a "separation" that does not accept mediation. "And the wicked shall be silent in darkness," for had Korah merited, he would have been grasped by the Holy **Severity** that corresponds to Aaron the Priest (a man of **Kindness** who prepared the lamps) and Moses our Teacher (the Line of Mediation). Because they did not desire the decision, they wore a "curse like a garment" <note>Psalm 109:18</note> and separation was declared regarding them.

<column-break/>

...from them. And he took pity, for they were established as "right" and "left"—that is **Kindness**. And from His goodness, he bestows kindness to others and shadows the right side, etc. And He is the **Foundation** [Yesod], called "He is Good," which is drawn from the **Kindness** which is the essence of the "Good" within the building of the world, as it is written: "I said, 'The world shall be built with kindness.'" This is not the case with the "Foundation." Therefore, they returned to "His Goodness" to refer to the **Foundation** [Yesod] which is drawn out, and it is entirely light because he does not distinguish between the essence and the source. And as for why he did not say "In His Kindness" but rather "In His Goodness," it is so he could later explain it by saying "In Grace and in Kindness." For "Good" and "Kindness" are two aspects. It is found that he is "Good," and the language used regarding the lamps <note>Referring to the Tabernacle Menorah</note> is a language of "betterment," which is like being a "dove" <note>A symbol of the Shekhinah</note> containing all six directions. It is revealed in the "deciding" factors to be the one that includes the entire building. In this, his love is shown, as it says "I said, 'The world shall be built with kindness,'" using a term of "grace" <note>Hebrew: *Hen*</note>. This is the Secret of the Eighteen [Benedictions] and the 270 [years/measures] built with kindness. And so they said in the Zohar regarding the portion of *Vayakhel*: therefore, the day of **Kindness** is called the "Day that goes with all days" because it is included in all days. And behold, the "gates" mentioned are called "Good"; she is the writing in which the "Heads" were written, and they returned what they had seen opposite it. And this is in the building, and afterwards they were spread out and became those things. And is the Kindness sufficient on its own for the good and the bad? This is the "Second Quality." Therefore, one needs (before it) "His Goodness" so that it may be clarified and revealed, and afterwards it spreads to the good and the bad. And so it returns to "Surely Goodness and Kindness shall follow me," etc. From the side of **Severity** [Gevurah], the flow is withheld until one becomes perfectly righteous. One must gather strength and fear, and stand in trial as in the matter of "He shall come to judge his people," etc. It is a "refined" and "cleansed" light for the righteous, like the activities of the Sefirot. And it pursues the wicked to destruction. Since the world could not endure if it was only one of these, he combined them with the Quality of **Mercy**, the Middle Line that mediates between the extremes. It is the "Line of Mercy," for from the side of Kindness, their days would all be for merit, and from the side of Severity, their days would be for liability. The Quality of Mercy mediates between them.

**The intention** is that one would be sufficient—namely, "Good" included in all—but it was not built and did not spread below. **Kindness** descends and spreads below to both the righteous and the wicked together. Since he said "In His Goodness," he then said "Who feeds the whole world in His goodness, in kindness." **The intention** is that **Greatness** [Gedulah/Chesed] is called "Good" in an aspect that changes toward Understanding [Binah], as proven in the *Alphabet of Rav Hamnuna* regarding the letter *Tet*, that "Goodness is hidden within it." Its shape is like a *Lamed*, except that this one influences downward while the other brings in the "pipe" of influence in the secret of "How great is Your goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You; You have performed for those who take refuge in You." It is a portion for the World to Come. He said that from the side of the "Hidden Light," the gates of the Palace were sunk into the earth. "From His Goodness" refers to the part of the Good that is revealed through the lower level, which is the **Foundation** [Yesod]. And we seek to be sustained from the Source of Good of which it is said: "I said, 'The world shall be built with kindness.'" **And behold**, Kindness includes the entire building, as it is written: "By day the Lord commands His kindness." They explained this as "the Day that includes all days." And the "World," which is the sum of the circumference, is revealed first in this attribute in the aspect of "Good," from the language of "When he betters [cleans] the lamps," for they also shone from His glory as they went out to the revealed "Rectification" [Tikkun]. Afterwards, it spreads to influence both the good and the bad, and then it is called **Kindness**. Even though it is one level, the titles change as the aspects change.

### Chapter 2: Severity is an attribute that is very precise with the righteous, not to bestow influence

...upon one who has not stood in trial, and to act in trouble so that the nations cannot contain His wrath. The "Deciding Factor" is the Middle Line, which is influenced by the "Supreme Whiteness" and leans toward **Kindness**. "God judges the earth"—they open with merit first, for if they opened with liability, they could not judge at all. And behold, the Light is composed of Water and Fire and is called **Heaven** [Shamayim] in its leaning toward the water. **And we learned:** "Any dispute that is for the sake of Heaven will ultimately endure," like the dispute of Hillel...

# Gate 9: The Deciding Factors – Pomegranate Nectar

The end of the "Line of Mercy" is **Yesod** [Foundation], within the mystery of the "Holy Foundation," which mediates between the two "supports" <note>Netzach and Hod, the legs of the Sefirotic tree</note>.

**With** this, it has been explained that the locations requiring mediation are three:
1. Above in the "Roots," which are the three highest Sefirot.
2. Between "Greatness" [Chesed] and "Power" [Gevurah].
3. Below in the place of the "Branches," between the two supports [Netzach and Hod].

Furthermore, mediation is needed between **Greatness** [Chesed] and **Splendor** [Hod], and between **Power** [Gevurah] and **Victory** [Netzach], because they oppose one another. The mediator between them is **Tiferet**, for it receives from Greatness and bestows upon the "thighs" <note>The lower Sefirot Netzach and Hod</note>. It receives from **Kindness** [Chesed] and bestows upon **Victory** [Netzach]; it receives and bestows upon **Splendor** [Hod]. Sometimes it receives from Kindness and bestows that bounty upon Splendor, or receives from Power and bestows that nature upon Victory. There is no doubt that it does not bestow the bounty of Kindness upon Splendor in the exact manner it was received; rather, it blends it with "eight intermediaries" <note>Complex technical stages of divine transition</note>, adding to the kindness or the restriction. Similarly, it moves from Power to Victory, acting as a mixer and mediator.

The specific detail is great between the "path of outpouring" and the "path of foundation." Even though the bounty enters the vessel, it cannot act within a thick attribute without its action being diminished. Thus, there is mediation between Power and Victory... and the wonder is that this is used in several places regarding the attributes. According to this explanation, we find that the places where there is opposition and a need for mediation are five. Perhaps it was regarding this that the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an ancient foundational Kabbalistic text</note> said: "Ten Sefirot out of nothing... five against five."

->**Gate 10: On the Explanation of Colors**<-

# Chapter 1: The Ancients
I have prepared a gate to understand metaphors and allegories regarding the actions that proceed from the **Emanations** <note>The Sefirot</note>. Each "man" performs his work, and we attribute known colors to them to "settle the ear of the wise" <note>original: *leshaker ozen hamaskil* – a common phrase meaning to use human language to describe the indescribable</note> and to inform us of the lower understandings that are useful for awakening one's intention toward the required attribute. If we wish to unify two attributes, we must awaken the model of the "channel" [tzinnur] which is composed of the colors of both.

In the Torah portion *Mishpatim* <note>A section of the Zohar on the portion of Mishpatim</note>, Rabbi Isaac said: "As an apple tree among the trees of the forest" <note>Song of Songs 2:3</note>—"as an apple tree," and not a literal apple. It is "as an apple" because its colors are distinct, and through these colors, the matter is unified. Based on this mystery, the garments of the priests were all made of fine linen to awaken **Kindness** [Chesed], and the High Priest on Yom Kippur would serve in the inner sanctum in white garments, removing the golden garments, for "a prosecutor cannot become a defender" <note>A legal maxim: gold represents the sin of the Golden Calf (Judgment), while white represents purity (Mercy)</note>. The stones of the Breastplate are also faithful witnesses, corresponding to the twelve tribes of God according to the drawing down of their influence from on high. These things are well known to the masters of **Amulets** [Kameiot], though we have no desire for their [mundane] labor. Even those who offer incense to the "works of heaven" <note>astrologers or idolaters</note> understand themselves in their folly.

# And the Naturalists
They agreed that nature is awakened by what the eyes see, and following that, the spiritual forces are drawn from existence to existence until they reach the place of influence, according to the greatness of the power awakened from below. An example of this is the "crimson thread" that turned white on Yom Kippur; when the Upper Root transformed from Judgment to Mercy, it was immediately reflected in the physical world. The early pious ones used to pour water before them during their prayers on fast days for rain, so they could direct their hearts to the "Water" [Mercy]. Similarly, Samuel at Mizpah commanded: "And they drew water and poured it out before the Lord" <note>1 Samuel 7:6</note>, to draw upon themselves the waters of Kindness from the Upper Pool.

# Chapter 1 (continued)
Know that every attribution of color to anything in the **Highest Roots** [Keter and Binah] and the upper Sefirot is impossible. None of these described things exist there; there is no color, nor is there any physical or intellectual eye that can grasp or look upon them. Rather, the matter of "colors" mentioned regarding the Sefirot is by way of a metaphor for the actions that proceed from the Upper Roots.

For example, when a warrior is angry with an enemy in battle, he is associated with **redness** because he becomes enraged and heated, increasing the flow of blood. Similarly, for a Sefirah that conducts the attribute of **Power** [Gevurah] and strength, its affairs are attributed a red color—all to "settle the ear" with what it is capable of hearing. Furthermore, there is no doubt that spiritual matters are beyond the expression of any intellectual grasp, as was explained in the Gate of Radiance [Nogah]. The Sefirot are associated with colors based on the "result" that proceeds from them.

For this reason, when a person needs to draw down the flow of mercy from **Kindness** [Chesed], he should visualize in his heart the name of the Sefirah in its appropriate color. It is even better if he also clothes himself in the color of the required attribute, just as the High Priest would clothe himself in white garments on Yom Kippur to awaken the attribute of Mercy. For that which awakens the eye and is visualized in the mind will affect the **Vitality** [Nefesh]; the Vitality awakens the **Spirit** [Ruach]; the Spirit awakens the **Soul** [Neshamah]; and the Soul rises from existence to existence until the place of its nourishment and attachment, awakening the powers above. For the awakening that rises from below causes an awakening above.

(Furthermore, regarding this, even though it is also the way of the "Other Side" <note>Evil forces/Satan</note>, the twelve stones [of the Breastplate] correspond to the drawing down of the twelve tribes of Israel in a high place. Thus, one finds those who engrave their forms on amulets, indicating Judgment with **red**, Kindness with **white**, and Mercy with **green/yellow** <note>Hebrew: *Yerok* can mean green or yellow; in Kabbalah, it often refers to the blended color of Tiferet</note>. All of this is according to the true paths that have been established.)

# The Gate

For through this "decision" (mediation), the power of **Kindness** is now drawn toward **Kindness**, and the secret of assistance in **Malchut**. So too the opposite of the action of these in **Severity**, which are heat and dryness. Out of Mercy, it becomes like the **Middle Column** to the "before," and just as **Tiferet** is the mediator between two and two <note>Chesed/Gevurah and Netzach/Hod</note>, so too **Yesod** will be the mediator between them. Everything that was said of Jacob <note>Tiferet</note> applies to Joseph <note>Yesod</note>. So too its extension through the six directions, etc. The matter of its mediation is explained in the early writings at length, and specifically in the Portion of *Vayikra* [Leviticus] regarding the verse: "the Law of the Peace Offering" <note>Leviticus 7:11</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: "The Law of the Peace Offerings" <note>original: *Zevach Shelamim*</note> refers to "Peace" [Shalom] <margin>blended (it is known that she is)</margin> and "Law" (it is known he is) **Malchut**. For after it mediates between **Tiferet** and **Malchut**, she is protected from all the "Damagers" <note>demonic forces</note> so that she is not swallowed by the "External Kingdoms" <note>the *Sitra Achra* or "Other Side"</note>. So too will be the accompanying "receptacles" and the "subtleties of the water."

Since the mediation of **Tiferet** is at the beginning of everything when **Malchut** is silent, so too is the mediation of **Yesod** to clarify between <unclear>the grades</unclear> when **Malchut** is silent. Everything is according to the intention of the Will of the Emanator, so that all the "houses" <note>Sefirot</note> do not lean only to the Right.

->Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 10: The Colors, Essence of Pomegranates<-

A universal reality, lovely to behold, is the color of **Gold**. When it blends with the **Blue** <note>Hebrew: *Techelet*, the biblical blue/cyan</note> of Wisdom, it becomes **Green** like the grass of the earth. This is because it precedes the Act of Creation; therefore, Green precedes all the *Sefirot* <term>Sefirot: the ten creative powers or attributes of God</term>.

## Chapter 3: On the Torah Portion "Terumah"
Gold exists in a hidden way; this is the **Higher Gold** which shines and sparkles more than all seven types of earthly gold. This is the gold that shines and sparkles to the eyes, and it is the "Male" principle that goes out into the world. Whoever clings to it is hidden within it. From there, all types of gold emerge and are drawn down. When is it called "Gold"? When it is in a state of light, rising in the glory of strength with supreme joy to gladden those below. But when it is in a state of **Judgment**, it changes from that color to the colors of **Blue, Black, and Red**; then it is in a state of "Powerful Judgment." However, Gold in joy exists in the ascent of awe and joy, and in the awakening of joy.

And **Silver** below is the secret of the "Right Arm" <note>Symbolizing *Chesed* or Kindness</note>, for the higher side is Gold, as it is written: "You are the head of gold" <note>Daniel 2:38, referring to the joy of the head</note>, while the arms are of Silver below. When Silver is perfected, it is then included within the Gold. The secret of this is: "Apples of gold in settings of silver" <note>Proverbs 25:11</note>. It is found that the silver returns to gold, and then the "Place of Gold" is perfected. They also mentioned **Blue, Black, and Red**, meaning a "Blue" that is a compound, acting as a mediator between the two.

**The Sage, of blessed memory** <note>Likely referring to Rabbi Moses Cordovero</note>, wrote in the name of one of the commentators that there are three types of Gold above in the secret of the "Awesome Face": 
1. **Closed Gold** <note>Hebrew: *Zahav Sagur*</note> which "no eye has seen." 
2. **Beaten Gold** <note>Hebrew: *Zahav Shachut*</note> at the borders of the "Six of the Beard."
3. **Tarshish Gold** <note>Hebrew: *Zahav Tarshish*</note> at the borders of Hermon, where Judgment is included with it. The secret is "Two-Six" <note>A wordplay on *Tarshish*: *Trei-Shesh*</note>, which are six hundred times.

There are four types below in the secret of "Sparkling Fiery Stones":
1. **Yellowish-Green Gold** <note>Hebrew: *Zahav Yerakrak*</note>. 
2. **Ophir Gold**: The place of Judgment that follows Judgment. It seems to me this is in the emanation of **Victory** (*Netzach*). 
3. **Sheba Gold**: A place of Judgment hidden in the secret of the "Female." As it is said, "Sheba fell upon them and took them," which Rabbi Joseph translated as "The guilty Lilith" <note>original: *Lilita Chayavta*, a demonic figure representing harsh judgment</note>. It seems to me this is in **Majesty** (*Hod*).
4. **Sheba Gold** (second type) refers to **Foundation** (*Yesod*) according to his path. 

He stated there were seven types of hair on the head of King David <note>representing the earthly reflection of the Divine King</note>: on his head, his eyelids, his eyebrows, his beard, his throat, his chest, and under his arms. The **Sheba Gold** was in his throat, in the place of the "Croup" <note>Hebrew: *Askara*, a disease of the throat associated mystically with the demonic</note>, for there in the "Great Knee," Lilith rests until she is uprooted from root to branch in the time of Redemption. Before the "Son of David" <note>The Messiah</note> enters the place of the *Askara*, it is written: "May he live and may he be given of the gold of Sheba" <note>Psalm 72:15</note>, based on the secret of Life.

**However**, in the *Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkunei HaZohar*</note>, they said David had seven types of gold in his hair: Yellowish-green, Upaz gold, Ophir gold, Parvaim gold, Closed gold, Tarshish gold, and "Comprehensive Gold" which includes all colors, which is the Gold of Sheba. This is the gold purified seven times. All this was explained in the *Idra De-Vei Mashkana* on the portion of *Yitro*. 

The book of *Adam Kadmon* <term>Adam Kadmon: The Primordial Man, the first stage of divine emanation</term> says the image of the first Messiah is arranged thus: the color of his face is Yellowish-green Gold; the color of his beard is Ophir Gold...

## Chapter 3: Kindness and Severity
The beginning of **Silver** <note>representing Kindness</note> is hidden. All aspects of refined silver (unless the masters of <unclear>Hizolka</unclear> confuse it, as the Rashbi <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> said) represent the King from this aspect. This is the beginning of the "Pardes" <term>Pardes: The mystical orchard of knowledge</term> and the **Kindness** (*Chesed*) between the Whiteness of the Crown (*Keter*) and the Whiteness of Kindness. Sometimes a "pale color" is attributed to it, like the color of Kindness. Perhaps the reason is because the Whiteness is derived from the Higher Kindness, which is the Crown above it.

**Severity** (*Gevurah*) is attributed to the color **Red**. Because it is the possessor of Judgment, it also takes on the color of **Gold**. This is the "Closed Gold" and it relates to the color Red as an aspect of Judgment approaching **Harmony** (*Tiferet*), which receives the deciding vote. It is a clear color, sometimes including Gold (closed, yellowish, and strong). 

<margin>Victory (*Netzach*), and this is</margin>
**Ophir** is the place of Judgment coming after Judgment, and it draws from the secret of **Sheba**, which is the place of hidden Judgment.

<margin>Majesty (*Hod*), and this is</margin>
**Beaten Gold** [Shachut]... as explained in the *Tikkunim*... in the seven places of the hair... see the Zohar, portion of *Yitro*... The color relates to the "Daughter" <note>The *Shekhinah* or Divine Presence</note> in her coverings. **Kindness** is strong and awakens the sweetening of the blow. Immediately, this color relates to **Understanding** (*Binah*) and is attributed to the color **Blue** <note>Hebrew: *Techelet*, which also sounds like *Kilyon*, "destruction"</note>. In the aspect of the Judge who rules with holy power, the Kingdom (*Malchut*) will be a glowing coal. In joy, it will be a "light fire," but it is attributed to the color **Black** in the aspect of the "Harsh Judgment" that extends from it to the "External Forces" <note>The *Kelipot* or husks of evil</note>. (This is the "Fire of Purgatory" [Gehenna]... it did not want the mediation, therefore it was drawn down to the depths).

The **color** of **Harmony** (*Tiferet*) is attributed to the color of a **Leek-Green** <note>Hebrew: *Morika*</note>, because it includes both White and Red, since it includes both Judgment and Mercy. It is mentioned that it decides between them. Some attribute the color of **Sapphire** to it, for its internal essence is like the "Sapphire of the Firmament" existing above in the secret of the Crown. The most significant attribution is the color of the **Pomegranate**, which includes all colors because it includes all the "Six Extremities" <note>The six emotional Sefirot</note>. Therefore, it is called "Thick Beauty" and is "clothed in colors." The meaning of "Pomegranates" is as the Sages explained regarding the Chariot: Michael, Gabriel, and the six legs of the Chariot, which are the seven colors... Michael is Kindness, Gabriel is Strength... Ariel...

<meta>This page continues the technical exploration of the spiritual colors assigned to the Sefirot, focusing here on the highest triad: Keter (Crown), Chokhmah (Wisdom), and Binah (Understanding). It draws heavily from the Zohar’s *Idra* (Assembly) sections and the *Tikunei Zohar*.</meta>

# Chapter 2: The Crown (Keter)
One should distinguish three aspects of the Crown as explained in the *Idra* <note>The *Idra Rabba* and *Idra Zuta* are central sections of the Zohar describing the "Divine Face"</note>:
1. The "Morning of Darkness" which is hidden even from the other emanated beings <term>Emanations: the Sefirot, or divine attributes, that flow from God</term> within their own crowns. They have no grasp of it because of its equality with the Emanator, the Holy One, Blessed be He.
2. The aspect of its own being, described as **Dew**, which possesses no color at all.
3. Its aspect in relation to the other Sefirot. This is called the "peeling of the white" <note>Referencing Jacob’s sticks in Genesis 30:37</note> in the secret of the revelation of intense whiteness. This occurs when the drops of **Dew** intensify within the "Awesome Crystal" <note>The *Ke'en HaKerach*, a mystical firmament</note>. Its "garments" and the "hair of its head"—which are the hidden rectifications within it—are described as "white as snow" and "pure as wool" <note>Quoting Daniel 7:9</note>.
In the *Tikunim* <note>The *Tikunei Zohar*, a commentary on the first word of the Torah</note>, they attribute three types of darkness to it: The first is absolute absence and darkness, for "He is Black" before the Cause of Causes. The second is the aspect of its essence hidden from the other Sefirot emanated after it. The third is the aspect of the "hollows" within it, as we mentioned in the eighth gate.

## Wisdom (Chokhmah)
The color of **Sapphire** is attributed to it, and this is appropriate because it is the opening of all colors—from no-color to color. From it, all colors spread according to its revelation, clarity, and expansion. Some add the color of **Blue** <note>Hebrew: *Techelet*, the biblical sky-blue/cyan</note> to it, and this is also correct, for it is the "purpose" <note>The word *Techelet* shares a root with *Takhlit*, meaning "purpose" or "end"</note> of all colors; they extend from it and return to it, as it is the source of all actions through its influence on Understanding (*Binah*). Just as the first opening of darkness is toward the color blue, so too the first spark of the Crown is toward Wisdom.
There are those who attribute to it the "Nut" <note>referring to *Ginnat Egoz*, the "Nut Garden" of the Song of Songs</note>, whose outer shell resembles a blend of **Green** and **Blue**. This corresponds to the Kingdom (*Malkhut*), which is called the "Nut Garden," whose "feet go down to death" <note>Proverbs 5:5</note>, referring to the "shells of the nut" <term>Klipot: the "shells" or "husks" of spiritual impurity</term>. These are the "Kings who reigned in the land of Edom," which means they arose in Thought in the secret of Judgment. This is the meaning of "You were in Eden, the garden of God" <note>Ezekiel 28:13</note>.
We also say it is called this because of the seven colors of the eye:
1. **Red**, which surrounds the eye.
2. **White**, which is adjacent to it.
3. A **Green-like** color, seen and yet not seen.
4. **Leek-green** (*Kartiy*), which corresponds to those who transgress commandments punishable by spiritual excision (*Karet*).
5. **Blue** (*Techelet*), which gives light to the first four colors, located in the pupil of the eye.
6. A **Water-like** color between Green and Leek-green; from here comes the influence between the Wise and the masters of the commandments.
7. The **Holy of Holies**, which illuminates them all and is drawn from the Crown (*Keter*).
It is said that "all sevenths are holy," and from here all "Wisdoms" are named. The Crown surrounds this attribute with the color **White**. Correspondingly, the High Priest would wear white garments on Yom Kippur <note>The Day of Atonement</note>. The order of the Sefirot here seems to be Majesty, Victory, Foundation, Dread, Kindness, Beauty, and Understanding. This is the secret of Wisdom, for Beauty (*Tiferet*) in colors is the Higher *Yod* and Lower *Yod* <note>The letter Yod (י) represents a point of wisdom</note>. Even though the "Open Eye" is white without color in the Crown, while eyes with colors appear in Strength (*Gevurah*) as explained in the *Idra*, this inquiry may still apply to Wisdom through the **32 Paths** that extend downward, changing their actions between Judgment and Mercy.

## Understanding (Binah)
This is the **Green Line** that surrounds the world, as will be explained in Chapter 5. It is a green light like a **Leek** (*Kartiy*). Its essence is the power of "Water," and "Judgments are awakened" from it. The color **Saffron** (*Murka*) is attributed to it, which is a blend of **White** and **Red**. Similarly, the three lines that extend from it—White, Red, and Saffron—necessitate its existence.

<column-break/>

## The Crown (Keter)
<margin>As written in *Pa'aneach Raza* <note>A 13th-century Kabbalistic commentary</note> and the *Mahal*</margin> It is attributed three colors [based on] the three aspects within it:
1. The aspect of **White** within it, which shines to it from the Crown above it. This relates to the color of an **Apple Slice**, as it is written: "Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest" <note>Song of Songs 2:3</note>.
2. The ultimate aspect of its own being. It is revealed and yet not revealed until it is examined. It is like the "medicine of life," as the Ramban <note>Nachmanides, 13th-century scholar</note> of blessed memory said: being pure and internal, it is revealed, yet no color can truly encompass it.
3. The aspect of its influence on the Sefirot. In relation to the internal reality of others, it is attributed the color **White**, like the **Dew** that condenses below. It is delayed and "clothed" against the "vapor" <note>Hebrew: *Kitor*</note>. Its garment and hair are like the Crown; from this, worlds are produced like "peeled poplar" <note>Genesis 30:37</note>, as stated in the *Ilana* <note>The "Tree," a common Kabbalistic diagram/text</note>.

## More on the Crown
In the *Mashan* <note>likely a reference to a specific manuscript or teacher</note>, he mentions three aspects:
1. The aspect of its whiteness being strong relative to the internal face. (He calls it "Substantial" to relate its lack of color relative to the Higher Light, which is the First Inclusion, and calls it "Darkness" in comparison). (And see R. Shimon bar Yochai in the *Tikunim* regarding the "Cause of Causes"... so it may be prior to the Cause of Causes).
2. The aspect of it being hidden from everything below it.
3. The aspect of it containing all the "Ends" <note>The six directions/Sefirot</note>. It is attributed a color like **Gold**. This aspect relates to the lower part of the Crown, through which the Sefirot are "sold" or transferred (and it receives from the higher aspects within it, therefore it was all "female").

## And Wisdom (Chokhmah)
Some attribute to it the color **Red**, for the judgment that encompasses the Master of Judgment <note>Ba'al Din</note>. In this gate and in the *Kanah* <note>The *Sefer HaKanah*, a classic Kabbalistic work</note>, it is assigned the color of **Sapphire**, which is the color that receives all colors. This is to say that from it come all colors, powers, and actions. Some attribute the color **Blue** (*Techelet*) to it, meaning "completion" (*Kelyah*) or the "end" (*Ketz*) for every soul; it is the purpose of the work of Creation. The reason they attribute Sapphire and Blue to it is that the color of "Blackness" precedes the opening of the color Blue. Through this reason, the hiddenness of the Sefirot spreads—namely, the Crown. (And there is a Blue that lacks Judgment except in Wisdom, and it will be explained).

## And Understanding (Binah)
Some attribute to it the color **Red leaning toward White**, for the judgment that encompasses the Master of Judgment. In the *Kanah*, it is described with various colors. When it descends, "blood" is found, or a color close to the sign of **Green like a Leek**. The reason is that the color green precedes all fruits, just as this Sefirah was the first to "begin" the act of Creation (as in "And God said, 'Let there be...'"—which originates in Understanding). However, this is not sufficient, for it is not fitting for the "Spread of the Plane" to be for Mercy. Others say that because "Judgments are awakened from it," its color should be like **Saffron** (or like **Yellow**). In the end, it blends with the Blue, which is its opposite, refining the leek-green. (And this is the color of the "Grass of the Field," the nature of the Prophets).

## More
Others say that because it is the "Mother" and the secret of Strength (*Gevurah*), Saffron—which is Beauty (*Tiferet*)—descends from her. She would then lean toward a blend of their natures (forming **Leek-green**). Finally, it is refined by the Blue of Wisdom into Leek-green. (Therefore, Understanding is attributed the color of **Green like grass**, because it is the acquisition of Wisdom, Kindness, Strength, and Beauty together).

Behold, the light that will be drawn into the glass lantern is the *Yod* of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) which is the first *Yod* of the Name of 72. It will be found that the colors of the *Gevurot* are composed of the colors of the recipient and the colors of the influencer. It is more reddish than the green of Beauty (*Tiferet*), since it leans toward the Left. Some say it is the **Sapphire** color influenced by *Tiferet*. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said it is "a tree pleasant to the sight" <note>Genesis 2:9</note>, for all beautiful colors are seen in it. The sign for this is: "And Joseph was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance" <note>Genesis 39:6</note>. At the time of her diminishment, she says of herself: "Do not look at me because I am swarthy" <note>Song of Songs 1:6</note> due to the absence of her light. She has a second aspect, a garment for the first, in the secret of "Fine linen and purple is her clothing" <note>Proverbs 31:22</note>, which includes the colors of all six extremities in Mercy, for she clothes herself in them in the secret of the "Purple" (*Argaman*) mentioned previously. She has a third aspect in her proximity to the "depths of the sea," which is the color **Blue** <term>Blue: *Techelet*, the ritual dye used for Tzitzit, often associated with the sea and the sky</term> to hide from them. She also has a **Green** color that is the mean between the whiteness of *Tiferet* and the blue of *Gevurah*; this occurs at the rising of the morning star, which is between *Gevurah* and *Tiferet*.

One must know that the essence of all these colors explained in this Gate refers to the attributes included within Kingship (*Malchut*), for the primary focus of their actions is within her. Truly, the Name **YHVH** <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> has no color at all in its essence; colors only exist in the Name **ADNY**. The twelve stones of the Breastplate <note>The *Choshen* worn by the High Priest</note> are hinted at in the twelve letters of its "filling" <term>Filling: *Milui* - a method of expanding a Hebrew name by spelling out each letter's name</term>. However, the light from above that shows the color of the "glass lantern" which is below—the light is the Name of Four Letters (YHVH), and the glass lantern is the **Palace of the Name** (*Hechal HaShem*). Furthermore, one must know that within the Name YHVH itself, there is a difference between the *Yod* and the other letters. The *Yod* signifies the simplicity of the Light itself, while the other letters show the appearance of the colors in *Malchut*. There is also a difference in the Name of the Palace between the letters of **ADNY**, which receive the colors in detail, and the final *Yod*, which includes them all together in the secret of the **Sapphire Stone**.

### The Eleventh Gate: The Resplendencies (Zachzachot)

# Chapter 1: The Writing
->Rav Hai Gaon in a response to Rav Paltui:<-
->The thirteen attributes spoken of in the Torah<-

These are the branches of the outcomes that emerge from the ten levels called *Sefirot*. These correspond to those, along with the three hidden ones, the "Heads of Heads." The outcomes, which are the actions, are called **Attributes** (*Middot*). Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai taught that those which are the "Fathers" are called *Sefirot*. This does not mean they have a literal number or that they themselves are a count or tally; rather, it is until the secret of the "Ten Worlds" that were renewed from them. These have no number and no way to grasp them, except for He who created them alone, for He is the Master of all. Regarding them it is said: "And worlds without number." The **Ten** Sefirot are divided in their creation into three...

# Chapter 1: The Revealer
<gloss>Regarding the Merciful One in the matter of the Essence. This is the voice of the Gaon, Rav Hai, of blessed memory, to Rav Paltui, and his words are clear.</gloss>

Behold the words of Rav Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, as follows: Let our teacher instruct us, for we have heard of the 13 attributes [of Mercy] being received... and our teacher has written upon it "Peace"... and Abraham our father in his haste... and it is said regarding the multitude and the "how"... and we need to say, because of the holiness, if there is a unity there... then we find 13 attributes but we do not find 13 Sefirot. Then the 13 attributes are a separate matter... to your request, we are required... and to your intention, we are directed. And he is Rav Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, who is very much needed in his response, and it is clarified in the *Pardes HaKadosh* <note>The "Holy Orchard," Moses Cordovero's primary work</note>... and I am the one writing this... the summary... to write...

> The gold used in our building: Its color is **Parvaim gold** <note>original: "zahav parvaim," a reddish gold mentioned in 2 Chronicles 3:6</note> found in the carvings over the eyes. Its color is **pure gold** <note>original: "zahav sagur"</note> in the hair of the head. Its color is **refined gold** <note>original: "zahav mupaz"</note> upon the chest, on the tablet over the heart. Its color is **Tarshish gold** on the two arms. All seven of these colors were engraved on all those places of the hair. From this, we understand that all colors are included in the Head, and they are designated for their specific locations. And in the Midrash Rabbah <note>A collection of ancient homiletic interpretations of the Bible</note> on the portion "On the day Moses finished" (Numbers 7:1), it is taught regarding the gold: The entire House was covered in gold except for the back of the doors. Rabbi Ibu said: This teaching refers to the Second Temple, but in the First Temple, even the backs of the doors were gold. Seven types of gold were there: Good, Pure, Beaten, Shut, Refined, Distilled, and Parvaim. Their distinctions are explained there in the scriptures.

### Chapter 4: Greatness (Chesed)

A white light like the whiteness of silver, which naturally tends toward **techelet** <term>Techelet: a biblical blue or violet dye</term> before the smiths whiten it. In this, it is distinguished from "Absolute White," for the **Crown** (Keter) is called "whitened blue" in the name of the revelation of the Hidden Kindness within Wisdom. Sometimes it is associated with the color of **milk**, according to the abundance of the Supernal Whiteness flowing upon it. **Might** (Gevurah) is a red color, close to the color of gold, which represents the awakening of **Understanding** (Binah) together with Might in the secret of the "wine that gladdens," approaching the Balance that arouses Love. And in the Zohar's portion of *Terumah*, three colors are added: Red, Black, and Blue.

> Red is its own color from the second day, corresponding to the color of the Head, and this is the name *Elohim* <note>The Divine Name associated with Judgment</note> and the secret of the color of gold, for they are all one color. Blue emerges from the edge of that red color, and as it descends below, the red color moves further away into that place called "The Sea," and it is dyed blue. That red takes the edge of the sea and its appearance weakens, turning to blue. This is also the name *Elohim*, but not as powerful as the first. **Black** <note>original: "okham"</note>—this color emerges from the melting of the red when it weakens and turns downward into the pit of filth, etc.

And this Blue is the secret of "Righteous Judgment" <note>original: "Din Tzedek"</note> which flows through the Holy One to the **Kingship** (Malchut), which is the "Weakened Judgment." In it is the power of the "Blue that consumes all," to finish the transgression and end sin. And the Black is the aspect of the Name *Adonai* when it is "struck" and becomes black, which blackens the faces of creatures—it is the fire of Gehenna, the darkness that was separated from the light, may the Merciful One save us. **Beauty** (Tiferet) is a **green** color like an egg yolk <note>In Kabbalah, "green" (*yarok*) often refers to a yellow-gold or chartreuse color</note>, which includes both the pure white and the red. This is from the composition of Glory and Beauty. Stones whose color is like saffron are effective for peace. It includes the colors of Kindness and Might in one of two ways: either in the upper aspect, close to Wisdom and Understanding—meaning the mixture of gold and silver together in the secret of **Knowledge** (Da'at) which includes them in their root—or in the lower aspect, which is a mixture of red and white. It is not the color of **Sapphire** in its inner aspect, which is called the "Firmament." Our color is also **Purple** (Argaman) in the secret of the four legs of the Chariot which include the six extremities, for such is the beauty of all colors. The angels Uriel and Guriel both appear in the place of the Central Line, for it includes both the Right and the Left.

### Chapter 5: Victory (Netzach)

The color is a red leaning toward white, which is the "Green of Mercy," blended and leaning toward its root which is—

<column-break/>

<margin>Tower of Prophets</margin>
from the side of Kindness... <note>The text here is highly abbreviated/formulaic</note>
<margin>Seven lacking</margin>
From the right... and from the left... **Victory** (Netzach) is associated with the color red leaning toward white—meaning a red that lacks the intensity of the Great Strength of Kindness. **Splendor** (Hod) is associated with the color white leaning toward red—meaning a red that is above, lacking the full power of the "Judgment-bearing" Might. **Foundation** (Yesod) is sometimes associated with the color of **Sapphire** (and it is possible to view it as the Crown), and some associate it with a color including white and red—from the white leaning toward red and the red leaning toward white. This is to say it is a blend that includes the attributes of all. Therefore, its color is like **saffron-green**, and its greenness is more refined than the green of Tiferet... a color that receives all colors, meaning it receives the attributes and mixes with all the flows. Therefore, it is called the "Eye of Joseph" or the "Moon" (And the sign is: "And Joseph was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance").
<margin>A foundation for every color which is the sign...</margin>

### Chapter 4 [sic]: And Kingship (Malchut)

When she operates through the lower forces... according to her illumination to us. She is associated with the color white, like the whiteness of the **Moon** from the side of Kindness. Her essence is associated with the color **Hermon**, because she is composed of all the colors and all seven extremities and Sefirot. (And she is called "Ses" <note>original: 'סס', perhaps a shorthand for lily or marble</note> because she is truly composed of six and sixty colors... and she is called Hermon because she receives thirty colors...). She is also associated with the color **Blue** (Techelet) because she is sometimes clothed in the attribute of "Weakened Judgment" from the side of Might. By this name, all creatures are finished/consumed. In this state, she exists within the Holiness, giving over the "Outer Shells" <term>Shells: "Qlipot," the forces of impurity or evil in Kabbalah</term> known as the "Depths of the Sea." By this aspect of Blue, all the "Damagers" <note>Demonic forces</note> are subdued and broken. (Therefore, seeing this color in a dream is a good sign). This color rules at night in the secret of the Shells (Therefore, it is forbidden to judge capital cases at night). When the deeds of man are improved, she turns to White, and then the time of the morning prayer arrives, when one can distinguish "between Blue and White"—meaning the Kingship turns from the side of Kindness to a "Greenish-Blue" <note>original: "karti," leek-green</note>. This signifies the strength of Judgment. Sometimes she is associated with the color **Black** when she is clothed in the strength of the awakening of the Accuser, becoming a "Harsh Judgment," giving power to the Shadow to execute judgment.

...which is Kindness and Splendor, and to incline it toward the red, as it also draws from the Form and leans toward its root. **Foundation** <note>Yesod: the ninth Sefirah, associated with transmission and the biblical Joseph</note>: its color is green, a mixture of the white in Victory (Netzach) and the red in Splendor (Hod). Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar</note> said it is "a tree pleasant to the sight" <note>Genesis 2:9</note> because all beautiful colors appear in it. **Kingship** <note>Malchut: the tenth and final Sefirah, associated with the physical world and the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> includes every color. However, its essential color is a white derived from the "radiance of the heavens," which is why she is called the "White Moon" <note>original: "Levanah"</note>. In the time of her lack <note>Referring to the moon's waning or the state of Exile</note>, she says of herself: "Do not gaze upon me because I am dark" <note>Song of Songs 1:6</note> due to the absence of her light. She has a second aspect: a garment for the first, following the secret of "fine linen and purple are her clothing" <note>Proverbs 31:22</note>, which includes the colors of all six directions in mercy. She clothes herself in them according to the secret of "purple" <note>original: "argaman"</note> mentioned before. There is a third aspect in her proximity to the "depths of the sea," which is the color **techelet** <term>Techelet: a specific biblical blue or violet dye representing the vastness of the sea and sky</term> to cover herself from them. She also has a green color, the intermediate between the white of Beauty and the blue of Strength (Gevurah), which appears at the rising of the dawn when she is between Strength and Beauty.

**And one must know** that the essence of all these colors explained in this gate belongs to the attributes included within Kingship, for their primary actions are through her. Truly, the divine name Y-H-W <note>the first three letters of the Tetragrammaton</note> has no color at all. Colors only exist in the name A-D-N-Y <note>Adonai: the name of God associated with divine sovereignty and the Sefirah of Malchut</note>. The twelve stones of the Breastplate are hinted at in the twelve letters of the "filling" <note>a method of expanding a name by spelling out its letters</note> of that name. However, the light from above that shows the color of the **glass vessel** <note>original: "ashashit"</note> below—the light is the four-letter Name (Y-H-W-H) and the glass is the "Palace of Abundance." 

Furthermore, one should know that in the name Y-H-W-H itself, there is a difference between the letters H-V-H and the other letters. For H-V-H <note>Heh-Vav-Heh</note> are the appearances of colors in Kingship, and the Y-D <note>Yod-Dalet</note> is the simplicity of the light itself. There is also a difference in the name of the Palace between the letters A-D-N-Y which receive the colors individually, while the final Yod includes them together in the secret of the "sapphire stone."

For Kingship includes all appearances because it is the "lower pupil" that fills all the actions of the lower worlds. 

But as for the "upper pupil"—which is within Wisdom—there is no color in it at all. Even though all colors are contained within it in their purity, they are not revealed. No color can be found there, but only a single, unique Upper Light within it. (Analogous to a glass vessel made with many colors; as long as there is no light inside it, no color will be seen.) And behold, the light that shines through the vessel is the "Only One" <note>original: "Yechidah"</note> of Wisdom, which is the Y-D <note>the letter Yod</note> of the name. Wisdom is the Yod, and it will not be seen except through the flow that is poured into it. And the source of Wisdom will be found; that is, the light that will be at the head of the colors will be through Wisdom, which is the final Yod of the expanded name. And the colors themselves will be included in the light. 

Know that just as the colors are attributed to the essence of the Sefirot, so too the colors are attributed to the "garments." Each color is attributed to its own aspect according to its matter and according to what we have explained regarding the garments of the ten Sefirot. This means each level is unique to its matter, like a palace for the divine essence. The colors of the garments are woven from the colors of the one who receives and the colors of the one who bestows...

### Gate Eleven: The Radiants

<margin>
Regarding Isaac,
it is said:
</margin>

## Chapter 1: Rav Hai Gaon wrote in a response to Rav Paltoi:
->The thirteen attributes mentioned in the Torah<-

These are branches of offspring emerging from ten levels called *Sefirot*. These correspond to those, along with three hidden ones, the "heads of heads" <note>The super-celestial "Radiants" or Tzachtzachot above the first Sefirah, Keter</note>. The offspring are the actions called "Attributes" (Middot), and the roots, which are the "Fathers," are called *Sefirot*. Not that they possess a number, but they themselves are the account and the tally, only up to the secret of the ten worlds renewed from them. They have no number or way to be grasped except by their Creator alone, who is Lord over all. Concerning them, it is said: "And worlds without number" <note>Job 25:3</note>. **Ten** Sefirot were divided in their creation...

<column-break/>

## Chapter 1: Revealing the first matter regarding the Radiants, which is the tradition of
->Rav Hai, of blessed memory, to Rav Paltoi, and we will clarify these<-

Rav Hai Gaon <note>A 10th-century leader of Babylonian Jewry</note>, may his memory be a blessing, said: May our master teach us, for we have found mentioned in the words of our Sages thirteen attributes. Regarding this, our master, peace be upon him, replied: Abraham our father, in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Creation, an ancient mystical text</note>, mentioned the name of God and the ten Sefirot... and we need to understand from the mouth of the holy ones if there is a "Unique One." We found thirteen attributes, but we have not found thirteen Sefirot, only ten. However, we found these things in the Torah, and for his response, we must be attentive. Rav Hai Gaon elaborated on this matter, and it is clarified in the holy and pure words... and I, the scribe, will be brief in the explanation to write it for you.

The gold that appears in its hues: its color is "Parvaim gold" <note>A legendary reddish gold mentioned in 2 Chronicles 3:6</note> in the incisions upon his eyes; its color is "Closed gold" <note>Gold of high purity</note> in the hair of his head; its color is "Refined gold" <note>original: "Mofaz"</note> upon his chest; on the tablet over his heart, its color is "Tarshish gold" <note>A gold with a sea-colored or gemstone-like hue</note> upon the two arms. All these seven colors were inscribed upon all those places of the hair. Thus it is implied that they are all included in the head, but are designated for their specific locations. And in the Midrash Rabbah <note>A collection of ancient homiletic interpretations</note> on the portion "On the day that Moses finished," regarding the verse "its mid-section was paved with gold," it is taught that the entire Interior <note>referring to the Tabernacle or the Divine Palanquin</note> was of gold, except for the back of the doors. Rabbi Ibu said: This teaching refers to the Second Temple, but in the First Temple, even the back of the doors was made of the seven types of gold. These are: Good, Pure, Beaten, Closed, Refined, Purified, and Parvaim. Their distinctions and scriptural sources are explained there.

## Chapter 4: Greatness <note>Chesed: The Sefirah of expansive love and kindness</note>

White light, like the whiteness of silver that tends toward its natural state. First is the "Sky-Blue" <note>original: "Techelet," the dye used for the fringes (tzitzit)</note> before the smiths whiten it. In this, it is distinguished from absolute whiteness. For behold, they call the Crown <note>Keter: the highest Sefirah</note> "Whitened Sky-Blue" because of the revelation of the Kindness hidden within Wisdom. Sometimes it is compared to the color of milk, because of the great abundance of the supernal whiteness flowing upon it. **Might** <note>Gevurah: The Sefirah of restriction, judgment, and fire</note>: its color is red and close to the color of gold, which represents the awakening of Understanding (Binah) together with Might in the "Secret of the Rejoicing Wine" <note>A kabbalistic metaphor for the sweetening of judgments</note>, which is close to Beauty (Tiferet) and receives its balance while lacking [absolute] Love. In the portion of Terumah <note>A section of the Zohar</note>, three colors are attributed to it: Red, Black, and Sky-Blue. Red is its essential quality from the second day [of creation], matching the color of the head, and this is the name *Elohim*. There is the color of gold, which is all one color. Sky-Blue emerges from within that red color, and as it descends below, the red color distances itself into that place which is the "Sea" <note>Malchut</note>, and it is dyed the color of Sky-Blue. That red is taken into the sea and its appearance is weakened, and it turns into Sky-Blue; this too is the name *Elohim*, but it is not as strong as the first. Black emerges when the red color is exhausted and turns downward into the dregs of the refuse, etc. Thus far [from the Zohar]. This Sky-Blue is the secret of the "Judgment of Righteousness" that is channeled through holiness to Kingship (Malchut), which is the softened Attribute of Judgment. In it, it is like a lamp composed of Sky-Blue, to consume the husks <note>original: "kelipot," the forces of impurity</note> and to finish off sins. The black is the aspect of the red that was struck and became black, which "blackens the faces of creatures"; it is the fire of Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note> and darkness that was separated from the light—may the Merciful One save us. **Beauty** <note>Tiferet: The central Sefirah, balancing Kindness and Might</note>: a green color <note>original: "yarok," which in this context often means yellow-green or golden</note> like an egg yolk, which includes pure white and red; from their combination, glory and beauty emerge. Stones whose color is like saffron are conducive to peace. It includes the colors of Kindness and Might in one of two ways: either its upper aspect is close to Wisdom and Understanding, which is the mixture of gold and silver together in the "Secret of Knowledge" (Da'at) that includes it in its root; or its aspect below, which is the mixture of red and white. It is not the sapphire color in its inner aspect called "Firmament," for its colors are also purple <note>original: "argaman"</note> in the secret of the four legs of the Chariot which include the six extremities, for such is the beauty of all colors. Uriel and Guriel <note>Archangels</note> both came to the place of the Middle Line because it includes the Right and the Left.

## Chapter 5: Victory <note>Netzach</note>

Its color is red leaning toward white, for it draws from blended mercies and leans toward its root, which is

<column-break/>

from the side of Kindness, as mentioned above. Therefore, from the side of Might, it includes the measure of red... <note>The text here contains technical kabbalistic abbreviations and angelic names like Raphel, Hasdiel, and Zechariel</note>. **Victory** (Netzach) is attributed to a red color that tends toward white, meaning its red is whiter than any other red, because it draws from Greatness (Chesed). **Splendor** <note>Hod: the eighth Sefirah</note> is attributed to a white color that tends toward red, meaning its white is redder than any other white, because it draws from Might (Gevurah), being the cause of Judgment. **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>: Some define it as the color of sapphire (and for some, it is like Beauty). Others define it as a color including white and red; from the white that tends toward red, and from the red that tends toward white—meaning a blended and inclusive sun, combining the attributes of Victory and Splendor. Therefore, its color is like a leek-green, and its greenness is more divided than the greenness of Beauty. Some assign it a color that receives all colors, to say that it receives all attributes and mixes their flow. Therefore, it is called the "Eye of Joseph" <note>A reference to the biblical Joseph, who represents Yesod</note>... it adds to all the colors of the Sefirot.

## Chapter 4: Kingship <note>Malchut: the final Sefirah, representing the physical world and the Divine Presence on earth</note>

Based on the deed of Rabbi Hila... Three colors are attributed to Kingship according to three aspects: First, it is attributed to a white color, like the moon that receives from the side of Kindness. This is the color of the "Crown of the Bride." Second, it is attributed to a purple color <note>original: "argaman"</note> because it is composed of all the colors and all seven extremities and seven Sefirot. It is called purple because it includes six colors, which are the six extremities it receives from; it is called *Argaman* <note>The Hebrew word is an acronym for the angels Uriel, Raphael, Gabriel, Michael, and Nuriel</note>. It clothes itself in mercies. Furthermore, through it, the actions of the six Sefirot are enacted. Third, it is attributed to the color of Sky-Blue <note>Techelet</note> because it clothes itself in the softened Attribute of Judgment from the side of Might. Because of this, it "consumes the creatures." In this aspect, it is among the Sefirot within holiness, like the coal that is attached to the "husks" <note>kelipot</note>... This color will rule at night in the secret of the husks (therefore it is forbidden to judge capital cases at night). When the moon turns to white, it is the appearance of... as they said, "distinguishing between blue and white." Then it will be the watery nature of the blue, which is Kingship from the side of the light of Kindness, or it blends and improves into green, as Rabbi Eliezer says, "between blue and leek-green." This is the blue that is inclusive, indicating the essence of judgment. It is sometimes attributed to a black color when it clothes itself in the awakening of the dregs and the smoke of the "husks," becoming a harsh judgment. It possesses the power to execute judgment (this occurs during the days of the moon's waning when it is far from the mercies of the sources).

That just as the actions of the Sefirot change, so too when the colors are mixed throughout all the upper Sefirot; for the Sefirot do not lack colors...

## Chapter 2: The foundation of faith and the core of Kabbalah in this noble inquiry is that the Emanator, blessed be He, knew all

beings through His own intellection, a unique knowledge in His unity that is not divided by their divisions. The Sefirot are the mold of all beings, perceived by Him in a single gaze that encompasses them in the Crown. There lies the "hiding-place of His power" <note>A reference to Habakkuk 3:4</note> in the heights of the levels accepted in His emanation. There is a "different spirit" <note>A biblical idiom for a distinct nature</note> to them from the Unique Master, who brought up total counts, all of them six levels for His Throne of Glory. These are the three double-aspects necessary for the truth of the existence of any effect <note>The "effect" refers to anything emanated or created</note>. His level cannot be compared to the completion of the deed or the fulfillment of the intent in His emanation: after being crowned with all of them. **First**: His equality with the Cause closest to him, and great is the honor of the Cause of Causes, who has the Living God and Eternal King close without a mediator, being something near Him from twenty <note>The Hebrew letter 'Khaf' stands for 20, perhaps referring to the twenty aspects of the light</note> faces. First, in his concealment near Him as an existence close to non-existence; and second, his revelation there. Regarding both, he then saw that the word "Or" <note>Meaning 'Light' or 'Or'</note> indicates the priority of the Will. **However**, his rising to be "shining faces" is associated with the language of "seeing" by the Master of Will and not to any other at all, which is the plain meaning of the verse. The second aspect relates to his essence from two faces: first, its *Sefirah* <note>here used to mean its counting or specific boundary</note>, which is the emanation of the essence of the "Saphir" <note>Gemstone/Sapphire</note> in its place without its improvements; and second, the Understanding, for the Lord will place His spirit upon him to bring forth his improvements that were hidden in his existence. And the third aspect is in his equality with his own effects <note>the lower levels he produces</note> from two faces: first, when the spirit rests upon him to reveal his improvements within himself, which he called "and he searched it out"; and second, it is "said to man" <note>A reference to Job 28:28</note> that He permitted him to emanate the Wisdom that includes them all in concealment. There is also a general division of these six aspects into only two categories: for the first three are aspects of concealment for the effect, above which there is no height for the lower beings at all, and there in its place it is called a "Sefirah." The last three are aspects of revelation for this effect, which learns by permission of its Cause to be revealed below and to be a cause for others; and here it is called a "Utterance" <note>Ma'amar</note>, as we have already mentioned above. **However**, in the Zohar they only mentioned in this verse four times that the Holy One, blessed be He, looked into the Torah before He brought forth His work, for they did not count the "Simple Desire" nor the "Strike of the Hammer" <note>Kabbalistic metaphors for the earliest stages of creation</note>, since both are causes for the effect by shared name only—this one for its excellence as being nothing but a Cause, and that one being nothing but the existence of the effect itself.

And it enters into the collective of all the other Sefirot which are its root: these are Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, the third being Mercy <note>Tiferet</note>, and it is the Law <note>Gevurah/Din</note>, and they are included in them, all the other Sefirot. By this He brought up the secret of the "Vav" <note>The letter Vav, numerically 6</note>, Grace <note>Chen</note>, like the three points... and so the points and the Cause of the Infinite <note>Ein Sof</note> are all one thing. However, in relating them in peace, and since they are three and the source for three branches that emerge from there, which are in the Crown... and from Understanding (and not Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding as mentioned, not Crown, Might, and Understanding) that are depicted in the Crown itself; in this is the vitality of the beginning of its expansion. Sometimes in the *Bereshit Rabbah* <note>The midrashic commentary on Genesis</note> they are related in three aspects... three Sefirot which are in Wisdom and Crown in an essential aspect (meaning the relationship of all the Sefirot, for they are the root of all emanation, in which both Judgment and Kindness and Mercy are included...). And even these three Sefirot are unified in one end... as said regarding the three lights that came. The main point is for the researcher to know the value of the foundation of the three hidden lines in the Crown, and accordingly, the value of the foundation of the fifty upper lines in which the first root is hidden... and the Infinite Cause... and especially in it until no end. And for the totality of the three points... the root is hidden, which is the Holy One and the Intent, and it is the precise Radiant Light, the Light of Darkness, and so on. In the specific existence of the ten Sefirot included in them... to the points in the aspect of the relationship and expansion of the ten Sefirot, and this is according to the opinion of one branch in the purpose of the foundation of the building, the fragment and the glory.

of my predecessors wrote that the "ignorant ones" <note>Niv'arim: possibly referring to hidden or "consumed" lights</note> that are hidden are the ten Sefirot... and one root, and they are attached to the root of all the lines like a flame to a coal. # Juice of Pomegranates | Gate 11: The Effulgences | Slice of the Pomegranate

To you is given the general principle arising from the image related to our subject. It is written regarding the fire <note>referring to the divine light</note> that the thirteen attributes of mercy in the Torah are branches and derivatives hanging from the ten levels called <term>Sefirot: the ten creative powers or "vessels" of God</term> along with three "hidden mercies" which are counted with them. They are called "Swiftly from the mouth of the Swift" <note>likely a poetic or liturgical reference to the speed of divine emanation</note>. The "Fathers" are the Sefirot, and the "offspring" are the thirteen attributes. They have no beginning, for they are the very cause and root of all the "Fathers" <note>the primary Sefirot</note>. Human thought cannot grasp them. We have received from the mouth of the Kabbalah <note>original: "m'pi ha-kabbalah" — meaning the oral tradition</note> that their essence is the **Inner Primordial Light**. This light spreads into the root of the revealed realm, and its form emerges in its expansion like the likeness of three great "openings" of radiant and pure light. This is all one light, one cause, and one root, elevated within the <term>Ein Sof: the Infinite, God before any manifestation</term>, and so on. Thus far, we have sought to understand the words of the Great Rabbi <note>likely referring to an early authority like Rabbi Hai Gaon or the author of the Sefer HaIyyun</note> in explaining what is necessary for our subject.

## Chapter 2: Know
The Great Rabbi did not intend to say that there are thirteen Sefirot—heaven forbid. He was precise in his language when he said the thirteen attributes of mercy in the Torah are "branches and derivatives" emerging from the ten levels called Sefirot, corresponding to them along with the three hidden things. He did not say "thirteen Sefirot," but rather "ten levels called Sefirot," and the cause to the right of the levels refers to thirteen when including the three hidden things. He said the "Fathers" are the Sefirot and the "offspring" are the attributes. This concerns the matter of **Essence and Vessels** <note>a core Kabbalistic debate: are the Sefirot God's actual essence or just tools He uses?</note>. For the attributes are the vessels prepared to act with mercy according to His ways, through which the Name <note>God</note> is revealed as good or stern, for they are the cause of change. However, the "Fathers," which are the Essence, do not possess the power of change at all, as is explained in the "Gate of Essence and Vessels." They are called "Fathers" because they are the progenitors of the "offspring," which are the attributes. They have no beginning, meaning they cannot be grasped even in the <term>Keter: the Crown, the highest Sefirah</term>, as is explained in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar</note>. One cannot grasp the three hidden things there above in the Crown, and therefore they have "no beginning," for one does not know from what life-force they emerged. They are the cause and root that preceded the ten Sefirot.

If so, since there are three hidden things above the Crown, are there not ultimately thirteen Sefirot? Why then does the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an ancient foundational mystical text</note> return to the number "Ten and not nine, ten and not eleven"—and certainly not thirteen? The language used here explains that he relates the structure of the Sefirot to five, and then six with the hidden ones and the root of all the Fathers, which are three things; yet all is one and all is the Infinite. For the Infinite is the Cause, and the Cause is the Root, and all is the Infinite, blessed be He. Therefore, they are not called Sefirot except when associated with the Infinite: **Primordial Light**, **Radiant Light**, and **Clear Light**. These three "existences" indicate the Cause through the power of this light—so bright that the eye cannot master it. These are the three hidden things considered within the Name. The first is called "Primordial" to indicate it is prior to everything. This will be explained regarding the Crown later, God willing: at what "time" they are prior, the reason for the division into these three existences, and the nature of their expansion within their own essence. This expansion is not for the sake of revealing themselves to others, but rather an expansion within their own being. This is the meaning of "He spreads within the root of the revealed." Though they are called "three lights," they are nonetheless one light in their essence. For this reason, he said, "It is all one light."

## Chapter 3: Know
When a person thinks to do something, even though he forms the image of the thing in his mind, it remains as nothing until he brings his thought from potential into actuality through labor. But with the Creator, it is not so; His thought is not like ours. Rather, as soon as it arose in His Will to emanate the emanations, they were immediately in His thought, within His essence, without change in Him. He is unique and unified with them; there is no difference at all between the "Request" and the "Unification" in the Light of the Infinite. He and His Name are one Cause. When He formed within Himself the three points...

...the first three: The first is the **Wondrous Light**, a light that cannot be perceived; it is only attributed and compared to the Pure Thought. Compared to it are the lights of **Knowledge** <term>Da'at</term> and **Intellect** <term>Sekhel</term>, for the Thought considers them both. From them come five lights: the "Scale of Merit," the "Scale of Guilt," and the "Tongue of Forgiveness" which decides between them. The fourth light is the "Renewer of the World of Souls," which they called the "Righteous One of the World" <term>Tzaddik: the foundation of the world</term>. Furthermore, there is an external light called "Consuming Fire," and its companions, "North" and "South," and it encompasses all the lights and is the beginning of all actions.

Now I will hint to you regarding the three Upper Lights above the ten Sefirot: they have no beginning, for they are "There," their foundation and the Root of all Roots. Thought cannot grasp them. From the name of our holy Elder <note>referring to a traditional lineage or a specific teacher</note>, we have received their names: **Inner Primordial Light**, which spreads into the Hidden Root and sparkles from the power of simplicity like the likeness of two great lights: **Radiant Light** and **Clear Light**. All are one light, one essence, and one hidden root of the Infinite. Concerning them, they <note>the Sages</note> said: "You have no business with hidden things" <note>a quote from the Wisdom of Ben Sira, often cited in the Talmud to limit speculation on the divine essence</note>. They have no known name other than the description of "lights." Likewise, the Root of All has no known name. Even the four-letter Name <term>Y-H-W-H: the Tetragrammaton</term>, let alone the other descriptive titles, are only attributed to the created Glory.

However, the name **YHWH** is the foundation of the levels. The form of the first letter <note>The Yod (י)</note> is like a very thin point. It was drawn in its writing—a writing known to the masters of mystical marks—to indicate a wondrous secret. For a "mass" and a spiritual form were solidified and depicted through the power of three levels which are the essence of the Root. From the Hidden Root, it ascended and spread over it, a simple conceptual light. Through the expansion in the essence of the Root, they came into being—not outside of it. From them, the power of **Knowledge** and the power of **Intellect** were solidified and depicted; these are the beginning of the hidden spiritual creation. This point <note>the Yod</note> received the power of the Wondrous Law-giving Image to be depicted within it as seven levels of the utmost thinness. Therefore, their number reached ten <note>3 hidden + 7 levels within the Yod</note>. By the power of this point, the ten levels were solidified and depicted in the form of the letter **He** (ה) established after it. All the powers were hidden within it like a spiritual light. By the power of the form of the *He*, the six directions of the world of "the mass" <note>the physical/manifest world</note> were solidified and depicted—a simple spiritual mass and form, revealed from the first which was hidden in the second letter. These are the beginning of the revelation of the hidden worlds. Concerning this, the scholars of the Sefirot called this Sefirah "The Vision of the Hidden World." The final **He** (ה) of the Name prepares and brings out all the powers into complete action; she is the perfection of all powers.

I say the likeness of the **Yod** (י) is like a thin point because every point is written in two ways. The first has a "spike above" <note>Hebrew: Kotz</note>, a "spike below," and the body in the middle. These are the secrets of the letters, points, and cantellation marks in the *Tikkunim*. The second way is this form: ', which adds to the first image a second spike below, drawn from its body toward its front. According to the way of the Gaon, the upper spike hints at the Source, the body at the Primordial Light, and the two spikes at the Clear and Radiant lights. And according to the "Way of Gold" <note>perhaps a specific school of interpretation</note> which we will encounter: the upper spike hints at our Will <term>Ratzon</term> and the *Segolta* <note>a three-dot vowel mark</note> to guide us; or the spike to indicate it, and the *Segolta* for the three intellectual powers <term>Chokhmah, Binah, Da'at</term> within the Crown; or the spike for those three in the Crown, and the *Segolta* for the roots of existence...
