# 39 Slice of the Pomegranate | Gate 11: The Effulgences | Juice of Pomegranates

The <term>Sefirot: the ten creative powers of God</term> mentioned below refer to the presence of the "Kingdom" <note>original: "Malchut"</note> within each of them. They also attributed ten "Effulgences" <note>original: "Zahzahot"</note> to the Sefirah of "Beauty" <note>original: "Tiferet"</note> in its secret aspect, which reaches the "Supreme Whiteness." **In the book** *The Fountain of Wisdom*, it is stated: These are the ten colors that gush forth from the "Darkness" <note>a term for the unknowable aspect of the Infinite</note>. They are: Light from Light, Splendor from Splendor, Radiance from Radiance, Splendor from Light, Light from Splendor, Radiance from Light, Radiance from Splendor, Splendor from Radiance, and Glory from Glory. Thus, there are ten. The first is **Wondrous Light**, which is Light from Light. The second is **Hidden Light**, which is Splendor from Splendor. The third is **Sparkling Light**, which is Radiance from Radiance. The fourth is **Pure Light**, which is Splendor from Light. The fifth is **Polished Light**, which is Light from Splendor. The sixth is **Radiant Light**, which is Radiance from Light. The seventh is **Refined Light**, which is Light from Radiance. The eighth is **Pure and Polished Light**, which is Radiance from Splendor. The ninth is **Bright Light**, which is Splendor from Radiance. The tenth is **Brilliant Light**, which is Glory from Glory. Thus far the quote. These matters are obscure and sealed until a spirit from on high is poured upon us.

<column-break/>

The "Tablets" <note>primordial archetypes</note> will be the specific details of their reception, for the Divine Essence exists in each one. This essence should not be compared to a created being or even to a source. Just as in the "Vessels" <note>the Sefirot as containers for light</note>, the quality of the Sefirot will be hidden under a Name, so too in the aforementioned Vessels, the Essence is spread within them. However, the Torah <note>the Divine blueprint</note> is the Essence as it emanates and reveals itself more fully within them, until they become His very Essence. **To understand** the existence of the aforementioned Effulgences, one must know how He knows all beings through His Essence. His knowledge is not like the knowledge of created beings, for if it were, His knowledge would be divided according to the division of the beings. This is impossible regarding His true Unity. Just as His Unity cannot be divided into parts, so His knowledge cannot be divided, for He and His knowledge are one simple unity. It is not a knowledge acquired from outside; rather, He perceives them through the Intellect itself. From the perspective of His Essence, He grasps every being, for all beings exist within His Essence. He and their souls are all one unique whole. Therefore, he was precise in the "Places of the Sefirot" <note>a reference to a specific text or concept</note> regarding the essential details within His Essence. Because the Sefirot are a pattern and a framework for all beings...

### The Gate

...and regarding the essential details in His Essence, by which He knows all beings—whether many or few, small or great—nothing is missing from them. This is because the form of "Spheres" <note>or "Circuits"</note> exists in the mind of the designer in two ways: one is before it exists (this is the potential within the power of the designer before it is revealed in reality), and the second is in his design after it exists (where it is already revealed in a body). Since knowledge in the "Soul" <note>referring to the higher Divine level</note> is the aspect of knowing matters both before their existence and after, and there is no difference or lack in His vision, it follows that there must be two types of knowledge within created things: the first are the "Essential Details and Primordial Visions" which are constant in the Essence. These are the foundations of the design that emanate from the Source Light—the essence of the <term>Keter: the Crown, the highest Sefirah</term>—and from the aspect of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> within it. These are not the grosser forms of the revealed world; on the contrary, they serve as a "garment" for that which is contracted, much like a body is a garment for the soul. **According to this**, the "Tablets" and "Effulgences" mentioned are not the usual Sefirot of Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding <note>Keter, Chokhmah, Binah</note>. Rather, they are more sublime realities. They clothe themselves in the sources of the Sefirot, but they are not the "vessels" of the Sefirot themselves. Instead, they are the Essence that spreads into the Sefirot—pure emanations of the root, where everything is one. This explains the statement: "These are the youths, and these are the spirits, but they are not in bodies." This means the "youths" are the sources of the Sefirot, and the "spirits" are the Sefirot themselves. The Essence within the Sefirot is the "Soul." This clarifies the intention of the <term>Rashbi: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</term>, who explained that the secret of the Essential Crown is the Soul, Wisdom (the secret of the points) is the Spirit, and Understanding (the secret of the letters) is the Soul <note>Nefesh</note>. The Infinite Light <note>Ein Sof</note> is the root of all these lights.

### Chapter 5

The Crown of the Rashbi, the Crown of the <term>Ramak: Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</term>. He writes: The Infinite <note>Ein Sof</note> is not established to be known. Just as there was nothing before it, so no "Head" <note>beginning</note> emerged from that which is not a "Point" <note>the first manifestation</note>. It does not reside in bodies but in the depths of the Infinite. It cannot be clung to. Before this, in the Holy Zohar, it says: "The Head of the Hiddenness" cannot be looked upon at all, for there is no knowledge of it. This is the secret of "it is not established to be known"—it cannot be grasped except through its actions. Therefore, in <term>Adam Kadmon: Primordial Man, the first stage of emanation</term>, there is no "head" or "end," for the Essence exists through the emergence of a thing from beginning to end. Since there is no change or emergence within Adam Kadmon, one cannot say "head" or "end." This is because the "Hidden Crown" does not resemble the Infinite, even in its holy writing. For the Crown reveals itself in head and end—Wisdom within the Crown is the head, and Understanding is the end. Regarding the Infinite, however, "head" and "end" do not apply. Even though the Sefirot and the Essence are found there fundamentally, they do not resemble the Infinite.

<meta>This page transitions from the discussion of the "Effulgences" (Zahzahot) in Gate 11 to the "Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom" in Gate 12. It includes a significant critical commentary by the editor, Shimeon Cohen, regarding the reconciliation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy with the ten-Sefirot structure.</meta>

# Slice of the Pomegranate: Gate 12 — The Paths | Juice of Pomegranates

**Shimeon Cohen, the editor, said:** I wonder at the "Ancestors of the World" <note>A respectful term for foundational Kabbalistic authorities.</note> who disagreed in the first chapter of this Gate concerning the matter of the Thirteen Attributes. Surely their words are the "words of the living God," but not for the reason stated. For how can the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy be the ten Sefirot <note>The ten divine emanations or "vessels" of God's light.</note> and the three hidden lights? Are not the ten Sefirot the secret of the three vertical lines—the Line of Kindness, the Line of Mercy, and the Line of Judgment? They are not usually called the "Attributes of Mercy" in their entirety.

Furthermore, I find a difficulty in the words of the Excellency, Rav Hai Gaon <note>One of the last leaders of the Babylonian academies (939–1038 CE), known for his early philosophical and mystical writings.</note>, of blessed memory, for his words seem to contradict one another. At first, he says the Thirteen Attributes mentioned in the Torah are branches and offspring emerging from the ten Sefirot along with the three hidden lights, and these thirteen are what "measure out" a man's reward according to his ways and the fruit of his deeds, whether good or bad, for they are subject to change as explained above in Chapters 1 and 2. 

But then, because he was troubled by the idea that there would then be thirteen Sefirot <note>Kabbalah strictly maintains there are only ten primary Sefirot.</note>, he said that the three hidden lights superior to the ten Sefirot have no beginning, for they are the essence and "Root of all Roots." Thought cannot grasp them, therefore they are not included in the count of the Sefirot, Heaven forbid, for they are three aspects and all is the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), may He be blessed, as he explains their names in Chapter 2. Yet, if they are so hidden that we cannot count them among the Sefirot, how can we count them among the Attributes? 

And if you say that it is the branches extending from them that are the Attributes, and not their essence—why then do we not count them among the Sefirot, just as we count the "Three Primordials" <note>The top three Sefirot: Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding.</note> which are also only grasped through their extension? Even the "Days of Building" <note>The lower seven Sefirot associated with the seven days of creation.</note> are not grasped in their essence, only through their "vessels," yet they are counted. Furthermore, the phrasing does not easily support this interpretation.

Therefore, I say—after asking for forgiveness—that the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy are all contained within *Tiferet* (Beauty/Compassion), for it is the central Line of Mercy. The numerical value of the Hebrew letters *Vav* (6), *Aleph* (1), and *Zayin* (7) equals thirteen <note>13 is also the value of the word *Echad* (One) and *Ahavah* (Love).</note>. For within it are two diagonal boundaries, which are the twelve permutations of the Name YHVH. Although some permutations lean toward Judgment, the source of the Name is Mercy. Regarding this, our Sages said: "Great are the righteous, for they turn the Attribute of Judgment into the Attribute of Mercy." They do this by arousing through their good deeds the "Gate of Love," which is the thirteenth gate in the secret of *Da'at* (Knowledge). Then, they become the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. This is why the Name of God appears twice in the Thirteen Attributes, one referring to Knowledge and one to Beauty, at which point Mercy prevails.

All of them are called "Mercy," otherwise we could not call it the Line of Mercy. Because the first Name refers to Knowledge, the commentators explained it refers to God "before a person sins," for that is the secret of the [Divine] Thought. This is also the intention of the first verse of the *Shema* prayer: one must focus on the word "One" (*Echad*) as it relates to *Tiferet*. Therefore, the verse begins "Hear O Israel"—this is *Yisrael Sava* <note>An aspect of the Sefirah of Understanding or Knowledge.</note> which is the secret of Knowledge—and then "the Lord is One." 

When the people of Israel below act with love and unity, they arouse the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy above, as "One" (*Echad*) equals thirteen. This is the meaning of: "When my children do according to this order, I am filled with mercy for them." For "the joining of Ephraim..." etc. This is also the meaning of "Abraham was one (*Echad*) and he inherited the land." See the book *Divrei Shmuel* (The Words of Samuel) on the portion of *Vayishlach* regarding the verse "And the sons of Jacob were twelve," for I do not have his words at hand to quote. This is also the secret of the "Thirteen Rivers of Balsam" <note>A legendary reward for the righteous in the afterlife, symbolizing an overflow of divine pleasure.</note> which the righteous arouse in their lives. It is also noted that the students of the Ari <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria (1534–1572), the father of modern Kabbalah.</note>, of blessed memory, were accustomed to say during the Thirteen Attributes: "Hear O Israel, the Lord, the Lord is a Merciful God..." to hint at this secret in the mystery of faith. Understand this.

### Gate Twelve: The Paths

**Chapter 1:** We have learned there: "With thirty-two wondrous paths of wisdom, Yah, the Lord of Hosts... engraved His world with three books: Scroll, Scribe, and Story." <note>A famous quote from *Sefer Yetzirah* (The Book of Creation).</note> As explained in Chapter 2: twenty-two foundational letters—three "mothers," seven "doubles," and twelve "simples." These paths are counted in the order of "Cause and Effect." They are the pipes for the abundance flowing from Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) to Understanding (*Binah*), where the "rivers" begin. Understanding is called "Glory" and "Heart" (*Lev*) because of them, following the secret of the thirty-two (*L-B*) mentions of the name "Elohim" in the story of Creation. For Understanding acts with the power of its strength, as the King cast the mold of all created things through Wisdom. In its paths is the "thickness of the earth," which is the "hyle" <note>The Greek term *hyle* (matter), used here to describe the primordial, formless substance that carries all potential forms.</note> equal to the numerical value of "Wisdom," which is the matter supporting all forms. From there they are drawn out in subtle form from 32 to 32. All of them are held by the "Unique Covenant" called "Peace," which brings them to the Great Sea <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut (Sovereignty).</note>. There, the "lower 32" are paths for the Lower Wisdom. 

Regarding both of them, it is said: "In wisdom You have made them all." The Mishnah clarifies that He engraved this world with 32 paths, which are like the "eye of the needle" <note>original: 'Kof el hakote,' likely a variant of 'eye of the needle' or a similar metaphor for a narrow conduit.</note>. They also imprint, with the precedence of their form, the depths of Thought, and they give shape to things below. From the verse "Stand by the roads and look, and ask for the ancient paths," we know that the "World of Paths" is one where things are not seen, and their trails are most hidden. Regarding the matter of Wisdom, they said the trails are narrow and short, and the paths...

<column-break/>

**Chapter 1: Explaining the 32 Paths of Wisdom.** Know that these thirty-two paths are designated within Wisdom; they represent the division of its levels. By their power, every "cause" becomes an "effect" for the next, and so on. The upshot is that the first path is the cause for the second, and the second for the third, in this order. There is no doubt that these paths are the roads and pipes for the abundance; they are sources spreading from the depths toward Understanding. Therefore, Wisdom is called "Glory" (*Kavod*), which has the numerical value of 32, and it is also called "Heart" (*Lev*) because of the "Fifty [Gates of Understanding]." 

By way of the paths, everything done in Creation was enacted. The matter is that the molds for all created beings are in Wisdom, as it is written: "In wisdom You have made them all." From there they are drawn out in subtlety, leading 32 paths to Understanding until they spread down to Sovereignty (*Malkhut*). In Sovereignty, there are also 32 paths, and they are called the "32 Lower Paths," etc. From them, all the branches emerge into the world of Creation. This [Sovereignty] was the "Final Wisdom" (the "Lower Wisdom"). The 32 paths from it are those which the King engraved to be the mold for all created things. 

Therefore, some call Wisdom "What" (*Mah*), as in "the power of the Lord" (*Koach Mah*). It rises in Thought to the value of 73 <note>Gematria of 'Chokhmah' (Wisdom) is 73.</note>, like the value of "Revealed" (*Galah*). This explains its "hyolic" <note>from Greek 'hyle'</note> power—meaning it is the "prime matter" carrying all the forms in the world. Regarding this secret, it was said of the 32 wondrous paths of wisdom: "Yah, the Lord of Hosts, engraved His world with three books: Scroll, Scribe, and Story," etc. The word "wondrous" (*peli'ot*) implies concealment, for through the power of Wisdom, they are covered. It also implies the word "all" (*kallah*). It says "His world" to show that the Sefirah of Sovereignty (*Malkhut*) merits them.

<meta>Continuing from the previous discussion on the hidden lights, this page focuses on the nature of the three "Effulgences" (Zahzahot) which exist prior to and above the ten Sefirot, specifically their relationship to the Crown (Keter) and the expansion of the Divine Name.</meta>

# Juice of Pomegranates | Gate 11: The Effulgences

Regarding the essence and existence of the **Effulgences** <note>Hebrew: *Zahzahot*; these are three supreme, hidden lights that precede the emanation of the ten Sefirot.</note>, despite their reality, their order is not revealed to the **Sefirot** <note>The ten divine attributes or channels.</note>, and the Sefirot cannot grasp them due to their extreme concealment. Being the "roots," they are engraved, established, and known only to Him as **Crown**, **Wisdom**, and **Understanding** (*Keter*, *Chokhmah*, *Binah*), as will be explained. Although they are part of the total unity, they are not equal in their governance. From the perspective of the hidden **Crown**, specifically the level called the **Supreme Will** <note>Hebrew: *Re’u Ila’ah*.</note> of the **Ancient One** <note>Hebrew: *Atika*; a reference to the most ancient, hidden aspect of the Divine.</note>, these hidden orders remain like a thought in the heart. One may only occasionally understand them—specifically during their ascent to the uppermost Effulgence in secret. 

These mysteries, relative to His simple existence, are the "offspring" of His Will. When they are there, we say they are "opposite Him," meaning that their reality was not yet spread out to reveal the Effulgences in His concealment. Now, in the great expansion of the Effulgences, they become abstracted in those sources. This is the nature of their "revelation"—not that they are revealed in their actual essence (for His power is beyond the reach of the high, the noble, or the base), but rather that relative to their presence, He is revealed to "others." This expansion does not imply a change in Him, but rather a contraction in the perception of the second Effulgence. In the "days of building" <note>A term referring to the lower seven Sefirot or the creative process.</note>, they do not ascend beyond **Understanding** (*Binah*), which is the secret of the **Jubilee** <note>Hebrew: *Yovel*; associated with the Sefirah of Binah and the return to the source.</note>. They do not rise or change further up than that, but from there, they draw from Wisdom in the Crown.

The hidden order in the Crown descends because the Crown's highest hidden aspect is the **Supreme Will**. It is the hidden source for the "winter" <note>Likely a metaphor for a state of concealment or gathering inward.</note>. It is the aspect of Grace (*Chen*) that attains the Effulgences. Because the root is always united with the hidden Effulgences, He and His causative power are all one thing. The beauty found there is because the hidden Effulgences dwell within Him.

### Another Chapter: 7

Since it has been explained that these levels are above the Crown, the focus turns to their expansion within our "windows" <note>Metaphor for the vessels or channels through which light passes.</note> in the **Rectifications** <note>Refers to the *Tikunei Zohar*, a foundational Kabbalistic text.</note>. It says: "The Supreme Crown, and then the Ancient Primordial Light returned to its bosom, then the Clear Light, then the Refined Light <note>original: *Or Kadmon, Or Tzach, Or Metzuchzach*.</note>, Wisdom..." From his words, we see that the hidden Effulgences are within the Crown. (Furthermore, the order is sometimes reversed from the usual sequence, for the usual order is: Primordial Light, Refined Light, and Bright Light. The Refined Light is more hidden than the Bright Light alone.) **And it is possible** to say that just as the Effulgences are ordered as the "first four" <note>Referring to the first four Sefirot or stages of emanation.</note> including the ten in the world of **Emanation** (*Atzylut*), so too when the Effulgences expand further down into the Crown, their reality is established there. 

The reason the *Tikunim* placed the "Clear Light" before the "Refined Light" is perhaps because the Power of the Effulgences preceded the Effulgences of the Crown; therefore, it is difficult for it to be revealed in the Crown, as it was the lowest part, closest to revelation. **Know** also that these Effulgences in the Crown are associated in the *Tikunim* with the name **YHVH** (Yod-He-Vav-He). The **Yod** represents "He judges the judges," a virtue of the holiness hidden in the Crown. This does not mean the name is literally in the Crown as it is in the Soul, but rather refers to the levels of Wisdom and the secret of the "External Wisdom" which gazes upon the image of the "Skull" <note>Hebrew: *Karkafta*; a term from the Zohar describing the highest part of the divine "head."</note>. Sometimes the Name is filled with the letter Yod, like this: **YOD HE VAV HE** <note>The spelling that equals 72, known as the Name of *Av*.</note>. This is the image of the Yods that return to the three rectifications in the concealment of the Crown. The **Vav** of "Mercies" is the image of the three Mercies that are in the branch of the side, by the power of the three points (the upper tip, the lower vertex). These Effulgences contain the images of the three letters, representing eight sources for the existence of eight. (All these letters are in Wisdom, and their number proves it, as it equals the number of Wisdom, which is 72. The Name of 72 is the building of Wisdom.) These Effulgences in the hidden Crown were perceived by the Kabbalists as equal lines in letters, combinations, and vowel points:

| YHVH Crown | YHVH Wisdom | YHVH |

| YHVH Kindness | YHVH | |

The secret of the Effulgences in the Crown is that they are so refined that they even have names. It is possible to say that as they expand above, each one is associated with the holy names of the lines. Just as they are associated with names in the Crown, so they are in **Beauty** (*Tiferet*). The reason for this is that it reaches the image of the Supernal Ones in the secret of the **Hidden Knowledge** (*Da'at*), which is raised higher and higher. Because Beauty (*Tiferet*) includes two Mercies, it is called "Open-Eyed" and resembles the Crown and Wisdom. This is difficult to explain here, but will be clarified in the Gate of Appellations.

**Severity** (*Gevurah*) in this creation, the letters *Lamed* and *Bet* <note>The letters spelling "Heart" (*Lev*), which equals 32</note> appeared at the beginning and end of the Torah <note>The first letter of the Torah is *Bet* in *Bereishit*; the last is *Lamed* in *Yisrael*</note>. Two names of 42 letters are joined to them, which reside in *Gevurah* through the mystery of the **32 Paths** and the **10 Utterances** with which the world was created. **However**, the name *Elohim* in the narrative of creation appears as follows: in the first two verses, twice; in the "Firmament" section, 4 times; in "Let the waters be gathered," "Let the dry land appear," and "And it was good," 3 times; in "Let the earth sprout" and "And it was good," 2 times; in the "Lights," 4 times; in "Let the waters swarm," the "Great Sea Monsters," "And it was good," and the "Blessing," 4 times; in the "Beasts of the earth," 3 times; and from the "Making of Man" until "And behold it was very good," 7 times. All of them are called **Intelligences** (*Sekhalim*), for "intelligence" resides in **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*). It is written in the *Great Alphabet of Rabbi Akiva* that the Creator of the Sabbath formed them with knowledge, understanding, and intelligence in order from bottom to top:

**Behold**, the first is called the **Wondrous Intelligence**; the second, **Illuminating**; the third, **Sanctified**; the fourth, **Constant**; the fifth, **Rooted**; the sixth, **Separated Influence**; the seventh, **Hidden**; the eighth, **Complete**; the ninth, **Pure**; the tenth, **Sparkling**; the 11th, **Polished**; the 12th, **Bright**; the 13th, **Guiding Responsibility**; the 14th, **Illuminating**; the 15th, **Sustaining**; the 16th, **Eternal**; the 17th, **Intellect of Sensation**; the 18th, **House of Influence**; the 19th, **Secret of Spiritual Actions**; the 20th, **Intellect of Will**; the 21st, **Desired Object**; the 22nd, **Faithful**; the 23rd, **Enduring**; the 24th, **Imaginative**; the 25th, **Experimental**; the 26th, **Renewed**; the 27th, **Perceptible**; the 28th, **Natural**; the 29th, **Tangible**; the 30th, **General**; the 31st, **Perpetual**; the 32nd, **Worshipped**. These should be examined in the **Book of Formation** (*Sefer Yetzirah*).

**Chapter 3: The ancients wrote** in their books that the **Cause of Causes** <note>The ultimate Source of all</note>, blessed be He, causes the **Supreme Crown** (*Keter*) to be drawn from Him. It is a simple intellect in the ultimate state of simplicity, such that there is nothing between it and its Cause except that this is the Cause and that is the Result. This intellect perceived three perceptions: it perceived itself, it perceived its Cause, and thirdly, it perceived the difference between itself and its Cause. Each of these three has these same perceptions: the first perceived itself, its Cause, and the difference; the second perceived itself, its Cause, and the Cause of its Cause; the third perceived itself, the Cause of its Cause, and the difference. This results in nine perceptions, and the Root of all Causes brings the total to ten. Each of these has a beginning, a middle, and an end, totaling thirty. Adding the power of the Cause and the power of the Result, these are the **32 Powers** for the **Paths of Wisdom**, which is the letter *Yud* <note>The first letter of the Name of God, representing Wisdom</note> abstracted from all matter and form, being purely intellectual.

**And they said** that all of them were "nested" in **Wisdom** and given to **Understanding** (*Binah*), as it is written: "The Lord by Wisdom founded the earth, He established the heavens with Understanding" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>. For Understanding gazed into Wisdom, which possesses the 32 Paths, and created the world. All these paths were given to all the **Sefirot**. Know that all these paths and everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created correspondingly in **Man**, so that from the revealed one might understand the secrets of Wisdom. [Kabbalistic authors] expanded on the specific placements in Man according to the order of the paths; it is a long, deep, and pleasant inquiry which belongs in its proper place.

**And they said** that 32 paths are found in Man in many places in his body, for they are all scattered throughout the body. Thus, there are 32 primary limbs by which every living creature is guided. There are also specific places where they are all gathered, such as the **32 teeth** in the mouth, which are the paths for the source of the letters <note>Speech sounds</note>, and the **32 joints** in the fingers of the hands. The explanation is: there are 28 known joints in the fingers of the hands, plus a joint hidden from the eye that is felt at the base of the thumb on both right and left, and the joint connecting the hand to the arm on both sides. The same applies to the toes. Corresponding to these are the **31 Kings of Canaan** whom Joshua killed, and Canaan itself whose memory was lost with them—making 32. Alternatively, perhaps the kings were not 32, based on what is said in the Masorah <note>The tradition of the biblical text</note>, that the teeth in the mouth are not exactly 32 except for those "of the covenant" <note>Israelites</note>, while others may have one less or one more.

**And they said** that there are 32 beautiful stars from the first and second magnitude, just as the teeth are divided into two rows. Corresponding to them are the **thirty kings of the House of David** from Abraham, the "first moon," to... <note>unclear shorthand</note> ... "I am a stranger with you" <note>Psalm 39:13</note>, until Zedekiah in whom the moon was extinguished, as it is written: "And he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah." Including David himself, that makes 31, and the **Kingdom of Heaven** makes 32.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the 32 Paths of Wisdom, focusing on the linguistic and metaphysical origins of the "Three Books" mentioned in the Book of Formation (Sefer Yetzirah). # Juice of Pomegranates | Gate 12: The Paths | Slice of the Pomegranate

What is called "World" and the "Books" are the three letters **Y-H-V** <note>Yod, Hei, and Vav—the first three letters of the Essential Four-Letter Name of God</note> etc. The second "T" <note>Referring to the letter Tav</note> represents **Knowledge** (*Da'at*). The fourth "Book," which is the final **H** <note>The final letter Hei of the Name</note>, refers to **Kingdom** (*Malchut*). Its purpose is significant because the world was not yet established from the hidden realm, and the totality was included within **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*), **Understanding** (*Binah*), and **Knowledge** (*Da'at*). Its nature is described through the concept of the "Book" (*Sefer*), for within it, all the subtle sources for the details of things are included, finalized, and recorded in an orderly fashion. Therefore, it is called the "Supreme Book" for the power of the whole. 

In this context, the term "Book" (*Sefer*) relates to the linguistic root for "counting" or "recounting" things, such as the attribute of **Kindness** (*Chesed*), as David "counted" them <note>A reference to Psalm 56:9, playing on the Hebrew root S-P-R meaning to count, tell, or record</note>. This indicates that details exist as specific entities, one by one. Similarly, through **Understanding** (*Binah*), details emerge like words standing in the "Book of Wisdom." It is also called the "High Living Book" because it was the source for all things emerging from the Holy One, Blessed be He, which is the "Moistness" <note>Original Hebrew: *Lach* (לח), suggesting vitality or sap</note> that activates the powers established by the Creator.

**Beauty** (*Tiferet*) is called **Story** (*Sippur*) because it is the narrative itself, being the "actor" through the "Book." It represents the elevation of the things being recounted, for through it, the "Six Extremes" <note>The six emotional Sefirot from Kindness to Foundation</note> emerge from **Understanding**. It includes the seal and the matter of the "Heavens," namely **Beauty**, and they "tell" (*mesapprim*)—meaning they shine and radiate toward the Kingdom, which is called the "Glory of God," flowing from these Books.

Reflect and receive: Therefore, it says "they tell" (*mesapprim*), a language related to "Sapphires" (*Sappirim*), and "the work of His hands" refers to the Holy One. The "Firmament" tells and adds to this, which is the mystery of **Knowledge** (*Da'at*), as mentioned above. All of this is implied in the **Zohar** <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> in the portion of *Terumah* on the verse "The heavens declare..." 

In them, there is the **Yod** alone, and all of them are **H**. There, **Understanding** (*Binah*) is the **Yod** of the Sabbath, the **Y-H** of **Wisdom** and **Understanding**. The Holy One, Blessed be He, is the **Y-H-V**. The "World of Formation" (*Yetzirah*) is **Yod-Yod**. **Beauty** (*Tiferet*) is the five-fold **H**, and **Kingdom** (*Malchut*) is the final **L**. To understand the whole, the mystery of the "hooks" <note>Refers to the silver hooks of the Tabernacle, symbolizing the connection between spiritual levels</note> includes the **Yod**... <unclear>illegible text</unclear> in his **Victory** (*Netzach*)... <unclear>illegible text</unclear>. For first they were tied in a knot, and afterward they were spread out. There, the world was engraved, and every single script was written. Thus, the "Year" shall be included, and all writings are there. There they are called "Paths" (*Shevilim*), which are like narrow trails, while the "Writings" are the "Ways" (*Derakhim*). Similarly, when the dreams and the Crown spread out and move from **Understanding** outward, they are called "Ways," which are wider than "Paths." Regarding "Ways," it says "broad," and regarding "Paths," it says "eternal paths." 

And behold, the **Slice of the Pomegranate**: those entering the exile <note>original: *Golah*</note>... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear>... the seal of our lives. This means the Seal and the Matter are like a scale in the perfect balance. There, the paths of the **Sefirot** are placed, providing leadership—that is, the writing of the 32 paths of the world, each one of the 32 writings being drawn into the system of Creation.

## Chapter 2: The Hint of the 32 in the Name ADONAI
->According to what is appropriate for the balance and the unfolding of matters<-

Those drawn from **Wisdom**, which is the "Source of Wisdom," therefore emerge there through the Name **Shaddai** <note>Almighty</note>, the root of the Pomegranate... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear>. The reason they come through the name **Shaddai** is in its letters and its vocalization, which is appropriate for the "House of Honor" to hint at the strength of **Judgment** (*Din*) which prevailed over the creatures of the world. ## Chapter 2: The Division of the Paths
->The four modes of leadership, all within the essence<-

In the division of the paths, the Teacher explained four levels of Divine Leadership, all within the essence of the Sefirot:
1. **The First System:** The blending of all Ten Sefirot together. This is a perfect leadership of absolute Mercy.
2. **The Second:** The **Three Mothers** (*Aleph, Mem, Shin*) alone. This means the Sefirot act with Mercy after the influence of only the first three Sefirot. This is "Blended Mercy."
3. **The Third:** The **Seven Doubles** <note>The 7 letters with two sounds</note>. When these seven prevail with Judgment, this is "Absolute Judgment."
4. **The Fourth:** The **Twelve Simples** <note>The 12 basic letters</note>. These are the "Six Extremes" spreading out from **Beauty**, mixed with Judgment and Mercy. This is "Blended Judgment."

The Mothers, Doubles, and Simples were explained in the third Gate. Since every single path revealed its action through **Understanding** (*Binah*), it was appropriate that they be called by her name.

# Juice of Pomegranates | Gate 13: The Gates | Slice of the Pomegranate

The Sabbath of the Jubilee consists of seven times seven years. Just as the power of the <term>Nidda</term> <note>refers here to laws of ritual purity, used as a metaphor for the cycles of spiritual distancing and return</note> follows a set path, so too do the souls wander and find support from their inner secrets to move forward. Therefore, it is written in the Torah that the Exodus from Egypt occurred through a great miracle and kindness, repeated fifty times to correspond to the **Fifty Gates of Understanding**. Every verse reveals to us a specific "gate."

For if the arousal of these fifty gates had not occurred to bring them out, they would never have left. Thus, fifty gates were required, for one power cannot break another of a different kind; since there were fifty gates of impurity, fifty gates of Understanding were needed to subdue them, as one gate alone would not have the strength to break them all.

### Chapter 3: Understanding the Opening of the Gates of Understanding

Everything in Understanding <term>Binah</term> will be clarified through the seven "Sabbaticals" of the world, for the power of all returns and rests in the root. Therefore, they shall ascend. This is the secret of the "Great Jubilee" and the reception of the twelve months, which require 30 days and 10 days of formation on the Sabbath. The 365 days of the year are the foundation, and the **Ten Days of Repentance** serve as the time for Understanding to repair what was twisted. As a sign of this, the year's cycle is like a wall, where each day is doubled. 

Even though a year might be 354 or 355 days according to the leap year calculations, if you divide the calculation into seven parts: 1) The soul, 2) The Sabbatical years, 3) The years, 4) The months, 5) The Sabbaths, 6) The hours, and the fixed cycles—every one of these is a hint to the seven Sephirot that encompass the entire structure and the movement of the spheres. This is proven in the *Sefer Ha-Malkhut* <note>The Book of the Kingdom</note> in the portion regarding sanctifying the Sabbath of the Land, which is the Jubilee.

# Gate 14: The Gates

These matters are from the perspective of the actual <note>original: "Mamesh"</note> substance, for we were in the aspect of the soul of the Upper One. It spread out as if to sweeten and hide the power of the <term>Klipah</term> <note>the "shells" or "husks" of impurity that conceal divine light</note> and extracted Israel from its hand. This flow was primarily through <term>Binah</term> <note>the Sephirah of "Understanding," often viewed as the divine womb or mother</note> itself. It was a revealed redemption for the Levite, focused on the future destiny that will be awakened by the "Great Shofar," which is the essence of Understanding itself.

### Chapter 5: And After
Since the level of the Fifty Gates of Understanding has been clarified as mentioned, and these are their details: Know that the fifty gates correspond to the seven Sephirot, which are: <term>Gedulah</term> <note>Greatness/Kindness</note>, <term>Gevurah</term> <note>Strength/Judgment</note>, <term>Tiferet</term> <note>Beauty/Harmony</note>, <term>Netzach</term> <note>Victory/Endurance</note>, <term>Hod</term> <note>Majesty/Splendor</note>, <term>Yesod</term> <note>Foundation</note>, and <term>Malchut</term> <note>Kingship/Kingdom</note>. Each one of these is comprised of ten sub-aspects. Thus, seven times seven equals forty-nine, and with the essence of Understanding itself, they become fifty. 

Understanding is the fiftieth gate. From below, fifty worlds are elevated to it, which are prepared in its space. From it, they draw sustenance. Therefore, they are "gates" for it, while the <term>Keter</term> <note>the "Crown," the highest Sephirah</note> and its higher qualities remain hidden and concealed. This is how the later Kabbalists wrote, and it is found in the <term>Tikunim</term> <note>referring to the Tikkunei Zohar, a classic Kabbalistic text</note> that the seven "openings" of the "Small One" <note>referring to the lower Sephirot or the feminine presence, Malchut</note> are the seven attributes of her nurturing. The number fifty is derived from Gevurah, and according to the secret of the "forty-two" <note>referring to the 42-letter Name of God</note>, the source is from Yesod, from its own essence. It was a point within the void surrounded by these seven "walls," and these are the seven times seven that make forty-nine.

### Chapter 6: From Within
From the *Tikunim*, it emerges that the fifty gates are the Sephirot that spread out from Understanding until <term>Hod</term>. These are five Sephirot in order: Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, and Hod. Each one is comprised of ten, making forty. <term>Yesod</term> then receives these fifty gates and adds them to Malchut. Therefore, Yesod is called "All" <note>Hebrew: *Kol*</note> because it receives the secret of the fifty gates of Understanding. This is hinted at in the verse "Yours, O Lord, is the kingdom" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>, where the sovereignty reaches Understanding by the secret of the fifty gates spreading to the five Sephirot (Tiferet, Netzach, Gevurah, Hod, and Yesod). All of this is funneled into Yesod, which is called "All" <note>L-K, numerically 50</note>. The "Yours" <note>Hebrew: *Lekha*</note> refers to the height of the outpouring, and Yesod pours into the "Leah" <note>a persona of the Sephirot</note> which is Malchut. For each of the five contains the ten gates included in the five Sephirot there.

### Chapter 7: And to Understand
To understand the third perspective, one must know that the relationship of Understanding to the seven Sephirot of the "Building" <note>the seven lower Sephirot used to construct the world</note> is like the relationship of a mother to the building. This is not just in the sense of her being placed over them to watch them, but rather she hints at the secret of the "hidden brain" that conceives and carries the drop of seed and gives birth. 

In the aspect of repairing the "vessels" until they return to the world, Understanding received the Sephirot, gave birth to them, brought them in, brought them out, and sealed them for their task, placing them in their proper positions. However, a question arises: when the time comes and the child is born, does the mother remain empty of the contents she once held? Just as a human mother, after she has given birth to her children, the essence of the child is no longer within her as it was before birth, it would seem that the details of these "gates" are no longer within Understanding in their unified state. 

However, it has been clarified in the words of the Zohar that the divine nurturance remains hidden within her, even as it changes below. For the attributes below—from Kindness to Kingship—are seven "walls." Yet, in the "upper building," they are only five. This is because Yesod and Malchut are unified in the "Upper World" as a single Sephirah. Therefore, there are not seven Sephirot above in Understanding, but rather Malchut and Yesod are expansions of Tiferet. These "sources" are within the fifty gates of Understanding. Each is comprised of ten until they reach fifty. These sources that are hidden in Understanding open below in the "Building" as fifty gates. From these sources, the "Building" Sephirot receive their life, nurturing, and influence. 

The gates open in two ways: 
1. When Tiferet and Malchut are unified through Yesod, the sources in Understanding are unified as a complete Yesod and included in the ten. The light of the Crown and Wisdom <note>Keter and Chokhmah</note> then shine upon them, and these sources open with complete mercy. The lower gates are then included in the fifty across five Sephirot up to Hod. 
2. However, when Tiferet, Yesod, and Malchut are not unified as one below, but are separated, the mother (Understanding) does not pour out her abundance from her own power alone. The light of the Crown and Wisdom will not be revealed with them because of the absence of the "Hidden Yesod." Therefore, the Sephirot and the gates do not open except as seven times seven, which only reach forty-nine.

This explains why, when they open as six, they reach forty-nine, and the fiftieth gate is hidden. But when they open as five, they reach a full fifty, and the fiftieth gate is not hidden. The meaning is that when the Sephirot below are unified, the sources are "sweetened." When the union occurs in Malchut and Tiferet, Yesod is also revealed and the hidden gate above them—which is the Crown—is revealed, as explained in the *Tikunim*. 

This is also found in the *Tikunim* regarding the verse "Hear O Israel..." <note>The Shema</note> which has six words and twenty-five letters, and "Blessed be the Name..." <note>Baruch Shem</note> which has six words and twenty-four letters. Together they total forty-nine letters, corresponding to the gates. They said that the twenty-five are in Tiferet and the twenty-four are in Yesod. Why is one gate hidden? Because we are dealing with Yesod, and one letter is missing. (One cannot say that the missing one is the fiftieth gate which is hidden, for it would be more appropriate to count it in Tiferet, which is higher than Yesod). The fiftieth gate is high up in the "Lower Understanding." For Tiferet receives ten from Kindness, ten from Strength, and five from the Crown, Wisdom, and Great Understanding—totaling twenty-five in Tiferet. Then Tiferet gives twenty-four to the "Bride" (Malchut) through the secret of Yesod. Yesod receives three from Victory, three from Majesty, and one from the "Ancient One" <note>Atik</note>—this is the secret of the Foundation of Kingship. Tiferet receives the upper twenty-five, which are the "Upper Unions," and these are not of the "Lower Building." Yesod does not receive that light except to provide for the Bride. Therefore, there are twenty-five in Tiferet and twenty-four in Yesod. The fiftieth gate always transcends and is not counted. As I explained, that which is "hidden" is the fiftieth gate. If there were fifty full gates revealed in the Sephirot, it would be different. But when Yesod is not found in union, the revelation is only in the forty-nine. The merit of Understanding is that she pours out even when she is not unified above with Wisdom and the Crown. In that case, the fiftieth gate of Understanding is hidden and concealed, just as the gates in the Crown and Wisdom are. According to this, the power of the fiftieth gate depends on the level of "inclusion" <note>how the Sephirot are grouped</note>. When the fifty gates are in the secret of ten, the fiftieth gate is the number twenty-five. When the fifty gates are in the secret of six times six, the fiftieth gate is Understanding. Each part is adjusted to the other.

# The Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 14: Existence — Pomegranate Juice

Impurity originates from the earth, while He established His name in all the worlds and His glory shall be seen upon us. Behold, the many <term>epithets</term> <note>Hebrew: kinnuyim; referential names for God like "The Merciful" or "The Great"</note> that appear in the Torah and the many hints regarding the performance of the commandments—all of which correspond to the hint and the hidden secret within them—are faithful witnesses. They show that every single <term>attribute</term> <note>Hebrew: middah; another term for a Sefirah</note> is a power equal to its purpose and its counterpart, according to how it unites with another or how it is influenced or influences by the will of the Master of All, who illuminates them all. Based on these matters, it is not difficult to understand what we find regarding the <term>Tabernacle</term> <note>Hebrew: Mishkan; the portable sanctuary in the desert</note>, which itself hints at the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note>, as do the courtyard of the Tabernacle, the inner Sanctuary, the Cherubim, the Tablets, the Ark, the Table, the Showbread, the Candelabra and its flickering lamps, the outer Altar, the sin-offering, the frankincense, and many others. Because of the **depth** of these secrets and the scarcity of those experts in them, the commandments do not strictly require "intent" <note>Hebrew: kavanah; conscious spiritual focus</note> to be valid, even though they are only fully completed through proper intent to a degree that thought cannot contain. For God does not despise the commandment itself <insert>performed even by the simple</insert>, and as for the reward, who would cease to strive to understand and do good in the depth of the secrets? For the entire Torah includes the great descriptions of all the worlds, both in its revealed and its hidden aspects. He who merits it will distinguish between "one who does much and one who does little," provided that he directs his heart toward Heaven.

Judgment alone, and sometimes they are established as a single <term>Sefirah</term> <note>One of the ten emanations through which the Divine interacts with the world</note> based on its own specific action, and sometimes as <term>Hesed</term> <note>Kindness or Mercy</note> mixed in its action with another Sefirah, such as two parts Mercy or three parts Mercy and so on. The Twelve Simples represent the diagonal expansion of the twelve boundaries which are the ten generalizations plus Judgment and Mercy. These are not [new] Sefirot, but rather ten structures in the arrangements of the "Seal."

The perfection in all the generalizations of the name <term>Yod-He-Vav-He</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, the Tetragrammaton</note> comes from the ten rising to the number of six perfections. 500 is the ultimate foundation of all good, as is known. And the "seventy" all hint at a part, meaning that the seventy are also within the secret of the seven attributes that encompass everything in a "great generalization." This is why it was done so. For the pomegranate represents this great secret: just as the pomegranate is surrounded by a shell and its exterior is numerous, so the wine [juice] within points to the Sefirah of **Tiferet** <note>Beauty/Harmony</note> when it is included, etc.

### Chapter 3 and Further
There are also two aspects to the Sefirot having a relationship with **Atzilut** <note>The World of Emanation, the highest spiritual realm</note> in general. After the Sefirah of <term>Binah</term> (Understanding), the first six Sefirot are hinted at by the letter **Yod**. The attribute of **He** is called the "He of the expansion." There are two aspects of existence with Atzilut. This is hinted at by the Yod having eight parts of Mercy from Binah, and the "Gate of the He" from Binah. The human form <note>Hebrew: Adam</note> is called by this name because it contains three "lives" or three cups. Thus: the right hand is Mercy (*Hesed*), the left is Judgment (*Gevurah*), and the leg that is suspended is Beauty (*Tiferet*), and they are hinted at in this.

# Pomegranate Juice | Gate 14: Existence | Pomegranate Slice

### Gate Fourteen: Existence

## Chapter 1: An Explanation 
->An inquiry into the existence of the Sefirot within existence, similar to the concept of a "drawn sword," which I will further explain to the best of my ability.<-

It is known that things connected as matter and branch are all part of a consensus; nothing is lacking from the existence of the first Recognized One, which remains consistent in its essence. Although it changes through its power, specifically within the "wing" of the Kingdom <note>Hebrew: Malkhut, the final Sefirah</note>, in its own being and existence, it sheds its previous form and becomes entangled, moving from what it was to clothe itself in another, smaller form. 

The reason for all of this is as stated: in every "work" or action performed, nothing is lost from the original existence and strength that existed previously. Even though it sheds its form and takes on a different appearance, it is as Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar, often abbreviated as "Rashbi"</note> said: even when they spread out and are revealed from where they were before, the previous entities do not move from their place. Their essence remains as it was before spreading; rather, they go out, branching out and multiplying like a candle lit from another candle <note>A classic Kabbalistic metaphor for emanation where the source provides light to another without losing any of its own brilliance</note> until the Infinite. 

Furthermore, the general rule regarding things connected to the Pomegranate <note>Referring to the author's system or the text "Pardes Rimmonim" by Cordovero</note> is that these connected things usually become "entangled" or interwoven for a more sublime purpose, adding to their strength. We find that the more they rise in holiness, the more they become the "essence and prey" <note>An idiom for the core sustenance</note> of the unified, spreading existence. Their simple nature is never diminished by their ascent from level to level, up to the Cause of all Causes, blessed be He. Therefore, the importance of holiness is recognized even in these "entangled" states. Even when holiness descends to a lower place, its existence remains like "matter" <note>In the philosophical sense of a substratum or potential</note> even though it has moved from its original location. 

Because of this, our Sages of blessed memory taught: regarding the verse "I will bring your sanctuaries to desolation," they explained that even when they are desolate, they remain in their holiness. This is because the Divine Presence <note>The Shekhinah</note> once descended there, and a recognizable mark of holiness remains in them that the physical eye cannot perceive, but can be grasped by the "eye of the mind" according to our holy Torah. 

This was the manner of the Sefirot in the "Ascent of the Pomegranate," where we concluded that the existence of the minute, hidden "points" act like channels in the Gate of Points. Their holy, subtle life-force allows their divisions to reach a state of prepared revelation. These are the life-forces between the Infinite (Ein Sof) and the Crown (Keter). Though they are as subtle as the Infinite, they begin to take form in the Crown. We call this "revelation," adding further pathways to the subtle roads of the Crown. The "matter" spreads to be revealed in the Crown while its life-force remains in its place. In this way, they descend level by level to the lowest rung. The closer the levels are to the world of Emanation (Atzilut), the more they are called "Face" <note>Panim; representing directness and clarity</note>, and as they approach physical matter, they are called "Back" <note>Achoryaim; representing concealment or indirectness</note>. Thus, there are many levels of "Face to Face" and "Back to Back," as the Rashbi explained in his place. The separator does not encompass the Infinite; rather, within every single Sefirah, there are many existences and worlds that the window of the mind can barely explain.

## Chapter 2: And Besides
This will settle several analytical perspectives on the Sefirot. Sometimes they are intended to be viewed as being included within one another, and sometimes from the perspective of their standing as...

<column-break/>

## Chapter 1: Not
From the beginning, I did not speak in secret. We have discussed how the unique Emanation (Atzilut) goes forth and shines from one level to another until it is beyond investigation, awesome to all those around it. Its spreading forth does not change it, nor does it alter it even by a hair's breadth. This is unlike lowly spiritual beings who shed one form and clothe themselves in another—good into bad or bad into good. Consider the work of a craftsman with an animal: after whitening, beating, dyeing, and spinning the wool, each stage changes the appearance of the material for its improvement, and it can never return to its first state; its original place is no longer recognized.

**Not** so is the spiritual existence. Though it is high, it "sees the lowly." From a hidden, awesome existence, it emanates into many branches that spread from one another. All of them are "grasped, each one to the face of its friend" <note>A reference to the unity of the Sefirot</note> back to the first Root in complete unity, "He who keeps truth forever." 

Regarding this hint, we were warned in the laws of holiness that worn-out sacred items <note>Hebrew: Belaut; items like old scrolls or prayer shawls</note> require burial and separation <note>The practice of Genizah</note>. Even though new vessels used in the sanctuary are highly valuable and require more care than the worn-out ones that no longer perform their function, this is only due to the nature of physical matter which exists and then perishes. Therefore, the physical metaphor does not resemble the spiritual reality in all its parts. A spiritual entity does not have "perishable matter" that carries its holiness for a time and then ceases; rather, it is called "holy" for a person forever. Our Sages of blessed memory interpreted: "I will bring your sanctuaries to desolation"—even when they are desolate, they stand in their holiness.

### The Chain of Emanation
The chain of Emanation from the Essence to the Sefirot, and from the first three to the "structure" <note>the lower seven Sefirot</note> has already been explained. This is not just one isolated detail, but rather includes many existences and worlds. It is said in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar</note>: How many are the inner Sefirot and how many are the outer Sefirot! They are "one above the other," as it is written: "For one high official watches over another, and there are higher ones over them." Concerning them, it is said: how many "Faces within Faces" are there that are awesome, and how many "Backs within Backs" that are not seen and are inner. These are the fourteen <gloss>Hebrew: Yud-Dalet</gloss> names <note>A complex breakdown of divine name permutations follows</note>... 

**And they** said: The Divine Presence (Shekhinah) is certainly included in everything. Because of this, she is sometimes called an "Eagle," sometimes a "Beast," sometimes a "Dove," and sometimes a "Bird." She is called by the name of whatever she rules over. Among the herbs, she is called a "Rose" or a "Fruit-bearing tree." When she rules over the land, she is called "Earth," and when she rules over the sea, she is called "Sea." When she rules over the mountains, she is called "Rock." There is no creature in the world she rules over that she is not called by its name. However, since she rules over all, she creates a separation between the levels that are "Brain" and "Fruit" and the "Husks" (Klipot) of the Other Side <note>Sitra Achra; the realm of evil/impurity</note>. These are like the shells of a walnut that cover the brain. This is the secret of the verse: "And God divided between the light and the darkness." Woe to the one who mixes the husks of the Other Side with the levels of this holy Side!

**Therefore**, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, wished to bring merit to Israel, He gave them many Torah laws and commandments—some of them to remove impurity...

### Chapter 2
Know that from the beginning of the **Emanation** <note>Atzilut; the highest of the four spiritual worlds</note> and the end of the Ten [Sefirot] in general,
the Light descends and turns back. Even though in each
of the Sefirot, Light and its reflection are recognized, for all those from the higher Sefirot
that return and reflect with **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, we do not simply mean the nine from Crown to Foundation and the nine
from Foundation back to Crown, and similarly the hundred from **Majesty** <note>Hod</note> to Crown, etc., and so on in every single Sefirah.
The reason is that every Sefirah serves as a source for all the levels beneath it,
and from every lower Sefirah, its cause acquires the Upper Light. For just as
the Light is lowered into the **Kingdom** from the **Foundation** and is rectified, so it is in every Sefirah. Just as there is Direct Light from the Crown, it exists in Wisdom and Understanding, and so on in every Sefirah until
the Lights are delayed. From the higher to the lower, they act as a garment and a secret; they align as they descend
and return in a cycle without end, like the image of a wheel that turns in a circle and then
becomes quiet. This is explained in the *Tikkunim*: "A tree from which branches go out, the work of Pharaoh," etc.
They are called its blessings... and the "hosts" are the masters of... and it comes
from the side of the worlds that are engraved for you... and its cause is the "nine" for the **Righteous One** <note>Tzadik; a title for the Sefirah of Yesod</note>. It is nine
from above to below and nine from below to above. The explanation is that upon the Righteous One depend all
sustenance and kindness, according to his deeds and according to the length... and the nine which are called their "nourishment"
like the beams of the living creatures. And now he returned... and the name of
the Righteous who are called "living," for the Righteous One is the vitality of the Covenant. And they are the masters
of Life in the secrets they guard, which is the "Life of the Worlds." Through this, one gives birth to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the **Divine Presence** <note>Shekhinah</note>.
And after that, they are precious to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and a cause of life to bring forth to the Righteous.
And the **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note> is included in the Righteous... and the Mother <note>Binah</note> is nine from bottom to top
and nine from top to bottom. And if this is so, from the Foundation in Direct Light, it returns...
thus... for "Life" is to say the Divine Presence is a Sefirah from bottom to top,
and Foundation... and how did he say there would be... and if so, it is in the Reflected Light from top to bottom
and it is nine, and the Reflection that returns from bottom to top is nine. Even though for the Foundation
all the lights emerged from one source, nevertheless there was a difference between light that rolls from
one source and light that cascades from a higher source. So too in all the Sefirot, there is a distinction between Direct Lights
and Reflected Lights. For the Direct Light is the essence of the Foundation falling into Emanation,
but the Reflected Light is secondary to it. Therefore, the direct return will be from the side of the essence itself.
Then the light will resemble its own essence. And because the Reflection is a derivative,
one of its products... and in the Direct [Light] is the essence of the alignment itself,
etc. The light does not resemble the complete light... more like a "shining mirror" <note>Aspaklaria ha-Me’irah; a prophetic or clear vision</note> reflecting through
a shining partition. So too, "nourishment" is only said for that which is lacking from the measure...
then sustenance... and therefore they change beneath the Kingdom.

In the *Book of Clarity* <note>Sefer ha-Bahir, one of the earliest Kabbalistic works</note>, his students said to him: "Our Master, from above to below
and from below to above—we do not know if they are the same."
[He replied:] "From above to below and below to above—Our Master, it is not the same. We know
that one who ascends is not like one who descends, for the one who descends moves quickly, while the one who ascends does not.
Furthermore, the one who ascends can potentially ascend by another path than the one he descended."
He said to them: "Go and see." He settled it for them: "The **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> is below just
as the Shekhinah is above. And what is this Shekhinah? It is the light emanated from the
First Light, which is Wisdom. It also surrounds [all things], as it is said: *The whole earth is full of His glory* [Isaiah 6:3].
What is its work here? It is like a King who had
seven sons, and he assigned each one his place. He said to them: 'Dwell one on
top of the other.' The lowest one said: 'I am at the bottom, I will not be far from You.' He said to him:
'I am surrounding and seeing you.' This is the meaning of *The whole earth is full of His glory.*
And why is He among them? To stand them up and sustain them. And what are these sons?
I have already told you: the Holy One, Blessed be He, has seven holy living creatures..." etc.,
and they have been explained.

### Chapter 2
Behold, to these perfect students of their companions,
their Master said: "It is not the same." They answered
and said that there are two distinctions between the one who ascends and the one who descends. The first: the one who descends

Not so the one who ascends, which is in the secret of **Judgment** <note>Din</note>. Second: the one who descends influences through the Right [side]

because it is also possible to ascend via the Right side, from Foundation to Victory, and from there to Kindness

The Master answered and said: "The Shekhinah below is just as the Shekhinah above,"

# Pomegranate Juice | Gate 11: The Splendors

In the word *ADNY* <note>The Name of God associated with the Sefirah of Malkhut (Kingdom).</note> and in the cooling of the waters, a portion will be of the Divine. Through the letters 'H' and 'K', the five flows <note>Hebrew: *nezzilot*; refers to the streaming of divine influence.</note> descend from the Understanding <note>Binah</note> to the fourteen flows, which are the secret of the ten fingers and the four letters of the Name. For in the first flow, the Crown <note>Keter</note> is included with the first ones, and now it divides into its emanations. This is the service of the Levite in years, indicating the ascent. The knowledge is the revelation of the second flow. This means that on that day, the flow of the Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note> and the three mentioned flows will be refined. These three flows are contained in the word "Head" <note>Hebrew: Rosh</note>... ### Chapter 4: And With
Behold, when the word and the speech look upward to receive influence, the flow does not depart entirely, but remains in its place. Only at the end, when the flow emerges, do the branches and the flows suckle from their expansion completely and return to their source and become hidden. Because of this, everything returns to its unity and its light, as it is written: *Then our heart will be as his heart...* Similarly, the Rashbi <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar.</note> explained in his command regarding the three times "Holy": "Holy" in the **Crown** <note>Keter</note>, "Holy" in **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>, and "Holy" in the **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>. All three are one, for "Holy" is received from the Supreme Holiness, which is the Crown. Rashbi questioned: is there no "Holy" in the Crown? He answered that the *Chayot* <note>Holy living beings/angels</note> ascend to the Crown and provide the "Holy" for the ten Sefirot. This "Holy" is its flow... it is the firmament that clothes itself in its flow... and so in all the Sefirot, when they prepare to receive influence, they do not separate entirely, for their flow remains in its place.

-># The Fifteenth Gate: From Below to Above<-

### Chapter 1: Already
We have already mentioned that the emanation of the **Direct Light** <note>Or Yashar; divine energy flowing downward from God.</note>, which spreads from above to below in ten levels, establishes a state for itself in the Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note>. From there, it returns and ascends in the order of the levels: **Crown** in Kingdom, **Wisdom** in Foundation, and **Understanding** in Grace <note>Chesed</note>. This is like the spark of the sun shining in a polished mirror, which then turns back toward its source. Also, after this, to the place where the emanated beings go, they return again, and the cycle repeats many times. Not only this, but from the Kingdom, the movement toward the Crown causes ten lights to expand downward, and they too ascend and descend through those same levels without end, as light emanates to light and light to light... **And by this** one can also examine the Crown in relation to each of the other seven "youths," for each one receives and turns its face upward. The **Reflected Light** <note>Or Chozer; light that hits a "vessel" and bounces back.</note> from a "dim mirror" <note>Malkhut</note> differs from the light returning from a "shining mirror" <note>Tiferet</note> or an intermediate one. The laws of the colors mentioned previously must be preserved. It returns likewise from Kingdom to Wisdom, or Understanding, or Grace, and so to all of them, for each one is a source for what is beneath it, even within a single Sefirah from one aspect to another. Thus, the lights are found to move and multiply into countless aspects and worlds.

### Chapter 1: On the Explanation
Of the expansion of the light from below to above.
<gloss>Know that just as the Sefirot are ten levels downward...</gloss>
In their order... so too shall be their suckling upward: Crown in Kingdom, Wisdom in Foundation, Understanding in Grace, Greatness <note>Chesed</note> in Victory <note>Netzach</note>, Strength <note>Gevurah</note> in Splendor <note>Hod</note>, Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> in Strength, Grace in Greatness, Foundation in Understanding, Foundation in Wisdom, and Kingdom in Crown. This is the explanation of the expansion that strikes the first Greatness so that the light turns and returns to its root. The first expansion is called **Direct Light**, and the second is called **Turned Light** or **Reflected Light**. This is the secret of the "Day" mentioned in the *Sefer Yetzirah*: "Ten Sefirot of nothingness... their end is embedded in their beginning and their beginning in their end." For the Crown will be tied and fixed in the Kingdom, and the Kingdom in the Crown. Every part, even as it is refined, will have its light return and descend below. From here, its descent is like the descent of the first light. This entire wheel revolves forever... until the end. Everything is like its end in its beginning and its beginning in its end, as explained in the secret of Direct Light and Reflected Light. This is the letter 'Vav' [ו], and the mentioned secret will be the secret of the Existences in direct order and the secret of the Existences in the chain of *Y-H-W-H*. So too, the *Yod* is the filling of the letter **Aleph** [א], and in the *Yod* are ten levels of Direct Light. The *Vav* is the lower part, representing the thirty levels of Reflected Light. Thus Rashbi explained in the commentary on the Mishnah of the Ten Sefirot... the *Yod* at the beginning and the end... and the *Yod* as a king... hinting at the ten of Direct Light, and the ten below hinting at the ten of Reflected Light.

It returns, for the Direct Light <note>Hebrew: *Or Yashar*; the initial flow of divine energy from the Creator toward the creation.</note> descends from the source, which is the letter *Yod* of the name *YOD-HE-VAV-HE* <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God.</note> until the letter *He*. This is the secret of the Name in the **Crown** <note>The Sefirah of *Keter*, the highest emanation.</note>, for it is the King of Kings. Just as in the Crown there are 100 over 30, so too there is a sign over the **Understanding** <note>The Sefirah of *Binah*.</note>. And since in the **Kingdom** <note>The Sefirah of *Malkhut*, the lowest emanation.</note> there is a 'He' upon the 'He'... in the assembly of the pomegranates <note>A reference to the title of the work, *Pardes Rimonim* (Orchard of Pomegranates).</note>. The letter *Kaph* of the Name hints at the Crown, where the lights are unified. The direct light returns in the *Yod* of existence, and the reversing return occurs in the *Yod* of the Kingdom. ### Chapter 2: Know that the light begins from the Crown and ends at the Crown alone.
->The light shall descend and turn back, exchange and change.<-
Each of the Sefirot <note>Divine emanations or "spheres" of God's manifest power.</note> will be filled with light, and it turns back toward each of the upper Sefirot. It circles and is encountered within them. How so? There are nine blessings from the Crown to the **Foundation** <note>The Sefirah of *Yesod*.</note> and nine from the Foundation back to the Crown, and likewise 100 from the Foundation to the Crown, and so on in every single Sefirah. The reason is that every Sefirah becomes a source for all the subsequent ones beneath it. Within every Sefirah, a form will be established, and the cause will descend and the effect will ascend, bound to the upper realms. For just as there is a return of light traveling between the structures and repairs of each Sefirah, so too there is a direct hole from the Crown to the structures, and between every Sefirah until the end. These lights roll between the upper and lower realms in the heights. This is the meaning of "they were descending and returning" like a wagon wheel until the ultimate grace, similar to a wheel that turns from night to day. This is explained in the *Tikkunim*: "At night the gates are closed..." These are the levels of the tablets. And the forces are prepared to be revealed from the secret of the worlds, to bring the 100 blessings and the stars to the **Righteous One** <note>Hebrew: *Tzaddik*; a title for the Sefirah of *Yesod*, which acts as the funnel for all divine energy.</note>... from top to bottom and nine from bottom to top. The meaning is that the Righteous One possesses all the Grace according to his deeds and his bundle of commandments. There are hidden things in the holy unifications and ascents... and the righteous are called "Tablets," for the Righteous One is the Tablet of the Covenant. And there are righteous ones who, through their compassion, sustain the worlds, and they bring the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence, associated with the Sefirah of *Malkhut*.</note> near to the Holy One, Blessed be He. They unify the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Shekhinah through the power of prayer. To the Righteous One, nine are added, becoming included in the Righteous One as 100 through compassion. Thus, nine are drawn upward and nine from top to bottom. This is the secret of the Direct Light and the Reflected Light. Let there be 100 blessings <note>A Jewish tradition to recite 100 blessings daily, here given a mystical interpretation as the completion of the 10 Sefirot, each containing 10 sub-levels (10x10=100).</note>. For one should not say that the number decreases as it goes up, or that it is only nine when going down. Rather, it is like a circle that does not rise above nine, yet the Grace becomes 100. Rather, it must be the secret of the Direct Light from top to bottom being nine, and the Reflected Light from bottom to top being nine. Even though all the lights are as one point... the difference between the light that ascends from one source and the light that turns back from another source is this: in the Kingdom, all ten are included; in the Foundation, nine; in Majesty <note>The Sefirah of *Hod*.</note>, eight; and so on through all the Sefirot. There is also a distinction between the direct lights and the "turned" lights. For the Direct Light is the essence of the Foundation standing outside, and every Reflected Light is secondary to it and does not compare to the Direct Light. This is like the stones of a wall that do not block the source. The light is an offspring of the source... the light is bound and fused to the existing Sefirot. Likewise, the light that is drawn from the souls to the spirits will not be shaken, but rather expands to provide space for Grace. According to how they receive it, so shall be its measure.

# Pomegranate Juice &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gate 11: The Splendors

In truth, our Sages of blessed memory <note>Hebrew: *Chazal*</note> wrote that with a change, there will be a change. These Splendors <note>Hebrew: *Tzahtzahot*; refers to three primordial, hidden lights that exist above the first Sefirah, Keter (Crown).</note> are meant to reach a state of rest... for the intentions regarding the Splendors are connected to the source... and the Splendors of the "Secret of the Weights" are learned from this. Some explain that in the *Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkunei HaZohar*, a classic Kabbalistic text.</note> it is noted that on the Day of Atonement <note>Hebrew: *Yom Kippur*</note>, the wine... and these Splendors explain the **Kingdom** <note>The Sefirah of *Malkhut*.</note> as well. In the **Foundations** <note>The Sefirah of *Yesod*.</note>, the Splendors of the Splendors... and the three lines are like a wing which is the Foundation, which receives the voice. And the main part of the Splendors is divided among the three lines... this is called the "Voice of Unity" regarding the Hidden One and the World.

And these Splendors of the Splendors... in the **Kingdom**... it is called the "Voice of the Crown" regarding the verse "and the Levite stood" [referring to] the service of the Levite in **Understanding** <note>The Sefirah of *Binah*.</note>. It is called the "Voice of Unity" regarding the hidden realm, and the "Voice of Revelation" regarding the specific unifications. This is explained in the *Zohar* in the section of the *Yanuqa* <note>The "Child" prodigy mentioned in the Zohar.</note> on the verse: "In that day living waters shall go out from Jerusalem" [Zechariah 14:8]. "Living" refers to the Ancient Life <note>Hebrew: *Chayyim HaKadmonim*</note>... and the "Voice" on that day is the **Kingdom**. These Splendors follow the beginning of the thought, rising to **Wisdom** <note>The Sefirah of *Chokhmah*.</note> through the letter *Yod*, and the end of the action is in the **Kingdom**. Note that all these unifications... indicate the initial unification... and this is the "ascending to the house of her father," meaning the unification of the Splendors... through the windows of the divine flow. There are twenty-two types of white milk <note>A metaphor for the purity of the divine flow (Shefa).</note> flowing from the **Understanding**... "Jerusalem" signifies the twenty-two decorations... the "Ancient Sea" is **Understanding**, which is a "reversing light" <note>Hebrew: *Or HaMit'hapekh*</note>... and the "Last Sea" is the end of the flow to prepare the lower beings...

### Chapter 4: And With
From what has been clarified regarding the intention of the *Tikkunim*... they are intended to raise the *Sefirot* <note>The ten divine emanations through which God interacts with the universe.</note> to **Understanding** and even higher. Through this, greatness increases in the world by way of the "Great Unification" on the right side. All the "branches" <note>The secondary spiritual forces or extensions of the Sefirot.</note> rise to the **Understanding**. When the Splendors rise to the right, to receive the flow, the light will not be hidden... as mentioned in the *Tikkunim* regarding the "Great Palace." The branches and the Splendors withdraw their expansion entirely and return to their root. Thus, everything returns to its correction... as it is written, "If He sets His heart upon man, if He gathers unto Himself his spirit and his breath" [Job 34:14]. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Hebrew: *Rashbi*, the traditional author of the Zohar.</note> explained this in the *Tikkunim*... all three of these levels receive holiness from the "Highest Point," which is the **Crown**. The *Rashbi* emphasized that in the **Crown**, there is no "holy" in the singular sense, but it is the "Holy of Holies." When the light rises to the **Crown**, it becomes most holy. This is the secret of the "Thin Firmament" <note>Hebrew: *Raqia HaDaq*</note> that clothes the **Kingdom**, which acts on the living... so that in all the *Sefirot*, the action is to receive flow so they do not become empty... for their Splendors are arranged in the *Tikkunim*.
