# Gate Fifteen: From Bottom to Top

### Chapter 1: In Explanation
Regarding the continued, returning, surrounding, and touching flow: Know that just as the *Sefirot* are ten and extend downward in their order—**Crown, Wisdom, Understanding, Greatness, Power, Beauty, Victory, Majesty, Foundation, and Kingdom**—so too they exist from the bottom to the top. **Crown** is within **Kingdom**, **Wisdom** is within **Foundation**, **Understanding** is within **Majesty**, **Greatness** <note>Also called *Chesed* (Mercy/Kindness).</note> is within **Victory**, **Power** <note>Also called *Gevurah* (Severity/Judgment).</note> is within **Beauty** <note>Also called *Tiferet*.</note>, and **Beauty** is within **Power**. **Victory** is within **Greatness**, **Majesty** is within **Understanding**, **Foundation** is within **Wisdom**, and **Kingdom** is within **Crown**. 

This is the explanation of the "expanding and reaching" light. That which reaches the **Kingdom** is bound and returns to its source. The initial expansion of the light is called "Direct Light" <note>Hebrew: *Or Yashar*</note>, and from the bottom up it is called "Reversing Light" <note>Hebrew: *Or HaMit'hapekh*</note> or "Reflected Light" <note>Hebrew: *Or Chozer*</note>. This is the secret of the "Ten Sefirot" as they are arranged... **Kingdom** in **Crown**. Each one stands against the other... returning and directing to the **Foundation**. From here is the descent of the first light... so that the light will always return and produce "light within light" and "light to light" without end. Everything is connected: the "end is in the beginning and the beginning is in the end," as we have said. In the secret of Direct and Reflected Light, this is the secret of the "Living Creatures" <note>Hebrew: *Chayot*; the angelic beings in Ezekiel's vision who "ran and returned."</note>. The letter *Yod* of the name represents the thirty levels of Direct Light, and the lower *Yod* represents the thirty levels of Reflected Light. This is how the *Rashbi* explained it... "He tells the end from the beginning" [Isaiah 46:10]. The upper *Yod* (10) represents the Direct Light, and the *He* that is split represents the Reflected Light.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 1: Already
We mentioned that the emanation of the **Direct Light**—which spreads from above to below in ten levels—gains a state in the **Kingdom**. From there, it returns and rises through the same levels in reverse: **Crown** in **Kingdom**, **Wisdom** in **Foundation**, until the **Kingdom** returns to the **Crown**. 

This is similar to a sunbeam shining into a polished mirror <note>Hebrew: *Asis* or *Mar'ah*; a classic metaphor for how divine light hits the "floor" of creation and bounces back.</note>, which then reflects back toward its source. Also, after this, "to the place where the streams flow, there they return to go" [Ecclesiastes 1:7], circling back even many times. Not only this, but from the **Kingdom** that sparkled in the **Crown**, ten lights spread downward, and they too rise and fall through those same levels without limit, as light emanates to light, over and over.

**And by this**, one can also examine [the flow] from the **Crown** to each of the other seven attributes. For each one receives and then turns its face upward. The **Reflected Light** from a "mirror that does not shine" <note>Hebrew: *Aspaklaria she-eina m'ira*; usually refers to the Sefirah of Malkhut.</note> differs from the light reflected from a "shining mirror" <note>Hebrew: *Aspaklaria ha-me'irah*; usually refers to Tiferet or the higher Sefirot.</note> or a medium one. One must observe the laws of the colors <note>In Kabbalah, each Sefirah is associated with a specific color (e.g., White for Chesed, Red for Gevurah).</note> mentioned previously. The light returns likewise from **Kingdom** to **Wisdom**, or to **Understanding**, or to **Mercy**, and so on to all of them. Each one is a source for what is beneath it. Even within a single *Sefirah*, one can distinguish between different aspects and levels of its composition. Thus, the lights are found to be moving and multiplying into infinite aspects and worlds.

# Juice of Pomegranates: Gate 11, The Splendors

Regarding the word *Emanation* <note>Hebrew: *Atzilut*, referring to the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah.</note> and the answer to "with whom shall these parts be," it is through the Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God.</note> that one reaches the ultimate purpose. Therefore, it was through the tribe of Levi, the "joined one," because in the emanation of the *Splendors* <note>Hebrew: *Tzachzachot*, three hidden, translucent lights that precede the Sefirot.</note> which dwell in the secret of the eight, with the Splendors... and now the secret of the matters... and the emanation of the garment within it. Do not think emanation is in vain; rather, it is the Holy Congregation <note>Hebrew: *Kahalat Yaakov*</note> when it calls out, for in these are the "thorns" <note>A reference to the decorative flourishes on Hebrew letters, often holding deep mystical secrets.</note> that signify the secrets of the emanation of these hidden lights.

These emanations are also in the Kingdom <note>Hebrew: *Malkhut*, the lowest Sefirah.</note> and in our Rabbis’ words, its shadows are the Splendors. Their secret is the secret of the *Foundation* <note>Hebrew: *Yesod*</note> that is received, which is the emanation of the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*</note>. Its essence is the Divine Will. Its emanation bows to it and receives the secret of the thorns. Regarding the weak emanation within it, it is called the "day of visitation"; the word *pazak* <note>A technical term used here to imply hiddenness.</note> indicates concealment and hiddenness. This is the emanation of the Splendors, for Understanding <note>Hebrew: *Binah*</note> dwells in the emanation of the "Point" <note>The letter *Yod*.</note> mentioned in the secret of the Zohar on the verse "and the Levite shall stand." This means the service of the Levite is rooted in Understanding <note>Binah is often associated with the "left side" and the Levites.</note>.

It is called a "portion," which indicates hiddenness, while the definite article "the" indicates the revelation of the attributes within it. This is explained in the Zohar in the section of the "Child" <note>Hebrew: *Yanuqa*, a famous section of the Zohar where a wonder-child reveals deep secrets.</note> on the verse regarding Understanding: "it contains these." From this, we establish "from Jerusalem to the Ancient Days." The "Child" interpreted that Understanding and Kingdom are linked to their emanation. The "End of the Action" was originally in the "Initial Thought" <note>A classic Kabbalistic principle: *Sof ma'aseh be-machshavah techilah*.</note>, which is high up in Wisdom <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</note>, and the "End of the Action" is in the emanation of the attributes. The definite article "the" points to the revealed emanation, while the hidden part points to the concealed emanation. This is her ascent to "her father's house," fixed in the emanation of the Splendors, which is the emanation of the letter *Yod* in the externality of the flow of Understanding.

## Chapter 4: With what has been explained, one can understand how the foundations were designated to raise the Sefirot to
-> Understanding, and even higher, to the "Great Jubilee" <note>Hebrew: *Yovel HaGadol*, a term for the Sefirah of Binah (Understanding), signifying total liberation and return to the source.</note> where the branches return to their root in Understanding. <-

This is because when an attribute <note>Hebrew: *Middah*, synonymous with a Sefirah.</note> ascends to receive the flow, it withdraws. Every emanation, in its proper order, is included in the Great Jubilee. The branches and the extremities of their expansion are completely gathered back to their source, and they ascend. In this way, everything returns to being one. As it is written: "He gathers His spirit and His soul unto Himself" <note>Job 34:14</note>. This was also explained by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero <note>The "Ramak," the 16th-century master of this system.</note> in the secret of the sacrifices: the elevation of the "Crown" <note>Hebrew: *Keter*</note> and the "Foundation" <note>Hebrew: *Yesod*</note>. All three levels receive holiness from the Supernal Ancient One, which is the Crown. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar.</note> was asked: Is the Crown called "Holy" or "Holy of Holies"? He answered that the attribute of Beauty <note>Hebrew: *Tiferet*</note>, when it ascends to the Crown, is what becomes "Holy" through the flow of the "Holy of Holies." This is the secret of the Firmament that spreads out in the revealed emanation, which the verse calls "Heaven." Similarly, in all the Sefirot, when their function is to receive flow, they withdraw entirely, for their emanation and their form are hidden in the secret.

# Gate Fifteen: From Bottom to Top

### Chapter 1: Explaining the inversions and the "Returning Light." Know that
-> Just as we mentioned: a gate that ascends from the bottom <-

In their order, from the flow above: Crown <note>Keter</note> is in Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note>, Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> is in Foundation <note>Yesod</note>, Understanding <note>Binah</note> is in Glory <note>Hod</note>, Greatness <note>Gedulah/Chesed</note> is in Victory <note>Netzach</note>, Power <note>Gevurah</note> is in Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, and Beauty is in Power, and Victory is in Greatness, and Glory is in Understanding, and Foundation is in Wisdom, and Kingdom is in Crown. This is the structure of the flow that spreads out. When it reverses and returns to its essence, the expansion from above is called "Direct Light" <note>Hebrew: *Or Yashar*</note>, and the expansion from below is called "Reflected Light" <note>Hebrew: *Or Chozer*</note>. This is the secret of the Sefirot returning to their totality. When Kingdom is in Crown, it is called a "Return." From here begins its descent. This "Returning Light" of the Kingdom ascends through the worlds until it reaches the infinite. Everything is a matter of the "End being wedged in the Beginning" and the "Beginning in the End."

<column-break/>

### Chapter 1: We have already mentioned that the emanation of Direct Light spreads
-> from top to bottom through ten degrees, establishing <-
a state for itself in the Kingdom. From there, it returns and ascends through the order of levels: Crown in Kingdom and Wisdom in Foundation, until the Kingdom returns to the Crown. This is like the
**reflection of the sun's spark shining in a polished mirror** <note>Hebrew: *Aspaklaria*, a common metaphor for how divine light is mediated and reflected.</note>, which turns back to its source. Furthermore, "to the place where the emanated ones go, there they return to go," circling back even many times. Not only this, but from the Kingdom that is sparked in the Crown, ten lights spread downward, and they too ascend and descend through those same degrees without limit, as light emanates to light.

In this way, one also examines the Crown in relation to each of the other six attributes. For each one receives and turns its face upward. The **Reflected Light** from a "mirror that does not shine" <note>Hebrew: *Aspaklaria she-eina me'ira*, usually referring to the Sefirah of Malkhut.</note> differs from the light reflected from a "shining mirror" <note>Referring to higher Sefirot like Tiferet.</note> or a medium one. The laws of the colors <note>Each Sefirah is traditionally associated with a color: e.g., white for Chesed, red for Gevurah.</note> mentioned previously must be preserved. The light also returns from Kingdom to Wisdom, or to Understanding, or to Kindness, and so to all of them, for each is a source for what is below it. Thus, the lights are found to be moving and multiplying into countless aspects and worlds.

It uses the metaphor of a polished mirror to describe how these lights interact and multiply across different levels of reality.</summary>

<meta>The previous page introduced the concept of the "Splendors" (Tzachzachot) and how the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) acts as a conduit between the hidden upper realms and the manifest lower world. This page continues that exploration by detailing the fifth, sixth, and seventh reasons for the movement of Divine light, specifically focusing on the "Returning Light" (Or Chozer) that ascends from the created world back to the Creator.</meta>

# Slice of the Pomegranate: Gate 15, From Bottom to Top / Essence of Pomegranates <note>Title refers to the works of Moshe Cordovero, a 16th-century Kabbalist. "Essence of Pomegranates" (*Asis Rimonim*) is a commentary/abridgment of his primary work.</note>

It begins with merit first, and then the return in reverse, as we mentioned in the previous chapter. **The fifth** is the equalization of the measures <note>The Sefirot, or Divine attributes.</note> which was explained at the end there. From all these perspectives, the statement in the *Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkuney Zohar*, a classic Kabbalistic text.</note> is verified: every existence where the Name <note>Y-H-V-H</note> rules over the Aleph <note>The first letter, representing unity or the source.</note> and the Vav-He <note>The latter letters of the Name</note> over the Yod <note>The first letter of the Name</note>—it is the Feminine <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingdom.</note> and it is Judgment. **The sixth** also causes the return of the light from bottom to top through the secret of withdrawal. For sometimes the light will return backward because there is no one doing good, and the Divine Presence withdraws its dwelling far from man. **The seventh** is a "reason for beauty" which will be explained in its own chapter to provide "space between the joined parts" <note>A phrase from the Talmud regarding the recitation of the Shema, here used to mean a conceptual pause.</note>.

## Chapter 4, Continued

We have a seventh reason in this beloved study, and it is in the secret of the "raising of the hands" <note>The Priestly Blessing.</note>. When one of the Divine attributes receives an extra measure of flow <note>Hebrew: *Shefa*, the spiritual energy emanating from the Divine.</note>, it only bestows what is naturally ingrained within it for the sake of maintaining the existence that was established prior to that extra measure. When it bestows that extra flow, it only receives what is necessary for its own existence. **Therefore**, they said in the *Zohar* and the *Bahir* <note>The primary foundational texts of Kabbalah.</note> that it is forbidden for us to pray with raised hands for more than three hours. This is because the *Malkhut* <note>The lowest Sefirah, Kingship.</note> is called "Hour," and she receives her existence from the three <note>The three upper Sefirot: Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding.</note> during those three hours. Therefore, Moses our Teacher had to rest his hands during the war against Amalek to allow space so that the "six edges of above" <note>The six emotional Sefirot: Mercy, Strength, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, and Foundation.</note> could bestow light through the Supreme Crown, which includes the three upper sources. Then Amalek would seek to prevail against his will by claiming that the lower beings had stopped praying. But from Heaven, they will have double mercy for the opposite reason: the "prosecution" becomes a complete "defense." For one who nullifies his own will for the sake of Heaven’s will is assured that the will of others will be nullified before his own. **However**, it is only called "extra" if it is newly generated from now on. What is renewed from ancient merit returns to the receiver in a state of goodness. For the one who gives with a "generous eye" does not claim credit for himself. It is written, "and it was in his eyes..." <note>Likely referring to Jacob's love for Rachel, where years seemed like days.</note> because his whole salvation and desire is to give, and return, and give again. When the Sefirot are awakened upward to suckle the flow of "sevenfold will," the lower beings are satisfied with what is prepared for them—this is the aspect of Judgment. When the Divine Presence is among the lower beings, it is a "Higher Need," for it does not just receive extra flow, but actually requires it. This is only true within the Seven Sefirot of Construction <note>The lower seven Sefirot that build the manifest world.</note>. However, from there and above, it is the secret of the "river that never ceases." It always goes out from Eden to water its plants by the power of the High One who is needed by it, to cling to Him in a oneness and joy that never separate.

->The Gate<-

<column-break/>

The secret of receiving the Direct Light and the Returning Light. Here is a correction regarding the language of the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) within Wisdom (*Chokhmah*). For the letter *He* is an acronym, and furthermore, the entire Emanation and every revelation at the end of the world is called *Shekhinah*. This is because the primary revelation and expansion is through Understanding (*Binah*). Likewise, in the name *Y-H-D-V-N-H-Y* <note>A mystical weaving of the names Y-H-V-H and Adonai.</note> there are eight letters for the eight Sefirot from *Binah* downwards, as explained by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (may his memory be a blessing) in the *Tikkunim* on the verse "Prayer passed before God." (The matter is that the *Yod* and *Dalet* of the point are the *Shekhinah*). This matter was explained in the *Zohar*, section *Vayechi*, on the secret of Leah and her children versus Rachel and her children. Leah hints at *Binah* (Understanding) and Rachel at *Malkhut* (Kingship). The first four sons of Leah represent the four primary "legs of the Chariot." The letter *Lamed* is for the *He*, the fourth son for *Malkhut*, the fourth leg, etc., as it says, "and she stopped giving birth." For from Jerusalem and below is the "World of Separation," for from there it separates. Those born from there, even though they are unified with the four in the secret of the "two thighs" joined with the four legs of the Chariot. The children of the handmaids are the four crowns connected with the *Aleph*. There are the children of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin. Rachel’s children represent the secret of the preservation of the *Foundation* (*Yesod*) for the birthing mothers... in two aspects. So too in the hint and secret of the twenty-two women born from Rachel and Leah... the first writing is the ancient one, which is the Union, and then the connection flows. The lower "wine" passes through it in the secret of the Returning Light through contemplation... upward. The second writing is the flow from it, and this is in the "Two Kingships" through which the twenty-two <note>The 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet.</note> pass. This is from the "wine of the worlds" in the secret of the Direct Light and the "Presence of Presences." Then in this *Crown* is the secret of the Union, the tree of Emanation. Direct Light precedes the lines. Joseph hints at the first writing in the secret of Direct Light, whose "right hand" will connect unless the Returning Light is present. This is why it says, "May the Lord add (*Yosef*) another son for me." Benjamin is the secret of the Returning Light in the second aspect. This is the "heritage of my soul," similar to "To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul." Because he is in the secret of the light that is renewed and prays from bottom to top, he is in the World of Separation. This is only for the one who believes in him, in Joseph, being from the power of Jacob... Therefore his mother called him by that name, "Son of my Sorrow," but his father called him "Benjamin" <note>Son of the Right Hand/Strength.</note>. Even though in the Returning Light, in the secret of the "filling," he is "behold and return," he will take hold, for they return and expand from there and below, and it is "Direct," etc. When Joseph passes there, Benjamin is with his father in the place of Joseph... it was a matter of light and it turns over even within a single attribute.

### Chapter 5

Not only from Sefirah to Sefirah is there Direct Light and Returning Light, but even the letter *He* itself is divided within its body. Its division is increased; there is Direct Light and Returning Light. Not only this, but even the "Victorious Sefirah" <note>Netzach</note> that receives will be in the aspect of Direct and Returning Light. To this relates what we said in the *Tikkunim*: "six sons of *Dalet*"... hinting at the secret of the order of the points like this: *Yod-He-Vav-He*. Those who know the secret will learn in the *Supreme Crown* (*Keter*) which is the head of the "Male World." The matter is that after we explained that the business of the "writings" in the secret of Direct Light and Returning Light consists of additions and supplements, it must be that every single Sefirah is a supplement to itself, from the "Crown" within it to the "Kingship" within it. The light will return within its very essence and turn over from the "Kingship" within it to the "Crown" within it. And behold, certainly in the *Supreme Crown* there will be an aspect that is received from the "Highest Root" within it, which will bestow, and the *Vav* is added to the *Dalet* so that the world does not lack the flow from the side of the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), may He be blessed, who is hidden within it. This "writing" will never ascend as a "Name" forever because of its proximity to the "Calling." For just as it is called to be as a Name, so within it, it will not be related as a Name. This "Point," because it was always written for "Justice"—what is man that he should have within him a lacking aspect that receives from this aspect? It is the aspect of the "Female," and the flow which is the aspect of the "Writing," and this is supplemented in the "Reed of Mentioning" to be a "Beam of Writing" to receive and to bestow. Therefore there will be a "Bet" above... and the reception of the lights was in the "Finality" from him... to bestow. And so in the "Reed" it is supplemented so that the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) and Understanding (*Binah*) are related in the "Finality," and by the power of this, she will not feel anything or any creature except by seeing a thing and the intention...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Seventh Reason for the movement of Divine Light, specifically the "Returning Light" (Or Chozer), which moves from the lower realms back toward the Source. It builds upon the previous page’s introduction of the Sefirot (Divine emanations) and their dynamic interactions.</meta>

# Essence of Pomegranates: Gate 15, From Bottom to Top / Slice of the Pomegranate <note>Asis Rimonim (Essence of Pomegranates) is a 16th-century Kabbalistic summary of Moshe Cordovero's Pardes Rimonim.</note>

The Returning Light <term>Or Chozer: light that reflects back from a "vessel" or receiver toward the source</term> and through it, the ten Sefirot <note>The ten creative forces or attributes of God</note> are formed. This return originates from the Feminine <note>Nukvah/Malkhut, the lowest Sefirah</note> which acts as the receiver. This is the secret of the light that goes back and ascends, becoming hidden until it reaches the Foundation (*Yesod*). From there, it expands upward from the Foundation to Kindness (*Chesed*). It continues to cycle, expanding through the spheres of the world and the twelve constellations. Because the Returning Light from the Kingdom (*Malkhut*) to Kindness is like an arched back returning from the Foundation, it establishes the six planets that receive and the twelve constellations in their glory. Similarly, the Kingdom receives from the Foundation. This is the secret of the "End being wedged in the Beginning" <note>A classic phrase from Sefer Yetzirah meaning the lowest point of creation is linked back to the highest</note> for the "Blest" gives back more than the "Blesser," as the glory of the back of the Foundation is for itself, whereas the Masculine and Feminine are like Kindness in its place. When the "lights" are revealed, it is through the thinness that is drawn upward; therefore, it must return to its original place. Anything that is drawn out of its place exerts a strong force to return, like a heated stone. This is the reason for the "overturning" of Judgment.

### Chapter 3, Continued
There is a general rule regarding the difference between Direct Light <term>Or Yashar: the descending flow of Divine energy</term> and Returning Light. They are opposites, for Direct Light represents the level of higher things, the act of bestowing and being considered Mercy (*Rachamim*). Returning Light—which is the secret of the Feminine and the "Surrounding Foundation"—represents the one who bestows upward, which is characterized as Judgment (*Din*). This is because when the Feminine turns her face to receive, she bestows; and when the Masculine bestows, he does not receive. This matter applies to all the Sefirot: while a Sefirah is bestowing, it is not receiving, and while it is receiving, it cannot bestow. We find this in the *Book of the Pious* <note>Sefer Hasidim</note>: it is forbidden to delay the "Raising of the Hands" <note>The Priestly Blessing, Birkat Kohanim</note> in prayer for more than three hours. The reason is that the raising of the hands signifies bestowing—as in the verse "And Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them" <note>Leviticus 9:22</note>. Because the Kingdom (*Malkhut*) is called "an hour" and receives from the three Patriarchs <note>Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, corresponding to the Sefirot of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet</note> who are the bestowers, she receives only for two hours. If the hands are held up longer, it becomes dangerous, because while she is expanding, she is not receiving, and afterward, one must wait until the "vessels" can receive the influence. This is the secret of "And when he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed" <note>Exodus 17:11</note>, for then she was receiving and not bestowing, which resulted in Judgment. Even though the Sefirot are not limited by time, we use hours in the lower world as a hint to the upper worlds. If these days were to sustain the King through the constellations, we must understand them well: when she is receiving, she is then bestowing, and then it is a "Day of Judgment." But this does not occur from the perspective of the lower beings, for the "Mighty Waters" stand to prevent the ascent of the light back to its source. All the power of Judgment exists so that the light may be more hidden. The transformation only occurs in this being, and when the light passes, the nights are overturned—as in the matter of "from there it was parted" <note>Genesis 2:10</note>, leaving the "distant ones" to multiply. The concentration occurs in the overturning, as in the secret of a building. At the time of the overturning, the bestowing acts like a Feminine turning her face to receive. This explains why the "Straight Lights" lead to Mercy and the "Returning Lights" lead to Judgment. The "Straight" lights indicate the light that bestows according to the order of levels from the start, where one bestows to the next. The "Overturning" hints at the Returning Light that receives. Regarding this, the *Zohar* says: "All day not a single drop fell on the [letter] Yod," as the lower ones are transformed, for the [letter] He is the secret of the six [directions] and so on.

### Chapter 4, And Also
In the *Book of the Brilliant* <note>Sefer HaBahir, one of the earliest Kabbalistic texts</note> this was given as an answer to the students' question regarding "Above and Below." They said: "Above we know, etc." This refers to the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note> who dwells above, and this Shekhinah is the light that is consumed. From the first light, the Sefirah of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) is produced, and so on. This means Wisdom is at the beginning and Wisdom is at the end, which is the letter *Bet* and the Judgment that is divided...

<column-break/>

...among them "mighty waters," and it is written, "With strength You answered the deep" <note>Psalm 77</note> until the Holy One, Blessed be He, rebuked them. Afterward, He promised them: "Since you have done this for My honor, the Upper Waters shall not have permission to sing praise until the Lower Waters speak first," as it is said, "Above the voices of many waters... the Lord on high is mighty" <note>Psalm 93:4</note>.

### And the Essence
The main point of these matters is that when the Emanation (*Atzilut*) is revealed, it does not yearn for its source. It was necessary to equalize them through the secret of the Returning Light: "Its end is wedged in its beginning and its beginning in its end" <note>Sefer Yetzirah 1:7</note>, and its middle is wedged in both, like the appearance of the sun and its setting. Therefore, the essence of the Returning Light is "running" <note>Refers to the "running and returning" of the Chayot in Ezekiel 1</note> in order to equalize the Divine attributes. In the *Tikkunim* they said regarding the division "that which is for the sake of Heaven": The Lower Waters weep and say, "We wish to be before the King, the Cause of Causes," and they desire to ascend on high. This is the secret of equalizing them until the Cause of Causes makes them equal. This is the secret of the letter Aleph (*א*), with a Vav (*ו*) in the middle and a Yod (*י*) on this side and a Yod (*י*) on that side <note>The letter Aleph is visually composed of a diagonal Vav and two Yods</note>. These are all close to the Cause of Causes. This is the secret of the verse, "And God made the two great lights" <note>Genesis 1:16</note>—they were equal, as it is written: "And the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun" <note>Isaiah 30:26</note>.

### Chapter 3, Explained
It has been explained from what preceded that the essence of the Emanation is the Direct Light, whose quality is Higher Mercy, bestowing in the secret of the Masculine. The Returning [Light] derives its strength from one of the receivers; its quality is Lower Judgment, receiving in the secret of the Feminine. Thus, the World of Emanation is "a ladder set on the ground with its top reaching the heavens" <note>Genesis 28:12</note>, possessing a power equal to a thing and its opposite. "And behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it." This is for several reasons:

**First**, because the Direct is the "Kindness of God" that was not preceded by human merit. But the Returning Light is adorned according to the speech of human beings; it is the "small portion of the much" that we owe to the Place <note>God</note>.

**Second**, because the Direct Light comes in a rush, for all its conduct is like a mouth that gives. But the Returning Light follows the law of the balances, ascending according to the preparation of the lower beings. Regarding this, the verse says: "To make a weight for the wind and He meted out the waters by measure" <note>Job 28:25</note>.

**Third**, it was due to the abundance of His kindness, may He be blessed, that the servant should hope for a reward in exchange for his service, even though he is already obligated to it. However, the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not desire our obligation according to His power and His benefits toward us, but rather according to our own human strength. A righteous person who has stood in a trial is assured that "his reward is with him and his work before him" <note>Isaiah 40:10</note>. The prophet said a great thing: "You, O Lord, are our Father," like a man who desires children and has pleasure in them. In His mercy, He returned to Isaac, who saved his children from Judgment through the merit of the Binding <note>The Akedah</note>. He treated the Mercy of the Place like a man who carries a burden and said to him: "Take half and I will take half" <note>A Talmudic quote where Isaac negotiates with God to reduce the punishment of Israel</note>. Similarly, regarding the "Delight of the Sabbath": "Lend to Me and I will pay back." Likewise: "I remember for you the kindness of your youth" <note>Jeremiah 2:2</note>. It is clear from this that although the Direct Light is Kindness from its root, He nevertheless "thinks thoughts" so that the success of human action is considered a kindness from the lower beings toward Him. Therefore, the righteous person who is commanded and performs his obligation will be, so to speak, in the Divine presence, taking his reward from the side of Judgment.

**Fourth**, because the Direct Light is open...

<meta>This page continues the mapping of the spiritual realms, transitioning from the World of Formation (Yetzirah) into the World of Action (Asiyah). It discusses how Divine light descends through these layers and the specific spiritual status of the Land of Israel compared to other nations.</meta>

# Slice of the Pomegranate: Gate 15, I will bring the juice of my pomegranates <note>This title is a poetic reference to the Song of Songs, used here to title a section of Kabbalistic commentary by Moshe Cordovero or his students.</note>

And Metatron, the Prince of the Face <note>Metatron is a primary angel in Kabbalistic lore, often described as the celestial scribe or the "lesser YHVH," acting as a bridge between the Infinite and the finite</note>, is appointed over them in the "heart of the body," from which all the limbs draw their nourishment. Within them, the Supreme Light also clothes itself after it has already been clothed in the World of Creation <term>Beriyah: the second of the four spiritual worlds, associated with the throne of God</term>. These are called the Ten Sefirot of Formation <term>Yetzirah: the world of angels and spiritual forms</term>. The name "Formation" comes from the word for "designing" or "shaping," which brings the hidden potential of existence into a more revealed state.

# Chapter 2: The World of Action

The name "Action" <term>Asiyah: the lowest of the four worlds, encompassing both the physical universe and its immediate spiritual source</term> comes from the phrase "I have made it in secret" or "the work of a craftsman's hands." This world includes the ten shells <term>Kelipot: "husks" or "shells" that represent the forces of concealment and spiritual impurity</term>, as well as the firmaments, the constellations, and every detail of the Work of Creation down to the Great Abyss. The light that extends there from the World of Formation is referred to as the Ten Sefirot of Action as it clothes itself in ten holy branches to subdue the "shells." For there is no desire for the world to be led solely by the mechanics of "Action." This is the secret behind the sages' statement, "Anyone who dwells outside the Land of Israel is like one who has no God." <note>original: "כל הדר בחוצה לארץ כישראל שאין לו אלקי'" - a quote from the Talmud, Ketubot 110b</note>. This is because the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term>, which clothes itself in the Land of Israel sometimes as the Throne and sometimes as an angel, governs through them directly. However, in the "garments" of foreign lands, the governance occurs only through the "shells," and she "treads upon their high places" only to subdue them and nothing more. **But** in the Land of Israel, the "shells" are not permitted to enter; they are kept far away because "the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it" <note>Deuteronomy 11:12</note>. As explained in the Section of Vayakhel <note>A portion of the Zohar</note>, there are dividing partitions between the firmament of the Land of Israel and the firmaments of other lands. For two thousand cubits around these partitions, the shells are given no permission to enter. Even acts of strict judgment in the Land of Israel are carried out by an angel from the branches of the World of Formation, who clothes himself temporarily in fierce wrath or death—may the Merciful One save us. Regarding the state of exile in foreign lands, we have learned: "Pray for the welfare of the government," for were it not for the fear of it, the lower crowns <note>The spiritual powers governing the nations</note> would swallow one another alive. **And** it is a general rule that the light does not extend from the essence of the Sefirot to Formation or Action unless it clothes itself in the order of the levels: Creation first, then Formation, and then Action. However, it is possible for the world to be governed by the World of Formation while the World of Action is "conquered" before it. This occurs in the Land of Israel on weekdays, or during the time of exile when the King wears "weekday garments" to manage the world's labor and service. Through these, He covers the "Sabbath garments," which are the branches of the World of Creation that are seen only on Sabbaths and Festivals. At those times, the righteous are crowned with an "Additional Soul" <term>Neshamah Yeterah: an extra level of spiritual awareness granted on the Sabbath</term>, and the light is revealed from within the royal garment, while the weekday garments are conquered before it.

### Chapter 3: And However
Regarding the two lower worlds, we have a physical model of their governance in this material life, hinted at in the three parts of the Tabernacle: the Courtyard and the Tent. The World of Action is represented by the Courtyard, where the "slaughterers" <note>Priests/Levites</note> look toward the outer Altar. This hint refers to the "fitness of action" in general for all creatures of the world. Within it are all the partitions of skins for entering and exiting, for the laying of hands, the slaughtering, and the waving of the offerings—every man according to his task. **And** the Tent of Meeting, which is the Temple of the Lord: entry there was permitted only to the priests to prostrate themselves, to burn the fragrant incense, and for the needs of the inner sin-offerings, to arrange the Showbread on the Pure Table, and to tend the lamps. And the hint...

<column-break/>

...is one, and for the outer "cheek" and their pit, it is one. The explanation of "Kingship belongs to the Lord" refers to the "Secret Wisdom" as mentioned in previous introductions. Do not be surprised that today it is called "Holy King," for I have seen the King from the perspective of the limbs, which are the extensions of the essences within the Sefirot called "bones" or "limbs." So too, his "life-force" refers to his essence which extends into the Sefirot, giving them life from within, while the Sefirot themselves are the external aspect. Through the Sefirot, the secondary level and the "Chariot riders" of the Sefirot are unified with the Infinite, for they are not essences themselves but receive from the essence that expands through them. And the secret of "The King unified in His limbs" establishes our faith, our refuge, our service, and our prayer. For even though His essence cannot be described by any name, title, letter, or vowel point, nevertheless, through His garments that are unified with Him, we are able to describe and build the structures of the lower lights until we reach the level of titles and names for every single Sefirah. This is according to the actions that are drawn from Him. All the holy names are like "limbs" to His essence through His unified Sefirot. This is not the case in the World of Creation, and even more so in the World of Action, where there is no inherent power or might. Rather, the light extends into Creation and becomes hidden in a place where they are not unified in the same way. There, at the beginning, are the ten "letters" of the name *Adonai* <note>The name of God associated with lordship and the physical world</note>. I saw that the angel Akatriel <note>original: אכתריאל - An angel whose name means "Crown of God," often associated with the manifestation of God on the Throne</note> is the Prince of the World of Creation, and upon him are these names which include all ten Sefirot. For the letter *Yod* includes the first three, and the *Vav* includes the six directions... and the name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty</note> which is the sign of the Covenant on his flesh. This world itself is included in Kingship (*Malkhut*), which is the name *Adonai*. It says in the *Ra'aya Mehemna* <note>A section of the Zohar</note> that at the time of the "pomegranate" <note>referring to a spiritual state or time</note>, the steps of mercy are returned to the attributes while they are within the World of Creation.

This is the strength of the governance of the World of Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds, where the light is pure and unified with God</term> as it arose in His will to create secondary beings and matters through the way of Creation—meaning, in a more revealed and "thick" manner than the levels of Emanation. These are all included as one, and it is what is called by the name "The Glory." In the language of the Zohar, these are "Thrones." This is the meaning of the verse "In the beginning," which refers to Kingship (*Malkhut*), which is called "Beginning." "He created" refers to the World of Creation. "God" (*Elohim*) refers to the dwelling of the "Small Face" <note>Zeir Anpin: the emotional attributes of God</note> within the World of Creation from the perspective of Kingship. These are the Ten Sefirot of Emanation. Furthermore, the masters of the Mishnah said that the Sefirot are called by the name "YHVH," while the "Thrones" and "Chairs" of Emanation were created... and the name *Adonai* is the "opening" and the "door" for them to be included up to the ten levels... so they will be included from the ten levels of Emanation. And so the faithful shepherd <note>Moses, as referred to in the Zohar</note> said: the Crown is the "Cause of Causes," and from it the "Thrones" are made.

# Gate Sixteen: ABYA <note>ABYA is an acronym for the four spiritual worlds: Atzilut (Emanation), Beriyah (Creation), Yetzirah (Formation), and Asiyah (Action).</note>

As explained in the "Gate of Names and the Throne," and in the work *Strength of Yah* <note>original: "Hosen Yah"</note>, the "Revealing of the Hands" refers to the manifestation of divine power within the realm of the *Ra'aya Mehemna* <note>The "Faithful Shepherd," a section of the Zohar attributed to the soul of Moses</note>. It is said that in the future, the Divine is destined to withdraw from all creatures, just as the light withdrew to the place of the letter *Yod* of the Name. Originally, the "Beard of the Ancient One" <note>A Kabbalistic metaphor for the flow of divine mercy through thirteen channels or "locks" of hair</note> consisted of thirteen paths of mercy and merit. But now, it has withdrawn, and the two "hidden eyes" look upon all with mercy. This is the secret of the concealment: the "Revealing of the Hands" is higher than the "Revealing of the Alephs" <note>The letter Aleph often represents the first, most hidden movement of the Infinite</note>. Through the "Aleph," the light becomes a "Trace" <note>original: "Reshimah," a faint impression of light left after the initial withdrawal of the Infinite</note>. Furthermore, in the *Tikunim* <note>The Tikunei HaZohar, a classic Kabbalistic text</note>, it is explained that the "Revealing of the Hands" was a state of erasure, while the "Revealing of the Alephs" was a state of unification, both being hidden within the "Chariots." With what we have explained, there is no difficulty at all.

These words "emerged in royal garments." ## The Sixteenth Gate: ABYA

### Chapter 1: On the Explanation of ABYA

Know that the word **Atzilut** (Emanation) is derived from the expression "And I will draw <note>original: "ve-atzalti"</note> from the spirit." Its essence is that between the **Emanation** <gloss>the world of Atzilut</gloss> and the **Emanator** <gloss>the Infinite Source</gloss>, the relationship is like that of "lighting one candle from another." The source candle loses nothing by lighting the second, nor was the second candle part of the first before it was lit. The language of "drawing near" <note>original: "etzel"</note> indicates a profound Clinging <term>Dveikut: a state of intense spiritual attachment to the Divine</term>. Therefore, the qualities of the "Seventy Elders" who were with Moses <note>original: "MaR'aH"</note> are attributed to the language of Atzilut, for they were joined to him in an endless Clinging. This is why the verse says, "And I will draw from the spirit that is upon you," using the preposition "from," to show that it did not diminish his own light. This is a profound mystery.

**Creation** <note>original: "Beriyah"</note> refers to that which was previously hidden and now begins to move toward "distancing" and defined time. In common language, "Creation" implies something external, like a vessel. This is why the Torah uses the language of Creation regarding the "thick earth," such as "And the Lord God formed <note>original: "yetzirah"</note> man from the dust of the ground." It refers to something more revealed. This is rooted in the verse: "Everyone who is called by My Name, for My glory I have created <note>Bera-tiv</note> him, I have formed <note>Yetzar-tiv</note> him, even I have made <note>Asit-iv</note> him." "Everyone called by My Name" refers to the level of Atzilut. For in Atzilut, the Divine Names and the *Sefirot* <note>The ten divine emanations or attributes</note> are in a state of absolute and complete Unity, with no separation at all.

### Chapter 2: To Understand

One must know that the World of the Sefirot are the unifications of the Infinite <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note>. The powers of the Infinite expand through "Concealments" until they are clarified in the World of Atzilut in three aspects: 1) The aspect of the Infinite itself; 2) The aspect of the "Concealment" of the light; 3) The aspect of the Sefirot themselves. These are unified together as one, as I wrote in the Gate of Names. In the *Tikunim*, it is written that the Ten Sefirot of Atzilut are unique, whereas in the Ten Sefirot of Beriyah, there is a sense of "Him and His life-force are one," but they are not the same level of absolute unity as in Atzilut.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 1: Atzilut

### It shall be said to them: 1. Impression, 2. Engraving, 3. Hewing, 4. Action.

The **Impression** <note>original: "Reshimah"</note> is a subtle existence that cannot be grasped. Similarly, the World of **Atzilut** is unified with its source. In its expansion, it becomes the root of "boundaries" for all the worlds below it. However, the beginning of this limitation is found in its very first stage. Just as the power of the Emanator is within the Emanated, and the source neither loses nor gains—like lighting one candle from another—so too all the branches multiply and expand in subtleness and spirituality while remaining attached to their root. Atzilut is also related to the word "beside" <note>original: "etzel"</note>, as in "beside the altar," meaning proximity and closeness. This is like the Elders who were influenced by the prophecy of Moses: "And they shall stand there with you, and I will draw from the spirit which is upon you and put it upon them."

**The World of Beriyah** (Creation) is called **Engraving** <note>original: "Chakikah"</note>. Just as an engraving is made with a stylus, this realm is more revealed than the "Impression." It is the **Throne of Glory**, the base and "garment" for the World of Atzilut. Therefore, its levels must also be ten, for there is no existence, large or small, that does not consist of ten parts. Because the branches of Atzilut clothe themselves there, they are called the "Ten Sefirot of Beriyah." It is not that they are additional Sefirot—Heaven forbid! Rather, they are the original Sefirot themselves which "become" Creation as they reach that level and clothe themselves in it. The word **Beriyah** (Creation) implies an existence that is "outside" <note>original: "bar," Aramaic for outside</note> the camp of the absolute Unity that is hidden in the "Camp of the Shekhinah." Thus, Creation implies a "break" or "separation," as in "if God creates <note>Bara</note> a new thing." This is hinted at in the phrase "In the beginning, God created" <note>original: "Bereshit Bara Elohim"</note>. Here, the Sages interpret "Bara" as "He tore" <note>original: "Kera"</note>. This explains the essential difference between the "Righteous" who enter "outside"—meaning they require a "partitioning garment" from the World of Beriyah—and the "Sons of Ascent" who unify with the sources of Atzilut without any veil at all, like the Patriarchs who were themselves the "Chariot." See more on this in *Pardes*, the end of Chapter 3, and in the book *Visions of God* <note>original: "Mar'ot Elohim"</note>, Part 1, Chapter 17.

**The World of Yetzirah** (Formation) is referred to as **Hewing** <note>original: "Chatzibah"</note>, like a stone hewn from a rock and shaped into a circle or square. Thus are the ten classes of angels who are distinct within it, hewn and influenced from beneath the Throne of Glory. Some take the form of flaming fire or subtle light. They carry the Throne, which in turn "carries its carriers." And Metatron...

# Slice of the Pomegranate: Gate 15, The Flow of the Juice of Pomegranates <note>The title "Pelah HaRimmon" (Slice of the Pomegranate) is a classic commentary by Rabbi Menahem Azariah da Fano on the "Pardes Rimmonim" by Moses Cordovero.</note>

And Metatron, the Prince of the Face <note>A high-ranking archangel who serves as the heavenly mediator</note>, is appointed over them in the "heart of the body" from which all the limbs draw their vitality. Within them, the Supernal Light is also clothed after it has already been clothed in the World of Creation. These are called the Ten Sefirot of Formation <note>Yetzirah</note>, a term related to "form" <note>original: tziyur</note>, which brings the potential existences into a state of revelation.

### Chapter 2: The World of Action <note>Asiyah</note>
This name is derived from the verse "I have made it in secret" <note>Isaiah 48:16</note>—the work of a master craftsman. It includes the ten *Kelipot* <note>The "shells" or "husks" that represent forces of concealment or impurity</note>, the firmaments, the constellations, and all the specific details of the Work of Creation down to the Great Abyss. The light that spreads there from the World of Formation is referred to as the Ten Sefirot of Action <note>Asiyah</note> as it clothes itself in ten holy branches to subdue the *Kelipot*. For the Divine has no desire for the world to be led solely through the realm of Action. This is the secret of the Sages' statement: "Anyone who dwells outside the Land of Israel is as if he has no God" <note>Ketubot 110b</note>. This is because the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence</note>, which clothes itself in the Land of Israel—sometimes in the "Throne" and sometimes in an "Angel"—leads the world through them, but in a way where they are merely a garment. However, <note>outside the Land</note> it is said that leadership occurs only through the *Kelipot*, though "it shall tread upon our high places" <note>Deuteronomy 33:29</note> to subdue them, and nothing more. **But in the Land of Israel,** the *Kelipot* are not permitted to enter; they are kept far away because "the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it" <note>Deuteronomy 11:12</note>. The Sages explained in the section *Vayakhel* <note>from the Zohar</note> that there are dividing partitions between the firmament of the Land of Israel and the firmaments of other lands. For two thousand cubits around these partitions, the *Kelipot* are given no permission to enter. Even acts of Judgment carried out in the Land of Israel are done by an angel from the branches of Formation, who clothes himself temporarily in "cruelty and wrath" <note>divine attributes of justice</note>, may the Merciful One protect us. Regarding the leadership during the Exile outside the Land, we have learned: "Pray for the welfare of the government" <note>Pirkei Avot 3:2</note>, for if not for the fear of it, the lower "crowns" <note>the forces of the Kelipot</note> would swallow one another alive. **And it is clear** that the light does not spread from the essence of the Sefirot to Formation or Action except by clothing itself in the order of the levels: Creation first, then Formation, and finally Action. However, it is possible for the world to be led through Formation while Action is suppressed before it; this occurs in the Land of Israel during a "favored time" <note>original: be-yamin rahul</note> or during the time of Exile when the King puts on weekday garments to lead the world according to its needs and labor. Within these, He hides the "Sabbath garments," which are the branches of the World of Creation, which are seen only on Sabbaths and Festivals. At those times, the righteous are crowned with an "Additional Soul," and the light is revealed from within the royal garment, and the "weekday garments" are suppressed before Him so they do not conceal Him. Indeed, the clothing within the World of Creation is necessary at all times to weaken the souls in this lower world from perceiving the light without a mediator.

### Chapter 3: But
Regarding the two lower worlds for which we have a parallel in our physical lives, they are hinted at in the three parts of the Tabernacle: the Courtyard, the Tent of Meeting, and the Holy of Holies. For behold, the Courtyard of the Tabernacle represents the World of Action, where the offerings are brought to the Most High on the Outer Altar. This hints at the rectitude of action in general among all creatures of the world. In it are all the partitions of the courtyards for entering and exiting, for the laying of hands <note>semichah</note>, for slaughtering, and for waving the offerings—each person according to his hand and every desire. **And the Tent of Meeting,** which is the Palace of God—entry there was permitted only to the Priests to prostrate themselves and to burn the incense of sweet spices, and for the needs of the inner sin-offerings, and to arrange the Showbread on the pure Table, and to trim the lamps. The hint here...

44 • He, His life-force, and His limbs are one <note>original Aramaic: "Ihu ve-chayohi ve-garmohi chad" — a central Zoharic tenet regarding the unity of God in the world of Atzilut</note>. The explanation of "The King and His Life" refers to the [Ten Sefirot], as proven previously. There is no wonder in this, for the verse says "The King" as a part of the King whose existence is from the King of Kings. "His limbs" refers to the aspect of the spreading of the light hinted at in the Sefirot. "His limbs" <unclear>MD BKON</unclear> what he does not possess, etc., according to the spreading light. There is no truth except above in the Sefirot of Emanation <note>Atzilut</note>. This is the "Place" that will be the whole, meaning the hidden light that spreads within the vessels. I shall not pray forever... it reaches everything in Creation, Formation, and Action, which are called by various names as explained. And so it is said: "The King who is glorified in the Crown of Glory" <unclear>TKIK HMUKTKON</unclear> and our coverings, our service, and our prayers. For even though in His own Being He cannot be described by a name, a nickname, a letter, or a vowel point, nevertheless, through His attributes that emanate from Him, we can describe and name the "shapes of the soul" of the species with nicknames and names. To every single Sefirah, we give a name according to the actions that flow from Him. All the holy names are within their structure—the Name of 42 letters, the Name of 30, and *Elohim*—they are all structures for His essence through His emanated Sefirot. This does not apply to the Worlds of Creation, Formation, and Action, which possess neither power nor might on their own. Katriel is the Prince of the World of Creation. It is said, as it were, that He had a "time of favor" and "May Your mercy suppress Your attributes"—meaning the spreading of mercy over the attributes as they live within the World of Creation.

### Chapter 3: And After
The life of the level of Emanation <note>Atzilut</note>, etc. It arose in His Will, blessed be He, to bring about the existence of the creatures and that which contains them by way of "Creation" <note>Beriyah</note>. That is to say, they are more revealed and "thicker" <note>more material/dense</note> than the levels of Emanation. They were all included as one, and this is what is called "The Glory" <note>Kavod</note>, and in the language of the Zohar, "The Throne" <note>Korsaya</note>. They interpreted the verse "In the beginning" <note>Bereishit</note> as referring to the Sefirah of *Malchut* (Kingdom), which is called *Be* ("in"). Through her, He brought about "Creation" <note>Bara</note>. *Elohim* is an acronym for "The Throne" <unclear>A"S A"S</unclear>. Creation is from the power of *Malchut*, and the "Throne" is the name for the Ten Sefirot of Emanation <note>when they descend to Creation</note>. Furthermore, they were established as two Sefirot called by the name of *Havayah* <note>YHWH</note> and the name of Divinity... and the name of the Throne is equal to "One Thousand" and is a garment for what will be... they descend until the ten levels of the "Children of the Palace," which descend from the ten levels of Emanation. And so it says in the *Ra'aya Mehemna*: "Afterwards He made a garment for these, which is the Throne..." it has four pillars and six steps to the Throne... and in general, "He is the Throne." This means that the Ten Sefirot of the Throne are supported by the pillars and the steps, and then they are the Ten Sefirot. Therefore he said, "The whole of it is the Throne," which consists of pillars and six steps...

While the previous page touched upon the lower worlds of Formation and Action, this section provides a formal definition of the "Emanation" (Atzilut) and establishes the hierarchy of the entire system using metaphors of writing and stone-cutting.</meta>

# Gate Sixteen: ABYA <note>ABYA is the foundational Kabbalistic acronym for the four levels of reality: Atzilut (Emanation), Beriah (Creation), Yetzirah (Formation), and Asiyah (Action).</note>

As explained in the Gate of Unity and Intention, and in the work *Hosen Yah* <note>original: "Hosen Yah," a reference to a Kabbalistic commentary</note>, the matter is summarized here. For here, the expansion returns to a revealed state... <note>The text here uses dense technical shorthand regarding the Divine Names and their numerical values (Gematria)</note>. The revealed hand is a sign of what is above it... the Voice is like the "Simple 45" <note>The Divine Name YHVH spelled out to equal the value of 45, associated with the human level</note>. In the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkuney Zohar</note>, it returns to explain that the "revealed hand" is a sign of the Comforter <note>original: Menachem</note>... regarding what we have written, there is no difficulty at all.

The Annotator says: Thus far, we have placed between two "half-moons" <note>parentheses or brackets used by the printer</note> the additions made by the pious Master, our teacher Rabbi M. <note>likely Rabbi Menachem Azariah da Fano</note> and from the teacher of the House of Yatza, who wrote in the "Garment of Royalty" <note>Levush Malkhut</note>. But from here onward, we have found the actual "Body of the Trees" <note>the core text of the Pardes Rimmonim</note> with his own additions without any special garment or sign, except for a distinction between wool and purple. We have said that "a person's will is his honor," and we have left it as such. May his merit stand for us, so that the "Moon" <note>symbolizing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> may be filled, and the verse fulfilled: "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" <note>Isaiah 30:26</note>, speedily in our days.

### Gate Sixteen: ABYA

### Chapter 1: On the Explanation
Know that the word *Atzilut* <note>Emanation</note> comes from the expression "And He took <note>original: va-ya'atzel</note> of the spirit" <note>Numbers 11:25</note>. Its meaning is that the Emanated comes from the Emanator, yet the Emanator loses nothing from the process of emanation. Nothing is added to the prior state except like one who "lights one candle from another" <note>A classic metaphor: the second flame exists without diminishing the first</note>. The term is also related to "proximity" <note>original: etzel</note> and closeness. Everything that was previously hidden or lacking becomes revealed in the vessels... and therefore the Sefirot <note>Divine Attributes</note> are associated with the language of *Atzilut*, as they draw the Holy Spirit from the Source. They are attached to it with a profound longing... and thus it says, "I will take from the spirit." This is distinct from *Beriah* <note>Creation</note>, which implies a "cutting off" or a separation of the thing from its source... a more revealed state. In the world of *Beriah*, the thick "Element of Earth" is found. We also find the scripture using the language of "Formation" <note>original: yetzirah</note>, as in "And the Lord God formed <note>original: va-yitzer</note>... man of the dust," which refers to a more revealed level. Regarding this, the verse says: "Everyone who is called by My name, and whom I have created <note>Beriah</note> for My glory, I have formed <note>Yetzirah</note> him, yea, I have made <note>Asiyah</note> him" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. This explains the progression from the hidden to the revealed... Know that these four levels are the "Causes of Causes" and they follow the path of emanation. **Atzilut** is the subtle level that remains in its place even after the Divine Will rose to create... there they are unified with their Root in a perfect union.

### Chapter 2: To Understand
The matter requires knowing that the World of the Sefirot consists of unique unifications of the Infinite Light <note>original: Ein Sof</note> through the concealments of the Infinite Light that spreads through them until they are distinguished in the World of Emanation... as I wrote in the Gate of the Essence. These levels are mentioned in the *Tikkunim*...

<column-break/>

### Chapter 1: The Emanation
They are described by three stages: Tracing, Engraving,

Hewing, and Action. Behold, the "Tracing" <note>original: Reshimah</note> is a subtle reality that cannot be grasped. Similarly, the World of Emanation (*Atzilut*) is unified with its Source; through its expansion, it becomes the root of limitation for the other worlds below it. However, the manifestation of this limitation is its product. Just as the power of the Emanator is within the Emanated, and the Emanator loses nothing—like "lighting one candle from another"—so too all the branches multiply and spread in subtlety and spirituality, while remaining attached and held by their Root. They are called *Atzilut* from the word *Etzel* <note>beside/near</note>, implying proximity and closeness, as was said regarding the Elders who were influenced by the prophecy of Moses: "They stood there with you, and I will take <note>va-atzalti</note> of the spirit that is upon you and put it upon them." **The World of Creation** (*Beriah*) is called "Engraving" <note>original: Hakikah</note>, like something engraved with a fingernail, representing a reality more revealed than a mere trace. It is the "Throne of Glory," a foundation and garment for the World of Emanation. Therefore, its rank is essentially "Ten" <note>referring to the ten Sefirot</note>, for there is no existence, large or small, that is not measured by ten. Because the branches of Emanation clothe themselves there, it is called the World of Creation—not that there are additional Sefirot, God forbid, but rather it is the original Sefirot themselves as they relate to Creation upon reaching it. The word "Beriah" implies an existence that comes "outside" <note>original: bar</note>, separated from the hidden Unity in the "Camp of the Divine Presence." The language of *Beriah* implies a "cutting off," as in "if He creates <note>yivra</note> a creation" or "In the beginning God created <note>Bara</note>." From this, one can understand the essential difference between the Righteous who enter "within" <note>without a veil</note> and those who require a partitioning garment from the World of Creation. So too the "Children of the Ascent" who unify with their source in Emanation without any screen at all, in the manner of the Patriarchs who were themselves the "Chariot." See the book *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimmonim by Moses Cordovero</note> at the end of Chapter 3 and the book *Marot Elohim* <note>Visions of God</note> in the first part, Chapter 17. **The World of Formation** (*Yetzirah*) is referred to by the term "Hewing" <note>original: Hatzivah</note>, like a stone hewn from a rock and shaped into a circle or a square. Thus are the ten classes of Angels included within it, hewn and influenced from beneath the Throne of Glory. Some are in the form of flaming fire or subtle light, and they "carry the Throne that carries its carriers," and Metatron...

<summary>This page defines the four spiritual worlds (ABYA) using metaphors of proximity and craftsmanship. It explains that "Emanation" (Atzilut) is like lighting a candle from a candle, while the lower worlds represent increasing levels of separation and "coarseness," from engraving to stone-hewing.</summary>

->**Gate Sixteen: ABYA**<-

...and the secret of including them according to the mystery of the letter *Lamed* <note>The letter Lamed (ל) in Kabbalah often represents the heart or the "tower flying in the air," acting as a connector between levels.</note> to nourish the ten Sephirot there. The numerical values of 26 and 66 <note>26 is the value of the name YHVH; 66 is the value of the name "Adonai" (65) plus one for the word itself, or related to the "filling" of the name</note> are integrated. The explanation of 26 refers to the five letters interwoven in their proper order in this manner, etc. It is found that each one is arranged according to the order above, acting as a **garment** for the letters which are the Sephirot, and the letters themselves are garments for their inner essences. Truly, one should never separate the "Covenant of the Parts" <note>A reference to the biblical covenant with Abraham, here used to mean the integrated structure of the Divine levels</note>. Now we shall explain this further: our teacher the Rashbi <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, of blessed memory, said in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkuney Zohar</note>: "Woe to the one who drives a wedge between the King and the Matron <note>original: *Matronita* (The Queen/Shekhinah). Driving a wedge means causing a spiritual separation between the masculine and feminine aspects of God.</note>," for they are like a single entity.

# Chapter 4
After the existence of the levels of "Inclusion" <note>original: *Kelelah*. A stage where the Sephirot are integrated before becoming distinct</note>, it arose in the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, to bring about the existence of the "Ends" and the "Rectifications" <note>original: *Tikkunim*</note> by way of the **World of Formation** (*Yetzirah*). This means that the levels of Inclusion become more revealed and more "thickened" <note>In Kabbalah, spiritual "thickness" or "coarseness" refers to the descent from pure spirit toward material existence</note>. They are included in the Name and in the Matron <note>original: *Matronan*, referring to the Archangel Metatron as the "Matron" or dwelling place for the Shekhinah in the lower worlds</note>.

The "Inclusion" acts as a crown over them to give to each one its portion and its flow of light. This is the quality of **Kindness** (*Hesed*) which acts upon all the angels like a body that provides strength and vitality to all, just as a body does. These angels constitute the World of Formation (*Yetzirah*). They too are completed into ten levels—the levels of Inclusion—and are placed as ten spiritual Sephirot which spread through the two levels of Inclusion. These then spread further into "two wings" and clothe themselves in two levels of Formation through the power of the Name. Four branches for each one are clothed in the two levels of Formation. This is what is called the "Eighteen" <note>original: *Chai*, the Hebrew word for Life, numerical value 18</note> for the Upright, according to the path I have written regarding the ten Sephirot of the World of Creation (*Beriah*).

The essential light remains hidden within the levels of Formation that are included in Metatron. When this light expands, it becomes revealed in Metatron, and then Metatron is called by his full name with the additional letters. Because there were "Four Directions" <note>The four winds/cardinal directions</note> mentioned in the scripture, the quality of Kindness (*Hesed*) descends and is hidden and concealed within him, and the Work <note>The creative process</note> performs its actions through his hand. This was explained in the *Tikkunim* on the verse "And a thousand were not for his eye," which I have interpreted as the triad of Kindness, Strength, and Beauty (*Hagadat*) acting upon the Kingdom (*Malkhut*) when she is within the chosen Metatron. This involves the "Mystery of the Union" <note>original: *be'ilah* (cohabitation/union)</note> and the musical notation of the *Segol* vowel <note>Kabbalists often use vowel points as metaphors for specific spiritual energies</note>.

According to his view, this is the **Foundation** (*Yesod*) <note>The 9th Sephirah, the channel of procreation and flow</note>, for the Beauty (*Tiferet*) and the Foundation prepare the lower "Kings" who serve with Him—sometimes constantly with the *Tiferet* itself through the *Yesod*, and sometimes through the "Righteous One" (*Tzadik*) <note>A title for the Sephirah of Yesod</note> alone within the Matron. This occurs when the *Tiferet* removes the "Husband" (the aspect of Malkhut) and gives the Righteous One to her will. This is the secret of the prohibition of making a separation in the ten Sephirot. On the **Sabbath** (*Shabbat*), however, the "Foundation" (*Yesod*) stands in the place of the "Five-Hundred" <note>A reference to the cosmic distance between levels</note>, for on that day the Action begins...

It is also said there that the letter *Yud* from the name Metatron represents the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note> hidden within him. She is called *Yud* (10) to hint that she is included of all ten Sephirot when she is within him. Furthermore, all the actions of the Sephirot are performed through Metatron, for all Sephirot act within him. It is not the actual Shekhinah herself who descends into him, but rather what is "clarified" <note>original: *mitbarer*. The process of extracting holy sparks from the lower realms</note> from the Shekhinah. Those breaths are included in ten letters. This state is what is called the **Exile of the Shekhinah** <note>The concept that the Divine Presence dwells among the lower, broken worlds to sustain them</note>. It was necessary for the Shekhinah to be included of all ten within him because all the five higher "Kindnesses" clothe themselves in Metatron to perform their actions through him, and also to ensure no separation is made. Therefore, it is known that as much as the Shekhinah ascends within Metatron, all the Sephirot descend with her.

The meaning of "Exile" is that when the Shekhinah is in Metatron, she does not receive the flow of light from herself, but only through Metatron. This does not mean she receives *only* through Metatron, but rather that the Shekhinah in the *Tikkunim* appears like a Queen who has left her palace. As long as the Queen is in the palace, she blesses the palace directly. But when the merits of the lower beings are clarified, the Kingdom (*Malkhut*) stars the world with clouds <note>metaphor for protection/veiling</note> and provides food and flow to all existences, first above, "face to face," receiving from above in a revealed way, and the flow of power increases. But when the sins of the lower beings are clarified, the Kingdom is in exile and clothes itself during the weekdays in the level of Metatron. Then, the preparation and flow of the world is through the "Nile" <note>metaphor for a lower channel of sustenance</note>, and she too receives blessings through him.

# Chapter 5
It will be further explained that on the **Sabbath** the "Higher Union" occurs through the **Foundation** (*Yesod*), whereas during the week it is through Metatron. What is the benefit of an angel entering into the holy place to unite the Sephirot? Before [the Sabbath] departs from the world, it provides life to everyone from above. After the Shekhinah—which is Kindness—is unified with her Husband through her entry...

<margin>The soul of the angel is the garment of Beauty (*Tiferet*).</margin>

Is it right that this "body" <note>The angel's form</note> should enter into the most refined place of the Perfect One to unite the Sephirot? Necessarily, the union is through his **soul**, and thus specifically through the Angel. One should not say, as some do, that they are unified through the Name of *Shaddai* <note>The Divine Name associated with the Sephirah of Yesod and the World of Formation</note>, for He is the Creator. How is it possible for a husband and wife to be unified except through the "Holy Covenant" <note>The *Yesod*</note>?

Regarding the secret that the union is through the Angel *Yesod*, we must first look at the matter of the union of the *Yesod* and the flow that passes to the Earth. The *Yesod* receives additions to its roots and prepares the "Food" which are the "Waters" for the feminine letters—the "Feminine Waters" <note>original: *Mayim Nukvin* (the spiritual yearning from below that triggers a flow from above)</note>. These are the spiritual aspects of prayer. This is the "Rest" and the spirituality that is raised up to the *Yesod*. He raises them higher. It is said in the *Tikkunim* that the acceptance of prayers on the Sabbath is through the *Yesod*. For every word from a person's mouth who prays with intention—according to the level of his soul, so shall be his power and his ascent.

Because the Sabbath has three "additions" <note>The extra levels of soul/light received on Shabbat</note> from the Upper Spirit, the spirituality of the letters of the breath of his mouth also ascends to the *Yesod*, which is the source of his soul, through the "Incense" on the Sabbath and Festivals. According to the level of the light, they return and ascend. This is why they said that the *Yesod* receives the prayers of Israel on Sabbaths and Festivals. As it says in the *Zohar*, the prayers of the weekdays are delayed until the Sabbath, and they ascend with the prayer of the Sabbath day. Even though the weekday prayers do not have the power to reach the *Yesod* on their own, they wait for the hand of the Sabbath and ascend with it. Therefore, the "Creator" <note>the light-giver</note> on the Sabbath is through the *Yesod*—that is, according to the level and the "refining" of the *Yud*. It awakens and flows the "Lower Waters" <note>human efforts/prayers</note> upward, and thus the Beauty (*Tiferet*) is awakened to pour out its flow... to all the holy sparks. Even though there is an "Extra Soul" (*Neshamah Yeterah*), the spirit and the breath of the mouth still ascend through Metatron... and this is the "Ascent of the Souls," meaning the breaking through of the firmaments as explained in the *Zohar* (Parashat Naso and Pekudei). There it says that the Gate of the Inner Palace, the Holy One, is closed during the six days of work, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened. The "Holy" shall open and add there... to teach us that through it [the union occurs]...

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic transition between the weekdays and the Sabbath. During the week, the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) is "in exile," acting through the intermediary Archangel Metatron; on the Sabbath, the intermediary is bypassed for a direct union through the Sephirah of Yesod (Foundation), allowing prayers and souls to ascend to higher realms.</summary>
