<meta>This page continues the exposition of the Four Worlds (ABYA), moving from the general theory of "clothing" the Divine Light into the specific functions and angelic hierarchies of the World of Formation (Yetzirah) and the World of Action (Asiyah).</meta>

->**Essence of Pomegranates, Gate 16: ABYA, Slice of the Pomegranate**<-

In the World of Formation <note>original: *Yetzirah*. This is the third of the four worlds, associated with the emotions and the angelic choir</note>, the World of the Ministers who prostrate themselves before the Creator every day and so on. Their actions are likened to the incense offering and their service is for Divine favor, much like the presentation of the inner blood <note>A reference to the sacrificial service in the Temple's Holy of Holies</note>. There, the Table is placed in the North, and upon it is the "bread of the mighty" <note>Psalm 78:25</note>, from which the ministering angels are nourished. The Menorah <note>The seven-branched lampstand</note> is in the South to illuminate the chambers of the Torah, the secret chambers of the Garden of Eden which are located there. From there, the abundance of the cloud of incense rises twice daily, constantly ascending as a pleasing aroma toward the Throne of Glory. This is hinted at by the Inner Sanctuary <note>original: *Dvir*</note>, before the Presence of the one who dwells among the Cherubim.

He appeared in ten noble garments <note>The ten Sephirot or Divine attributes as they manifest in this world</note> which are not separated in space. The High Priest <note>original: *Kohen Gadol*</note> would not gaze upon them on the Day of Atonement <note>original: *Yom Kippur*</note> except through the "Prince of the Throne" who encompasses the whole. When this Great Prince bestows influence upon the lower worlds through the "Garments of the Sabbath," the governance of the World of Formation is entirely hidden, following the principle of the inner service of the Tetragrammaton <note>original: *H-Y* (The Name YHVH)</note>: "And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place" <note>Leviticus 16:17</note>. Our Sages said this even applies to those of whom it is said "their faces were the face of a man" <note>The angels of the Chariot vision</note>, and it certainly applies to the "worthless man" <note>original: *Adam Belial*, representing the forces of spiritual impurity</note>. For when holiness is at its peak strength, the "worthless man" is submerged within the "female of the great abyss."

Behold, the relationship of each of these worlds to the one above it is like the relationship of the world of Emanation <note>original: *Atzilut*</note> to the Divine Will that clothes itself within it. Just as the depiction of Emanation was verified in complete simplicity within the Supreme Thought in the previous sections, such is the simplicity of the World of Creation <note>original: *Beriah*</note> and its depiction within Emanation. Thus, you may discern the World of Formation and its rooting in Creation. This is why the transformations "between the poles" <note>A reference to the Ark of the Covenant poles</note> were necessary according to the measure of the Day of Atonement. It goes without saying that the subtlety of the World of Action <note>original: *Asiyah*</note> was depicted in Formation. From all these worlds, physical tangibility—defined by generation and decay—is entirely removed, until the boundary and separation reach the edge of the World of Action. There, the "Damagers" <note>original: *Mazikim*, or destructive spirits</note> are found, the messengers of destruction and finality. Yet for those of lower soul, these spirits sometimes act as angels for good. In the Tractate Me'ilah <note>Talmud Me'ilah 17b</note>, it is told that Ben Temalyon <note>A spirit/demon in Jewish folklore</note> came out to meet Rabbi Shimon; because the time of that generation caused it, he said, "Let the miracle come from any source."

<column-break/>

The "Slice" itself and the matter of the thirty levels and nine steps... they are arranged according to the divisions of the Sephirot <note>The ten Divine emanations</note>, as mentioned in the book *Lekach Patim*. Weigh the fourfold and the later acquisitions and return to the Crown <note>original: *Keter*</note>. This means returning to the inner void of the hollows and all the branches that branch out from the Sea. Furthermore, according to his words, the Throne of Glory descends twenty levels, with ten levels beneath the "Reasons" in the "Bolt," and the branches are hidden like guests within the ten Sephirot.

These transformations in the level of the "Chair" shall be called "Sparks for the Righteous." The intention is not the "Inclusion" <note>original: *Kelelah*</note> which is the "Chair of the Worlds," but rather the "Sparks for the Righteous" are the ten branches of the Sephirot of the hollows that spread out and hollow out these ten levels for the righteous. According to the truth, these are the Sephirot of the hollows, meaning these groups spread out over the "Inclusion" which is the Throne, making it "Sparks within Sparks." The hidden part of the Inclusion and the Chair is because it is said that in its value and its activity, the "Hand of the Lord" was upon him to explain its knowledge.

The matter of his words is that every single Sephirah is found in comfort and tranquility, and there is one branch. When they were unified and fixed into six branches for the uprightness of the levels, they made for it a Throne, which is the "Throne of Honor." These six branches shall be a palace for the upper seven, and they shall be chargers <note>original: *mifsa'im*, runners or officials</note>, each man over his service toward the lower branches. Because these branches will be for the purpose of governance, they are called by the name "Godly" <note>original: *Elohi*</note>. They are divided according to the division of the Sephirot into seven circuits, and one encompasses them all... For here the Sephirot are divided into chargers.

In the Portion of Mishpatim <note>Exodus 21-24</note>, the Inclusion is called "Beast" and "Prey" in relation to the Kingdom <note>original: *Malchut*</note>, which is the "Higher Beast." Regarding this, Ezekiel said: "The beast that I saw under the God of Israel" <note>Ezekiel 10:20</note>. The "God of Israel" is Malchut, which is the Indwelling Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> of the "Beauty" <note>original: *Tiferet*</note> who is called "Israel." That "Beast" which was beneath it is the "Inclusion." Its appearance is as a beast and prey... some say it refers to Tiferet and its "prey" is Malchut, while others say it refers to the levels of the Chariot.

We have already stood upon the "Seraphim" of the levels of Emanation that were created... regarding the mystery of the hollows that were included. They are the generations and the noble levels... just as the garment of the first hollows is in the likeness of a spiritual body for the primordial Emanation, which is called "Creation" <note>original: *Beriah*</note>, and they call it...

### The Gate
->**Gate 16: ABYA**<-

The Prince of the Heights and the second to him... his name is **Pali-S-H** <note>Names here are technical angelic titles associated with the Sephirot</note>. He is the Prince of the Heights of Wisdom <note>original: *Chochmah*</note>. We have received that his name, through which his creation was revealed, is **Yekusi-H**. He is the provider... and the honor of the face of the elder. He is the Staff of Wisdom, the "Staff of God" to be counted. And the second is the Prince of the Lower Chariot... he is prepared for all who know understanding <note>original: *Binah*</note> and those of great fear. His name is **Yaloz-el**. I have been careful about what is written in the Torah in a single verse: "You shall rise before the aged and show deference to the old; you shall fear your God" <note>Leviticus 19:32</note>.

The third is called "Spiritual Bodies," attached one to the other in the world, and Malchut which is called "Inner and the Inmost of my skin." Nine levels... another sixty-six levels... in the likeness of bodies. Just as there are stones, so too there is the furnace. The third is **Yekusin**, who is the Prince of the Kindness <note>original: *Chesed*</note> designated for the "Water." The second to him is **Geviruson**, he is the Prince of the "Strong Strength" <note>original: *Gevurah*</note>. The fifth, his name is **Yediduron**, he is the Prince of Mercy <note>original: *Tiferet*</note>, for he is a "Friend of God" <note>original: *Yedid Hashem*</note>. The sixth, his name is **Setiron**, he is the Prince of the Foundation of the World <note>original: *Yesod*</note>, established and hidden in his power... who is called the "Supreme Secret" <note>original: *Seter Elyon*</note>, and "He who dwells in the Secret of the Most High" <note>Psalm 91:1</note>. The seventh for the "Bolt," its name is **Benotiron**, she is the Prince of the "Gathering," who is the "Assembly of Israel" <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*, or Malchut</note>.

**Zoliron** is the Prince of the "Covenant of Brothers," the secret of the sign. **Sepiron** is the Prince of the "Whole" and the "Noble ones," the end of the levels. These are the secrets of the Emanations which the "Men of Renown" <note>Genesis 6:4</note> merit. We have received that two "outer ones" were given at the end, the name **Chai**, and the secret of **Ozen** <note>Ear</note>, for these two are the "Garments of the Garments" that are included by the power of the Great Artisan who is above all, the Cause of all Causes and the Reason of all Reasons. These are like burning torches, illuminating each one without... the inner ones, which are in the likeness of inner garments, and they are like bodies for the Sephirot.

Therefore, understand that he said there are "two crowns," but they are "one garment" for these inner ones. They shall be a garment for these spiritualities... and these are the "Slices" of the Throne. For the "Inclusion" is the secret of the World of Creation. When the Sephirot of Emanation spread out and came to be revealed and "clothed," they were prepared for the level of the "Throne of Glory." As is found in the *Tikkunim* regarding the wheels of the Throne, which is the "Inclusion," and so it is said: "And the spirits went, ten within ten, which are..."

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the four worlds of existence: Emanation (Atzilut), Creation (Briah), Formation (Yetzirah), and Action (Asiyah), collectively known by the acronym ABYA. The previous page discussed the angelic service in the World of Formation; this page focuses on how the Divine light descends and "clothes" itself through these layers to manage the universe.</meta>

<header>->**Essence of Pomegranates, Gate 15: ABYA**<-</header>

And the heavens, virtues, and the light that spreads from the essence of the Sephirot <note>The ten Divine attributes or emanations</note> into everything, to clothe the higher realms, is called "The Holy One" in conjunction with the Foundation <note>original: *Yesod*</note> that spreads through it. For the spark of holiness that spreads into the World of Creation is called the "Ten Sephirot of Creation," and the spark that spreads into the World of Formation is called the "Ten Sephirot of Formation," and that which spreads into the World of Action is called the "Ten Sephirot of Action."

Ultimately, all spiritual activities are derived from the Supernal Light that spreads downward, and they themselves are the Sephirot. There is no doubt that within Creation there is the power of the Ten, and within Formation the power of the Ten, and within Action the power of the Ten. However, the World of Emanation <note>original: *Atzilut*, the highest world of pure divinity</note> does not clothe itself in the Ten of Formation except by way of the Ten of Creation which act as intermediaries. Likewise, the Ten of Creation do not clothe themselves in the Ten of Action except by way of the Ten of Formation. This is what is meant by saying that the Ten of Emanation do not clothe themselves in the Ten of Action except through the Seven of Formation. Thus we learn that the Ten of Action exist only through the seven higher levels of Emanation, Creation, and Formation.

But this is not the case from top to bottom <note>meaning the influence is not identical at every level</note>, for what exists in Emanation is not the same as what is in Creation, nor is Creation the same as Formation, nor Formation the same as Action. For the "deficiency" <note>the limitation of light</note> allows the world to live and be sustained in Formation. Regarding the "Gate of Action," Nachmanides <note>original: *Ramban*, a 13th-century scholar and mystic</note> explained that the reason for the suppression of the "External Shells" <note>original: *Klipot*, forces of impurity or concealment</note> is for the sake of existence and merit in every nurturing stage.

The governance of the world does not occur through the World of Formation except on weekdays. It is impossible for the world to be sustained by the World of Emanation alone, or even by Creation alone. Therefore, it is said that in the World of Creation are the "Garments of the Sabbath and Festivals," while in Formation are the "Garments of the Weekdays" and the time of Exile. The matter is this: on the Sabbath and Festivals, the Supernal Light is revealed without [dense] clothing, but rather through the essence of the light itself within the World of Creation. But when the Holy One desires to hide the light further within Creation to clothe it in Formation, these are the "Weekday Garments." This occurs when the King desires to wear weekday clothes, which is our state during the Exile. 

When a pure light reaches us without the "stirrings" of Formation, but rather through Creation, it is as if the light is clothed in "Sabbath and Festival Garments"—holy garments. In the time of Exile, there are additional "weekday clothes" added over the inner Sephiric garments. After explaining the levels of the Ten Sephirot, know that the World of Creation is to Emanation what the body is to the soul. Formation is to Creation, and Action is to Formation, in the same way. The words, hidden things, and "strikes" <note>Divine actions</note> are distant from the Essence but occur through the "vessels" <note>the Sephirot acting as tools</note>. The Essence itself remains in total simplicity and holiness, not subject to change or being affected, until the levels descend and clothe one another: Emanation in Creation, Creation in Formation, and Formation in Action. 

Through the World of Creation, all changes are enacted, and through the World of Action, all deeds are brought to completion. Through them, changes occur to punish the wicked, to reward the righteous, and to establish the world. Without the World of Action and the "Shells" <note>*Klipot*</note>, there would not even be an angel of the "Living of the Worlds." Even death in this world occurs through these forces and the inner "clothing" of judgment and cruelty, via the Angel of Death.

### Chapter 8: Know

Regarding our study of these four levels (ABYA), we have four proofs from Nachmanides and from the *Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkunei Zohar*, a classic kabbalistic text</note>. It says: "Do not take the mother with the young" <note>Deuteronomy 22:6, interpreted here as the relationship between the higher Sephirot and the lower worlds</note>. The "young" refers to the angels Michael and Metatron. It is also said that the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> "nests in the Throne" <note>the World of Creation</note> in the three upper Sephirot, while Metatron nests in the World of Formation, and the "Ofan" <note>a type of angel</note> in the World of Action. 

It is well known that the Soul, Spirit, and Breath <note>original: *Neshamah, Ruach, Nefesh*</note> correspond to Creation, the "Beauty" (*Tiferet*), and "Kingship" (*Malkhut*). The Holy One rules over the "Shells" by way of the angels, who are the "external garments." Nachmanides explained this regarding the verse "the heavens shall vanish like smoke" <note>Isaiah 51:6</note>. Furthermore, he explained that the Ten Sephirot are included in the Name YHVH <note>The Tetragrammaton</note>, consisting of four letters and two names totaling ten. This Name is rooted in the Emanation of *Tiferet* (The Holy One) and *Malkhut* (His Presence). On the Sabbath and Festivals, the Holy One reveals His light in the world without the "Shells," using the garments of Kingship.

### Chapter 9: And With

The explanation of ABYA links to what is said in the *Tikkunim* regarding the "Throne" and the "Chariot." To understand the process of the "Work of Creation" <note>original: *Ma'aseh Bereshit*</note>, we recognize four stages: **Engraving, Writing, Formation, and Action** <note>original: *Chakikah, Ketivah, Yetzirah, Asiyah*</note>. 

1. **Engraving** (*Chakikah*): A subtle impression that cannot be grasped, existing in the space between "nothingness" and "being." It is the most refined level of existence.
2. **Writing** (*Ketivah*): This corresponds to the World of Emanation and Creation. It is slightly more revealed than a mere "engraving," like a mark made by the point of a knife, yet still not fully graspable. 
3. **Formation** (*Yetzirah*): This is more revealed and "felt" than engraving. It is something the mind can begin to perceive as a distinct entity.
4. **Action** (*Asiyah*): This refers to a tangible, physical matter that is perceptible and revealed to all. 

All these levels descend from one another, from point to point, through the relationship of "Cause and Effect." There is no difference between one point and the next, or one level and the next, except for this chain of cause and effect, until they clothe one another...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the four worlds (ABYA), shifting from the theoretical structure of the Sephirot to the practical governance of the universe during the six days of the work week. It explains how the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) interacts with the lower angel Metatron to sustain the physical world.</meta>

<header>->**The Essence of Pomegranates, Gate 16: ABYA**<-</header>

How can we perceive the "What" <note>original: *Mah*, a reference to a specific Divine name associated with the human level</note> and so on? For He always watches over His world, and this is the meaning of "He stands and sustains," meaning He covers and prepares. Even now, while the gate is closed in the Hall <note>A reference to the Temple architecture used as a metaphor for the celestial palaces</note>, it is as if it were open; only the "rope of closure" remains. Regarding its being "fat," this refers to the weekdays when the world lives on the "taste of milk" <note>Sustenance that is processed or indirect</note>. Even now, our life is sustained by the portion of His kindness, for "the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year" (Deuteronomy 11:12). 

Through this, the matter of the "closing of the gate" is explained. It is an established principle that through the "ascent" <note>The withdrawal of direct Divine light</note>, the spiritual levels are unified during the weekdays. However, the power of the weekdays certainly stands within the "Living One" <note>original: *Chai*, often referring to the Sephirah of *Yesod* (Foundation)</note>. Although the Foundation of the "Vav" <note>The six directions or Sephirot of the emotive core</note> gives life to the weekdays through this ascent, it is specifically prepared for us through the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note>. This is why it says, "He went down to the thirty doors of the city"—this refers to the Shekhinah descending and revolving within the "Youth" <term>Metatron: the supreme angel who governs the World of Formation and acts as a bridge between the Divine and the physical</term>. 

The awakening of this union is achieved through the "lower levels" in this "inn" <note>The physical world</note>, even in a small way. Therefore, the abundance of the Male <note>The active, giving Divine force</note> is only a tiny amount, so that it does not flow with full sweetness and extra force. The flow is diminished according to the delicate nature of this angelic "messenger." For the aspect of *Malchut* <note>Kingship/the Shekhinah</note> gathers these small amounts according to the measure of this angel’s refinement. She shines upon her "husband" <note>the higher Sephirot</note> an abundance according to the spiritual delicacy of this angel, and that abundance flows to us... not as pure spirit, but according to the physicality of the "inn" <note>the material world</note>. Therefore, during the weekdays, the Shekhinah is found within Metatron. But do not think that she leaves him; rather, Metatron ascends to the spiritual realms, and there she unifies the sustenance with her "bridegroom," in the manner of the "Righteous One, the Foundation of the World" <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. Yet, in this world, the angel remains in his place, and this union occurs through the Foundation as is appropriate. There are many proofs for this in the *Zohar*.

# Chapter 6: Further Discussion

The "Holy Dove" <note>A traditional metaphor for the *Shekhinah*</note> is prepared during the six days of the week, though she is separated from her Husband <note>the higher Divine realms</note>. Do not think that she wanders the world without attachment to Him; rather, she remains protected. This is the meaning of what is written in the *Zohar* (Supplement, page 30): "What is Metatron?" Behold, the Shekhinah is revealed from place to place to those who are "masters of service" and "pious in action," to dwell within them. Through them, she unifies with her Husband, the "Tetragrammaton" <note>The four-letter name of God</note> who rules over them because they are occupied with the Torah. 

Therefore, she attaches herself to the "Lower Righteous One" <note>The tzadik/holy person on Earth</note> who establishes her foundation with her Husband through the "Upper Righteous One" <note>the Sephirah *Yesod*</note>. In this context, we expound on the verse "I will establish My covenant with you" (Genesis 6:18). Just as the covenant is established above, it is established through the "Righteous One" below. Understand this: every righteous person has a "standing" and their "sparks" are dependent on the Upper Foundation through the "Holy Covenant." This stirs the hidden depths. It is like a woman pursuing her husband; because of her great love for him, he takes her and unifies with her. So too, the Shekhinah dwells upon the Lower Righteous One with goodness and good desires, and the Upper Righteous One hastens and moves to unify with her. This is the secret of the "two Righteous Ones" mentioned in the *Zohar*. The deeds of the righteous act as "Feminine Waters" <term>Mayin Nukvin: the spiritual 'arousal from below' caused by human prayer and good deeds that triggers Divine blessing from above</term>. 

When a righteous person is ready, the Shekhinah dwells upon him. Even if there are no good deeds, there are always righteous people in the world... As it says in the Talmud (Berakhot, Chapter 1), "There is no single righteous person who is so pure" that he is always ready for the Shekhinah. Therefore, she is sometimes hidden within Metatron in the World of Formation. During the weekdays, this angel is called "The Small Bird" because he is "light" <note>quick/subtle</note> compared to the "Bird of the Nest" which is the Shekhinah. They also called him *Shaddai* <note>A Divine name meaning Almighty</note>, for this name is specifically used for the Foundation and the Shekhinah, whether in the Sephirah or in the angel who is the "Prince of the Interior." Since the Foundation is in the "Prince of the Interior," it is as if the Foundation of the World is there. This will be explained further in the "Gate of Titles" with the help of God.

# Chapter 7: And Another

Regarding the "Doors of the World of Action" <note>original: *Yetzirah*, but the context implies the transition to *Asiyah*</note>: it arose in His will to create a fourth existence in the way of "Action" <note>original: *Asiyah*</note>. These are all things made from the end of the level of Formation down to the "point of the abyss." This includes the visible "husks" <term>Kelipot: 'shells' or 'husks' that represent the forces of spiritual concealment or evil</term>, the elements, and all complex things. The ten heavenly spheres serve as "garments" for the ten Husks. Even the lower parts of Action are completed by the ten levels... which spread through the levels of Formation. We have further "tertiary branches" that clothe themselves in the ten levels of Action. These are called the "Ten Sephirot of Action."

It is explained in the *Tikunim* (Supplements to the Zohar) that if humanity returns to good, the "foreskin" <note>the blockage of the husks</note> is removed. For humanity in the World of Action, there is a "Husk" that clothes the soul to confuse it in everything. Holiness descends into these "husks" to subdue and humble them. For as long as the Husks are near Holiness, they are humbled and broken. From their "root," they receive a tiny spark from the side of Holiness to sustain them, but it is "purified" from their impurity. This is the secret of the "Seventy Princes" <note>The angelic guardians of the nations</note> who diminish; they were 70 corresponding to 70 nations who influence sustenance. This is the meaning of the verse, "A time when one man rules over another to his own hurt" (Ecclesiastes 8:9). This "man" refers to the "worthless man" <note>the side of evil</note>. It is "to his own hurt" because if the worthless man has dominion—meaning if the abundance of holiness flows to him as it does to the holy—it would actually be "to his hurt" because he would be nullified and consumed. 

The Shekhinah spreads into ten titles to clothe the ten Husks, to subdue them and gather them, to fulfill what is written: "And His kingdom rules over all" (Psalms 103:19). If the Husks existed outside of Holiness, it would imply a second power <note>dualism</note>, which is impossible. He, blessed be He, gives life to everything. Therefore, Holiness must "clothe" itself in the Husks. This is not a benefit to the Husk; on the contrary, it is "to its hurt" because it restricts it. Furthermore, the Shekhinah clothes herself in them to execute judgment through them... This is the secret of the "Exile of the Shekhinah" <note>The Divine Presence trapped in the lower, darker realms of existence</note>. She descends so that the "husks" do not consume the "seed of Israel." As explained in the *Tikunim*, this "clothing" is called the "Exile of the Shekhinah." Every Sephirah is within her, and there is no separation between her and the Sephirot. She clothes herself in the six weekdays, which are her "branches"—Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, etc. The "Exile" is thus the hiding of the Shekhinah within Metatron.

<summary>This page explains how the Shekhinah (Divine Presence) governs the lower worlds during the weekdays by "clothing" herself in the angel Metatron and even within the "husks" (Kelipot) of the physical world. This descent, termed the "Exile of the Shekhinah," is necessary to sustain existence, subdue evil, and allow human deeds to trigger Divine unity.</summary>

<header>### The Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 17: The Thigh of Jacob / The Juice of Pomegranates ###</header>

...and the legs of the "horse" <note>A metaphor for the celestial chariot or vehicle of divine energy</note> long for the "bread," and so too for the added Judgment <term>Din: the attribute of strict justice or limitation</term>, which is the secret of the "blood of the soul." This is the feminine aspect that was cast down in the beginning, and it is the secret of the "outer husk" <term>Klipah: a shell or spiritual obstacle</term> that is above the higher heads, but it does not enter within. 

Furthermore, one must know the reason why the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the dwelling presence of God</term> is called by His Name. For the attribute of Harmony <term>Tiferet: the central Sephirah, often called "The Torah"</term> decides between Kindness <note>Chesed</note> and Strength <note>Gevurah</note>. Through the secret of the Shekhinah, although it is a "branch" of Strength, it draws sustenance from the source of Kindness. And though it is a branch of Strength, it draws from Strength the reason and the secret of the unification of the attributes, making them more equal and strong. For example, if Strength seeks to enact Judgment, and the attribute of Beauty <note>Tiferet/Jacob</note>—which is the branch of Kindness and whose "taste" is Kindness—tempers that Judgment, then when it comes time to enact the Judgment, the inner Kindness suffices to sweeten the severity. This is the secret of the verse: "Your priests shall be clothed in righteousness, and Your pious ones shall sing for joy" <note>Psalm 132:9</note>. 

We explained this at length in Gate 10. And behold, it is clear that the lower Strength <note>represented by the prophet Samuel</note> was not worthy except when sweetened through the influence of the attributes, specifically through Kindness. Then the influence of Judgment is born in "splendor" and is called "my left" <note>associated with the Sephirah of Hod</note>. And when the influence is through mercy, it is called "the right days" <note>associated with Nezach</note>. For the essence of "Right" and "Left" refers to whether the action is tempered or strict. Above, in the foundational concepts, what they said originally was that the secret of "the ox" <note>associated with the Left side/Judgment</note> was not yet sweetened, for it was "sitting in the shadow" of Kindness, which is the right side.

<column-break/>

the prophecy <note>of the Sephirah of Hod</note> entirely, in the sense of "my splendor was turned into corruption" <note>Daniel 10:8</note>. It is written, "And Israel went down very low." Even if sometimes "the Lord was with the Judge," it was not a lasting thing because there was no merit in that generation. Rather, it was as said in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, that the Holy One, Blessed be He, restored the border of Israel for a short time, even though they did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. 

So it was in the days of the Judges: "every man did what was right in his own eyes." The smoke of Micah’s idol was intermingled with the smoke of the altar in Shiloh. Consequently, the attribute of Victory <term>Nezach: the right "leg" of the Sephirot</term> was unstable, for even from the side of the Right, its influence did not flow properly until Samuel came and "cleansed" the Judgment. This Judgment had been attached to the Right, affecting the priests who were the sons of Eli. Judgment also affected Splendor <note>Hod</note> regarding Saul and his house because of Amalek, who was attached to the "prince" <note>the guardian angel</note> of his grandfather. With this, there was Judgment below and no Judgment above. 

Afterward came David, peace be upon him, and he appeased the attribute of Victory <note>Nezach</note> with his songs and melodies, so that it might draw properly from the side of Kindness. This is the secret of "pleasantness in Your right hand forever" <note>The Hebrew word for "forever" is *Nezach*</note>. And "what is sweeter than honey?" Through this introduction, we understand what is found in some Midrashic commentaries: that it was Michael, the Prince of Kindness, who touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh. Both views are true, since Kindness agreed to push the attribute of Splendor <note>Hod</note> away from it so that its Judgment would not be mixed in. Once Victory was properly attached and bound to the Right, Splendor was also bound to the Left, to "rebuke with equity" the kings of Judah and all the people of the land, to end transgression and finish sins. The songs of David in the mouths of all Israel are somewhat effective in every age, and at specific times of favor, David merited that his will became the will that blends the attributes as in the days of old, as it is written: "Your priests shall be clothed in righteousness." For the great servants, the men of Kindness, will repair the attribute of Splendor. My left side, from the perspective of Righteousness, is the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note> which draws from it, according to the secret of "She is in Nezach and She is in Hod." "And Your pious ones shall sing for joy"—meaning the branches of Kindness influenced by Him through Victory, they shall sing to appease Strength and Understanding <note>Binah</note> which are above them, as is known. So it is destined to be renewed and sustained speedily in our days. The sages have another way of explaining the "limping," which is a second explanation found in its place in the book *Or Yakar* on the section of *Bereishit*, and in the book *Elimah* in the fifth spring, palm 4. There is no room to elaborate further here.

Know that Jacob is the secret of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> and the parable of the body. <margin>His thigh</margin> The "thighs" <note>Nezach and Hod</note> are like the legs that support the body. <meta>This page continues the exploration of the spiritual hierarchy, transitioning from the general structure of the four worlds (Atzilut, Briah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah) to a specific examination of the Sefirot Nezach (Victory) and Hod (Splendor), symbolized by the "Thighs of Jacob."</meta>

# The Juice of Pomegranates, Gate 16: ABY"A, The Slice of the Pomegranate

**General Rule.** And behold, the beginning of the array of the *Sefirot* <term>Sefirot: the ten divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe</term> is what is called "Head, Middle, and End" <note>original: "RT"CH" - an acronym for Rosh, Toch, Sof</note> and "Elijah," and it is divided into two halves: Inclusion and Withdrawal, which are also called "Engraving" and "Hewing." The first half is the world of Metatron <note>The highest archangel in Jewish mystical tradition</note>, the world of the angels which contains ten classes; these are "thicker" <note>more material/less spiritual</note> than that which they receive from. They receive from the Throne <note>original: "HaKise"</note>, for the Throne receives from the flow of Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds, the realm of pure divinity</term> and bestows it upon the angels. These are referred to as the various classes of celestial beings <note>original: "AcY"A and ZYL"S," acronyms for angel groups like Ophanim, Chayot, etc.</note>. 

The second division, from the midpoint onward, concerns the "Lower Ones" and all matters known as the "Work of Creation." These are called the "Ancient" <note>original: "Atik"</note>, and every level and part of these thirty levels is called "Z"N" <note>Z'eir Anpin and Nukva, the masculine and feminine aspects of the divine</note>. There are parts like the part of Emanation which has ten levels, but there is a great distinction between the ten of Emanation and the ten of Glory <note>original: "Kavod"</note>. Despite this, it is not far-fetched that there are four levels in these matters, similar to the four worlds of ABY"A <term>ABY"A: Atzilut (Emanation), Briah (Creation), Yetzirah (Formation), and Asiyah (Action)</term>. For when the *Sefirot* of ABY"A are named, the intention refers to the order of the levels of revelation. Thus, when ABY"A is called "Creation" <note>Briah</note>, it is in relation to the subtlety of the "Marrow"; "Formation" <note>Yetzirah</note> is in relation to the "Crown" <note>Keter</note>; and "Action" <note>Asiyah</note> is in relation to "Wisdom" <note>Chokhmah</note>. I will not elaborate on them here as ABY"A, but rather they shall be "this opposite that," in the way of the Great Glory. This is the general rule regarding the form of the letters, and in this way it will also be explained regarding the attributes of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, Foundation <note>Yesod</note>, and Sovereignty <note>Malkhut</note>, and in the rest of the *Sefirot*. 

In the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar, a classic kabbalistic work</note> it says: "In the beginning He created the Marrow," and these are the five upper points and the five lower points. The upper ones are in the triad of Binah, Gevurah, and Tiferet <note>Understanding, Strength, and Beauty</note>, and the lower ones are in Nezach, Hod, and Yesod <note>Victory, Splendor, and Foundation</note>. In another place it explains that there are divisions for all the ancients: as it is written "Lions," etc., for the world of Formation <note>Yetzirah</note>; "Oxen," etc., for the world of Creation <note>Briah</note>; and "Eagles," etc., for the world of Action <note>Asiyah</note>. And who are the four angels? These are the ones established upon the Chariot <note>The Merkavah or Divine Chariot</note> over the three lower triads. The "Actions of the Patriarchs" are the "Sign for the Children," and some say that the angel of the world of Formation is less than the Patriarchs, as explained above. 

The reason all three are called "Upper" and "Lower," etc., is that each one of the ten *Sefirot* is included within all the others. Furthermore, in all the *Sefirot* there are three or four levels of this number. Behold, when they say ABY"A in the world of Emanation, the intention is the order of the levels of revelation, as we said. Some explain it in another way: that when one of the *Sefirot* enters and "clothes" itself in the world of Creation, it is called its "Creation" aspect, and likewise for Formation and Action. According to the *Tikkunim*, Understanding <note>Binah</note> is the higher Soul <note>Neshamah</note>, Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> is the Spirit <note>Ruach</note>, and Sovereignty <note>Malkhut</note> is the lower Soul <note>Nefesh</note>. This is like Creation, Formation, and Action, because Understanding clothes itself in the Throne, Beauty in the heavenly wheels <note>Ophanim</note>, and Sovereignty in the lower wheels. It is like a candle flame.

# The Seventeenth Gate: The Thigh of Jacob

## Chapter 1: In Explanation
->The location of the entry: Know that this follows the Zohar on the portion of Vayishlach, 171b<-
## Chapter 1: The General Rule
->That which emerges from the *Pardes* according to its path, and likewise in the book *Or Yakar*, full of wisdom and perfection<-

<margin>A sapphire in our place, and for it the wellspring and the book of nature</margin>
The path regarding the "Thigh of Jacob" and the soul is missing the letter *Vav* in the word "Vayehi," according to the language of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Rashbi</note>. It was known regarding his thigh, and it lived and became like the strength of Israel. It is written "his thigh" <note>singular</note> and not "his thighs" <note>plural</note>, because this is the fourth level that was not rectified until he took hold of the ladder <note>Jacob's ladder</note>. Therefore it is written, "The sun rose for him," meaning for Issachar, etc. "And Jacob touched his thigh"—he took the strength of the thigh from there, for the children are the strength outside the body. Jacob is the "Body" <note>symbolizing Tiferet</note>, and the body includes the mystery of the two arms <note>Chesed and Gevurah</note>. He sealed the generation and included it in the "Wing," as it is written regarding the wings of the mother bird, and this is written only regarding the "Wing" etc. Because of this, he came to be crowned at the end of his strength, and the sun rose for him. Therefore, every appointment is at the beginning and at the end. 

One must be precise: this section of "Light and Evil" <note>original: "Tover/Tor"</note> is the "Wing," because it is written "his thigh," and this is the "Shoulder." For the level in its connection becomes Splendor <note>Hod</note>, as the thigh is also Splendor. Furthermore, it is written that the "left side" in holiness was damaged. Behold, the *Sefirot* are concepts beyond grasp, especially regarding the Holy Sovereignty, and certainly regarding the Divine Holiness. Furthermore, in the *Raya Mehemna* <note>a section of the Zohar</note> it implies that the "Thigh" is the secret of the "Left Thigh of Jacob," which is Splendor <note>Hod</note>. This is where the "adversary" <note>Samael/the angel of Esau</note> attached himself, making it "weak all the day" <note>Lamentations 1:13</note>. This is also implied in the *Tikkunim*. 

**We must explain and understand** this matter. We must first establish three premises. First: do not think that the "Husk" <term>Klipah: spiritual impurity or evil</term> enters within the Holiness, God forbid! Regarding what is written in books—that the Husk enters the Holiness—the matter is this: when the Husks rise up around the Tabernacle, they are the general levels of the "Shell" in the depths, and they prosecute the righteous of Israel. Then the "Face of the Pomegranate" <note>The attribute of Mercy</note> withdraws, and the attribute of Supernal Judgment is awakened. This awakens the sin, like a fire that spreads from the attribute of Judgment. Then it "touches" the Holiness and the holy levels, to enact judgment and to remove the "Husk" of sin that has attached itself above, until the "Face of Mercy" is revealed again and the place of the veil is repaired.

<column-break/>

The beauty of his limping—that of our father Jacob, peace be upon him—is what we have "sweetened" and explained at length in our conduct according to the short introductions of the Sage <note>Rabbi Moses Cordovero</note>, peace be upon him. And even now, more "salt and spice" have been added for a primary flavor, so that the transcription of our earlier words here will not be a mere repetition without innovation. 

The matter is this: since the six days of Creation, the sustenance of Victory <note>Nezach</note> was drawn from the side of Strength <note>Gevurah</note>, and Splendor <note>Hod</note> from the side of Kindness <note>Chesed</note>. This was not according to the order of their emanation—for the whole world agrees that Victory is the branch of the Right <note>Kindness</note> and Splendor is the branch of the Left <note>Strength</note>—but rather in the secret of the "Blending of Attributes." From the moment sin caused a disruption and the "channels" became confused, no "men of valor" were able to repair the damage until our father Jacob took the judgment upon himself. This was on account of his marrying two sisters, his temporary neglect of Torah study, and the honor due to his father and mother. 

In his hour of distress, he said: "If Esau comes to the one camp" <note>Genesis 32:9</note>—meaning his ministering angel above awakens judgment against the one camp, which is Splendor <note>Hod</note>, the "female" aspect among the hosts (for "camp" and "host" are one and the same). From that time on, not only was the strength of Splendor weakened in its feminine aspect, but "he struck it," weakening the strength of the entire "Stature" <note>the divine configuration</note> hinted at within it. Or, as it says, the "Truth to Jacob" was full with the letter *Vav*, but his mercy was corrupted. Then the remaining camp, which is Victory <note>Nezach</note>, strengthened itself to escape and take hold of the attribute of Kindness <note>Chesed</note>. And so it was: the angel of his brother touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh, and immediately the order of sustenance was reversed through the cancellation of that "Blending" we mentioned. Thus, Splendor returned to being influenced by the side of Strength <note>Gevurah</note> alone, by the necessity of its original emanation.

**However**, throughout the days of Moses—of whom it is written, "He is faithful in all My house"—the attribute of Judgment did not prevail. Also in the days of Joshua—of whom it is written, "You shall put some of your splendor <note>hod</note> upon him"—who is the "Face of the Moon." I will be with the "Splendor" <note>Hod</note>, mentioning the Splendor from the strength of Moses to assist Joshua in his prophecy. The merit of Moses availed throughout the days of the Elders; but in the days of the Judges, prophecy ceased.

# Slice of the Pomegranate, Gate 18: The Diminishing of the Moon, Juice of Pomegranates

The Torah and Prophecy are dependent upon this topic, which was brought in the *Pardes* <note>The "Orchard," referring to the classic kabbalistic work *Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the fourth gate. We have moved it here because we saw that these subjects are dependent upon one another, and one cannot be fully understood without the assistance of its fellow. There is no area in the secrets of the Torah greater than these. However, the accepted literal meaning <term>Pshat: the plain, literal sense of the scripture</term> is also true in itself, and everything derived from it in truth and uprightness through the parables of the Sages and their teachings provides real assistance in descending to the depths of these matters. Everything is according to the person contemplating them; each according to their own grasp. "He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no lack" <note>A quote from Exodus 16:18 regarding the Manna, used here to describe spiritual comprehension</note>, provided that one directs their heart toward Heaven.

Behold, Knowledge, the Sun, and Mercy are three "greats" of the world, each according to its place and hour. Corresponding to them are three "lights" <note>original: "kalei," literally "lightweights" or "swift ones"</note> of the world: Choice, the Living, and Judgment. When we say "lights of the world," it is not to disparage them, but rather refers to the nature of the feminine attributes, whose mind is "light" <note>original: "da'atan kalah," a Talmudic idiom meaning flexible, soft, or sensitive</note>, soft, and humble. This is their beginning and their existence: to stand before those who possess absolute power, and in the place of the "greats" who require them; in this, they are praised. If so, they too are great in their own watches. 

This is like the parable in the *Zohar* on the Song of Songs, which says: "A lion is called a lion, but the tail shall never be the head." This implies that it is impossible for them to be equal, for "women are arrogant," as the Jerusalem Talmud says, and the contention would last forever. If equality were to rest upon them, they would come to disparage their husbands in their own eyes. Therefore, equality between them is not praised at all—not in the intellectual world, nor in the sensory world, nor in the world of oaths <note>original: "mushba," perhaps referring to the world of manifested decrees</note>, as we will explain shortly. Otherwise, it might be thought there is a "duality" in the divine leadership, Heaven forbid, which would lead to "contempt and wrath" <note>A reference to Esther 1:18</note>. 

This is what was hinted at in the *Baraitha of Rabbi Eliezer*, Chapter 6, where it is taught: "A dispute entered between them. This one said to that one, 'I am greater than you,' and there was no peace between them. What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He made one great and diminished the other." 

Now, if you were to say: "Let them be equal, and all 'wives' shall give honor to their 'husbands,' and it would be considered an additional praise and holy elevation for both," know that this is not possible. For the nature of Judgment and its unique quality is to be surrendered to Mercy and to obey its command. In such a state, Judgment itself becomes complete Mercy through absolute equality. However, the title "Great" is only appropriate for one whose praise is "Greatness" <term>Gedulah: another name for the attribute of Chesed/Mercy</term>, and there is no greatness except simple Mercy, in the sense of "Yours, O Lord, is the Greatness." Thus, the intended "fix" would become a "ruin," for it is not pleasing before Heaven that the attribute of Judgment should be damaged and the "sinner" profit.

However, in the intellectual world, where the Supernal Will acts as officer, guard, and ruler, and behold, Wisdom and Understanding are with it—they are considered as one in the conduct of Mercy. But because Wisdom and Understanding are the roots of Mercy and Judgment, it is very appropriate to interpret this prevention using the parable from the *Zohar* on the Song of Songs: A certain King—who is the Will—has two crowns—Knowledge and Intellect—to choose the good and reject the evil. For the Supernal Will desires Choice in order to justify the Heavenly Judgment over all creatures. There is room for the "Master of Judgment" to complain, saying: "It is better that Knowledge, by its own will and desire, hide its face slightly, so that Choice is not weakened, lest the benefit gained from it—to punish the wicked and give a good reward to the righteous—be diminished." It is possible to support this claim from the well-known idea that when a woman is "bitter" <note>original: "mura'at," likely referring to the pains of labor or the struggle of physical manifestation</note> first, she gives birth, etc. See further.

<column-break/>

...before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Master of the Universe! Is it possible for two kings to use one crown?" <note>This is the famous Midrash where the Moon complains about sharing status with the Sun</note> He said to her: "Go and diminish yourself." She said before Him: "Master of the Universe! Because I said a proper thing before You, must I diminish myself?" He said to her: "Go and rule by day and by night." She said to Him: "What is the greatness in that? What use is a candle at noon?" He said to her: "Let Israel use you to count the days and the years." She said to Him: "The Sun too—it is impossible for seasons not to be calculated by it, as it is written: 'And let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years.'" He said: "Go, the righteous shall be called by your name" <note>e.g., Jacob the Small, Samuel the Small</note>. Since her mind was still not eased, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "Bring an atonement for Me for having diminished the moon." From this, we hear that her complaint was aligned with Wisdom and Understanding, for it was "secret" <note>original: "Sod," a mystical secret</note> for them to use one crown—that is, the power of Mercy, which is superior to them.

### Chapter 2: In the Zohar
On the Song of Songs, it does not seem this way. For there, it returns to the verse "And God created the two great luminaries," and it says that the Moon asked the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Is it possible for one King to use two crowns as one?" And their beginning and existence for all was in the Kingdom <term>Malchut: the final Sefirah, representing the feminine/physical manifestation</term>... from which we hear that her complaint was that she received from the five <note>The five attributes of the "Body" or the 50 Gates of Understanding</note>... And furthermore, there is a teaching in the hidden parts [of the Zohar] regarding two marks that were prepared... and it is explained that she said to the "Living One" <note>Z"er Anpin</note>: "Is it possible for kings to use one crown?" The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to her: "Go and diminish yourself," because the rule of two kings is like this... and this implies that she said "If so, three kings," meaning the Moon, the Sun, and the Crown above them. This implies that there was no dispute with the Sun specifically, whereas the "three kings" mentioned above implies her dispute was with the Sun, as explained.

### Chapter 3: To Understand
This matter, one must know how the order of Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest spiritual world</term> occurred. Know that when it arose in His blessed Thought to illuminate the Emanation for the benefit of the lower beings—so that through it His greatness would be revealed, allowing those who "dwell in houses of clay" <note>human beings</note> to delight in the splendor of His glory and be sanctified by it—He established a fixed order. Before they were [fully formed] in the simple Crown <term>Keter</term>, they were a superior point in a diminished state of existence. When they were immediately formed before Him—as explained in the "Gate of Configurations"—there was the union of the Kingdom <term>Malchut</term>... which was greater than all other existences because they were the goal of the Union. Through them was the primary preparation, such that the powers in the Supernal Thought—namely Wisdom, Understanding, Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>, and Kingdom—constitute the essence of the Emanation and include all other existences within them.

The essence of the Emanation and the Throne are Beauty and Kingdom, which are the clarified inclusions from Understanding, clothed in a masculine aspect. This is the secret that they are the inclusions of the Emanation from Understanding downwards. This is the order of the Union: for every Union is formed through a pause, which is the letter *Vav* <note>Numerical value 6, representing Tiferet and the six extremities</note> and the Queen, the letter *Heh* <note>Representing Malchut</note>. Therefore, in their holy relationship to the Emanation, they were Beauty and Kingdom. This is what the Sages meant by "This teaches that they were pairs before Him." 

The order of the Unions is Beauty and Kingdom, and they were before Him in the secret of the "couches" <note>metaphor for divine union</note> that preceded the birth of the world. The radiance of the Kingdom was greater, receiving blessing from the vitality of Beauty, for it was the "Goal of Memory." This is what they meant by "The end of action was first in thought," which refers to the Kingdom through...

# Gate 17: Jacob’s Thigh

However, the aspect of this "Body" was <term>Tiferet</term> <note>The central Sefirah, often associated with "Beauty" or "Harmony," which acts as the torso of the divine form</note>, and within it were prophesied the three "arms": Kindness (*Chesed*), Severity (*Gevurah*)—representing right and left—and the Body itself. Because of this, it is called "Man" (*Adam*), for it is the inclusion of the three "Faces": the Lion, the Ox, and the Eagle <note>The celestial faces seen in the Prophet Ezekiel’s vision of the Divine Chariot</note>. This is not from another aspect within it, but from the aspect of the Throne, which includes all six "extremities" <note>The six emotional Sefirot from Kindness to Foundation</note>. These are expressed in the five "arms" without the Foundation (*Yesod*)...

Consequently, it was not possible for Jacob <note>original: "Ya'akov"</note> to be fully rectified, as the "thigh" was struck <note>A reference to Genesis 32:25, where Jacob’s thigh is injured in a struggle with an angel; kabbalistically, this represents a vulnerability in the lower Sefirot</note>. This is why the prophet Samuel said, "The Eternity of Israel will not lie, nor will He relent, for He is not a man to relent" <note>1 Samuel 15:29</note>. Therefore, His judgment does not turn back. The inner soul is small, and upon the halves within it, a "stranger" <note>Representing external or harsh forces</note> is drawn into the power of the judgment. He relents only to bestow mercy upon it to repair the judgment.

For he did not find rest there—meaning his palate, a branch revealed in *Tiferet* called "Man," as mentioned—so that He might have mercy and reveal His compassion over the judgment. Therefore, the "fullness" of Samuel's name rises through the "crushing" <note>A complex linguistic play on the Hebrew letters of Samuel’s name and their numerical or spiritual values</note>. And because of this rectification, Samuel acquired his status, as he included "Silver" (*Chesed*) within "Splendor" (*Hod*)...

Yet, even so, it was not completely rectified until David came to repair it. His crown was lowered because the light of Kindness rested upon him until he was repaired. This is what is meant by "Pleasures at Your right hand forever" <note>Psalm 16:11; original: "Netzach," which means both 'forever' and the Sefirah 'Victory'</note>. It does not say "Your right hand saw," but rather implies that through the power of the Right, one should pray.

**Chapter 4: And behold,** his virtue arises from the lack. In the portion of *Terumah* <note>A section of the Zohar</note>, it is explained to us: "The expansion of the 'Good' is the one called 'Kindness' (*Chesed*)..." And if you should ask, it is written "Pleasures at Your right hand are *Netzach*"—this implies that the right side is where strength and the "binding of the right" belong. But it is not so; rather, every "Kindness" depends on the "Voice" <note>Tiferet</note> that emerges from it.

The left is included in the right, and the path of Splendor (*Hod*) is upon the right to provide shelter... and if you should say *Netzach* is on the right, the answer is that the Crown of the "Holy King" is on the right. This clarifies our words in the previous chapters... just as the Grace After Meals sustains the whole world in His goodness, through Kindness, which is called "Full of Good." 

All miracles come from the side of Kindness, for all "Might" (*Gevurah*) is within nature. Miracles are the opposite of nature, as is known, and thus they come from the side of Kindness.

# Gate Eighteen: The Diminishing of the Moon

## Chapter 1: In Explanation
This concerns the "Two Faces" that were created at the beginning, which were then separated into "He" and "She." The matter of the "Two Great Lights" <note>The Sun and the Moon, as described in Genesis 1:16</note> is mentioned often in our study. One aspect is the "Two Faces" which relates to the will of the lower beings; there, the state of "Two Great Lights" is a virtue in the higher realms. However, the "Diminishing" <note>The Moon being made smaller than the Sun</note> is considered a "evil" or a lack, until one is forced to offer an atonement for it, as mentioned in the Talmud <note>Tractate Chullin, Chapter "All are forbidden" (Elu Terefot)</note>. Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said: It is written, "And God made the two great lights," but then it is written, "The great light and the small light." The Moon said before the Creator: "Sovereign of the Universe, is it possible for two kings to wear one crown?" He replied: "Go and diminish yourself."

## Chapter 1: With my own heart
<margin>The diminishing of the moon is a sign for the Children of Israel</margin>
I say to my heart: The Lord will complete this for me, to explain a sufficient measure for every wise and understanding person through his own knowledge. In a special discourse on the secrets of the Torah—I have known them, I have called them by name in righteousness—the discourse of the "Great Lights." How great are the foundations of these two wondrous and deep lessons! They stand at the height of the world.

This first one is the "Diminishing of the Moon," and its place is here in the *Pardes* <note>The Orchard of Pomegranates</note>. We are now explaining it with extreme brevity, without wandering too far from the intent of this book, according to the measure that stirs us to engage with it. I will explain and search out the "Discourse of Knowledge and Choice," which are the very foundations of the Torah.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the structure of the Sefirot, specifically focusing on how the Divine attributes relate to the concept of time and the "Diminishing of the Moon"—a kabbalistic metaphor for the exile and eventual restoration of the Divine Presence (Malchut).</meta>

# Slice of the Pomegranate: Gate 18 — The Diminishing of the Moon (Juice of Pomegranates)

Let us count for you, O Israel, days and years according to the meaning of *This month shall be for you* <note>Exodus 12:2; the foundational verse for the Jewish calendar</note>, for Israel sanctifies the New Moons and Israel sanctifies the seasons. Many commandments are dependent on the "proclamations of holiness" <note>The festival dates</note>, and that which is hidden is learned from that which is explicit. Behold "these are the festivals of the Lord"—what is written concerning them? *Which you shall proclaim* <note>Leviticus 23:4</note>, implying: whether you proclaim them intentionally, accidentally, or even if you are misled. I have no festivals other than these, and even "on the hidden day of our festival" <note>Psalm 81:4; often referring to Rosh Hashanah when the moon is hidden</note>. And regarding the fact that the Blessed God establishes His throne for judgment, what is written of it? *For it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob* <note>Psalm 81:5</note>, as is well known.

### And Still
One might argue against this: surely *which you shall proclaim* was only said when we establish these holy proclamations according to the Torah—meaning that Passover must be in the spring, and near the time when the moon is at its point of conjunction with the sun. Similarly, Rosh Hashanah must be close to the "attachment" of the two, when the moon is found directly under the sun at a single point during the harvest season. If so, every high court that intercalates the years and fixes the months throughout history undoubtedly relies on their calculations and nothing else; for they saw the paths of the sun to establish the lunar months by them. But if a court that is not expert acts willfully or errs in the opposite direction, Heaven forbid—did the Torah say "to them you shall listen"? We are not dealing here with the wicked or with corrupted judgment. If so, there would be no absolute free choice here.

### And the Answer Comes
The righteous are called "righteous" based on the fact that before the Blessed One there is no favoritism at all. How could those possessing free choice be called righteous if their goodness was not in their own hands? What can we say? That those who diminish themselves of their own will—according to the meaning of "my heart" and "go and diminish yourself" <note>A reference to the Midrash where the Moon is told to diminish herself, representing the virtue of humility</note>—are the ones characterized by a just and perfect choice. This is the meaning of *The Lord knows the way of the righteous* <note>Psalm 1:6</note>; He knows their *choice*, and therefore it does not say He knows their *deeds*. Even though they are one and the same, we are careful not to err here, for the text explains that their "way" and their "actions"—that is, their choice—is what is known before the Blessed One. Thus, the deeds are elevated through choice, and the choice is held within Divine knowledge, as stated. Knowledge and Choice are always compatible, though there is no human solution to the paradox between them. And if there were among us those who cast off the yoke, by the thousands and tens of thousands, through our sins and the iniquities of our fathers—concerning these, a covenant was struck at the end of the Reproofs in Deuteronomy, where it is written: *He did not give rest, nor shall there be repose for the sole of your foot* <note>Deuteronomy 28:65</note>. This is the essential proof for what comes at the conclusion of the passage: *and there is no buyer* <note>Deuteronomy 28:68</note>. For such is the way: every buyer becomes a master to himself, and "the eyes of servants are toward the hand of their masters, and the eyes of a maidservant toward the hand of her mistress." But in a state of exhaustion, failing eyes, and an aching soul, they have no master. Immediately following this are the words *These are the words of the covenant*. This is the ultimate good, for the line of justice conducts itself: the first remains the first. He, the True Ancient One, "buys" (acquires) everything and remembers the kindness of the patriarchs.

### And This
Is the reason for the "five acquisitions" that the Sages taught: the Torah, Heaven and Earth, Abraham, Israel, and the Holy Temple. For indeed, the Torah is entirely from the mouth of the Almighty, and it is the first "acquisition" in the consensus of its parts. Through it, He looked to create the work of Heaven and Earth, for it was His professional tool. One learns from the other: just as the Torah is a single acquisition—such that one who denies even a single letter of it has "despised the word of the Lord"—so too nothing is missing from the entire heavenly host.

<column-break/>

The emanation of the "Return" <note>The process of the Divine Feminine returning to her source</note> is 205. <term>Malchut</term> <note>The Sefirah of Sovereignty/Divine Feminine</note> existed before the emanation of <term>Tiferet</term> <note>The Sefirah of Beauty/Divine Male</note> from the mystery of the Firmament, and then returned to the "World" <note>Hebrew: *Olam*</note>. For if not, *Tiferet*—which encompasses all six extremities—would not be "World," a term implying "encompassing." This is a miraculous mystery, so that we do not err by saying that her emanation in "Thought" was prior to his emanation in the mystery of "Knowledge" <note>Da'at</note>. This occurred after the "cloud and thick darkness," which are the perplexities that *Tiferet* has, such as Kindness and Severity being revealed, becoming manifest and clothed within them. Through this, the emanation of the Return to the world occurred. And his students, who held the true tradition among them that the emanation of *Tiferet* preceded her emanation, questioned: how is it possible to think she is a product of *Tiferet*? Rather, she is the life-force of the "vessels" of *Tiferet*, and twice it branches out over him; at the very least, she shall be a "crown upon his head."

And these are the words of the *Explanation of Issachar* <note>original: "Bi'ur Yissachar," likely referring to a commentary by R. Issachar Baer</note>: Man is a crown before giving birth to a "small one." The term "Firmament" according to his vision was for its life-force; "Man" was in the "Foundation" <note>Yesod</note>, the mystery of "your youth," so that you may return, etc. And it was more refined than the "Thought of Abraham," a "Crown," etc. For the Crown is more revealed and possesses some quality. Afterward, this returned to the intent of "connection," that she should rise within the worlds in tranquility. She is "my heart," and the mystery of her emanation is the Crown—the crown of *Tiferet*. The letter *Yod* in the name *Boaz*, the letter *Vav* in its rising to "her father's house." And because it was still difficult for the emanation, as they had not yet received the emanation of *Tiferet* that is within <term>Binah</term> <note>Understanding</note> and the order of the *Rebus* <note>A complex kabbalistic configuration</note>, and for the Crown—they excluded those who were uncertain about the births of "Knowledge." It is known to the soul that deserves it: that which was a "circle" in Thought—the intent being that the emanation of *Tiferet* in its ascent rose in Thought and was depicted in the mystery of Knowledge. The mystery of Knowledge was the "memory" between them, the "Upper One" that was explained regarding the "covering spice" as we have written, etc. The "Judges of Thoughts"—Thought is concealed within.

### Chapter 4
After the emanation of the "Kings" has been explained, one must know the matter of the <term>Nesirah</term> <note>The "Sawing" or separation of the Divine Male and Female who were originally back-to-back</note>, as the Sages taught: "The Holy One, blessed be He, sawed the woman from the man" and the part became complex. How was the "emptying" prior to the Sawing? And why were they created thus, needing a Sawing? As is explained in the precious section of *Acharei Mot* on the verse *And after her life...* To understand the matter of the Sawing in its causes, one must know that "Judgment" <note>Din</note> never exists except through "Kindness" <note>Chesed</note>, for "the world shall be built on kindness." Therefore, of necessity, Judgment is swallowed and hidden, as the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (may he rest in peace) in the chapter *Acharei Mot*. It is proper to know that *Binah* is carved as the first letter *He* of the Name, for there resides every Will that was impressed from within her. However, the essence of her "carving" was as explained in the "Gate of Diminishing." One must further know: in the ten formations, there were seven <term>Partzufim</term> <note>Divine Personas or "Faces"</note> for every creation. This means for the "Revealed Kindness" of his being. Perhaps there would be four in Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, four in the Light of Life—a name revealed to all inhabitants of the world until it was explained. All of this unified Wisdom within *Binah*; she was clothed within it and became pregnant by it with the offspring of *Tiferet* and *Malchut* that were within him. The power of *Tiferet* was revealed more than theirs in the holy way at the beginning, emerging before the emanation of *Malchut* in the "Nose." The emanation in *Binah* was explained as being in the aspect of "The Small Face and the Feminine" <note>Z'eir Anpin and Nukva</note>, so that the *Binah* (5) is before the *Dalet* (4), seven before him, and all as mentioned above. This gives life to the matter of her "grasp" in the World of Creation. That is the measure. And in the "two secretings" there will be some revelation in her. There, this will be understood: the name *Yah* in Wisdom—the *Yod* is Wisdom in the return of *Binah* so that it becomes "Two," and at first "Five" and "Six." The Sages (of blessed memory) said: the *Partzufim* are within the life-force and the reception of the perfect *Binah* which is a circle. The emanation is of four or seven *Partzufim*. All life is from the "Birthgiver," for *Malchut* was above *Tiferet* to be "frightened" there. The Kindness of *Tiferet* in the emanation of *Tiferet* is to make known what is destined for him—to give life to all his emanations. And finally, *Malchut* in her emanation is in the mystery of Wisdom within *Binah*, in the aspect of the *Yod* in the Nose, whereby 316 *Partzufim* were repaired.
