# Nectar of Pomegranates — Gate 32: On the Explanation of Intention

A student should not think to themselves: "If [God is the source of all], then let us pray to Him alone without involving His attributes <note>original: "Middot"—referring to the ten Sephirot or divine emanations.</note>," for He is the core of everything. Know that it is a high matter: one is not exempt if they pray to the attributes alone without involving the Emanator <note>The "Emanator" (*Ma'atzil*) refers to the Infinite Source, the *Ein Sof*, who brings the attributes into being.</note>. Yet, our life and strength come from the Truth. Because the Emanator (blessed be He) has no end, no limit, and no defined point, and because His desire is Light, He is related to us through Names. This is because His desire acts through specific limits and changes; our life changes from one will to another, though He does not change from action to action. Therefore, we must not speak of any limit, place, or boundary regarding Him, Heaven forbid. All Names and titles should be viewed as "garments" <note>A common Kabbalistic metaphor where the divine light "clothes" itself in attributes to become accessible to creation.</note> for the Soul, and His transformation is through His hands in the attributes of life. The Essence <note>original: "Atzmut"—the core, unknowable being of God.</note> alone is holy. Through the Names, our sanctuary and refuge are established. All our cries are directed to Him and not to His attributes, but we rely on saying: "He is called 'Mighty' in the attribute of Might (*Gevurah*), and 'Merciful' in the attribute of Kindness (*Chesed*)." For, Heaven forbid, He grants power to Might to perform mighty acts, and to Kindness to perform acts of kindness. Therefore, in our prayers, when we mention "The Great" <note>Referring to the attribute of *Chesed* (Kindness).</note>, it hints at the Might, and we direct the Essence within His Might. Our intention should be toward the Essence that spreads through the "Greatness" <note>Another name for the attribute of Kindness.</note>. This is the intention for all Names and titles: they return to the totality of the Emanations (*Sephirot*). There is nothing among all things that does not hint at the Essence. The meaning of "Intention" is to direct everything to Him alone. We must think that the Infinite (*Ein Sof*, blessed be He) unites everything; He is the foundation of the attributes and flows through the Essence that spreads from Him into them. Through this, there is power for the "Soul" of the attributes to perform their actions. Thus, all actions are attributed to the Infinite (blessed be He), as was explained in the Gate of Essence and Vessels.

According to what I have written regarding the matter of Intention (*Kavanah*), Heaven forbid that a simple person <note>original: "Hedyot"—an ordinary or unlearned person.</note> should be required to focus his words and letters on the complex secrets of the Names and titles; to suggest such a requirement would be heresy. Rather, one should direct their heart toward the Essence that spreads from the Infinite. Regarding the intention of the Emanations, Heaven forbid one should imagine a separation between the Emanations and the One who intends through them. It is forbidden to create division or to separate the "limbs," Heaven forbid—meaning to attribute a thing to a specific power alone. Instead, one should view it as a table of the Infinite, where the Emanations are the "salt" that seasons everything. The Intention must be articulated in this language: that one intends for the standing of the Names mentioned here to hint at the inner spiritual Essence. This Essence comes to enter the Emanations that spread from the Infinite, which are unified in absolute unity. One should remove from their mind any thought of "dividing" the matter of the attributes. One should focus on the four letters <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God (YHWH).</note> and their vocalization as explained previously in Gate 1, Chapter 5. One should walk in the straight path and also intend that these four letters include the ten Emanations, for all the Emanations and their inner spiritual dimensions act through the specific attribute being addressed. There is no division in His house. How good it is for a person to direct their heart toward the specific "Countenance" <note>A specific manifestation or persona of the Divine.</note> known in the secret of the "Garden of Pomegranates" <note>A reference to the primary work of Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, *Pardes Rimonim*, of which this text is an abridgment.</note>. See the Gate of Nicknames, for through this, his prayer will be accepted. One should pray and direct themselves toward Him alone, and turn away from all else! Then the world of separation ceases, and He is a "Gracious and Merciful God."

<column-break/>

### Chapter 3: To Understand

The ultimate goal of the essence of Intention is that a person must draw down spirituality from the conduits <term>Tzinorot: the spiritual channels through which divine energy flows</term> into the attributes, which are the "vessels." This is done so that one can separate the "veil" over the service. You must awaken to perform our mission. The intention is that everything follows the heart. This "spirituality" is formed from the heart into the "spirituality of the Voice." One must draw strength from above to distinguish the attributes and elevate them, and to raise the service within the spirit to the Most High. The core of Intention is to draw strength so that through them, the Voice may cause the attributes to ascend and be renewed in the place of the "Spirit of the World," returning them to their original state.

However, it is proper to know that the intention of mentioning the Names does not change based on the change of place. The intention of mentioning the Names must always include the totality of "Being" (*Havayah*). When one mentions "God" (*Elohim*), it is proper to intend the general scope of the Emanation and those spiritual forces acting to enter the world that spreads from the Infinite. When we mention a specific name from the attribute of Kindness (*Chesed*), we should direct our focus to that specific Emanation and the power of the inner Essence within it. Sometimes, even with a general Name, it is proper to focus on a specific Emanation, for although it hints at the whole, the inner aspect will have a specific awakening according to the context and location. Know that when we mention Names that are not in their usual "place," we must still intend for the general flow of Being as hinted at by the "Voice." Afterward, one should focus intensely on how all attributes and various aspects are included within it. We must always focus on the specific Emanation within the context of the "Forty-Two Letter Name" <note>A mystical name of God used in Kabbalistic prayer.</note> and the constant flow of Kindness that includes everything. See the explanation regarding "Hints and Shared Aspects," for through this, the Voice will exist and the Emanation will return as explained in the Gate of Conduits and the attributes of the Emanations. One must focus on the specific aspect of the "Life-Force" within each and every Emanation, according to the title, its location, and its context.

We must also know what specific aspect a certain "nickname" <note>Terms used to describe God other than His formal names, such as "Merciful" or "Just."</note> refers to, and how it differs from other aspects of the Emanations. This is the secret they hinted at: do not be confused by the doubling or changing of hints. Everything is within the attribute of the "He" <note>The letter *He* in the Divine Name, often associated with the feminine presence of God or the attribute of Sovereignty.</note>. Sometimes it hints at one place, and sometimes it returns to its own context. Therefore, it is proper to intend for each and every thing according to its relationship and value, specifically regarding the details of Divine actions.

However, in the general prayer, one must intend that the "Voice" is in Beauty (*Tiferet*) and the "Speech" is in Sovereignty (*Malchut*). These should be the "internalizing houses." One should intend that they be unified together—Voice with Speech—into the Name YHWH. This "Spirit" belongs to the "Foundation" (*Yesod*). Furthermore, one should intend that the Voice and Speech are included in the names *Yah* and *Yaho*. Again, one should intend that the intentions of Understanding (*Binah*) be combined together, composed of various divine names, and return to hint at the totality of the "Brains" <note>original: "Mochin"—the intellectual faculties of the divine structure (Chachmah, Binah, Da'at).</note>. Finally, it is proper to intend in every single prayer for the specific attribute that "rules" at that time, according to the changes of the times—such as the afternoon prayer (*Minchah*). When that specific attribute is present, our intention should follow its context and time. It is also proper to intend for every name and every kindness... this is discussed in the Gate of Specific Names.

->Finished and complete, praise be to God, Creator of the universe.<-

# Nectar of Pomegranates — Gate 31: The Souls

There is a matter that is slight, accidental, and somewhat changing and frequent; according to how one continues in it, so too will they cause a blemish <note>original: "pigm" — a spiritual flaw or defect caused by sin</note> above. This occurs because the Shell <note>original: "Klipah" — plural "Klipot"; the "Husks" or "Shells" of impurity that conceal divine light in Kabbalistic thought</note> gains dominion in the aforementioned place that the person passes over. For death is dependent upon the Attributes <note>original: "Middot" — the Sephirot or divine emanations</note>, and through Mercy <note>original: "Chesed"</note> it passes over the Kingship <note>original: "Malkhut"</note>, and Mercy shall rule over His thread <note>original: "chuto"</note> in the place where the power of the Shell has strengthened itself. Through this, the portions of the Kingships are wiped away. This is for the one who causes damage, for by drawing a Shell upon himself, he takes hold of the seal above as well. The intention is not that the Shell enters the place of Holiness, God forbid, for that would be a movement of darkness and the gravity of evil thoughts. Rather, it happens that the transition occurs in their place, and the Shell reveals itself through the screen of the body upon itself. It becomes mixed in their place and enters into the Shells; yet the intention in the essence <note>original: "be-ikkar"</note> of its strengthening is not that it enters the Shell, God forbid. And this returns to the aforementioned, as is known regarding the High Covenant <note>original: "Brit Elyon"</note> which is protected from the Shells. The excess is abandoned, and just as the alternating voice <note>original: "kol"</note> nurses from the right side, so too the flow and existence of the life-force and all the levels of Holiness from the right side are drawn from the pure and holy abundance. Thus, the life-force nurses from the left, and there will be a flow and existence of the life-force for all levels of Holiness included within it. From the aforementioned movement, the flow is bestowed upon it, and there is no blemish from this, for it nurses from a level of Holiness and goes under to separate the Shell. This is the secret of his soul; just as we see that this flow spreads through the simple movements of the life-force, it ceases from the holy flow and is prepared to be divided from its place. Just as the holy flow that bestows life upon the walls will be lacking its portion, and they will wait for other waters to be strengthened by them, so too at the time one is separated from the world, the upright person bestows through his deeds upon...

<meta>This page transitions from the end of Gate 31, which discussed the nature of the soul and the impact of sin on the spiritual garments, into Gate 32. This new section focuses on the "Ways of Intention" (Kavanah), specifically how a person should direct their mind during prayer to bridge the gap between the physical words spoken and the divine "Essence" of the Infinite.</meta>

# Nectar of Pomegranates — Gate 32: On the Explanation of Intention

The seeker should not think to say: "If so, let us pray—Heaven forbid—without the explanation of His Attributes <note>original: "Middot"; the ten Sephirot or divine emanations through which God interacts with the world</note>," for this is the core of everything. Know that this matter is a sin—not to be bound in one's actions to the Attributes through the explanation of the praise. Despite all this, our voice and speech arise from physical moisture, for the voice is composed of moisture, heat, air, and the striking of the breath, which creates it. It is a physical action that settles in the bones. Because the palate is composed of membranes and fibers, the palate changes from one desire to another, and from one action to another. Therefore, it is fitting for us to intend that the prayer is called out to His portions <note>meaning the specific Sephirot</note> and the names and titles. 

However, let all the essences and titles be regarded only as "matter" <note>original: "chomer"; the vessel or physical container for the light</note>, or like drops. According to their value, they should be the "garment" of the Intention, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, exists within the Essence of the Sephirot alone. Do not think that you are calling out to the vessels themselves, but to their Essence. As the Sage <note>likely referring to Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, the author's teacher</note> in all his holiness said: "To Him, and not to His Attributes." 

This means that the Infinite <note>original: "Ein Sof"; the Godhead prior to any manifestation</note> is called, for example, by the Attribute of Might <note>original: "Gevurah"</note> because the Infinite provides the power within Might to perform mighty deeds, and within Mercy <note>original: "Chesed"</note> to perform merciful deeds. Therefore, when you intend to say: "The Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome," the Attribute itself is within that Greatness. All our intentions must focus on the Essence that spreads within the Greatness. This is the intention for all the names and titles said regarding all the Sephirot. The core of all things is that his mind should be elevated toward the Essence. This intention means that a person should focus on Him alone, for from the Infinite, Blessed be He, comes everything. He is the one who unifies the Attributes and pours influence through the Essence that spreads from Him into them. By their dwelling, He gives power to the Sephirot to perform their actions. Thus, all actions are attributed to the Infinite, Blessed be He, as was explained in the Gate of Essence and Vessels.

Regarding what was explained in the matter of Intention: what must a person intend in his words and his titles? That the Sephirot are like a "garment" to the Essence that spreads from the Infinite. Returning to the matter of intending upon the Sephirot: it appears that a person should intend in a Sephirah in this way—to imagine in his mind the matter of the Sephirah and fix his intention on them according to what arises in his leaning thought. He must be careful, for he could reach a point of making a "separation" <note>original: "pirud"; the theological error of viewing the Sephirot as independent gods rather than unified aspects of the One</note>. This is because it is impossible to attribute anything to the Creator except as "matter," as something containing, affected, or leaning. If a person intends this toward the Sephirot, he will—Heaven forbid—fill himself with errors and further separation. 

Rather, the Intention must be in this manner: he should intend toward the Essence of the Being <note>original: "Atzmut ha-Havayah"</note>—these are the "pomegranates"—within the "bone" <note>original: "etzem"; also means essence</note> of the Sephirah and its inner spirituality, which is prepared to enter the Sephirot that spread from the Infinite, which are unified in the ultimate unity. So must the one who intends direct his heart. One must remove from his mind the idea that we have anything that can truly define the matter of the Attributes, or distinguish them, or provide a boundary for them. We cannot even hint at them or include their inner spiritual matters, except through the aspect of the specific Sephirah assigned to it. One should visualize in his mind the Four-Letter Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> punctuated with the vowels according to their specific Sephirah, as explained above regarding the Name of Four Letters in Chapter 30. Then he shall go his way in peace. 

He should also intend that these four letters include the ten Sephirot, hinting at the inclusion of all ten Sephirot unified with the actions of that specific Attribute which is known to him through the spread of the Sephirot among them. How good it is if he also focuses his heart on the specific "garment" known to be the hint for that Sephirah... for his path is otherwise fraught with danger. Generally, he should intend toward Him with this secret: that everything is included and unified from the beginning of the world before it was taken into this specific matter.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 3

To understand the ultimate purpose of the core of Intention, it seems to me that one must intend to draw down the spirituality from the upper level to the letters that he is mentioning. This is so that he can cause his letters to "fly" <note>original: "lehafriach"; a metaphor for the words of prayer ascending to the divine realm</note> toward the upper level to arouse the "Setting of the Table" and to prepare them. For everything is according to the words—meaning, a "breath" of air is a spirituality that is formed from him. To that spirituality, one must draw power from the higher level to make his "table" fly and to raise the vitality to the high levels to achieve the "Union" <note>original: "Zivug"; the mystical coupling of divine aspects</note>. The core of Intention is to draw power so that by that power, the letters will ascend above and be formed in the place of the Spirit of the World, and be formed in their smallness.

However, it is proper to know that the intention of mentioning the Names does not change... even though his intention must always include the Being <note>Havayah</note>, etc. The matter is this: when a person mentions "The Place" <note>original: "HaMakom"; a name for God</note>, it is proper to intend toward the essence of the "inclusion" of the Sephirah and the inner spirituality prepared to enter the Essence that spreads from the Infinite. When we mention the name of the Sephirah appointed to us in its place, it is proper to intend toward the specific Sephirah of the ten Sephirot—such as Mercy <note>Chesed</note> on the right, and so on—toward the essence of the inner Sephirah in which is the Being, etc. 

Sometimes, even with the Four-Letter Name, it is proper to intend toward a specific Sephirah. For even though it hints at the inclusion of the inner core, there will be a specific arousal for a Sephirah according to its matter and place. Know that when we mention the Name of Names that are not in their place, one should intend generally toward that Sephirah which is hinted at in it, without detailing any specific aspect. Sometimes we will have another explanation where all the Attributes are included in it, and several other aspects for each and every one. We must intend that this specific Sephirah, in its greatness, is unified with all the other ten Sephirot through the letter *Vav* <note>the third letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the six emotive attributes</note>. Each one of them includes all of them. Through the "Mights" <note>Gevurot</note>, they become "face to face" and in a true union, for through this, there will be a crowning and unification of the Sephirah, as explained in the Gate of Crowns and the Forms of the Sephirot.

Behold, just as the intentions must focus on the aforementioned details regarding how each Sephirah is included, it depends on the title according to its place and matter. We must know this intention to sustain the... and the matter of Divinity from the aspects of that general Sephirah... hinted at by this law... and the prayers which are all hinted at in place X. For what is hinted here is not hinted there; every single place has a special tension, power, and property unique to itself. Therefore, it is fitting that we intend in each and every thing according to its relationship and value, and all this is according to the specific levels.

However, in the generality of the Prayer, we must intend that the **Voice** is in Beauty <note>original: "Tiferet"</note> and the **Speech** is in Kingship <note>original: "Malkhut"</note>. They shall be in Foundation <note>original: "Yesod"</note>... and he should intend that they be unified together, Voice with Speech. There is also the "Double-Headed" hint, which refers to the Foundation between them. Furthermore, he should understand that the Voice and the Speech include Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, Kingship <note>Malkhut</note>, and Understanding <note>Binah</note>... and achieve the Union as is known, for the Voice ascends from Wisdom and Understanding... and he should intend that they be like the inclusion of the "N-H-Y" <note>an acronym for the Sephirot Netzach, Hod, and Yesod</note> so that through the three of them, the union will be complete. 

It is also proper to intend that in each and every prayer below, it is completed in its beauty according to the division and strength of the times, and also because of our sins, and in the aspect of that Attribute that our intention is focused on according to its matter and our distress. It is also proper to intend in each and every Name, the Four-Letter Name and the Twelve-Letter Name, which were in the Gate of the Details of the Names...

---

->Completed and finished, praise be to God, Creator of the World.<-

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic concept of Kavanah (mystical intention), emphasizing that while prayer uses physical voice and speech, the mind must focus on the divine Essence (Atzmut) within the Sephirot to draw down spiritual energy and achieve divine union.</summary>

<meta>This page concludes Gate 31, which details the spiritual dynamics of the soul and the consequences of sin, and begins Gate 32, which focuses on the "Ways of Intention" (Kavanah). It builds on the previous discussion of how human actions affect the divine realms.</meta>

-> **Nectar of Pomegranates — Gate 31: The Souls** <-

Refining and purity [allow the soul] to face forward, and through this, the aforementioned [soul] will connect with the Marrow <note>original: "M"CH" - Moach; refers to the higher cognitive Sephirot: Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge</note>. So too the wicked, by their lack of spiritual repairs and their transgressions, [stray] like them. "The commandment is a lamp" <note>a reference to Proverbs 6:23</note> from the aforementioned [source], which bequeaths strength to the Marrow. The vitality of the whole will be spread thin, and you shall remember the good judgments, etc., until you ascend. The whole will be separated and divided like its rows, drawing from the waste <note>original: "psolt"; the impure spiritual byproducts</note>. The soul of that wicked person will cling like a liquid, and his portion [will be there]. It writes the power of the Shells <note>original: "Klipot"; the forces of impurity that conceal divine light</note> and arouses it to suckle from the "bitterness of asps" <note>a biblical metaphor for the poisonous nature of sin</note>, and his portion will be joined to him as is known. This is the matter of the "blemish" and "cutting the shoots" <note>a Talmudic idiom for heresy or damaging the spiritual hierarchy</note> of the drop of the Marrow above. 

With this, the matter of the wicked can be understood, of whom it is said: "What right have you to recite My laws?" <note>Psalm 50:16</note>. For the research of the wicked enters within the Shells like a burden. He blesses and moves these Shells through the blessing, for through that blessing, abundance <note>original: "shefa"</note> is drawn upon him from the Marrow, and he [instead] provides suckle into the Shells until the "grain" is demanded. The prayer of the "uncircumcised" <note>referring to one whose heart is closed or who is spiritually impure</note> belongs to us, and the intention of the transgression is in all his joy; this is the secret of "and the stumbling block," for his fall is swift. This is the reason why to every place Jerusalem [the people] were exiled, the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> went with them. Because of the aforementioned connection, all the transgression that flows through Jerusalem [causes] the Shell to be cooked and vitalized. 

Nevertheless, the power of [repentance] is great, and one can merit to repair everything when he feels regret. For when he returns and purifies the power of the Shells, he returns some of the transgression and the blessings that were taken from his soul. They will relate and ascend for nothing as a longing of the soul, and [God] will account his sins as merits, until his level is raised. This is "a time when man ruled over man to his hurt" <note>Ecclesiastes 8:9</note>—to his own hurt, Heaven forbid, for from his palate he shall pervert the prey. He shall illuminate those attributes and take them from the side of impurity. Therefore, the Righteousness departs, and this is the [exile of] the Divine Presence.

<column-break/>

There is a matter lighter than our judgment, and its filth is lighter than its dwelling. According to what one draws upon himself, so will he cause a blemish above. For the rule of the Shell in the aforementioned place arouses [judgment] upon it. For the commandments are dependent upon the Divine Attributes <note>original: "Middot"; the Sephirot</note>, and when one transgresses against God, the Shell rules over that place where the sickness rests. This is the power of the Shell from the perspective of his higher soul's existence. By drawing down [impurity], he adds to its vitality and strengthens its power above as well. 

This is the meaning of the Shell entering the place of Holiness, Heaven forbid. A sinner is judged, and the severity of the "strange woman" <note>a metaphor for the "Other Side" or evil inclination</note> descends to the lower depths of the belly. He "vomits" the higher holiness, and the Shell rules over the body itself. It becomes mixed, and their suckling enters the Shells. To the center it enters the Shells, Heaven forbid, becoming like a barren woman. She enters the Shells, and Heaven forbid, she suckles from the aforementioned "lamp." As is known regarding the Higher Covenant <note>original: "Brit"; often referring to the Sephirah of Yesod and spiritual/sexual purity</note>, the sin reaches the source of the Shells and the "creeping things." 

Just as a drop suckles from the "Right" <note>the side of Mercy/Chesed</note>, so it is taken for their vitality and blessings. All the holy pearls and the flow of the Right come from pure and holy abundance. So too, through his sin, he suckles from the waste, and through him, the abundance of his place of vitality—all the holy levels in which he is included—comes from the aforementioned "bitterness." Abundance is flowed [to the Shells] in exchange, as you have heard. There is no greater blemish than this: that a holy level must suckle from the side of "menstruation" <note>a term for extreme ritual impurity</note> and flow to the Shell, through the "pipe" of his soul. It is like one who flows vitality into a lowly place. This is the "shame" of the soul, when the transgression causes the Holiness to flow to the Shells. His portion and his strength will be "clothed in plaster" for the soul's vitality, to be despaired of when it departs from the world. Just as the small blemish flows to...

<column-break/>

## Gate Thirty-Two: On the Explanation of the Ways of Intention

Aside from the cause of the generations of the souls' vitality, etc. The general rule: know [the difference] between the few of the wise and the common people. For the wise man, within his Intention <note>original: "Kavanah"</note>, when he intends [to climb] the levels of the ladder, first his soul is like its openings. Its level [rises] to the level [above], and that level to the one above it, until it is before the Blessed One. He is proven and clings to his source in the Source of Life, until He flows upon it a bit of great abundance. He becomes a place of resting, and in his intention to flow it, the suckling is divided to the whole world, as explained in the Portion of Terumah. 

This continues until the Divine Presence clings to him, for he desires that the abundance should come through him. The power of the aforementioned "Righteous One, the foundation of the world" <note>original: "Tzaddik Yesod Olam"</note> will rest [upon him]. Therefore, he clings to the power and vitality. The intention of the plain meaning of the words is not like the intention of the secrets and mysteries of the Kabbalah <note>original: "Kab"</note> and the depths of contemplation. For according to the place of the soul's ascent, so shall be the abundance. As explained in the portion [of the Zohar] regarding the fat and the blood: if one intends the secrets of the higher rulers, he shall not enter the surrounding spirits. If he transgresses this, it will be a reversal, like one who turns his back to the King. Through the "pardon of the North," the King is hidden.

### Chapter 2: After we have spoken of the greatness of the Intention, it is proper to know how the Intention should be. 
Know that it is not proper to desire that one's Intention be solely in the Attributes <note>original: "Middot"</note>; that is, that he should only think of ascending to the Attributes. Rather, everything should be within the secret of joining with the Infinite <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note>, which is [achieved] through thought. Because the Beginning is ungraspable, we pray to the Infinite through His Attributes.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 1: In the Explanation of the Ways of Intention
Know that because the soul is a "portion" [from above], it is drawn from the Marrow of its Father in the Holy Countenance <note>original: "Partzuf"</note> through the chain of descent of his soul from level to level. Through the awakening of his deeds, [the soul] ascends to the higher source. Through this, abundance and blessing are drawn to the spread-out areas, and from there to the lower level until it reaches and rests upon him via the entire "ladder." 

According to the measure of the awakening and the preparation of the deed, so will be the aforementioned clinging and the illumination of great abundance. Likewise, according to the place of the soul's source, so will be its level and the illumination of the abundance. The light of the abundance flowed through a person at a "donkey" level <note>a lower, more physical level of soul</note> is not the same as that flowed through [a higher soul]. Similarly, a blemish caused by a soul of a lower level is not the same as one caused by a higher soul. One cannot repair what the other can. There is no "grace" before the Heavens except through [spiritual effort], as is written: "Then you shall delight" <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>. 

With this, the reason for the statement that "the Holy One, Blessed be He, is as precise with the righteous as a hair's breadth" is clarified. For as it is written: "And round about Him it is very tempestuous" <note>Psalm 50:3; the Hebrew 'nis'arah' (tempestuous) is related to 'se'arah' (hair)</note>. According to the level the righteous man reaches, if he performs one of the commandments [imperfectly], he diminishes the flow of vitality that was supposed to be flowed through him. Had he performed it perfectly, the lack would not have been so great. He would have been a "pipe" for light and abundance. Similarly, the blemish made by a righteous man is not comparable [to others], according to his high level. When he deviates, the abundance is redirected to the "Other Side" <note>original: "Sitra Achra"; the side of impurity</note>, even if the deviation is only slight.

<summary>This page concludes the discussion on how sin damages the soul and diverts divine abundance to the "Shells" (evil forces), before transitioning to a detailed explanation of "Intention" (Kavanah) in prayer as a ladder for the soul to reach the Infinite.</summary>

### The Apology of the Proofreader

**Blessed** is the Lord who has brought me to this heavenly work, which until now was hidden from me, for it is a craft and not just a wisdom. Rabbi Shimon Cohen came to me and served as my guide in the work of proofreading, until my hand reached the sweetness of pomegranates <note>This is a poetic pun on the book's title, "Pardes Rimonim" (Orchard of Pomegranates).</note>. Master Jacob and I were among them once and twice, and a third time it came into the hands of Rabbi Shimon Cohen, who read it to refine and purify it from all error. For "The Wisdom of Solomon" <note>A humble play on the proofreader's own name, Solomon.</note> is found but a tiny bit in the Talmud, and regarding the "flesh and juice of pomegranates," not at all—not even like a pomegranate seed. Yet, I could not restrain myself from drinking from the pomegranate juice, not only to receive a reward, but to establish this heavenly work upon its foundation. If any error is found, let everyone judge me with merit <note>original: "melamdin zechut"; a plea for the reader to be forgiving of mistakes</note> and let no one judge me with guilt. May the Lord count it for you as good, for "who can understand errors?" even one who is expert in all expertise. Thus says the humble one, a trodden threshold, **Solomon** son of Ephraim Ha-Kohen, of the Kobrin family.

---

->By the worker engaged in this heavenly task with faithfulness, the young Chaim, son of the late<-
->Honorable Rabbi Gumpel Altshul (may the memory of the righteous and holy be for a blessing) from the holy community of Prague the capital; and currently<-
->in the holy community of Amsterdam.<-
